#### Make ericson_math an implementation detail, not a second public geometry API

- **File:** `engine/math/ericson_math.h:1-139`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T4, CONVENTIONS/Files, PHILOSOPHY/The public face

**What:** `ericson_math.h` is a public header of `MattMath` that holds no type, is named
after a person rather than the primary type it holds, and exposes sixteen geometry
functions that exist solely to implement `matt_math.h`'s named free functions — so the
library ships two overlapping public answers to the same questions, one of them
undocumented and none of it reachable from `matt_math.h`.

**Evidence:**

        // Real-Time Collision Detection
        // Christer Ericson
        // 2005

        #include "engine/math/matt_math.h"

        namespace mattmath
        {
            bool test_AABB_AABB(const mattmath::RectangleF& a,
                const mattmath::RectangleF& b);

The only non-test includer is `matt_math.cpp:2`; `matt_math.h` never includes it. Every
one of the sixteen declarations is called from exactly one place — the matching
`mattmath::*_intersect` wrapper — or from nothing at all.

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS/Files says headers are "named for the primary type they
hold"; this one holds none, and its name tells a reader about a book instead of about
the engine. Because it sits in `engine/math/` beside `matt_math.h`, with no
public/private split in the target, a stranger linking `MattMath` gets both surfaces and
no signal that one is internal — and the two disagree numerically in at least one place
(see `test_circle_circle`, below). CONVENTIONS/Namespaces already provides the
vocabulary for this: "`detail` wraps internals that headers must expose but users must
not touch." Deciding the header's status is also the cheapest way to close several of the
findings above: internals need a contract for the next maintainer, but public API needs
one for a stranger, and the answer determines how much documentation work `:74-138` is.

**Remedy:** Decide whether these are `mattmath::detail` internals or public API. If
internal, move them behind `detail`, rename the file for what it holds, and let the
tests exercise them through `matt_math.h`'s named functions. If public, they need the
contracts, the tests and the naming pass the rest of this report describes.

#### Fix the winding comment on signed_2D_tri_area — it is backwards for this library

- **File:** `engine/math/ericson_math.cpp:685-691`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** docs
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Collision ("edge ordering, winding")

**What:** The only winding statement in the file is the book's, written for a y-up frame,
and it is unqualified — so in MattMath, where y grows downward, it says the opposite of
what a reader sees on screen.

**Evidence:**

        // Returns 2 times the signed triangle area. The result is positive if
        // abc is ccw, negative if abc is cw, zero if abc is degenerate.
        float signed_2D_tri_area(const Point2F& a,
            const Point2F& b, const Point2F& c)
        {
            return (a.x - c.x) * (b.y - c.y) - (a.y - c.y) * (b.x - c.x);
        }

**Why it matters:** `Vector2F::DIRECTION_UP` is `{ 0.0f, -1.0f }` (`matt_math.cpp:1907`)
and `RectangleF::bottom_right()` is `(x + width, y + height)` (`:765-768`), so MattMath
is a y-down screen frame. For `a = (0,0)`, `b = (10,0)`, `c = (0,10)` the function
returns `+100`, and that traversal on screen goes right, then down-and-left — clockwise
as drawn. "Positive if abc is ccw" is the standard mathematical convention and is not
wrong in the abstract, but unqualified in a y-down library it inverts the only sense in
which "winding" is a useful word to a 2D engine's user. `tests/math/math_tests.cpp:63-67`
repeats it (`// a, b, c are in counter-clockwise order` above the `== 100.0f` check), so
the ambiguity is now pinned by a test that reinforces it. Anyone using this to decide
polygon orientation, normal direction or side-of-edge gets the sign backwards on the
first try. PHILOSOPHY/Collision names winding specifically as a contract that must be
documented.

**Remedy:** Restate the comment in the engine's own frame — positive means
counter-clockwise in a y-up frame, which is clockwise as drawn because y grows downward —
and fix the two test comments that echo it.

#### Guard or document the unguarded divisions that publish NaN through out-parameters

- **File:** `engine/math/ericson_math.cpp:738-741, 758-765`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6

**What:** `barycentric` divides by a determinant that is zero for a collinear triangle and
`closest_pt_point_segment` divides by `dot(ab, ab)`, which is zero for a zero-length
segment. Neither guards, and the resulting NaN is written into a caller-visible
out-parameter rather than raised.

**Evidence:**

        float denom = d00 * d11 - d01 * d01;
        v = (d11 * d20 - d01 * d21) / denom;
        w = (d00 * d21 - d01 * d20) / denom;
        u = 1.0f - v - w;

        t = Vector2F::dot(c - a, ab) / Vector2F::dot(ab, ab);
        // If outside segment, clamp t (and therefore d) to the closest endpoint
        if (t < 0.0f) t = 0.0f;
        if (t > 1.0f) t = 1.0f;
        // Compute projected position from the clamped t
        d = a + t * ab;

**Why it matters:** The previous review flagged both lines and neither is in
`IMPLEMENTED.md`, so what is new is that the NaN does not stay inside the function. Both
`t < 0.0f` and `t > 1.0f` are false for NaN, so the clamp is a no-op and `d` becomes
`(NaN, NaN)`. `mattmath::circle_segment_intersect` (`matt_math.cpp:334-341`) hands that
`d` straight back as the contact point *and* returns false, so a caller that stores the
contact point of a "no hit" — which the file's own conventions permit, see the header
finding — propagates NaN into game state. The input is not exotic: `Segment` has no
validation (`matt_math.h:995-1004`, `matt_math.cpp:4030-4037`) and its *default*
construction is `(0,0)-(0,0)`, a zero-length segment. On the triangle side,
`test_point_triangle` → `barycentric` is reached from `mattmath::triangle_point_intersect`
(`matt_math.cpp:448-452`) and thence `Triangle::contains`, used by
`rectangle_triangle_intersect`; every containment query against a collinear triangle
silently answers "outside", because every comparison against NaN is false.

**Remedy:** Return a documented answer for the degenerate case in each — the segment's
single point with `t = 0`, and "outside" with `u = v = w = 0` for a degenerate triangle —
and state it in the header. See also the third division in `closest_pt_point_triangle`,
above.

#### Fix the naming breaches the conventions passes left in this file

- **File:** `engine/math/ericson_math.cpp:16, 316, 370, 392` and `engine/math/ericson_math.h:74-138`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Never, CONVENTIONS/Types, CONVENTIONS/Variables

**What:** camelCase locals, uppercase acronyms in public function names, the off-allowlist
abbreviation `pt` in four public names, and a SCREAMING non-macro constant added by the
most recent conventions commit itself.

**Evidence:**

        constexpr float SEGMENT_PARALLEL_EPSILON = 0.000001f;

        float radiusSum = a.radius() + b.radius();

        float sqDist = sq_dist_point_AABB(s.center(), b);

        float sqDist = 0.0f;

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS/Never lists "SCREAMING constants — screaming means macro,
nothing else" and "Abbreviations off the allowlist" (the allowlist is closed: `dt, id,
src, dst, min, max`). `SEGMENT_PARALLEL_EPSILON` is the sharpest case because it is new —
`git log -S` places it in `2fa12fe`, "Wrap the engine in namespace artattack — the last
conventions rule" — and the eight-line comment above it at `:9-15` explains the rename it
came from while the replacement still screams, so a reader scanning for preprocessor
danger stops here for nothing. (That comment is also a changelog entry rather than a
contract: it explains what the constant *used to be called* and not what magnitude it
guards.) `pt` appears in four public names — `closest_pt_point_triangle`,
`closest_pt_point_AABB`, `closest_pt_point_segment`, `closest_pt_point_OBB` — abbreviating
a word spelled out two tokens later in the same identifier. CONVENTIONS/Types requires
acronyms cased as words (`JsonLoader`, `UiButton`), which makes `test_AABB_AABB`,
`sq_dist_point_AABB`, `test_circle_AABB`, `signed_2D_tri_area`, `test_2D_segment_segment`
and `closest_pt_point_OBB` breaches of the one rule the document says everything falls out
of. These are public names, so the rename is a breaking change that gets cheaper the
sooner it happens — the engine has one client today.

**Remedy:** Rename to `test_aabb_aabb`, `closest_point_point_segment` and so on in one
pass, give the epsilon a snake_case name, and rewrite its comment to say what it measures
rather than what it was called.

#### Fill or delete the empty test case, and cover the untested public functions

- **File:** `tests/math/math_tests.cpp:90-93`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** testing
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Collision, PHILOSOPHY/Tests and toolchain

**What:** `test_test_segment_AABB` is an empty body that reports as a passing test, and
seven of the header's public functions have no test of any kind.

**Evidence:**

        TEST_CASE("test_test_segment_AABB")
        {
            // tested below with rectangle_segment_intersect
        }

**Why it matters:** A green test named after a function that is not exercised is worse
than a missing one: `ctest` reports it as covered. The previous review's lesson from
`closest_pt_point_OBB` was precisely that an untested primitive stayed broken for every
input until someone read it. Counting from the header, `test_AABB_AABB`,
`test_circle_circle`, both `test_circle_AABB` overloads, `sq_dist_point_AABB`,
`intersect_moving_AABB_AABB`, `barycentric` and `test_point_triangle` have no direct
test — `test_AABB_AABB` and `test_point_triangle` are the trunk of every rectangle and
triangle containment query in the game, and `intersect_moving_AABB_AABB` is the one with
the defect at the top of this report. PHILOSOPHY/Collision requires each primitive
"pinned by behavioural tests in the commit that creates them". Every degenerate case
named in this report — zero-length segment, coincident triangle vertices, collinear
triangle, touching segments, zero relative velocity — is unpinned, so any fix has nothing
to regress against.

#### Record the licence for the transcribed book code

- **File:** `engine/math/ericson_math.h:3-5`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** docs
- **Tenet:** T9

**What:** The file is a near-verbatim transcription of code from a copyrighted 2005 book,
attributed by three lines and no licence terms, in a repository that has no LICENSE file
at all.

**Evidence:**

        // Real-Time Collision Detection
        // Christer Ericson
        // 2005

The transcription is literal enough that the book's page marker survived at
`ericson_math.cpp:788`:

        // 132

and four comments still hold `U+FFFD` replacement bytes where the book's typographic
quotes were lost in copying (`:532`, `:538`, `:543`, `:759`), e.g.:

        // Intersect AABBs ?a? and ?b? moving with constant velocities va and vb.

**Why it matters:** PHILOSOPHY opens with "intended, eventually, for developers other
than its author", and ARCHITECTURE treats the bought edge as "declared, not clicked" —
`vcpkg.json` names DirectXTK, `external/` holds rapidjson. This file is third-party code
with neither. `find . -maxdepth 2 -iname "*license*"` returns nothing, so the repository
states no terms for its own code either. Whatever the answer is — and the book's code is
widely reused — it has to be written down before a stranger can link `MattMath` into
anything they ship, and it is far cheaper to settle now than after the first external
user. T9 cuts the same way: the tenet's justification for hand-rolling math is "an engine
offered to others must be one its author understands completely and can defend line by
line", and a transcription still carrying its source's page numbers is the weakest form of
that claim.

**Remedy:** Add a LICENSE for the project and a licence line in this file naming the terms
under which the book's code is reused; while there, repair the four corrupted comments and
delete the stray `// 132`.

#### Delete test_circle_circle, a dead duplicate that has already diverged from the live one

- **File:** `engine/math/ericson_math.cpp:310-318`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T4 ("duplication is the opposite of clarity at scale")

**What:** `test_circle_circle` has zero call sites and zero tests; the same predicate is
implemented independently by `mattmath::circles_intersect` using a square root where this
one uses the squared form.

**Evidence:**

        bool test_circle_circle(const Circle& a, const Circle& b)
        {
            // Calculate squared distance between centers
            Vector2F d = a.center() - b.center();
            float dist2 = Vector2F::dot(d, d);
            // Spheres intersect if squared distance is less than squared sum of radii
            float radiusSum = a.radius() + b.radius();
            return dist2 <= radiusSum * radiusSum;
        }

against the version that is actually reached, `matt_math.cpp:301-305`:

        bool mattmath::circles_intersect(const Circle& a, const Circle& b)
        {
            return Vector2F::distance(a.center(), b.center()) <=
                a.radius() + b.radius();
        }

**Why it matters:** `Circle::intersects(const Circle&)` routes to `circles_intersect`
(`matt_math.cpp:3363-3366`), so every circle-vs-circle query in the game takes the
square-root path, and `test_circle_circle` — declared publicly at `ericson_math.h:77-78`
— is reached by nothing. `sqrt(dist2) <= r` and `dist2 <= r*r` are not the same predicate
in float, so a stranger who finds the header function gets a second, subtly different
answer to a question the library already answers. Graded low rather than medium because
the divergence is unobservable today: nothing calls it, so nothing can disagree. The
unused one is also the faster one, which is the wrong way round for an engine whose
headline is speed (T8).

**Remedy:** Delete `test_circle_circle` and reimplement `circles_intersect` in the squared
form, or keep exactly one and route the other to it.

#### Stop naming one type two ways in the same header

- **File:** `engine/math/ericson_math.h:74-115`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T4

**What:** `AABB` is a typedef of `RectangleF` (`matt_math.h:298`), but neighbouring
declarations in this header use both names for the same parameter, which reads as two
types with different invariants when there is one type with none.

**Evidence:**

        bool test_AABB_AABB(const mattmath::RectangleF& a,
            const mattmath::RectangleF& b);
        ...
        bool intersect_moving_AABB_AABB(const mattmath::AABB& a,
            const mattmath::AABB& b,
        ...
        bool test_segment_AABB(const mattmath::Point2F& p0,
            const mattmath::Point2F p1, const mattmath::AABB& b);

**Why it matters:** The `AABB` spelling promises an axis-aligned bounding box, which
carries a `min <= max` invariant; `RectangleF(float x, float y, float width, float
height)` (`matt_math.cpp:668-671`) is a bare member-init list that accepts negative width
and height, so nothing enforces it. Every routine in this file reads `b.top_left()` and
`b.bottom_right()` and assumes the first is componentwise smaller — `test_AABB_AABB`
reports non-intersection for two *identical* inverted rectangles, since
`a_max.x < b_min.x` holds. (The reviewer's claim that `sq_dist_point_AABB` "returns 0 for
a point nowhere near an inverted rectangle" is backwards: for an inverted rect both the
`v < b_min` and `v > b_max` branches fire, so it returns a large distance for every point
including ones a caller would call inside — wrong in the other direction.) The missing
`RectangleF` invariant is already an open item from review 1, which also notes
`from_top_left_bottom_right` building inverted rects straight from level JSON; what is new
here is only that this header disguises it, because a caller reading `const AABB&`
reasonably concludes the type checks. Graded low on that basis.

**Remedy:** Pick one spelling for the whole header, and either give the type a real
invariant or say in the header comment that the caller owns it.

#### Signature hygiene the previous review reported and the conventions passes did not touch

- **File:** `engine/math/ericson_math.h:114-115`, `engine/math/ericson_math.cpp:3, 304-307, 745`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** T5, T4

**What:** `test_segment_AABB` takes one point by const reference and the next by value,
seventeen `return 0;`/`return 1;` statements remain in `bool` functions, and
`test_point_triangle` has a doubled space in its definition — all reported at
`README.md`, "Modern C++ mechanics", and none fixed.

**Evidence:**

        bool test_segment_AABB(const mattmath::Point2F& p0,
            const mattmath::Point2F p1, const mattmath::AABB& b);

        if (a_max.x < b_min.x || a_min.x > b_max.x) return 0;
        if (a_max.y < b_min.y || a_min.y > b_max.y) return 0;
        // Overlapping on all axes means AABBs are intersecting
        return 1;

        bool  test_point_triangle(const Point2F& p,

**Why it matters:** None of these changes behaviour — `Point2F` is two floats, and `0`/`1`
convert to `bool` — but they are the visible surface of a file renamed four times without
being read. (The count is 17 `return 0/1` sites, not the 13 reported.) The
by-value/by-reference asymmetry in particular reads as an unfinished edit and will make
the next reader stop to check whether it was deliberate. Same category:
`ericson_math.cpp:3` has `using namespace mattmath;` immediately above the

**Remedy:** Take `p1` by const reference, return `true`/`false`, drop the dead

#### Declare what the compiler can enforce: no [[nodiscard]] and no noexcept in the header

- **File:** `engine/math/ericson_math.h:74-138`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T5

**What:** Sixteen declarations, twelve of which return a value that is the entire point of
the call, and not one carries `[[nodiscard]]`; none of the non-throwing ones carries
`noexcept`. `grep -c "nodiscard\|noexcept"` returns 0 for both `ericson_math.h` and
`matt_math.h`.

**Evidence:**

        bool test_AABB_AABB(const mattmath::RectangleF& a,
            const mattmath::RectangleF& b);

        bool test_circle_circle(const mattmath::Circle& a,
            const mattmath::Circle& b);

        float sq_dist_point_AABB(const mattmath::Point2F& p,
            const mattmath::RectangleF& b);

**Why it matters:** PHILOSOPHY/Tests and toolchain names the tools by name: "`const`,
`noexcept` and `[[nodiscard]]` carry information the compiler enforces (T5)." These
functions are the ideal case — pure predicates whose only effect is the return value, so
discarding one is always a bug, and every one except `closest_pt_point_OBB` (which throws
through `RectangleRotated::axis`) is genuinely non-throwing. The previous review recorded
"No `[[nodiscard]]` anywhere in the project" as a general item; here it is free, because
the annotation is also the cheapest half of the contract documentation the header is
missing.

**Remedy:** Mark all twelve value-returning declarations `[[nodiscard]]`, and add
`noexcept` where the body cannot throw — which also makes `closest_pt_point_OBB`'s throwing
path visible in the header.

#### Hoist the throwing runtime-indexed accessors out of closest_pt_point_OBB's loop

- **File:** `engine/math/ericson_math.cpp:768-786`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** performance
- **Tenet:** T8

**What:** The two-iteration loop calls `b.axis(i)` twice and `b.half_width(i)` up to four
times per iteration, and each is an out-of-line accessor in another translation unit whose
body is an `if / else if / throw` chain.

**Evidence:**

        for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++)
        {
            float dist = Vector2F::dot(d, b.axis(i));
            if (dist > b.half_width(i)) dist = b.half_width(i);
            if (dist < -b.half_width(i)) dist = -b.half_width(i);
            q += dist * b.axis(i);
        }

`RectangleRotated::axis` (`matt_math.cpp:4323-4335`) and `::half_width` (`:4348-4360`)
both end in `throw std::invalid_argument("Axis must be 0 or 1");`.

**Why it matters:** Two iterations make up to twelve cross-TU calls (not the ten
reported), each with a branch chain and a throwing tail the compiler cannot prove
unreachable, in what is meant to be a narrow-phase inner routine — and `/GL` is not set,
so these are real calls. `RectangleRotated` already exposes `x_axis()`, `y_axis()`,
`half_x_width()` and `half_y_width()` (`matt_math.h:1085-1091`), so the runtime index
buys nothing: it is the 3D loop's shape surviving in a routine with exactly two axes. The
function has no non-test callers today, so nothing is currently slow because of it; the
point is that adopting it into the narrow phase would carry the shape in with it.

**Remedy:** Unroll to two explicit axis steps using the named accessors, and drop the loop
and its runtime index.

#### Fix the copy-pasted comments describing spheres and 3D in a 2D library

- **File:** `engine/math/ericson_math.cpp:294, 315, 366, 376-377, 480-481`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** docs
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Non-goals (3D), T4

**What:** The book's comments came across unedited, so the file's only prose describes
spheres rather than circles, and one comment describes an entirely different function from
the one it sits above.

**Evidence:**

        // Returns true if sphere s intersects AABB b, false otherwise
        bool test_AABB_AABB(const RectangleF& a,
            const RectangleF& b)

and, on the actual circle tests:

        // Spheres intersect if squared distance is less than squared sum of radii
        ...
        // Returns true if sphere s intersects triangle ABC, false otherwise.

**Why it matters:** The comment on `test_AABB_AABB` names parameters (`sphere s`,
`AABB b`) that do not exist in its signature, which a reader has to stop and disprove.
More broadly, "sphere" is the vocabulary of the 3D book and MattMath's type is `Circle`;
PHILOSOPHY names 3D as a permanent non-goal, so the file's prose should not be the last
place in the engine where the 3D vocabulary is preserved. These are the only comments
these routines have, which makes them the closest thing to documentation a reader gets.

**Remedy:** Rewrite the comments in this library's vocabulary — circle, rectangle, two
axes — and give `test_AABB_AABB` a comment describing `test_AABB_AABB`.

#### The header carries an include for its .cpp, and the .cpp relies on a transitive one

- **File:** `engine/math/ericson_math.h:8`, `engine/math/ericson_math.cpp:1`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Tests and toolchain ("light headers, disciplined includes"), CONVENTIONS/Files

**What:** `ericson_math.h` includes `<cmath>`, which nothing in the header needs — it is
there for the `.cpp`'s `std::abs`. Meanwhile the `.cpp` uses `std::min`/`std::max` eight
times and no file in its include chain includes `<algorithm>`; it compiles only because
MSVC's `<vector>` pulls in `<xutility>`.

**Evidence:**

        // ericson_math.h
        #include "engine/math/matt_math.h"
        #include <cmath>

        // ericson_math.cpp — its only include
        #include "engine/math/ericson_math.h"

        tfirst = std::max((a_max.x - b_min.x) / v.x, tfirst);
        tlast = std::min((a_min.x - b_max.x) / v.x, tlast);

`grep -rn "include <algorithm>" engine/math/` returns nothing; `matt_math.h:3-9` includes
`SimpleMath.h`, `shape_type.h`, `<d3d11.h>`, `<cmath>`, `<memory>`, `<string>`,
`<vector>`; DirectXTK's `SimpleMath.h` does not include `<algorithm>` either.

**Why it matters:** PHILOSOPHY makes compile speed a maintained property via "light
headers, disciplined includes", and a header carrying its implementation's includes taxes
every consumer. The `<algorithm>` omission is the sharper half: `std::min`/`std::max` are
specified in `<algorithm>`, and their availability through `<vector>` is an MSVC
implementation detail. PHILOSOPHY/Targets and layout commits to a second platform being
"an addition, not a rewrite" — this is one of the small things that turns that into a
rewrite afternoon. CONVENTIONS/Files also states the include order this would follow: own
header first, then engine, then external, then standard library.

**Remedy:** Move `<cmath>` from the header into the `.cpp` and add `<algorithm>` beside it.

### Rejected

- **"Two OBBs resting exactly face-to-face report no contact"** (part of the
  touching-segment finding) — rejected. `rectangles_rotated_intersect` runs inclusive
  containment checks on all eight corners before reaching the edge tests, and for two
  convex shapes in contact a vertex of one always lies on or in the other. The finding
  survives on a narrower, verified case (single-point grazing contact) and was regraded
  high → medium.
- **"`quads_intersect` (`matt_math.cpp:400-401`)" and "`quad_segment_intersect` (`:439`)"**
  — rejected as labels. The line numbers are right but name the wrong functions:
  `:400-401` is inside `triangles_intersect` (`quads_intersect` is at `:493`) and `:439` is
  inside `triangle_segment_intersect` (`quad_segment_intersect` is at `:514`). Corrected in
  place.
- **"`sq_dist_point_AABB` returns 0 for a point that is nowhere near an inverted
  rectangle"** — rejected. For an inverted rect both excess branches fire and it returns a
  large distance for *every* point, including ones inside the intended box. The finding was
  regraded medium → low and the claim replaced with the verified `test_AABB_AABB` one.
- **"432 of the 929 lines are commented-out code"** — corrected, not rejected. 508 lines
  begin with `//`; roughly 422 of those are commented-out source. The claim that dead lines
  outnumber live ones (349) still holds.
- **"thirteen `return 0`/`return 1` statements"** — corrected to 17.
- **"up to ten cross-TU calls"** in `closest_pt_point_OBB` — corrected to up to 12
  (`axis` twice, `half_width` up to four times, per iteration).
- **"`test_circle_circle` … the two can disagree on a grazing contact"** as a medium — the
  observation stands, the consequence does not: nothing calls it, so nothing can observe
  the disagreement. Regraded medium → low.
- **"`pt` appears in six public names"** — corrected to four (`closest_pt_point_triangle`,
  `closest_pt_point_AABB`, `closest_pt_point_segment`, `closest_pt_point_OBB`); the
  reviewer double-counted declarations against definitions.
- **`triangles_intersect` tests only 4 of 9 edge pairs** (my own candidate finding) —
  rejected after analysis. The `i < 2` loop bound over a 3-element vector looks like a
  transcription error, but with the containment pre-check in place two overlapping
  triangles with no contained vertex must cross at ≥4 alternating boundary points, which
  forces at least one crossing pair from `{a0,a1} × {b0,b1}`. Accidentally sufficient,
  undocumented, not a defect.
- **`closest_pt_point_OBB` assumes unit axes** (my own candidate finding) — rejected.
  `RectangleRotated::axes_valid` (`matt_math.cpp:4536-4552`) checks both axes are unit
  length and mutually perpendicular, and the setters validate before committing, so the
  assumption is enforced at construction.
- **`cmake/settings.cmake` silently dropped `/fp:fast`** — real, but out of this group's
  scope; noted in the verdict for the build group rather than filed here.

<a id="g-math-collision-tools"></a>

## math-collision-tools — Collision tools and shape tags

*Group `math-collision-tools` · 11 findings (2 high, 3 medium, 6 low) · source `review2/verified/math-collision-tools.md`, verified report.*

**Verdict.** I re-opened all four group files in full (`collision_tools.h` 98 lines,
`collision_tools.cpp` 293, `shape_type.h`, `dimension.h`), plus every line the reviewer
cited outside them: `matt_math.h:1-120`, `matt_math.cpp:120-152` and all five
`shape_type()` overrides, `engine/collision/partitioner.{h,cpp}` in full, the three
CMakeLists and `cmake/settings.cmake`, `tests/math/collision_tools_tests.cpp` in full,
DirectXTK's `SimpleMath.h` include list as vendored under `out/`, `player.cpp:240-390`
and `510-669`, `game/objects/i_collision_game_object.h`, and the 19 prior findings
against these files in `docs/review/all-findings.md`. Every line number in the raw
report checks out; the arithmetic traces (the `(-5,-5)` diagonal, the `1/1.5^40`
residual, the 17 uncommented `CollisionTools::` call sites) all reproduce. What did not
survive is a set of consequences. **`Partitioner` is not a broad phase** — it splits an
integer range into N contiguous chunks for the render thread pool
(`partitioner.cpp:5-23`, used only at `level.cpp:401` and `menu_page.cpp`), so the raw
report's framing "the split put the broad phase in the right place" is false; the truth
is worse for the same finding, since `engine/collision/` today contains *nothing that is
collision*. `ICollisionGameObject` lives in `game/objects/`, not the engine, so `Shape`
is not yet reaching the engine through an engine seam. `std::max` without `<algorithm>`
is a discipline breach, not the portability break claimed — libstdc++ and libc++ both
reach `std::max` through `<string>`/`<vector>`, so "compile error on the second
platform" is dropped and the finding regraded to low. The two dead `collider_aabb`
locals sit beside 40 full `intersects()` calls, so calling them a performance defect
inflates them; the guardrail correction they carry is the real content, and the finding
is regraded to low. Four findings were regraded down for the same class of reason. What
the reviewer missed is the largest thing in the group: they read `all-findings.md` and
then filed nothing about it, so this document would otherwise have recorded a
whitespace complaint and stayed silent on the fact that **every recorded correctness
defect in this resolver is still live** — the band-case axis inversion, the
containing-direction inversion, the signed `std::max`, and a bisection that cannot
report failure. I added that as the second high finding, verified line by line against
the current file. I also corrected the claim that the suite has one diagonal case: it
has two, and both sit in the positive quadrant, which is precisely why the signed-`max`
defect has never gone red.

### Themes

- `engine/collision/` exists and holds no collision code; the entire narrow phase is in
  `engine/math/` under `mattmath::`, compiled into the library ARCHITECTURE says depends
  on nothing and sits *upstream* of collision.
- The record is not being worked: of the 19 prior findings against these four files,
  exactly one has been actioned (the tuning constants left the header) — and that one
  action introduced a fresh CONVENTIONS breach.
- Four independent correctness defects in ~250 lines of resolver, all reachable from
  the public API, none covered by a test, all previously written down.
- `ShapeType` is a closed variant set implemented with open inheritance plus RTTI: no
  compile-time exhaustiveness, and no way for a user to add a shape without editing the
  engine (T5, T11).
- The public header documents three of its six functions and the one contract it does
  state is contradicted by the body.
- The test suite pins the current search's literal outputs, including its over-resolution
  and, by tolerance, its iteration count.

#### The four recorded correctness defects in the resolver are all still live

- **File:** `engine/math/collision_tools.cpp:43-80, 102-118, 187-198, 220-240`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T2, PHILOSOPHY/Collision

**What:** `docs/review/all-findings.md` records four defects in this file
(`CollisionTools.cpp` #1, #4, #5, #9). None appears in `IMPLEMENTED.md`, and I confirmed
all four are present verbatim in the current source. The raw report mentions one of them
in a parenthesis inside a test finding and none of the others, so without this entry the
group's record would show its worst defects as unreported.

**Evidence:**

*(a) Band cases resolve on the axis that cannot separate them (`:187-198`). Reaching 187
requires `left && right && !top && !bottom` — I re-traced all five preceding branches
(163, 167, 172, 177, 182) and none fires in that state — which means the collidee spans
the collider horizontally, so only a vertical move can separate them:*

        if (left_edge && right_edge)
        {
            // check if the collider is more to the left or right of the collidee
            return compare_point_collision_depth_horizontal(collider->center(),
                collidee->center());
        }
        if (top_edge && bottom_edge)
        {
            // check if the collider is more to the top or bottom of the collidee
            return compare_point_collision_depth_vertical(collider->center(),
                collidee->center());
        }

*(b) The containment fallback picks the axis opposite to its own comment (`:105-117`):*

        // calculate the direction of the greatest distance between the two shapes
        Point2F collider_center = collider->center();
        Point2F collidee_center = collidee->center();
        float x_distance = collider_center.x - collidee_center.x;
        float y_distance = collider_center.y - collidee_center.y;
        if (std::abs(x_distance) < std::abs(y_distance))
        {
            return compare_point_collision_depth_horizontal(collider_center, collidee_center);
        }
        return compare_point_collision_depth_vertical(collider_center, collidee_center);

*(c) Signed `std::max` over direction components (`:232-239`):*

        if (collision_direction.x != 0.0f && collision_direction.y != 0.0f)
        {
            float larger = std::max(collision_direction.x, collision_direction.y);
            direction = collision_direction / larger;
        }
        collider->offset(opposite_direction(direction) * amount);

*(d) The bracket's failure is unreportable and its result is discarded (`:53-56`, `:262-271`):*

        else if (i == 1) // no collision in the first iteration
        {
            return false;
        }
        ...
            bracket_object_collision_generic(collider, collidee,
                                                opposite_direction(unit_direction),
                                                                    BRACKET_ITERATIONS);
        }
        ...
        return true;

**Why it matters:** (a) is the thin-platform case — a platform shorter than the player,
penetrated far enough that the player's top and bottom edges clear it, is reported as a
LEFT/RIGHT hit, and `player.cpp:529-536` dispatches `on_left_collision` /
`on_right_collision`, zeroing x-velocity and shoving the player sideways off a platform
it should have landed on. (b) reports a purely vertical separation as horizontal and is
the fallback for both the equal-size case (`:165`) and the catch-all at `:217`. (c) I
worked the four diagonals again: UP_RIGHT, DOWN_LEFT and DOWN_RIGHT come out correct;
UP_LEFT `(-0.707,-0.707)` gives `larger = -0.707`, `direction = (1,1)` and a push of
`(-w,-h)` — up and left, deeper into the collidee — and for a non-45° direction such as
`(-0.9,-0.1)` the divisor is the *smaller* magnitude and the push is 9x the overlap. I
confirmed the reachability caveat the prior record already carries: every direct
`resolve_object_collision` call in `player.cpp` passes a cardinal direction (`:293`,
`:313`, `:322`, `:331`, `:370`, `:579`, `:588`, `:597`, `:604`), where the
`x != 0 && y != 0` guard skips the divide, and the only diagonal path
(`calculate_object_collision_depth` at `:608`, `:622`, `:640`, `:658`, with
`DIRECTION_UP_LEFT` etc.) runs on a `clone()` whose caller reads only
`abs_x_greater_than_y()` — sign-insensitive. So (c) is a latent defect in a public API,
not a live gameplay bug. (d) is live: `bracket_object_collision` returns `false` only at
`i == 1`, which `resolve_object_collision:246` has already made unreachable by testing
`intersects` first, so a bisection that ends still overlapping returns `true` and the
caller cannot tell. Total displacement is also bounded by ~2x the collider's own
bounding box (the sum of `(1/1.5)^i`), so anything penetrating deeper than that stays
welded in, every frame, silently.

**Remedy:** These four disappear together under the design PHILOSOPHY/Collision already
specifies: a narrow phase returning `{normal, penetration}` and `position += normal *
penetration`. If they are fixed in place first, they are four small edits — swap the two
helpers at 187-198, invert the comparison at 113, `std::max(std::abs(d.x), std::abs(d.y))`
at 234, and make the bracket return `collider->intersects(collidee)` after the final
iteration and propagate it. Each needs a test; the suite has none for any of them.

#### The narrow-phase resolver is in engine/math/, and engine/collision/ holds no collision code

- **File:** `engine/math/collision_tools.h:1-98`, `engine/math/collision_tools.cpp:1-293`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** boundary
- **Tenet:** ARCHITECTURE/Modules, ARCHITECTURE/The tree, PHILOSOPHY/Targets and layout

**What:** All of the engine's narrow-phase collision resolution sits in `engine/math/`
inside `namespace mattmath`, compiled into `MattMath`. `engine/collision/` — the folder
ARCHITECTURE assigns "broad phase, narrow phase, manifolds, resolution" — exists and
contains exactly two files, and they are not collision: `Partitioner` splits an integer
range into N contiguous index chunks for the render thread pool.

**Evidence:**

    engine/collision/  (whole contents)
      partitioner.cpp
      partitioner.h

    engine/collision/partitioner.h:5-15
    namespace artattack
    {
        class Partitioner
        {
        public:
            Partitioner() = default;
            std::vector<std::pair<int, int>>
                partition(int num_elements, int num_partitions) const;

    game/objects/level.cpp:401
            this->partitioner_->partition(this->player_objects_->size(), num_threads);

    engine/math/collision_tools.h:6-8
    namespace mattmath
    {
        class CollisionTools

    engine/math/CMakeLists.txt:9-13
    add_library(MattMath STATIC
        collision_tools.cpp
        ericson_math.cpp
        matt_math.cpp
    )

ARCHITECTURE/The tree: `├── collision/  broad phase, narrow phase, manifolds, resolution`.
ARCHITECTURE/Modules: `| collision | core, math |` — collision is *downstream* of math,
so resolution living inside math inverts the stated direction. PHILOSOPHY/Targets and
layout: `| MattMath | static library | engine/math/ | nothing |`.

**Why it matters:** Three live consequences. (1) The engine's collision API is not in the
engine's namespace or the engine's library: a stranger who reads ARCHITECTURE, links
`ArtAttackEngine` and greps `artattack::` for collision finds a thread-work splitter and
stops. (2) `MattMath`, documented as the dependency-free math library, ships a stateful
geometry mutator that is not math. (3) The binding grows: `game/objects/player.h:14`
includes `"engine/math/collision_tools.h"` and `player.cpp` names `CollisionTools::` at
17 uncommented call sites (256, 292, 312, 321, 330, 352, 361, 369, 518, 578, 587, 596,
603, 608, 622, 640, 658 — verified by grep). The move is cheap today and I measured it:
three `#include` lines (`collision_tools.cpp:1`, `player.h:14`,
`collision_tools_tests.cpp:2`), one namespace, one source entry from
`engine/math/CMakeLists.txt:10` to `engine/CMakeLists.txt` beside
`collision/partitioner.cpp`, and a test target linking `ArtAttackEngine` instead of
`MattMath` (`tests/math/CMakeLists.txt:8-12`). Nothing inside `MattMath` references
`CollisionTools` — grep returns only its own `.cpp`, `player.h` and the test — so it is
dependency-clean today.

**Remedy:** Move both files to `engine/collision/collision_tools.{h,cpp}` in namespace
`artattack`, and move the test to `tests/collision/`. Move `Partitioner` out of
`collision/` while you are there — it is thread-work scheduling, so `core/` beside
`thread_pool.cpp` is its home. While the file is open, `CollisionTools` — every member
static, with a public `CollisionTools() = default;` at `collision_tools.h:11` so
`CollisionTools ct;` compiles — should become namespace-scope functions, which is what
its neighbour `ericson_math.h:74-100` already does for the same kind of geometry helper.

#### ShapeType makes Shape an extension point nobody can extend, and a wrong tag is UB rather than a compile error

- **File:** `engine/math/shape_type.h:5-13`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T5, T11

**What:** `ShapeType` is a closed tag enum whose sole consumer is a `switch` that
`dynamic_cast`s to a hard-coded concrete type and immediately dereferences the result, so
a `Shape` subclass that is not one of the five blessed types either throws or invokes
undefined behaviour, with no compile error saying so.

**Evidence:**

    engine/math/shape_type.h:5-13
    enum class ShapeType
    {
        rectangle,
        circle,
        triangle,
        quad,
        rectangle_rotated,
        none
    };

    engine/math/matt_math.cpp:120-137
    bool Shape::intersects(const Shape* other) const
    {
        switch (other->shape_type())
        {
        case ShapeType::rectangle:
            return this->intersects(*dynamic_cast<const RectangleF*>(other));
        ...
        default:
            throw std::invalid_argument("Shape type not recognized");
        };
    }

**Why it matters:** `Shape` is a public MattMath type and `CollisionTools`' entire public
API takes `Shape*` / `const Shape*`, so a game linking the library can and will derive
from it. Doing so leaves exactly two outcomes: return one of the five tags without
deriving from the matching concrete type, in which case
`*dynamic_cast<const RectangleF*>(other)` binds a reference to null and every member
access is UB; or return `ShapeType::none`, which lands on `default:` and throws from
inside a `const` query on the per-frame collision path. Adding a shape properly means
editing `shape_type.h`, adding a pure virtual to `Shape` (`matt_math.h:74-80` already has
seven) and implementing it on all five existing shapes — i.e. editing the engine, which
is what T5 and T1 exist to prevent. `TriangleRightAxisAligned` (`matt_math.h:908`) is the
existing proof: the one subclass beyond the five works only because it inherits
`Triangle`'s tag and so survives the cast by accident. `none` is dead by construction —
all five overrides return their own tag (`matt_math.cpp:726, 3322, 3444, 3791, 4241`) —
so its only effect is to force the throwing arm. The tag also leaks outward: seven game
files branch on `ShapeType::rectangle` (`paint_tile.cpp:74-75`, `player.cpp:180-181`,
`projectile_ball.cpp:68-69`, `projectile_jet.cpp:67-68`, `projectile_mist.cpp:69-70`,
`projectile_rolling.cpp:65-66`, `projectile_spray.cpp:69-70`). *Regraded from high:* no
first-party path can produce a null cast today (every concrete shape reports its own tag),
`ICollisionGameObject` is game code in `game/objects/`, not an engine seam, and the
prior record already carries the `dynamic_cast` (`MattMath.cpp` #17) and the dead `none`
(`shape_type.h` #1). What is new and worth keeping is the extension-point framing.

**Remedy:** Make the variant set explicit and checked — `std::variant<RectangleF, Circle,
Triangle, Quad, RectangleRotated>` with `std::visit`, or a two-argument dispatch table —
so exhaustiveness is a compile error, the RTTI walk leaves the hot path, and `none` and
the throwing `default:` both become unrepresentable.

#### The resolver's only behavioural tests pin the over-resolution PHILOSOPHY rules out, and their tolerance silently encodes the iteration count

- **File:** `tests/math/collision_tools_tests.cpp:36-41, 79-84`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** testing
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Collision, T3

**What:** Both resolve cases assert the literal output of the current search rather than
the contract, and both use a positive-quadrant diagonal — the one input shape for which
the signed-`std::max` defect at `collision_tools.cpp:234` is harmless.

**Evidence:**

    tests/math/collision_tools_tests.cpp:24-41
    RectangleF rect1 = RectangleF(0.0f, 0.0f, 10.0f, 10.0f);
    RectangleF rect2 = RectangleF(5.0f, 5.0f, 10.0f, 10.0f);
    ...
    bool resolved = CollisionTools::resolve_object_collision(&rect1, &rect2, direction, amount);

    CHECK(resolved);
    check_equal(amount.x, -5.0f, EPSILON_F);
    check_equal(amount.y, -5.0f, EPSILON_F);

I re-traced it: the AABBs overlap in a 5x5 square, `direction` is `(0.7071, 0.7071)`, so
`resolve_object_AABB_collision` (`collision_tools.cpp:232-239`) takes the
`larger = std::max(0.7071, 0.7071)` branch, normalises `direction` to `(1, 1)`, and
offsets by `(-1,-1) * (inter.width, inter.height)` = `(-5, -5)`. PHILOSOPHY/Collision:
"the narrow phase produces a contact manifold — normal and penetration depth — and
resolution is analytic (MTV), not iterative search." The MTV here is `(0,-5)` or
`(-5,0)`; `(-5,-5)` moves √2 times further than necessary and teleports the collider
diagonally past a corner it never touched.

**Why it matters:** Three costs. First, the assertions defend the behaviour the
destination replaces, so whoever implements the manifold cannot tell "I broke it" from
"the expected value was always the bug". Second — correcting the raw report, which called
this the only diagonal case — there are two, `:37` with direction `(0.707,0.707)` and
`:80` with the rect-vs-triangle direction `(0.707,0.707)` from centre `(5,5)` to
`(8.33,8.33)`; both are in the positive quadrant, which is exactly why the UP_LEFT sign
inversion has never turned a test red. Third, `:83-84` asserts to `EPSILON_F = 1e-6` a
value the bisection reaches with a final step of `10 * 0.7071 / 1.5^40` ≈ `6.4e-7` — a
1.5x margin — so the tolerance encodes `BRACKET_ITERATIONS = 40`, and dropping it to 38
turns a tuning change into a red test with no hint why. Lines 88-104 are a commented-out
rect-vs-ramp case carried verbatim through the doctest migration (prior record,
`CollisionToolsTests` #2, still open).

**Remedy:** Assert the post-conditions the contract promises — "the shapes no longer
intersect" and "no axis moved by more than its overlap" — rather than the literal numbers
the current search produces, add a negative-quadrant diagonal, and either restore or
delete the commented-out case.

---

#### Half the public collision API is undocumented, and the one contract the header states is false

- **File:** `engine/math/collision_tools.h:26-39, 56-65`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** docs
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/The public face

**What:** Three of the six public functions carry no comment at all, and the documented
promise that `calculate_object_collision_direction_by_edge` returns a zero vector for
non-colliding shapes is contradicted by an implementation that never tests intersection
and has no path returning zero.

**Evidence:**

    engine/math/collision_tools.h:29-31
        * are used to assess the collision. This function is less accurate
        * with non-rectangle shapes. If the objects are not colliding,
        * a zero vector is returned.

    engine/math/collision_tools.h:56-65   (three entry points, no comment between them)
        static bool resolve_object_collision(mattmath::Shape* collider,
            const mattmath::Shape* collidee,
            const mattmath::Vector2F& collision_direction);

        static mattmath::Vector2F calculate_object_collision_depth(
            const mattmath::Shape* collider,
            const mattmath::Shape* collidee,
            const mattmath::Vector2F& collision_direction);

        static mattmath::Vector2F opposite_direction(const mattmath::Vector2F& direction);

`calculate_object_collision_direction_by_edge` (`collision_tools.cpp:147-218`) contains no
call to `intersects` and no `return Vector2F::ZERO`; for two disjoint shapes all four edge
flags are false, every branch falls through, and `:217` returns
`calculate_containing_collision_direction(...)`, which always yields one of
UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT. Its sibling `calculate_object_collision_direction` (`:136-145`) *does*
guard with `if (!collider->intersects(collidee)) return Vector2F::ZERO;`, and both carry
near-identical doc comments.

**Why it matters:** PHILOSOPHY/The public face: "Every public engine header is documented:
the contract, the intent, and where it isn't obvious, a usage example. A stranger starts
from the headers, not from reading the implementation." A stranger learns nothing about
what `calculate_object_collision_depth` returns — it is a signed displacement obtained by
resolving a heap clone, not a depth, and the inner success flag is discarded at
`collision_tools.cpp:289`, so a non-colliding pair returns the same zero as a zero-depth
touch — and is actively misled about `_by_edge`. Today the lie is masked because
`player.cpp:518` reaches it only behind a caller-side `is_colliding` gate, but the
contract is what a second client builds on. Three smaller notes: the 3-argument
`resolve_object_collision` overload exists only to declare a throwaway local, which the
prior record attributed to the C++14 default the build has since left behind; the comments
are `/*` blocks, not `/**`, so the `@param`/`@return` tags are inert to any doc generator;
and `_by_edge` takes `const Shape*` while immediately reducing both arguments to
`bounding_box()` (`:150-151`), so the polymorphic parameter type advertises a generality
the body does not have.

**Remedy:** Document the three bare declarations; state on `resolve_object_collision`
whether its `bool` describes the pre-state or a successful separation (today it is
neither — see the correctness finding above); and either add the intersection
precondition to `_by_edge` or change its comment to say it assumes an overlap — but do
not leave the header asserting something the body cannot do.

#### The conventions pass that moved these constants left them SCREAMING, in the same three lines that cite CONVENTIONS

- **File:** `engine/math/collision_tools.cpp:9-14`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Never

**What:** The one prior finding against this group that has been actioned — moving
`BRACKET_ITERATIONS` / `ITERATION_POWER` out of the public header — kept the names in
SCREAMING_SNAKE, which CONVENTIONS reserves for macros alone, directly under a comment
citing the CONVENTIONS section whose rule they break.

**Evidence:**

    engine/math/collision_tools.cpp:9-14
        // The bisection resolver's tuning. It used to sit in the header, where
        // it was visible to every caller of a collision query and configured
        // nothing any of them could see (CONVENTIONS, Constants and
        // enumerators).
        constexpr int BRACKET_ITERATIONS = 40;
        constexpr float ITERATION_POWER = 1.5f;

CONVENTIONS/Never: "SCREAMING constants — screaming means macro, nothing else."

**Why it matters:** The rule's entire value is that a screaming identifier is a signal —
see a capitalised name, expect the preprocessor. Two counterexamples in a file that
advertises its conventions compliance teach the reader the signal is unreliable, which
costs more than the two renames. The same pass produced two more breaches in the migrated
test: `tests/math/collision_tools_tests.cpp:17` `constexpr float EPSILON_F = 0.000001f;`
and `:15` `namespace CollisionToolsTests` (CONVENTIONS: namespaces are "one lowercase
word") — both freshly written, not inherited. The test case at `:64` is still spelled
`test_rectagle_triangle_collision`, and `ITERATION_POWER` still does not describe what it
is: the decay base for the step size.

**Remedy:** `bracket_iterations` / `bracket_step_decay` (and `epsilon_f`, `namespace
collision_tools_tests`, `test_rectangle_triangle_collision`) — pure renames, all
file-local.

Neither `collider_aabb` is referenced again in either body.

**Why it matters:** The content worth recording is the guardrail gap, not the cycles.

#### The translation unit reaches four standard facilities with an empty standard-library include section

- **File:** `engine/math/collision_tools.cpp:1-3, 51, 234`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Files

**What:** The `.cpp` includes exactly one header and reaches `std::max`, `std::abs`,
`std::unique_ptr` and an unqualified `::pow` through transitive includes; `<algorithm>`
appears nowhere in the chain.

**Evidence:**

    engine/math/collision_tools.cpp:1-3
    #include "engine/math/collision_tools.h"

    using namespace mattmath;

    engine/math/collision_tools.cpp:234
            float larger = std::max(collision_direction.x, collision_direction.y);

    engine/math/collision_tools.cpp:51
                1.0f / pow(ITERATION_POWER, static_cast<float>(i)));

The whole chain is `collision_tools.h` → `matt_math.h`, whose includes are `SimpleMath.h`,
`shape_type.h`, `<d3d11.h>`, `<cmath>`, `<memory>`, `<string>`, `<vector>`
(`matt_math.h:3-9`). I read the vendored `SimpleMath.h` include list directly: `<cassert>
<cmath> <cstddef> <cstring> <functional> <compare>`, `<DirectXMath.h>`,
`<DirectXPackedVector.h>`, `<DirectXCollision.h>` — no `<algorithm>`.
`cmake/settings.cmake:19` defines `NOMINMAX`, so the Windows `max` macro is not what
resolves.

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS/Files fixes the include order as "own header first —
proving every header compiles on its own — then engine headers, then external, then
standard library"; here the standard-library section is empty while four standard
facilities are in use, and the file compiles only because MSVC's `<vector>` / `<memory>`
/ `<string>` pull in `<xutility>`. *Regraded from medium, and the consequence dropped:*
the raw report called this a compile error on the second platform, but libstdc++ and
libc++ also reach `std::max` through `<bits/stl_algobase.h>` via `<string>` and
`<vector>`, so the realistic cost is a latent dependency on an implementation detail, not
a demonstrated portability break. The unqualified `pow` at `:51` and `:61` has the same
shape — `<cmath>` is not required to declare `::pow`. `using namespace mattmath;` at `:3`
sits immediately before `namespace mattmath {` at `:5` and does nothing.

**Remedy:** Add `#include <algorithm>` and `#include <cmath>` to the `.cpp`, qualify `pow`
as `std::pow`, and delete the line-3 `using`.

#### Indentation mixes tabs and spaces inside single comment blocks

- **File:** `engine/math/collision_tools.h:11-21`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** T4

**What:** The header and the `.cpp` indent with four-spaces-then-tab on some lines and
eight spaces on others, alternating within the same declaration and the same comment,
with no `.clang-format` in the repository to settle it.

**Evidence:** (`cat -A` of `collision_tools.h:11-21`; `^I` is a tab, `$` end of line —
I re-ran this)

        ^ICollisionTools() = default;$
    $
        ^I/*$
        ^I* Determines the direction of the collision between two objects,$
        ^I* relative to the collider. If the objects are not colliding,$
            * a zero vector is returned.$
            * $
        ^I* @param collider The object that is colliding with the collidee.$
        ^I* @param collidee The object that is being collided with.$
        ^I* @return The direction of the collision.$
            */$

The same pattern runs through `collision_tools.cpp` — confirmed at `:17-21` and
`:228-240`, where `float larger = std::max(...)` is `^I^I` while the very next statement
`direction = collision_direction / larger;` is twelve spaces. `shape_type.h` indents with
tabs and `dimension.h` with spaces, in the same four-file group. `ls -a` at the repository
root shows no `.clang-format`.

**Why it matters:** A documentation comment that changes indentation style mid-block
renders differently at any tab width other than the author's, and this is one of the three
headers a game includes from `engine/math/`. PHILOSOPHY/The public face puts the header
first in a stranger's path; ragged whitespace is the first thing they see and the cheapest
thing to fix. It also guarantees noisy diffs on every future edit.

**Remedy:** Add a `.clang-format` at the repository root (spaces, four columns) and run it
over these files as part of the module move, so the reformat lands in a commit that is
already touching every line.

### Rejected

- **"`engine/collision/` contains the broad phase (`Partitioner`)"** (finding 1's central
  framing) — rejected as false. `partitioner.cpp:5-23` splits `num_elements` into
  `num_partitions` contiguous index ranges and its only callers are `level.cpp:401` and
  `menu_page.cpp`, both distributing draw work across threads. There is no spatial broad
  phase anywhere in the repository, and the prior record says so
  (`findings.json`: "'Partitioner' splits thread work while no spatial broad phase
  exists"). The finding survives with a stronger claim: `engine/collision/` contains no
  collision code at all.
- **"`Shape` is the type a game hands the engine through `ICollisionGameObject::shape()`"**
  (finding 2) — rejected. `game/objects/i_collision_game_object.h` is game code in the
  global namespace, includes `game/objects/collision_object_type.h`, and is not an engine
  seam; the split has not created one yet. The extension-point argument survives via
  `Shape` and `CollisionTools`' public `Shape*` API, which is how the finding is now
  written.
- **"`std::max` is a compile error on the second platform"** (finding 4) — rejected as an
  overstated consequence. libstdc++ and libc++ both make `std::max` visible through
  `<string>`/`<vector>` via `<bits/stl_algobase.h>`; the defect is an undeclared
  dependency on an implementation detail, so the finding is kept at low as an include-
  discipline breach rather than a portability break.
- **"40 discarded virtual calls per contact inside a quadratic pair loop"** as a
  *performance* finding (finding 6) — rejected as a category and severity. The count is
  right (41, counting the outer function) but the same loop performs 40 full
  `Shape::intersects` dispatches, so the dead calls are not measurable. Regraded to low
  and recategorised around the C4189/`/WX` guardrail gap, which is the part that is new.
- **"this is the only diagonal case in the suite"** (finding 3) — rejected as a fact.
  There are two, `:37` and `:80`, and both are positive-quadrant. Corrected in place,
  where it strengthens the point about the signed-`max` defect never going red.
- **"20 of the file's 107 lines (86-104) are commented out"** (finding 3) — corrected:
  the commented block is `:88-104`, 17 lines; `:86-87` are blank.
- **"three of seven public entry points are undocumented"** (finding 7) — corrected to
  three of six public *functions*; the seventh member is the defaulted constructor, which
  should not exist at all (see finding 1's remedy).
- **Severity high on finding 2 (ShapeType)** — regraded to medium. No first-party path can
  produce the null cast, the boundary type it was hung on is game code, and the
  `dynamic_cast` and dead `none` enumerator are both already on the record
  (`MattMath.cpp` #17, `shape_type.h` #1).
- **Severity medium on finding 5 (SCREAMING constants)** — regraded to low. It is a
  naming breach with no behavioural consequence; the framing (introduced *by* the
  conventions pass, in the lines citing CONVENTIONS) is what makes it worth writing down.
- No finding was rejected as a duplicate within this group, and none is recorded as fixed
  in `IMPLEMENTED.md` — which is itself the group's headline: of the 19 prior findings
  against these four files, only the two constants leaving the header have been actioned.

<a id="g-collision-input"></a>

## collision-input — Partitioner and input

*Group `collision-input` · 12 findings (2 high, 5 medium, 5 low) · source `review2/verified/collision-input.md`, verified report.*

I re-opened all three group files in full (`engine/collision/partitioner.h`, 18 lines;
`engine/collision/partitioner.cpp`, 29 lines; `engine/input/connection_state.h`, 10 lines)
and every line the reviewer cited outside them: `engine/app/application.{h,cpp}`,
`engine/core/thread_pool.{h,cpp}`, `game/game_data.{h,cpp}`, `game/objects/level.{h,cpp}`,
`game/objects/level_builder.h`, `game/objects/player_input.{h,cpp}`,
`game/objects/player_input_data.h`, `game/objects/i_collision_game_object.h`,
`game/states/menu_page.cpp`, `game/states/menu_input.{h,cpp}`,
`samples/minimal/states/hello_state.cpp`, `engine/math/collision_tools.h`, and all six
`CMakeLists.txt`. **Every line number and every quoted line in the raw report is correct** —
that is unusual at this scale and worth saying. What did not survive was consequence and
severity, not evidence.

I merged two pairs. Raw #5 ("move Partitioner out of `collision/`") and raw #2
("`collision/` contains no collision") are one statement about one folder seen from two
sides, and they share one remedy; they are now one finding. Raw #10 ("`ConnectionState`
is an orphan") and raw #1 ("the input API is a vendor pointer") are likewise one defect —
`engine/input/` holds no mechanism — and are now one finding carrying both bodies of
evidence. I re-graded three. The unchecked `num_partitions` (raw #3) drops high → medium:
the observation is exact, but no caller in the tree can reach it — `max_threads` defaults
to 16 and both call sites read it through `ThreadPool`, so this is a missing precondition
on a public API, not a live crash. The `size_t` overload and the per-frame allocation drop
to low: the truncation is unreachable in a 2D game and the allocation is one small vector
plus four copies per frame, which is a stated-destination miss rather than a measured cost.
I also corrected two sub-claims that were wrong on the facts: `app` depending on
`collision` does **not** invert ARCHITECTURE's module table (`app` may depend on
everything), and `mattmath` holding `CollisionTools` is a *placement* problem, not the
dependency violation the raw text implied — MattMath still depends on nothing.

I checked one thing the reviewer did not and it came back clean: `for (int i = 0; i <
partitioned_players.size(); i++)` at `level.cpp:404` and `menu_page.cpp:143` are
signed/unsigned comparisons that the *previous* review claimed were C4018, and `/W4 /WX`
is genuinely applied (`out/build/x64-debug/build.ninja:690`) with `level.cpp.obj` newer
than the ninja file — so the flags are real, the objects are current, and no warning fires.
There is no build-guardrail finding here.

I added two. The engine's most-included public header pulls in the whole collision module
to declare a pointer, and `partition()` hands back `std::pair`, so every call site in the
repository reads `.first`/`.second`. I also folded in the single sharpest fact about this
module, which the reviewer had the evidence for but never stated: **`partition()` has never
once partitioned.** Every call in the tree passes n ≤ k (4 players, 2 menu objects, 16
threads), so it always returns n singleton ranges — the engine's only "collision" module,
one heap allocation and nine pieces of lifetime plumbing, computes `i → {i, i+1}`.

### Themes

- Both folders are labels. `engine/collision/` and `engine/input/` exist to match
  ARCHITECTURE's tree, and between them they contain one range-splitter and one enum —
  57 lines standing in for "broad phase, narrow phase, manifolds, resolution" and
  "devices, action mapping".
- The mechanism the engine promises is written in `game/`, and in the input case twice.
- The one public API in the group has no documented preconditions, no validation and no
  test, and both call sites depend on an undocumented clamp in its loop condition.
- Platform SDK types reach the game through public engine headers, so the new-project
  template must name a vendor SDK in its own build file.
- Nothing in `ArtAttackEngine` calls `partition()` or names `ConnectionState`: both are
  engine-hosted game utilities, the inverse of PHILOSOPHY's litmus test.

#### `engine/input/` is a label: one orphan enum, and a vendor SDK pointer for an API

- **File:** `engine/input/connection_state.h:1-10`, `engine/app/application.h:17,123,158`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** boundary
- **Tenet:** T1 (mechanism over policy); ARCHITECTURE/Modules; PHILOSOPHY/The boundary

**What:** `engine/input/` contains one enum, no `.cpp`, and no `xinput/` backend, so
`ArtAttackEngine` links zero input code. The engine's actual input interface is
`Application::gamepad()`, which hands every client a raw `DirectX::GamePad*`. No engine
translation unit produces, consumes or even names `ConnectionState`.

**Evidence:**

`engine/input/connection_state.h`, the whole module:

    {
        enum class ConnectionState
        {
            connected,
            disconnected
        };
    }

`engine/app/application.h`:

    17	#include <GamePad.h>
    123		DirectX::GamePad* gamepad() const;
    158		std::unique_ptr<DirectX::GamePad> gamepad_ = nullptr;

Every reference to `ConnectionState` anywhere in `engine/`, `game/`, `samples/` and
`tests/` outside its own definition is in `game/`:

    game/objects/player_input_data.h:3	#include "engine/input/connection_state.h"
    game/objects/player_input_data.h:18	artattack::ConnectionState connection = artattack::ConnectionState::disconnected;
    game/objects/player_input.cpp:112	    result.connection = ConnectionState::connected;
    game/objects/player_input.h:37	// XInput pad slot. Absent pads carry ConnectionState::disconnected and
    game/states/menu_input.h:5	#include "engine/input/connection_state.h"
    game/states/menu_input.h:43	artattack::ConnectionState connection = artattack::ConnectionState::disconnected;
    game/states/menu_input.cpp:129	    result.connection = ConnectionState::connected;

The only input code the engine owns is suspend/resume forwarding, and it lives in `app/`,
not `input/` (`engine/app/application.cpp:307-346`):

    307	void Application::on_activated() const
    309		if (this->gamepad_)
    311			this->gamepad_->Resume();

The second client is written against the vendor type too
(`samples/minimal/states/hello_state.cpp:44`):

    const GamePad::State pad = this->app_->gamepad()->GetState(0);

— and the new-project template's own build file must therefore name the SDK
(`samples/minimal/CMakeLists.txt:4,21-25`), directly under a comment claiming the sample
is what keeps the boundary honest:

     4	find_package(directxtk CONFIG REQUIRED)
    21	target_link_libraries(ArtAttackSample PRIVATE
    22	    ArtAttackEngine
    23	    Microsoft::DirectXTK
    24	    artattack_settings

**Why it matters:** ARCHITECTURE's module table gives `input` "devices, action mapping"
with "XInput inside `xinput/` only", and PHILOSOPHY's boundary table promises the engine
provides "Input devices and action mapping" while the game provides "Which actions exist
and their bindings". Neither exists, and the consequences are already realised rather than
hypothetical: the sample, `PlayerInput` and `MenuInput` all read
`DirectX::GamePad::State` field names directly (`pad.thumbSticks.leftX`,
`pad.buttons.rightShoulder`, `pad.IsDPadUpPressed()`), so a second backend is a rewrite of
every client rather than an addition; nothing input-driven can be constructed for a
headless test, because `GamePad` talks to XInput; and ARCHITECTURE's "A project is an
ordinary C++ application that links two static libraries" is not true today — it links
three. `ConnectionState` is the tell: it passed the engine/game split by being renamed,
not by acquiring a producer, and it is undocumented, so the T6 carve-out that gives it
meaning ("A disconnected controller is a state (neutral input), not an error") is stated
in PHILOSOPHY and nowhere a stranger would look.

**Remedy:** Build `engine/input/` properly — a `DeviceState` value (per-slot axes,
buttons, `ConnectionState`), a device interface the shell polls once per frame, and an
action map keyed by a game-supplied action id — with `engine/input/xinput/` as the single
implementation and `Application::gamepad()` withdrawn from the public header. Document the
neutral-input contract on `ConnectionState` in the same commit. What the layer needs from
XInput is already written by hand in `game/`: per-slot `GetState(slot, deadzone)` with the
deadzone mode as a *parameter* rather than a constant, an engine-owned previous-frame
snapshot per slot so pressed/released edges are computed once, analog→digital thresholding
with separate presence and absence thresholds, stable never-compacted slot indices, and a
neutral value for absent pads. What stays in the game: which actions exist, which control
maps to which action, and the threshold numbers — which belong in JSON, not `constexpr`
blocks (`game/objects/player_input.h:9-11`, `game/states/menu_input.h:11-12`) (T7).

    303			}
    304		}

The collidability interface is `game/objects/i_collision_game_object.h:7-21`, and it names
a game type in its vtable:

    11		virtual bool is_colliding(const ICollisionGameObject* other) const = 0;
    13		virtual CollisionObjectType collision_object_type() const = 0;

The shape tests are `engine/math/collision_tools.{h,cpp}` (98 + 292 lines) under
`namespace mattmath`.

**Why it matters:** ARCHITECTURE calls itself "the authoritative roster of modules and
folders" and gives `collision/` "broad phase, narrow phase, manifolds, resolution".
A stranger who opens the folder to find the broad phase finds a `std::pair` generator; a
stranger who links `ArtAttackEngine` to collide two things must write their own object
interface, their own O(n²) loop, and reach into `mattmath::CollisionTools`. Meanwhile
`engine/app/application.h:5` includes the collision module for the sole purpose of
scheduling render work, which puts a header named "collision" in the include graph of
every translation unit that sees the shell. This is distinct from outstanding findings #13
(the interface carries a game enum) and #18 (`Level` is scene plus ruleset): those are
about what the existing code *says*; this is that the folder named in the tree has no
contents, so the tree misdescribes the engine. Note that MattMath holding `CollisionTools`
breaks no dependency rule — MattMath still depends on nothing — it is a placement problem
only.

**Remedy:** Two moves in opposite directions. Move `collision_tools.*` and a de-game-ified
`CollisionObject` into `engine/collision/`, and move `Partitioner` out of it — to
`engine/core/` beside `ThreadPool`, or out of existence (see the plumbing finding below).
What a broad phase will need from `Scene`, none of which exists yet: a stable id per
registered collidable so a candidate pair is `(id, id)` and no pointer is needed to
resolve it; an AABB per collidable, which `IGameObject::bounds()` already returns; an
engine-owned layer/mask pair plus an opaque game tag (PHILOSOPHY, Collision); a
moved-since-last-frame signal or licence to rebuild each frame; those four stored
contiguously rather than behind `vector<unique_ptr<ICollisionGameObject>>` and five
virtual calls per rejection; a caller-supplied output buffer so the frame allocates
nothing; and a defined insertion point, because `Level::update` pushes new projectiles
into `collision_objects_` *during* the same update (`game/objects/level.cpp:220-224`).

#### `partition()` divides by a game-supplied count it never validates

- **File:** `engine/collision/partitioner.cpp:5-11`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T2 (correctness over speed), T6 (loud failure)

**What:** `partition()` divides by the caller's `num_partitions` with no precondition
check. Zero is integer division by zero; a negative value silently returns an empty
schedule.

**Evidence:**

     5	std::vector<std::pair<int, int>> Partitioner::partition(int num_elements, int num_partitions) const
     6	{
     7		std::vector<std::pair<int, int>> result;
     8		int elements_per_partition = num_elements / num_partitions;
     9		int remainder = num_elements % num_partitions;
    10		int start = 0;
    11		for (int i = 0; i < num_partitions && i < num_elements; i++)

The argument arrives from `ThreadPool::max_num_threads()` (`game/objects/level.cpp:397`,
`game/states/menu_page.cpp:134`), which returns its constructor argument unexamined
(`engine/core/thread_pool.cpp:5-7,108-111`), which is `options_.max_threads`
(`engine/app/application.cpp:134-135`) — a bare public field on the options struct a game
fills in:

    engine/app/application.h:45		int min_threads = 1;
    engine/app/application.h:46		int max_threads = 16;

**Why it matters:** `ApplicationOptions` is the documented way a game configures the
shell, and nothing in the header, the struct's comment or the `ThreadPool` constructor
says `max_threads` must be ≥ 1. A game that sets it to 0 — a plausible "let the engine
decide" guess — dies of a `#DE` inside `engine/collision/partitioner.cpp` with nothing
naming the option that was wrong, which is the opposite of T6. A negative value fails
quieter and earlier: `ThreadPool`'s constructor has already handed
`static_cast<DWORD>(negative)` to `SetThreadpoolThreadMaximum`
(`engine/core/thread_pool.cpp:15-16`), then `partition()` returns empty, no draw tasks are
submitted, and the game renders a blank screen with no error at all. The previous review
asked for exactly this guard (`docs/review/all-findings.md:1135`, "Guard
`Partitioner::partition` against `num_partitions <= 0`"); it is not in IMPLEMENTED.md and
the code above shows it was not applied. **Not a live defect** — every caller in the tree
passes 16 — which is why this is medium and not high: it is a missing precondition on a
public API, and the API is the engine's promise to code that has not been written yet.

**Remedy:** Throw `std::invalid_argument` naming the argument when `num_partitions < 1`
(and reject a negative `num_elements` while there). More useful still, validate
`min_threads` and `max_threads` in the `ThreadPool` constructor so the failure names the
option the game got wrong rather than the arithmetic three layers down.

#### A stateless helper shipped as a heap service through four layers — that has never once partitioned

- **File:** `engine/collision/partitioner.h:7-17`, `engine/app/application.cpp:147`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T11 (the stack over the heap), T4, T8

**What:** `Partitioner` has no data members and one behaviour, yet it is `make_unique`'d
as an application service and threaded through `Application` → `GameData` →
`LevelBuilder` → `Level` as a `const Partitioner*`. And with every argument any caller
in this repository actually passes, the behaviour is the identity mapping.

**Evidence:** the class, entire:

     7	class Partitioner
     8	{
     9	public:
    10		Partitioner() = default;
    12		std::vector<std::pair<int, int>>
    13			partition(int num_elements, int num_partitions) const;

The plumbing, in nine pieces:

    engine/app/application.cpp:147		this->partitioner_ = std::make_unique<Partitioner>();
    engine/app/application.h:157		std::unique_ptr<Partitioner> partitioner_ = nullptr;
    engine/app/application.h:122		const Partitioner* partitioner() const;
    game/game_data.h:51			const artattack::Partitioner* partitioner() const;
    game/game_data.cpp:101-103		return this->application_->partitioner();
    game/objects/level_builder.h:27		const artattack::Partitioner* partitioner);
    game/objects/level_builder.h:42	const artattack::Partitioner* partitioner_ = nullptr;
    game/objects/level.h:77			const artattack::Partitioner* partitioner);
    game/objects/level.h:155		const artattack::Partitioner* partitioner_ = nullptr;

And the loop condition that makes all of it a no-op (`partitioner.cpp:11`):

    11		for (int i = 0; i < num_partitions && i < num_elements; i++)

Both call sites pass `num_partitions = max_threads = 16` and `num_elements` = the player
count (≤ 4, `game/objects/level.cpp:401`) or the menu-object count (exactly 2 at every one
of the nine `draw_mobjects_in_viewports` call sites, e.g. `game/states/main_menu.cpp:44-51`).
With n ≤ k the clamp fires, `elements_per_partition` is 0 and the front-loaded remainder
gives every partition exactly one element: `partition()` returns
`{{0,1},{1,2},{2,3},{3,4}}` and nothing else, ever.

**Why it matters:** One heap allocation, one `unique_ptr` member, two accessors, two
constructor parameters and two raw-pointer members to reach a pure function — and the
function's whole observable behaviour today is `i → {i, i+1}`. T11 names the
heap-allocated, pointer-linked object web as the loudest thing this engine is *not*, and
this is that shape with none of the excuse: there is no state to own and no lifetime to
manage. It also drags `engine/collision/partitioner.h` into `engine/app/application.h:5`.
This is code the split touched, not legacy the split has yet to reach.

**Remedy:** Delete the class. The abstraction the call sites actually want is one level up
— `ThreadPool::parallel_for(count, fn)` owning the split, the dispatch and the wait, which
the previous review also proposed (`docs/review/all-findings.md:2130`). If a standalone
splitter is still wanted, make it a free function in `engine/core/`
(`artattack::partition_range(...)`) and delete the member, both accessors and both
constructor parameters with it.
