#### The engine's only pure primitive has no documented contract and no test

- **File:** `engine/collision/partitioner.h:12-16`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** testing
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/The public face; PHILOSOPHY/Tests and toolchain; T3

**What:** The header is the whole documentation, and three of `partition()`'s behaviours
are load-bearing at its call sites while none of them is written down or pinned.

**Evidence:**

    12		std::vector<std::pair<int, int>>
    13			partition(int num_elements, int num_partitions) const;
    14
    15		std::vector<std::pair<int, int>>
    16			partition(size_t num_elements, int num_partitions) const;

Unwritten but relied upon: (a) the range is half-open, `[first, second)`; (b) the result
size is `min(num_elements, num_partitions)` and **not** `num_partitions` — the
`i < num_elements` clause at `partitioner.cpp:11` is the only thing keeping
`deferred_contexts->at(i)` in bounds at `game/objects/level.cpp:516` and
`game/states/menu_page.cpp:180`; (c) the remainder is distributed to the *first*
`remainder` partitions (`partitioner.cpp:14-18`), so partitions are not equal-sized.
`tests/` holds `assets/`, `core/` and `math/` only, and the root
`CMakeLists.txt:10,15-17` registers those three targets and no more.

**Why it matters:** PHILOSOPHY says "A new public primitive ships with behavioural tests
in the same commit" and "Every public engine header is documented ... A stranger starts
from the headers, not from reading the implementation." Both call sites inferred (b) from
the implementation, and both would break silently if the clamp were ever "fixed" to return
exactly `num_partitions` ranges — a change a reader of the header would consider obviously
correct. This is the cheapest possible test target in the codebase: a function with zero
dependencies and no state.

**Remedy:** Write the contract as a header comment — half-open ranges, clamped count,
front-loaded remainder, the precondition on the count — mark it `[[nodiscard]]`, and add a
test target covering `n < k`, `n == k`, `n % k != 0`, `n == 0` and the rejected `k < 1`.
The suite does not need to link the engine for this: `tests/assets/CMakeLists.txt`
already shows the pattern of compiling the one dependency-free translation unit directly.

#### `partition()` returns element ranges only, so both callers index worker arrays by element index

- **File:** `engine/collision/partitioner.h:12-16` (call sites `game/states/menu_page.cpp:175-181`, `game/objects/level.cpp:514-524`)
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T4 (clarity over cleverness), T2

**What:** The return type carries `[start, end)` over elements and no worker index, so both
call sites use the *element* index to select the per-worker deferred context, command list
and sprite batch — correct only while element count ≤ thread count.

**Evidence:** `game/states/menu_page.cpp` — `i` indexes `mobjects`, and is then used to
pick a context, a command list and a batch:

    175		for (int i = start; i < end; i++)
    176		{
    177			// Use the contexts passed in rather than re-fetching the same ones
    178			// through GameData from a worker thread.
    179			this->draw_range_of_mobjects_in_viewports(
    180				deferred_contexts->at(i),
    181				command_lists->at(i), sprite_batches->at(i), mobjects->at(i).first, mobjects->at(i).second);

`game/objects/level.cpp` — the same conflation, `i` indexing `player_objects_` and the
contexts:

    514		for (int i = start; i < end; i++)
    515		{
    516			if (deferred_contexts->at(i)->GetType() != D3D11_DEVICE_CONTEXT_DEFERRED)
    ...
    521			const int player_num = this->player_objects_->at(i)->player_num();
    523			this->viewport_manager_->apply_player_viewport(
    524				player_num, deferred_contexts->at(i), sprite_batches->at(i));

**Why it matters:** The contexts and batches are sized `options_.max_threads` = 16
(`engine/app/application.cpp:63-64,156-167`). Both callers are safe today only because
they pass fewer elements than threads (≤ 4 players, exactly 2 menu objects), which makes
`partition()` emit one partition per element so that element index *equals* worker index
by coincidence. The first caller to partition more than 16 elements gets
`std::out_of_range` from `at(i)` on a worker thread — recorded by the pool's barrier
(`engine/core/thread_pool.cpp:83-91`) and rethrown out of `draw()`
(`thread_pool.cpp:72-75`). The path is unreachable today, so this is a trap and not a live
bug, but it is a trap the API builds: nothing in the return type says which worker a range
belongs to, so each caller had to invent the mapping, and both invented the same wrong one.

**Remedy:** Return the worker index with each range (`struct Partition { int worker, first,
last; }`), or — better — replace the whole pattern with `ThreadPool::parallel_for(count,
[](int worker, int first, int last){ ... })`, which owns the mapping once and deletes the
question.

#### The action-mapping mechanism is written twice in `game/`, and the two copies have drifted

- **File:** `game/objects/player_input.cpp:18-37,120-146`, `game/states/menu_input.cpp:18-36,133-154`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T4 ("duplication is the opposite of clarity at scale"), T1

**What:** `PlayerInput` and `MenuInput` are the same mechanism — poll four XInput slots,
keep a previous-frame snapshot, edge-detect, threshold analog to digital, return one entry
per slot — implemented twice in full, with no shared code between them.

**Evidence:** the same skeleton, written out twice:

    game/objects/player_input.cpp:122	    RawPlayerInput current[MAX_PAD_COUNT];
    game/objects/player_input.cpp:135	    std::vector<PlayerInputData> result(MAX_PAD_COUNT);
    game/states/menu_input.cpp:135	    RawMenuInput current[MAX_PAD_COUNT];
    game/states/menu_input.cpp:144	    std::vector<ProcessedMenuInput> result(MAX_PAD_COUNT);

with the pad sampled under different deadzone modes:

    game/objects/player_input.cpp:21	    auto pad = this->gamepad_->GetState(gamepad_num, GamePad::DEAD_ZONE_CIRCULAR);
    game/states/menu_input.cpp:21		const auto pad = this->gamepad_->GetState(gamepad_num, GamePad::DEAD_ZONE_NONE);

and edge semantics chosen per call site rather than by the mechanism — within
`player_input.cpp` alone, jump fires on press and pause fires on release:

    game/objects/player_input.cpp:46	    bool jump_button_pressed = current.jump_button && !previous.jump_button;
    game/objects/player_input.cpp:54	    bool pause_menu = !current.pause_menu && previous.pause_menu;

Both files also end their per-pad calculation with the same line
(`player_input.cpp:112`, `menu_input.cpp:129`):

    result.connection = ConnectionState::connected;

**Why it matters:** This is the code that belongs in `engine/input/` — slots, snapshots,
edges, deadzones, neutral defaults are pure mechanism, and the only game-specific part is
which button means "jump". Because it lives in the game twice, a fix to one copy does not
reach the other. I am *not* claiming the deadzone divergence is itself a bug: `MenuInput`
applies its own presence/absence thresholds downstream (`menu_input.h:11-12`) and
`DEAD_ZONE_NONE` is a defensible choice for that, while `PlayerInput` wants a circular
deadzone for analog movement. The defect is that the choice is invisible — two files that
look identical sample the hardware differently, nothing says why, and neither header
mentions the other. That is what a mechanism with a deadzone *parameter* would have made
explicit.

**Remedy:** Lift the slot/snapshot/edge/threshold machinery into `engine/input/` as the
action-mapping layer with the deadzone mode as a parameter, leaving each game type as a
binding table plus its own action enum. The thresholds go to JSON (T7).

#### The `size_t` overload narrows silently and makes the overload set ambiguous

- **File:** `engine/collision/partitioner.cpp:25-28`, `engine/collision/partitioner.h:12-16`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T5 (compile-time over run-time)

**What:** The convenience overload exists only to hide a narrowing cast, and its presence
makes a call with any *other* integer type ill-formed.

**Evidence:**

    25	std::vector<std::pair<int, int>> Partitioner::partition(size_t num_elements, int num_partitions) const
    26	{
    27		return Partitioner::partition(static_cast<int>(num_elements), num_partitions);
    28	}

**Why it matters:** Two small costs. The cast is the engine silencing a warning instead of
deciding what a container larger than `INT_MAX` means — a `size()` above 2³¹ becomes
negative, the loop at `partitioner.cpp:11` never runs, and the caller draws nothing with no
diagnostic (T6). That is unreachable in a 2D game whose callers pass 4 and 2, which is why
this is low rather than medium, but it is the *reason the overload exists*: the engine is
shipping a silent-truncation API to save the caller a cast. Second, `int` and `size_t` are
both conversions from `unsigned int` or `long`, so `partition(some_uint32, k)` is an
ambiguous call — a compile error a user will read as an engine bug rather than as their own.

**Remedy:** Keep one overload over one index type and let callers convert explicitly.

#### `partition()` heap-allocates a fresh schedule vector on the per-frame draw path

- **File:** `engine/collision/partitioner.cpp:7,19`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** performance
- **Tenet:** T8; PHILOSOPHY/Performance

**What:** Every call heap-allocates an unreserved `std::vector` to describe a schedule that
changes only when the object count does, and the return type puts that allocation on every
caller.

**Evidence:**

     7		std::vector<std::pair<int, int>> result;
    ...
    19			result.push_back(std::make_pair(start, end));

and at one call site the result is then copied once per task, per frame
(`game/objects/level.cpp:406`):

    406			this->thread_pool_->add_task([this, i, partitioned_players,

`partitioned_players` is captured **by value** while each lambda reads exactly
`partitioned_players[i]`. `game/states/menu_page.cpp:145` captures by reference and pays
nothing, which is itself the evidence that the API leaves the decision to each caller.

**Why it matters:** PHILOSOPHY (Performance) says flatly that "Per-frame code performs no
heap allocation", on the path the engine's headline value is measured on, for a table that
is byte-identical every frame until a player joins or leaves. It is small — one vector plus
four copies plus `push_back` growth at four players — which is why it is low. The
by-value capture itself is already filed (`docs/review/all-findings.md:2141`); what is new
is that the engine API's *return type* is what forces an allocation, so no caller can opt
out.

**Remedy:** Fill a caller-supplied span, or return the single range for one worker index
(`Partition partition(int worker, int n, int k)`), so the frame allocates nothing. Deleting
the class in favour of `parallel_for` does this too.

#### `partitioner.h` is not self-contained: `std::pair` and `size_t` with neither `<utility>` nor `<cstddef>`

- **File:** `engine/collision/partitioner.h:3,12-16`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Files; PHILOSOPHY/Tests and toolchain (light headers, disciplined includes)

**What:** The header names `std::pair` and unqualified `size_t` while including only
`<vector>`, and the `.cpp` calls `std::make_pair` with no `<utility>` of its own.

**Evidence:**

     3	#include <vector>
    12		std::vector<std::pair<int, int>>
    13			partition(int num_elements, int num_partitions) const;
    16			partition(size_t num_elements, int num_partitions) const;

    engine/collision/partitioner.cpp:1	#include "engine/collision/partitioner.h"
    engine/collision/partitioner.cpp:19		result.push_back(std::make_pair(start, end));

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS puts the own header first specifically to prove "every
header compiles on its own", and this one compiles only because `<vector>` happens to drag
both in. I am *not* claiming this breaks on the second platform — libstdc++ and libc++
also reach `std::pair` through `<vector>`, so the practical portability risk is near zero.
The cost is the discipline: the file states two dependencies it does not declare, and
`size_t` unqualified at namespace scope is not guaranteed to be declared at all. That is
the rule the engine is trying to hold, in the smallest header it owns.

**Remedy:** Add `#include <utility>` and `#include <cstddef>` to the header and `<utility>`
to the `.cpp`; spell it `std::size_t`.

#### `partition()` hands back `std::pair`, so every call site reads `.first` and `.second`

- **File:** `engine/collision/partitioner.h:12-16`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** T4 (clarity over cleverness); CONVENTIONS/Variables and members

**What:** The element type of the returned schedule is `std::pair<int, int>`, so the
range's two ends have no names anywhere in the engine or in either caller.

**Evidence:** the declaration (`partitioner.h:12-13`) and what it reads like at both call
sites:

    game/objects/level.cpp:409			this->draw_player_view_level(partitioned_players[i].first,
    game/objects/level.cpp:410			partitioned_players[i].second,

    game/states/menu_page.cpp:149			partitioned_mobjects[i].first, partitioned_mobjects[i].second,

Both then receive them as `int start, int end` (`level.cpp:509`, `menu_page.cpp:169`), so
the names exist on both sides of the API and only the API itself declines to carry them.

**Why it matters:** `.first` and `.second` are exactly the naming CONVENTIONS rules out —
"names that say what they hold" — and here they are load-bearing, because the half-openness
of the range is undocumented (see the contract finding). A reader at
`partitioned_players[i].second` has no way to know whether the value is the last index or
one past it without opening `partitioner.cpp`. A two-field struct costs nothing, makes the
half-open convention nameable (`begin`/`end`), and is where the worker index would go when
the worker/element conflation above is fixed.

**Remedy:** Replace `std::pair<int, int>` with a named struct in the same header. The
previous review proposed the same shape (`docs/review/all-findings.md:2141`, "Replace
`std::pair<int,int>` with a named `struct PartitionRange { int begin, end; }`").

#### The engine's most-included public header pulls in the collision module to declare a pointer

- **File:** `engine/app/application.h:5,122,157`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Tests and toolchain ("Compile speed is a maintained property — light headers, disciplined includes"); T10

**What:** `application.h` — the header every game and the sample include to reach the shell
— includes the whole collision module, and every use of the type in it and in the three
game headers downstream is a pointer.

**Evidence:**

    engine/app/application.h:5	#include "engine/collision/partitioner.h"
    engine/app/application.h:122		const Partitioner* partitioner() const;
    engine/app/application.h:157		std::unique_ptr<Partitioner> partitioner_ = nullptr;

The same pattern repeats downstream, each time for a pointer member or a pointer
parameter:

    game/objects/level.h:19		#include "engine/collision/partitioner.h"
    game/objects/level.h:155	const artattack::Partitioner* partitioner_ = nullptr;
    game/objects/level_builder.h:15	#include "engine/collision/partitioner.h"
    game/objects/level_builder.h:42	const artattack::Partitioner* partitioner_ = nullptr;

`std::unique_ptr<Partitioner>` as a member does require the complete type at the point
`~Application` is defined, but that point is `application.cpp`, not the header.

**Why it matters:** Build time is named as an engine responsibility precisely because
"every behaviour change is a compile" (T10), and this is the header with the widest fan-out
in the project — the sample, every game state, every `GameData` consumer. Four headers pull
in a definition where a forward declaration would do. It is small on its own; it is listed
because it is the mechanical half of the module-placement finding above, and because it is
a one-line fix that survives even if `Partitioner` is deleted outright (the same applies to
whatever replaces it).

**Remedy:** Forward-declare `class Partitioner;` in `application.h` and in the two game
headers, and include the definition in the `.cpp` files that call `partition()`. If the
class is deleted in favour of a free function or `ThreadPool::parallel_for`, the include
goes with it.

### Rejected

- **Raw #5, "Move `Partitioner` out of `collision/`; it is a scheduling helper"** — merged
  into "`engine/collision/` contains no collision". Same folder, same evidence, one remedy;
  filing both double-counts one defect.
- **Raw #10, "`ConnectionState` is engine vocabulary with no engine mechanism"** — merged
  into "`engine/input/` is a label". Its evidence (no engine translation unit names the
  enum; the header documents nothing) is carried in the merged finding; as a separate entry
  it restates raw #1's conclusion with a different exhibit.
- **Raw #5's claim that `app` depending on `collision` "inverts the module table"** —
  factually wrong and dropped. ARCHITECTURE's table gives `app` "everything", explicitly
  and with a paragraph of justification. The placement objection stands on its own; the
  dependency-violation dressing does not.
- **Raw #2's "`collision_tools` ... is in the module ARCHITECTURE says may depend on
  *nothing*"** — misleading, rewritten. MattMath depends on nothing today and
  `collision_tools.h` includes only other MattMath headers. This is a placement problem,
  not a dependency violation, and the finding now says so.
- **Raw #3's high severity** — re-graded to medium. The unchecked divide is real and the
  causal chain is exact, but no caller in the tree can reach it: `max_threads` defaults to
  16, both call sites read it through `ThreadPool`, and no game code sets it otherwise.
  A missing precondition on a public API, not a crash.
- **Raw #6's "testing this pure function today would mean linking D3D11 and DirectXTK"** —
  overstated, trimmed. `tests/assets/CMakeLists.txt` already compiles two engine
  translation units directly rather than linking the library, so the workaround is in the
  tree and documented in a comment.
- **Raw #7's medium and raw #9's medium** — re-graded to low. The `size_t` truncation needs
  a container above `INT_MAX`; the allocation is one small vector plus four copies per
  frame. Both are real misses against stated destination properties and neither is worth a
  medium in a group this size.
- **Raw #11's "a stick position that moves a menu cursor may not move a player"** — kept as
  an observation, dropped as a defect. `MenuInput` applies its own presence/absence
  thresholds downstream, so `DEAD_ZONE_NONE` is a defensible choice there; the finding now
  says the divergence is undocumented rather than wrong.
- **Raw #12's "it will surface on the first non-MSVC standard library"** — overstated,
  trimmed. libstdc++ and libc++ both reach `std::pair` through `<vector>`. The convention
  point survives; the portability prediction does not.
- **Not filed: a `/W4 /WX` signed/unsigned regression.** I checked, because the previous
  review claimed `int i < v.size()` at `level.cpp:404` and `menu_page.cpp:143` was C4018.
  `build.ninja:690` shows `/W4 /WX` genuinely applied to `level.cpp`, and its `.obj` is
  newer than `build.ninja`, so the flags are current and no warning fires. No finding.
- **Not re-filed (still live, already recorded elsewhere):** `throw new std::exception` in
  two provably dead branches at `game/states/menu_input.cpp:66` and `:122`
  (`all-findings.md:7895`), and the by-value partition-table capture at
  `game/objects/level.cpp:406` (`all-findings.md:2141`) — the latter's engine-API cause is
  filed above.

<a id="g-render-device"></a>

## render-device — DeviceResources

*Group `render-device` · 15 findings (1 critical, 1 high, 4 medium, 9 low) · source `review2/verified/render-device.md`, verified report.*

I re-opened `engine/render/device_resources.h` (147 lines) and `device_resources.cpp` (777 lines)
in full and re-checked every line the reviewer cited; all twelve anchors land on the code quoted.
I then re-derived the facts the findings lean on rather than trusting the summary: `ls
engine/render` (38 files, no `d3d11/`, no `renderer.h`), `ls tests` (`assets`, `core`, `math` —
no `render`), `grep "pragma warning"` across `engine game samples tests` (exactly one hit, this
file), `grep AdjustWindowRect` (zero hits repo-wide), `grep -E "\bm_[a-zA-Z]"` (exactly three
files: this pair plus `engine/core/step_timer.h`), and a per-accessor caller count for all
seventeen D3D/DXGI accessors.

Three of the reviewer's supporting numbers were wrong and are corrected here. **Five** of the
seventeen accessors have an external caller, not four or seven as the report says in two
different places — `GetD3DDevice`, `GetD3DDeviceContext`, `GetRenderTargetView`,
`GetScreenViewport`, `GetOutputSize`; `GetWindow` and `GetRenderTarget` have **zero** (the
reviewer's grep for them caught `GetWindowLongPtr` and `GetRenderTargetView`), so twelve are dead
public API, not thirteen. `engine/render` holds 38 files, not forty. And the "two dialects eleven
lines apart" is 22 lines (`m_backBufferCount:123`, `deferred_context_count_:145`).

I re-graded four findings down. The `#pragma warning(disable : 4061)` is real and is the only one
in the tree, but C4061 is off by default and `/W4` does not enable it, so the line is inert — the
defect is documentary, not behavioural: **low**, not medium. The Windows.h/DXGI export finding
loses its headline consequence entirely: ARCHITECTURE's *A game project* explicitly lists "the
shared settings target — linked like everyone else's" in a project's anatomy, so a consumer
missing `NOMINMAX` is not doing what the doc describes; what survives is compile cost and an
unenforceable module wall, both consequences of the missing seam: **low**. The device-loss
testability finding claims the restore ordering is "unstated" when `cpp:442-444` states most of it
in a comment; only the *before-`OnDeviceRestored`* half is undocumented: **low**, narrowed. The
defaulted move operations stay low but gain a second stranded back-pointer I found
(`ViewportManager` also holds a `DeviceResources*`).

Everything else survived intact, and the two structural findings got stronger, not weaker. The
`SetWindow` bug is worse than filed: the same parameter is fed *client* pixels by `WM_SIZE`
(`application.cpp:515`) and `WM_EXITSIZEMOVE` (`:527-530`) and *window* pixels at startup
(`:59-61`), so the unit is inconsistent inside the engine itself — and the observable proof is
that re-selecting the resolution the game is already at silently *fixes* the picture.

I added three findings. The header's contract on `create_deferred_contexts` names the wrong
function as the one that rebuilds after device loss, which is a wrong statement about the exact
path that produced seven of the last review's criticals. `CreateFactory` contains a brace-less
`if` whose controlled statement sits on the far side of an `#endif`. And the two throws this file
actually authored discard the values that would name the failure, in a codebase whose T6 is
"loud, with names". I considered and did not file: the absence of `[[nodiscard]]` (there are zero
in the entire engine, so it is not this group's defect), and `m_options(flags | c_FlipPresent)`
forcing a flag the caller cannot clear (real, but template-inherited and dissolved by the seam).

### Themes

- The file is vendored third-party code adopted into the engine's namespace but not into its
  conventions, its tests, or its warning policy — neither bought (T9, tracking upstream) nor built
  (held to the standard), and nothing in the tree says which.
- Every D3D and DXGI type in the engine's public surface enters through this one header, and the
  interface ARCHITECTURE says should stand between them and everything else exists in no form: no
  `engine/render/d3d11/`, no `renderer.h`, no `tests/render/`.
- The class is far wider than its use — twelve of seventeen graphics accessors have no caller
  anywhere — which means the seam that replaces it is much cheaper than the class looks.
- The contracts live in the author's head, not the header: whether `SetWindow` wants client or
  window pixels, whether `deferred_contexts()` may return null, whether its vector keeps its
  address across a restore, and which function rebuilds the pool. Two of the four are already
  answered wrongly — one by the engine's own caller, one by the header's own comment.
- Ownership of the deferred-context pool is spread across three members that must agree where one
  `vector` would do (T11).

#### Build the renderer seam ARCHITECTURE promises; today D3D11 is the engine's public draw API

- **File:** `engine/render/device_resources.h:56-100`
- **Severity:** critical
- **Category:** boundary
- **Tenet:** ARCHITECTURE/The tree, PHILOSOPHY/Simulation and rendering, T1

**What:** ARCHITECTURE places the D3D11 backend in `engine/render/d3d11/` behind an engine-owned
interface. That folder does not exist, no `renderer.h` exists, and no renderer type exists.
Instead this header publishes seventeen raw D3D/DXGI accessors, and the `ID3D11DeviceContext*`
they hand out is the drawing vocabulary of both client games.

**Evidence:**

        // Device Accessors.
        RECT GetOutputSize() const noexcept { return m_outputSize; }

        // Direct3D Accessors.
        auto                    GetD3DDevice() const noexcept           { return m_d3dDevice.Get(); }
        auto                    GetD3DDeviceContext() const noexcept    { return m_d3dContext.Get(); }
        auto                    GetSwapChain() const noexcept           { return m_swapChain.Get(); }
        ...
        std::vector<ID3D11DeviceContext*>* deferred_contexts() const noexcept;
        // Throws std::out_of_range for an invalid index, so not noexcept.
        ID3D11DeviceContext* deferred_context(int index) const;

`samples/minimal/states/hello_state.cpp:62-85` — the file ARCHITECTURE names as the new-project
template and the second client that keeps the boundary honest:

        void HelloState::draw()
        {
            ...
            artattack::DeviceResources* device = this->app_->device_resources();
            ID3D11DeviceContext* deferred = device->deferred_context(0);
            SpriteBatch* sprite_batch = this->app_->sprite_batches()->at(0);

            sprite_batch->Begin(SpriteSortMode_Deferred);
            this->greeting_->draw(sprite_batch);
            this->hint_->draw(sprite_batch);
            sprite_batch->End();

            ID3D11CommandList* commands = nullptr;
            if (FAILED(deferred->FinishCommandList(FALSE, &commands)))
            {
                throw std::runtime_error("HelloState::draw - FinishCommandList failed");
            }

            device->GetD3DDeviceContext()->ExecuteCommandList(commands, FALSE);
            commands->Release();
        }

**Why it matters:** `engine/render/` holds 38 files and no `d3d11/`; `tests/` holds `assets`,
`core` and `math` and no `render`, because nothing above this file is constructible without a
window — which contradicts "Everything below the platform edge is testable headlessly"
(PHILOSOPHY, Tests and toolchain). The raw context type has already propagated into eight
game-side signatures (`game/objects/level.h:80,164,168,177,181`, `game/states/menu_page.h:38,48`)
and into `engine/render/viewport_manager.h:35,38`, so the `record → FinishCommandList →
ExecuteCommandList → Release` protocol is hand-written in four places
(`game/objects/level.cpp:606`, `:670`, `game/states/menu_page.cpp:120`,
`samples/minimal/states/hello_state.cpp:78`), each with its own hand-written `->Release()`. A
stranger starting from `samples/minimal/` learns Direct3D 11, not this engine, and "a second
platform is an addition, not a rewrite" is currently false.

The seam is much smaller than the class suggests. Counting callers for all seventeen accessors,
only five have one outside this file:

| Accessor | External callers |
|---|---|
| `GetD3DDevice` | `application.cpp:142,154` (device for `ResourceLoader`, `CommonStates`) |
| `GetD3DDeviceContext` | `application.cpp:285`, `game_states.cpp:328`, `menu_page.cpp:155`, `hello_state.cpp:83` — three of the four do nothing but `ExecuteCommandList` |
| `GetRenderTargetView` | `application.cpp:288` (in `clear()` only) |
| `GetScreenViewport` | `application.cpp:293` (in `clear()` only) |
| `GetOutputSize` | `application.cpp:350` (`on_window_moved`) |

The other twelve — `GetSwapChain`, `GetDXGIFactory`, `GetWindow`, `GetDeviceFeatureLevel`,
`GetRenderTarget`, `GetDepthStencil`, `GetDepthStencilView`, `GetBackBufferFormat`,
`GetDepthBufferFormat`, `GetBackBufferCount`, `GetColorSpace`, `GetDeviceOptions` — have no caller
anywhere in the repository. So the interface needs roughly: a per-worker draw-list handle
(replacing `deferred_context(i)`), `submit()` (the finish/execute/release protocol, written once),
`begin_frame`/`end_frame` (absorbing `Application::clear()` and `Present()`), `draw_sprite(...)`
as PHILOSOPHY already specifies, `back_buffer_size()`, and `begin_marker`/`end_marker` for the
PIX pair. `GetD3DDevice` is not a renderer concern at all — it is a resource-factory one, and
`RenderResources` already speaks `Handle<ID3D11ShaderResourceView>`
(`engine/render/render_resources.h:38`), so only the handle's payload type has to change.

**Remedy:** Add `engine/render/renderer.h` with that surface, move this file to
`engine/render/d3d11/` as its one implementation, and port `samples/minimal/` first — it is 85
lines and it is the acceptance test for whether the seam is real. Decide explicitly in
ARCHITECTURE whether "interface" means a vtable or a compile-time-selected concrete type: T8 rules
out a virtual call per sprite, so the document should say which kind of seam it means.

#### Size the back buffer from the client rect, not the window rect

- **File:** `engine/render/device_resources.cpp:394-401`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T2, PHILOSOPHY/The public face

**What:** `SetWindow(HWND, width, height)` treats its `width`/`height` as back-buffer (client)
pixels but does not say so, and the engine's only startup caller passes the *window* dimensions.
The windowed swap chain is therefore created larger than the client area DXGI stretches it into,
for the whole session.

**Evidence:**

`engine/render/device_resources.h:49` — the whole contract, undocumented:

        void SetWindow(HWND window, int width, int height) noexcept;

`engine/render/device_resources.cpp:394-401`:

        void DeviceResources::SetWindow(HWND window, int width, int height) noexcept
        {
            m_window = window;

            m_outputSize.left = m_outputSize.top = 0;
            m_outputSize.right = static_cast<long>(width);
            m_outputSize.bottom = static_cast<long>(height);
        }

`engine/render/device_resources.cpp:284-285` then uses that rect as the back-buffer size, and
`:330` chooses stretch scaling:

        const UINT backBufferWidth = std::max<UINT>(static_cast<UINT>(m_outputSize.right - m_outputSize.left), 1u);
        const UINT backBufferHeight = std::max<UINT>(static_cast<UINT>(m_outputSize.bottom - m_outputSize.top), 1u);
        ...
        swapChainDesc.Scaling = DXGI_SCALING_STRETCH;

`engine/app/application.cpp:112-117` passes `CreateWindowExW`'s `nWidth`/`nHeight`, which MSDN
defines as the width and height *of the window*, non-client area included:

                this->window_ = CreateWindowExW(0,
                    this->options_.window_class_name.c_str(),
                    this->options_.window_title.c_str(), WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW,
                    CW_USEDEFAULT, CW_USEDEFAULT, size.x, size.y,
                    nullptr, nullptr, instance, this);

and `engine/app/application.cpp:59-61` hands the same numbers to `SetWindow`:

            const mattmath::Vector2I size =
                this->resolution_manager_->resolution_ivec();
            this->device_resources_->SetWindow(this->window_, size.x, size.y);

The unit is inconsistent inside the engine itself. The other two feeders of the same rect pass
*client* pixels — `application.cpp:515`, `LOWORD(l_param), HIWORD(l_param)` from `WM_SIZE`:

                app->on_window_size_changed(LOWORD(l_param), HIWORD(l_param));

and `application.cpp:527-530`, `WM_EXITSIZEMOVE`:

                    RECT client;
                    GetClientRect(window, &client);
                    app->on_window_size_changed(client.right - client.left,
                        client.bottom - client.top);

**Why it matters:** `AdjustWindowRect`/`AdjustWindowRectEx` appears nowhere in the repository
(grepped across `engine/`, `game/`, `samples/`, `tests/`). With the default
`ScreenResolution::s_1280_720` and `fullscreen = false` (`application.h:37-38`), the window is
1280x720 *including* frame and caption, so the client area is roughly 1264x681 at 96 DPI while
the swap chain is 1280x720 with `DXGI_SCALING_STRETCH`. The scale factors differ per axis
(≈0.988 horizontal, ≈0.946 vertical), so the whole game is resampled and squashed vertically.

Nothing corrects it. The `WM_SIZE` that `ShowWindow` sends synchronously at `application.cpp:124`
is dispatched from inside `create_window` — *before* `SetWindow` runs at `:61` — so
`WindowSizeChanged` early-returns at `device_resources.cpp:406-407` (`if (!m_window) return
false;`). Afterwards `on_window_moved` (`application.cpp:348-352`) feeds `GetOutputSize()` back
into `WindowSizeChanged`, which the equality test at `:413` always rejects. The mismatch persists
until the user drags a border.

The proof is observable: `Application::set_resolution` (`:215-224`) calls `SetWindowPos` with the
same window-sized numbers, which produces a `WM_SIZE` carrying *client* dimensions, which
`WindowSizeChanged` accepts because they differ — so a player who opens the options menu and
re-picks the resolution the game is *already at* silently makes the picture correct. Both
`ArtAttackGame` and `ArtAttackSample` launch windowed by default. The fullscreen path
(`application.cpp:102-108`) has the same shape and a larger gap: `SW_SHOWMAXIMIZED` gives the
`WS_POPUP` window the full screen as its client area while `SetWindow` still says 1280x720.

**Remedy:** Document on `SetWindow` that the dimensions are back-buffer (client) pixels — that is
the one line that makes every caller checkable — and have `Application::create_window` run
`AdjustWindowRectEx` on the requested resolution before `CreateWindowExW`, or call `GetClientRect`
on the created window and pass that to `SetWindow`. If fullscreen is meant to render at a fixed
resolution and upscale, say so at the call site rather than leaving it as the same bug's shadow.

#### Stop handing out a raw pointer to a heap vector that is reallocated on every device restore

- **File:** `engine/render/device_resources.cpp:740-764`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T11, PHILOSOPHY/Services and lifetimes

**What:** `deferred_contexts()` is a `const` method returning a mutable
`std::vector<ID3D11DeviceContext*>*` into a `unique_ptr`-owned vector that
`create_deferred_contexts` destroys and re-allocates on every device restore. Nothing in the
header says the address changes, or that the pointer can be null.

**Evidence:**

`engine/render/device_resources.h:143-145` — three members holding one fact:

        std::vector<Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<ID3D11DeviceContext>> deferred_contexts_owned_;
        std::unique_ptr<std::vector<ID3D11DeviceContext*>> deferred_contexts_ = nullptr;
        int deferred_context_count_ = 0;

`engine/render/device_resources.cpp:744-745` — the address changes:

            this->deferred_contexts_owned_.clear();
            this->deferred_contexts_ = std::make_unique<std::vector<ID3D11DeviceContext*>>();

`engine/render/device_resources.cpp:466-469` calls it from the restore path:

            if (deferred_context_count_ > 0)
            {
                create_deferred_contexts(deferred_context_count_);
            }

`engine/render/device_resources.cpp:761-764` — a `const` method returning a mutable handle to
internals:

        std::vector<ID3D11DeviceContext*>* DeviceResources::deferred_contexts() const noexcept
        {
            return this->deferred_contexts_.get();
        }

**Why it matters:** No caller holds the pointer across a restore today — `application.cpp:286`,
`game_states.cpp:320` and `menu_page.cpp:130` all re-fetch per frame, and device loss is only
detected in `Present()` after `draw()` has returned — so this is latent, not live. It is still a
trap laid in a public header, and `application.h:126-129` documents the *opposite* guarantee for
the sibling accessor one file away: "The vector's own address is stable; only the pointers inside
it move." It is also the half-done part of a previous fix — the last review asked twice for the
`unique_ptr<vector<>>` indirection to be dropped, and a second parallel container was added beside
it instead. Separately, `deferred_contexts()` returns null before `create_deferred_contexts` has
run, which is undocumented and dereferenced unguarded at `application.cpp:298`
(`for (auto& deferred_context : *deferred_contexts)`); and the `const`-and-mutable signature exists
only so `Application::clear() const` can bind render targets through it.

**Remedy:** Make the member a plain `std::vector<Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<ID3D11DeviceContext>>` and
expose `std::size_t deferred_context_count()` plus the existing checked `deferred_context(index)`.
That deletes the raw mirror, the `unique_ptr`, the separate count and the finding below it in one
edit — or delete the accessor entirely when the renderer seam lands.

#### Bring the vendored DirectX template file under the engine's conventions, or move it back out

- **File:** `engine/render/device_resources.h:1-100`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Never, T9

**What:** The file is the DirectX Tool Kit VS template, now inside `namespace artattack` and
carrying local features, but it was skipped by every conventions pass: 41 `m_` members, PascalCase
methods, `Get`-prefixed accessors, an `I`-prefixed type, and a header comment naming a file that
no longer exists.

**Evidence:**

`engine/render/device_resources.h:1-3` — the comment still names the pre-rename file:

        //
        // DeviceResources.h - A wrapper for the Direct3D 11 device and swapchain
        //

`:107-109`, the member block (41 `\bm_` matches in this header alone):

        Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<IDXGIFactory2>               m_dxgiFactory;
        Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<ID3D11Device1>               m_d3dDevice;
        Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<ID3D11DeviceContext1>        m_d3dContext;

alongside the members in the same block that *did* get the treatment, `:143-145`:

        std::vector<Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<ID3D11DeviceContext>> deferred_contexts_owned_;
        std::unique_ptr<std::vector<ID3D11DeviceContext*>> deferred_contexts_ = nullptr;
        int deferred_context_count_ = 0;

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS/Never lists `m_`, `get_` on accessors and `I` prefixes explicitly,
and `GetRenderTargetView()`, `GetOutputSize()` and `RegisterDeviceNotify()` breach all three
families at once — in a header `engine/app/application.h:9` re-exports to every game translation
unit. A reader who learned the scheme from CONVENTIONS in one sitting then meets two dialects
inside one member block, `m_deviceNotify` and `deferred_context_count_` seven lines apart. And the
"is this ours?" question has no answer: `grep -E "\bm_[a-zA-Z]"` over `engine game samples tests`
returns exactly three files — this pair and `engine/core/step_timer.h`, the other DirectXTK
template — while the file itself is no longer upstream-updatable, because it holds a
deferred-context pool the template never had. The T9 exemption for bought code has therefore
lapsed without anyone deciding it had.

**Remedy:** Decide the file is ours: rename the members, the methods and the notify type to
CONVENTIONS, fix the header comment, and add a line saying it derives from the DirectXTK template.
If it is to stay bought, move it to `external/` and keep the deferred-context pool in engine code
beside it. Whichever way, `engine/core/step_timer.h` is the same decision.

#### Replace `interface` — it is a Windows SDK macro, not C++

- **File:** `engine/render/device_resources.h:17-24`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** T12

**What:** `IDeviceNotify` is declared with `interface`, which is a Windows SDK preprocessor macro
(`basetyps.h`: `#define interface __STRUCT__`, `#define __STRUCT__ struct`), so the engine's one
game-facing device-loss type is declared in a keyword the language does not have.

**Evidence:**

        // Provides an interface for an application that owns DeviceResources to be notified of the device being lost or created.
        interface IDeviceNotify
        {
            virtual void OnDeviceLost() = 0;
            virtual void OnDeviceRestored() = 0;

        protected:
            ~IDeviceNotify() = default;
        };

**Why it matters:** T12 names this exact construct as the thing the engine does not do — "no macro
that reads like a keyword… a stranger reading an engine header meets classes, templates and the
standard library, and nothing they must learn *this engine* to parse". It is worse than the
Unreal case T12 argues against, because the macro is not even the engine's: the declaration
expands to `struct` only because `<Windows.h>` (`:7`) and `<d3d11_1.h>` (`:9`) happen to precede
it, and the `protected:` on `:22` is load-bearing precisely because of which keyword it silently
became. The type is not internal — `engine/app/application.h:71` reads `class Application : public
IDeviceNotify, public StateContext`, so anyone writing their own shell inherits from it. On the
second platform ARCHITECTURE commits to, this header does not compile at all.

**Remedy:** Write `class DeviceNotify`, which drops the macro and the `I` prefix in one edit, and
move it beside the renderer interface when that lands.

#### Skip the frame when the swap chain is occluded

- **File:** `engine/render/device_resources.cpp:480-528`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** performance
- **Tenet:** T8

**What:** `Present` returns `void` and treats `DXGI_STATUS_OCCLUDED` as plain success, so nothing
above it can learn that the window is invisible — and a minimised game keeps clearing, fanning
the full render out across the thread pool, and presenting.

**Evidence:**

        void DeviceResources::Present()
        {
            HRESULT hr = E_FAIL;
            if (m_options & c_AllowTearing)
            {
                hr = m_swapChain->Present(0, DXGI_PRESENT_ALLOW_TEARING);
            }
            else
            {
                // The first argument instructs DXGI to block until VSync, putting the application
                // to sleep until the next VSync. This ensures we don't waste any cycles rendering
                // frames that will never be displayed to the screen.
                hr = m_swapChain->Present(1, 0);
            }
        ...
            else
            {
                ThrowIfFailed(hr);

**Why it matters:** `DXGI_STATUS_OCCLUDED` (0x087A0001) is a SUCCESS code, so `ThrowIfFailed`
passes it through and the `void` return discards it — occlusion is unreportable by construction.
`Application::window_proc` handles `SIZE_MINIMIZED` (`application.cpp:491-503`) by calling
`on_suspending()`, which suspends only the gamepad and the audio engine
(`application.cpp:323-333`); the `run()` loop at `:192-203` keeps calling `tick()`, and `render()`
at `:264-279` has no occlusion check either. So a minimised game still runs `clear()`
(`:281-305`, which touches all sixteen deferred contexts), the whole thread-pool fan-out in
`GameLevel::draw` (`game_states.cpp:312-339`), and a `Present` per iteration. Presents to an
occluded swap chain are discarded, so the sync interval quoted in the comment above no longer
paces the loop — which is exactly why DXGI's documented guidance is to stop presenting and test
with `DXGI_PRESENT_TEST` until the window is visible again.

**Remedy:** Return the `HRESULT` (or a small `PresentResult` enum) from `Present`, and have
`Application::render()` skip the frame and sleep briefly while the last present was occluded. The
enum is the better shape when the renderer seam lands, since `Present` becomes `end_frame()`.

#### The public contract on `create_deferred_contexts` names the wrong function

- **File:** `engine/render/device_resources.h:93-100`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** documentation
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Services and lifetimes, PHILOSOPHY/The public face
- **Origin:** added-by-verifier

**What:** The header tells the reader that `CreateDeviceResources()` rebuilds the deferred
contexts after device loss. It does not — `HandleDeviceLost()` does — and the difference matters,
because both are public and `CreateDeviceResources()` alone reproduces exactly the bug the comment
claims is prevented.

**Evidence:**

`engine/render/device_resources.h:93-97`:

        // Creates `num` deferred contexts on the current device. The count is
        // remembered so CreateDeviceResources() can rebuild them after device
        // loss - contexts belong to the device that made them, and using ones
        // from a removed device is invalid.
        void create_deferred_contexts(int num);

`CreateDeviceResources()` is `engine/render/device_resources.cpp:94-265` and never mentions a
deferred context. The rebuild is in `HandleDeviceLost`, `:464-469`:

            CreateDeviceResources();

            if (deferred_context_count_ > 0)
            {
                create_deferred_contexts(deferred_context_count_);
            }

**Why it matters:** `CreateDeviceResources()` is public (`:47`) and the shell calls it directly
(`application.cpp:62`). It replaces `m_d3dDevice` wholesale (`:262`), so a caller who follows this
comment and calls it on its own gets a new device while `deferred_contexts_owned_` still holds
contexts belonging to the old one — the precise state the second half of the same sentence says is
invalid. This is the path that produced seven of the previous review's critical findings, and the
header's own account of it is wrong. The comment is also silent on the constraint the engine
itself depends on: the pool must be rebuilt *before* `OnDeviceRestored()` fires, because
`Application::create_device_dependent_resources` constructs a `SpriteBatch` on each
`deferred_context(i)` (`application.cpp:160-167`).

**Remedy:** Change `CreateDeviceResources()` to `HandleDeviceLost()` in the comment, and add the
ordering constraint: the pool is rebuilt after the device and before `OnDeviceRestored`, so
notified owners always see a live pool.

#### Delete the codebase's only warning suppression

- **File:** `engine/render/device_resources.cpp:21-26`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Tests and toolchain

**What:** This file carries the only `#pragma warning(disable)` in first-party code, unscoped and
unexplained, against a promise of zero suppressions stated in three places. It is also inert.

**Evidence:**

        #ifdef __clang__
        #pragma clang diagnostic ignored "-Wcovered-switch-default"
        #pragma clang diagnostic ignored "-Wswitch-enum"
        #endif

        #pragma warning(disable : 4061)

**Why it matters:** `cmake/settings.cmake:11` sets `/WX` with the comment "warnings are errors,
zero suppressions", PHILOSOPHY/Tests and toolchain states "Warnings are errors with zero
suppressions", and `docs/review/IMPLEMENTED.md:101` records "`TreatWarningAsError` is on with zero
suppressions" as a completed remediation. `grep "pragma warning"` across `engine game samples
tests` returns this one line, so the claim is false by exactly one — which is the whole of the
defect, because C4061 is off by default and `settings.cmake` uses `/W4`, not `/Wall`, so the
pragma never fires. Were it ever to fire there is no `push`/`pop`, so it would silence the rest of
the translation unit. The `__clang__` block guards a compiler this build does not support.

**Remedy:** Delete both blocks. If a warning then appears, fix it, or state the reason in a
`push`/`pop`-scoped pragma on the line that needs it.

- **File:** `engine/render/device_resources.cpp:427-477`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** testing
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Tests and toolchain, PHILOSOPHY/Services and lifetimes

**What:** `HandleDeviceLost` is the most defect-dense path in this codebase's history and there is
still no test, no `tests/render` folder, and no supported way to trigger a device removal on
demand — so the remediation that landed is unverified by anything but reading.

**Evidence:**

        // Deferred contexts belong to the device that created them. They must go
        // with it, and be rebuilt below, or the renderer would keep recording into

        deferred_contexts_owned_.clear();

**Why it matters:** Seven of the previous review's critical findings (#3, #5, #6, #7, #8, #9 and
the `DeviceResources` items in `all-findings.md`) lived on this path, and the old finding's own
note said "this code has clearly never been run". The code reads correct now, and the comment at

actually load-bearing for the caller, that the rebuild must precede `OnDeviceRestored()` because

#### Stop exporting the whole Win32 and DXGI header surface to every game translation unit

- **File:** `engine/render/device_resources.h:7-12`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Tests and toolchain, ARCHITECTURE/Modules

**What:** This header includes `<Windows.h>`, `<d3d11_1.h>` and `<dxgi1_6.h>` and is re-exported
by the application shell, so every file in every game on this engine compiles the full Win32 and
DXGI surface whether or not it draws anything.

**Evidence:**

        #include <Windows.h>
        #include <wrl/client.h>
        #include <d3d11_1.h>
        #include <dxgi1_6.h>
        #include <memory>
        #include <vector>

`engine/app/application.h:9` re-exports it (`#include "engine/render/device_resources.h"`), and so
does `engine/render/viewport_manager.h:5` — the latter purely for a `DeviceResources*` member
(`viewport_manager.h:55`) that `viewport_manager.cpp` stores at `:11` and never reads again.

**Why it matters:** PHILOSOPHY/Tests and toolchain makes compile speed a maintained property and a
build-time regression a defect; every game TU pays for D3D11 and DXGI 1.6 to get at `Application`.
It is also what makes ARCHITECTURE/Modules' wall — "`render` … D3D11/DirectXTK inside `d3d11/`
only" — unenforceable, since the types arrive everywhere by include. Both are consequences of the
missing seam rather than independent defects, which is why this is low rather than higher.

*(The reviewer's `NOMINMAX` consequence does not survive: `cmake/settings.cmake:19` defines it on
`artattack_settings`, which `engine/CMakeLists.txt` links `PRIVATE` — but ARCHITECTURE/A game
project explicitly lists "the shared settings target — linked like everyone else's" in a project's
anatomy, and both `game/CMakeLists.txt` and `samples/minimal/CMakeLists.txt` do link it. A
consumer that omits it is not doing what the document describes.)*

**Remedy:** Once the renderer seam exists, `application.h` should include only the interface.
Before then, the cheap win is deleting the unused `DeviceResources*` member from `ViewportManager`
so at least the `render` module stops re-exporting the platform headers sideways.

#### Record the deferred-context count only after the contexts exist

- **File:** `engine/render/device_resources.cpp:740-759`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T2

**What:** `create_deferred_contexts` commits `deferred_context_count_` before creating anything, so
a mid-loop failure leaves the object claiming contexts it does not have — and that count is what
the next restore attempt uses.

**Evidence:**

        void DeviceResources::create_deferred_contexts(int num)
        {
            this->deferred_context_count_ = num;

            this->deferred_contexts_owned_.clear();
            this->deferred_contexts_ = std::make_unique<std::vector<ID3D11DeviceContext*>>();

            for (int i = 0; i < num; i++)
            {
                Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<ID3D11DeviceContext> deferred_context;
                HRESULT hr = m_d3dDevice->CreateDeferredContext(0,
                    deferred_context.GetAddressOf());
                if (FAILED(hr))
                {
                    throw std::runtime_error("Failed to create deferred context.");
                }

**Why it matters:** If `CreateDeferredContext` fails on iteration k, the throw leaves
`deferred_context_count_ == num` while `deferred_contexts_->size() == k`. From `initialize` the
exception reaches `wWinMain` and the process exits, which is the right outcome (T6). From
`HandleDeviceLost` (`:466-469`) it escapes *before* `OnDeviceRestored()`, so the `Application`
keeps its null `SpriteBatch`es and a `DeviceResources` that misreports its pool size. The same
review pass fixed exactly this shape in `RectangleRotated`'s setters — "validate the candidate
before committing" (`IMPLEMENTED.md:136-138`); this is its mirror. The count is also a second
source of truth for `deferred_contexts_->size()`.

**Remedy:** Build into a local vector and assign only after the loop completes, and derive the
count from `size()` rather than storing it — which the representation fix two findings up already
implies.

#### Delete the defaulted move operations on a type that publishes `this` to its owner

- **File:** `engine/render/device_resources.h:41-45`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** lifetime
- **Tenet:** T5, PHILOSOPHY/Services and lifetimes

**What:** `DeviceResources` is movable by default while holding a raw back-pointer to the object
that owns it and being pointed at by a second service, with no way to clear or re-point either.

**Evidence:**

        DeviceResources(DeviceResources&&) = default;
        DeviceResources& operator= (DeviceResources&&) = default;

        DeviceResources(DeviceResources const&) = delete;
        DeviceResources& operator= (DeviceResources const&) = delete;

with the invariant asserted in a comment rather than in code (`:137-138`):

        // The IDeviceNotify can be held directly as it owns the DeviceResources.
        IDeviceNotify*                                  m_deviceNotify;

**Why it matters:** The comment states an ownership invariant the move operations contradict: a
moved-from `DeviceResources` and its destination both point at the same `IDeviceNotify`, while the
notifier's `unique_ptr` owns only one of them. A move also strands a second back-pointer the
reviewer missed — `ViewportManager` stores a `DeviceResources*` (`application.cpp:144-145`,
`viewport_manager.h:55`) that would be left aimed at the husk. It is unreachable today
(`application.cpp:16-18` puts the object straight into a `unique_ptr` and never moves it, and
`Application` is non-copyable with a user-declared destructor so it has no implicit move), but
the previous review filed the mirror image of this on `Game`, and a defaulted declaration is what
keeps re-inviting it. `RegisterDeviceNotify` has no unregister either, so the pointer cannot be
nulled during teardown.

**Remedy:** `= delete` both move operations. The object is created once and never reseated, which
is what PHILOSOPHY/Services and lifetimes already says about services — T5 says make the compiler
hold that, not a comment.

#### Include what this file uses, and drop what it does not

- **File:** `engine/render/device_resources.cpp:6-17`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Files, PHILOSOPHY/Tests and toolchain

**What:** The translation unit uses `std::max`, `std::min`, `std::size` and
`sprintf_s`/`swprintf_s` without including `<algorithm>`, `<iterator>` or `<cstdio>` — and
includes `<DirectXMath.h>` and opens `using namespace DirectX;` for symbols it never names.

**Evidence:**

        #include "engine/render/device_resources.h"
        #include "engine/core/throw_if_failed.h"

        #include <DirectXMath.h>
        #include <stdexcept>
        #include <system_error>

        #ifdef _DEBUG
        #include <dxgidebug.h>
        #endif

        using namespace DirectX;

Used without a matching include at `:68` (`std::max(0l, std::min(ax2, bx2) …)`), `:172`, `:255`,
`:550` (`std::size(…)`), `:284-285` (`std::max<UINT>`), `:303`, `:513` (`sprintf_s`), `:592`,
`:619` (`swprintf_s`). In the other direction, `grep -n "XM\|DirectX::"` over the whole file
returns exactly one line — the `#include <DirectXMath.h>` itself. Nothing in the file names a
`DirectX::` symbol; `CD3D11_TEXTURE2D_DESC` and `CD3D11_RENDER_TARGET_VIEW_DESC` are global,
from `<d3d11.h>`.

**Why it matters:** It compiles only because `<vector>` reaches MSVC's `<xutility>` and `<cstdio>`
arrives transitively through `engine/core/throw_if_failed.h:4`. CONVENTIONS/Files makes include
discipline a rule and PHILOSOPHY makes compile time a maintained property; a transitive include is
the first thing to break on the second toolchain this file is meant to be portable to, and it
fails inside a standard header rather than here. The unused `using namespace DirectX;` at file
scope is the same problem pointed the other way — it widens name lookup across 760 lines for
nothing.

**Remedy:** Add `<algorithm>`, `<iterator>` and `<cstdio>`; delete `<DirectXMath.h>` and the
`using namespace DirectX;`.

#### The one throw this file authored discards the value that would name the failure

- **File:** `engine/render/device_resources.cpp:752-773`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** diagnostics
- **Tenet:** T6
- **Origin:** added-by-verifier

**What:** Both throws in the engine-authored part of this file report that something failed
without reporting *what* — the `HRESULT` in one case, the index and the pool size in the other —
even though `ThrowIfFailed`, which carries the code, is already included in this translation unit.

**Evidence:**

`engine/render/device_resources.cpp:750-755`:

                HRESULT hr = m_d3dDevice->CreateDeferredContext(0,
                    deferred_context.GetAddressOf());
                if (FAILED(hr))
                {
                    throw std::runtime_error("Failed to create deferred context.");
                }

`engine/render/device_resources.cpp:766-775`:

        ID3D11DeviceContext*
        DeviceResources::deferred_context(int index) const
        {
            if (this->deferred_contexts_ == nullptr ||
                index < 0 ||
                static_cast<size_t>(index) >= this->deferred_contexts_->size())
            {
                throw std::out_of_range("Invalid index.");
            }

**Why it matters:** T6 is "it says so immediately, with names and paths", and PHILOSOPHY calls
quiet failure "doubly so" expensive "for a user who didn't write the engine". `hr` is in scope one
line above the first throw and is dropped; the whole engine calls `ThrowIfFailed` (`:7`) for
exactly this. `"Invalid index."` is thrown on the frame path a game hits via
`deferred_context(worker)`, and it cannot distinguish the three cases it covers — pool never
created, negative index, index past the end — which are three different bugs in the caller. The
first is what a game hits when it draws before the shell created the pool; the message tells it
nothing.

**Remedy:** `ThrowIfFailed(hr)` for the first, and for the second a message carrying the index and
the current pool size, distinguishing the not-yet-created case from an out-of-range one.

#### A brace-less `if` whose statement is on the far side of an `#endif`

- **File:** `engine/render/device_resources.cpp:530-560`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** clarity
- **Tenet:** T4, T12
- **Origin:** added-by-verifier

**What:** `CreateFactory` ends with an `if` that has no braces and whose controlled statement is
separated from it by a preprocessor directive and a blank line, so the control flow of the
function depends on which build you are reading it in.

**Evidence:**

`engine/render/device_resources.cpp:532-560`, abridged to the shape:

        #if defined(_DEBUG) && (_WIN32_WINNT >= 0x0603 /*_WIN32_WINNT_WINBLUE*/) && !defined(__MINGW32__)
                bool debugDXGI = false;
                { ... }

                if (!debugDXGI)
        #endif

                ThrowIfFailed(CreateDXGIFactory1(IID_PPV_ARGS(m_dxgiFactory.ReleaseAndGetAddressOf())));
            }

**Why it matters:** In a release build the `if` does not exist and the `ThrowIfFailed` runs
unconditionally; in a debug build it is guarded by a condition three lines and one directive
away, at an indentation that gives no hint it is a controlled statement. T12's line is that the
preprocessor may not "hide control flow", and this is the textbook instance: adding a second
statement after the `ThrowIfFailed` — the most natural edit in the world here — silently changes
what runs in debug builds only, with no warning, because `/W4` has nothing to say about it. This
is inherited template code, which is exactly the argument of the conventions finding above: the
file is being maintained as ours while still being read as theirs.

**Remedy:** Give the `if` braces around the `ThrowIfFailed`, moving the `#endif` after the closing
brace — or restructure so the fallback path is written once outside any `#if`.

  says "only seven", which is also wrong. `GetWindow` and `GetRenderTarget` have zero external
  callers, not one each: their greps matched `GetWindowLongPtr` and `GetRenderTargetView`.
- **"`ls engine/render` returns forty files"** — corrected to 38.
- **"`m_backBufferCount` and `deferred_context_count_` are eleven lines apart"** — corrected; they
  are 22 lines apart (`:123` and `:145`). The nearer pair is `m_deviceNotify:138` /
  `deferred_context_count_:145`.
- **Finding 9's `NOMINMAX` consequence** — rejected. "Link `ArtAttackEngine` and nothing else" is
  not what ARCHITECTURE describes: its *A game project* section lists "the shared settings target
  — linked like everyone else's" as part of a project's anatomy, and both existing clients link
  it. The finding survives at low severity on the compile-cost and module-wall observations only.
- **Finding 8's "the ordering is unstated"** — rejected as written. `cpp:442-444` states why the
  contexts are destroyed and rebuilt. Only the `before OnDeviceRestored` half is undocumented; the
  finding is re-graded to low and narrowed to that plus the missing harness.
- **Finding 6's severity** — re-graded medium → low. The observation (the only suppression in the
  tree, against a promise recorded three times) is correct and kept; the consequence is nil,
  because C4061 is off by default and the build uses `/W4`, not `/Wall`, so the pragma can never
  fire.
- **Absence of `[[nodiscard]]` on this class** — considered as an addition and not filed: `grep`
  returns zero `[[nodiscard]]` in any engine header, so it is a codebase-wide gap, not this
  group's.
- **`m_options(flags | c_FlipPresent)` forcing a flag no caller can clear** (`cpp:88`,
  `header:38`) — considered and not filed. Real, but inherited from the template, unexercised (the
  only construction site passes two arguments), and dissolved by the renderer seam.

<a id="g-render-primitives"></a>

## render-primitives — Draw objects, drawer, visual, textures

*Group `render-primitives` · 17 findings (2 high, 8 medium, 7 low) · source `review2/verified/render-primitives.md`, verified report.*

I re-opened every cited line in all twelve group files and in every file the reviewer reached
outward into: `render_resources.h`, `sprite_sheet.{h,cpp}`, `animation_object.{h,cpp}`,
`text_object.h`, `text.cpp`, `engine/ui/widget.{h,cpp}`, `engine/core/i_game_object.h`,
`engine/core/registry.h`, `engine/CMakeLists.txt`, `samples/minimal/states/hello_state.cpp`,
`game/objects/{weapon,paint_tile,structure_paintable,level,level_object_builder,camera_tools}`,
the three level JSONs, `game/content/textures/sprite_sheet_1.json`, and the vendored DirectXTK
`SpriteBatch.cpp` in `out/build/x64-debug/vcpkg_installed/…/Src/SpriteBatch.cpp`. Every line
number checked out except one (`visual.h:16` for the `color` parameter — it is line 17), which I
corrected. The DirectXTK origin semantics, the 4×4 `nozzle` frame against a 5.0 `NOZZLE_SIZE`, the
72×32 `sprayer` against a 70×30 `size`, the 17 game headers carrying `DirectX::SpriteEffects`, and
the zero-caller status of `calculate_draw_rectangle` / `set_render_resources` all hold exactly as
written.

I threw out one finding and corrected the consequence on five. **Rejected:** the "no tests, and
cannot be given any" finding — it is the consequence half of findings 1 and 2, both of which
already cite `tests/` having no render folder as their own evidence; its remedy is verbatim theirs.
The non-duplicated fragment (the pure helpers are `protected`, so even a test written today cannot
reach them) is folded into the `Drawer` finding. **Corrected consequences:** (a) the "entire
drawing API is protected" claim is false for `TextObject` — `draw` and `draw_with` are public there,
which is how `samples/minimal` draws text without inheriting; it is *sprite* drawing that is
protected end to end, and I narrowed the finding to that. (b) the proposed `using
DrawObject::set_colour;` remedy does not work for `MTexture`, `MText` and `MTextDropShadow`: those
three implement `MWidget::set_colour`, a *pure virtual on an unrelated base*, and a using-declaration
cannot override it — so three of the five forwarding bodies are load-bearing, and only two are pure
re-exports. (c) `Weapon`'s duplicate `render_resources_` cannot "drift": neither copy has a setter,
so it is redundant state, not a synchronisation hazard. (d) the paint-tile gap numbers were computed
against a scale the game never reaches — the zoom-out camera runs 1.0 → 0.5 at 1920×1080 and
0.667 → 0.333 at 1280×720, so the resting overview loss is 25%, not 37%, and tiles are 4×12, not
4×4; the defect survives, the arithmetic is restated. (e) `no_rotation` is used by *five* of six
projectile definitions, not four — and `rotat_origin` is read by nothing anywhere, so the
"silently swallowed" branch is unreachable rather than live.

I re-graded one finding down: the `const`-stops-at-the-object hole is real and is the most valuable
item after the two structural highs, but it is an enforcement gap with no live defect and a
mechanical remedy, so it sits at the top of medium rather than in high.

**Four findings added.** The largest is a live wrong-picture bug the reviewer walked past twice:
`Visual`'s `RectangleRotated` constructor calls `rectangle_rotated_to_axis()`, which returns the
*unrotated* rectangle, and never applies the angle — and
`DrawObject::set_draw_rotation_by_rectangle_rotated`, the function that exists to do exactly that,
is an empty `// TODO` body. The reviewer read both files and quoted neither. I also added the
`frame_handle` cross-sheet contract hole in `draw_with`, the copyable-polymorphic-base problem on
`DrawObject`, and the fact that four of this group's six public headers carry no documentation at
all while the two the recent passes touched carry excellent documentation.

### Themes

- The renderer seam PHILOSOPHY specifies is absent, so DirectXTK types are the engine's public
  vocabulary rather than one backend behind an interface, and `engine/render/d3d11/` does not exist.
- Sprite drawing is delivered exclusively as `protected` members of a base class, which forces the
  one modelling grammar — a class per entity — that PHILOSOPHY's object model says the engine must
  not impose.
- `const` was applied to the objects but not to what they hand out, so the mechanism that makes
  parallel rendering sound stops exactly where the shared state begins.
- Virtual dispatch is the default idiom rather than a last resort (T11): twenty-one virtuals across
  the sprite chain, six virtual calls per sprite, and exactly two overrides in the whole codebase
  that could be deleted outright and three that only exist to bridge two unrelated bases.
- Contracts are asserted in comments and contradicted by the code beside them: `draw_with` "reads no
  per-draw members" then reads one; `default: // top_left` names the wrong enumerator; the origin
  parameter's units are unstated and both call sites get them wrong.
- Declared-but-never-implemented paths ship as public API: an empty rotation setter, a constructor
  that silently drops its rotation, and a base class whose entire helper surface has zero callers.
- Precision is discarded at the last step of every draw — the camera transform is computed in float
  and truncated toward zero — which is visible as stripes through the paint surface whenever the
  camera scale is not a clean fraction.

#### Give the engine the `draw_sprite` seam; DirectXTK is currently the render module's public API

- **File:** `engine/render/draw_object.h:3-31`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** boundary
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Simulation and rendering, ARCHITECTURE/Modules, T5

**What:** There is no renderer interface and no `engine/render/d3d11/`; `DirectX::SpriteEffects` and
`DirectX::SpriteBatch*` sit in the signature of every drawable the engine offers, so the platform
edge *is* the API rather than one implementation behind it.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/draw_object.h:3-4, 13-18, 25
    #include "engine/math/colour.h"
    #include "engine/render/render_resources.h"      // -> <d3d11_1.h>, SpriteFont.h, SpriteBatch.h
    ...
            DrawObject(RenderResources* render_resources,
                    const mattmath::Colour& color = colour_consts::WHITE,
                    float rotation = 0.0f,
                    const mattmath::Vector2F& origin = mattmath::Vector2F::ZERO,
                    DirectX::SpriteEffects effects = DirectX::SpriteEffects_None,
                    float layer_depth = 0.0f);
    ...
            virtual DirectX::SpriteEffects effects() const;

    // engine/CMakeLists.txt:50-53
    target_link_libraries(ArtAttackEngine
        PUBLIC MattMath Microsoft::DirectXTK d3d11 dxgi dxguid
        PRIVATE artattack_settings
    )

    $ ls engine/render/          # verified: no d3d11/ subfolder
    animation_object.cpp ... draw_object.h  drawer.h ... visual.h

**Why it matters:** ARCHITECTURE:113-116 says platform-specific code "lives only in the backend
subfolders (`render/d3d11/`, `input/xinput/`), behind engine-owned interfaces". None of it does, and
the cost is already paid in three places. (1) `DirectX::SpriteEffects` appears in **17** game headers
— verified by grep over `game/**/*.h`: every `projectile_*`, every `weapon_*`, `player.h`,
`structure.h`, `structure_paintable.h`, `paint_tile.h` and both builders — because each constructor
forwards it down to `DrawObject`. (2) `tests/` contains `assets`, `core` and `math` and no `render`,
and cannot have one: every sprite entry point takes a live `DirectX::SpriteBatch*`. (3)
`samples/minimal` — the file ARCHITECTURE:176 says a new project copies, and which the C++ series has
to be able to teach — does raw D3D11 command-list plumbing inside a state's `draw()`:

    // samples/minimal/states/hello_state.cpp:68-84
    artattack::DeviceResources* device = this->app_->device_resources();
    ID3D11DeviceContext* deferred = device->deferred_context(0);
    SpriteBatch* sprite_batch = this->app_->sprite_batches()->at(0);

    sprite_batch->Begin(SpriteSortMode_Deferred);
    this->greeting_->draw(sprite_batch);
    this->hint_->draw(sprite_batch);
    sprite_batch->End();

    ID3D11CommandList* commands = nullptr;
    if (FAILED(deferred->FinishCommandList(FALSE, &commands)))
    {
            throw std::runtime_error("HelloState::draw - FinishCommandList failed");
    }

    device->GetD3DDeviceContext()->ExecuteCommandList(commands, FALSE);
    commands->Release();

**Remedy:** Introduce the `Renderer` interface PHILOSOPHY names
(`draw_sprite(texture, src, dst, tint, rotation, origin, depth)`), have `DrawObject` and everything
under it take a `Renderer&` instead of a `SpriteBatch*`, and put `SpriteEffects` behind an
engine-owned `SpriteFlip` enum. The DirectXTK implementation then moves to `engine/render/d3d11/`
and `Microsoft::DirectXTK` becomes a `PRIVATE` link.

#### Sprite drawing is entirely `protected`, so putting a sprite on screen requires inheriting a four-deep chain

- **File:** `engine/render/texture_object.h:26-72`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T11, T1, PHILOSOPHY/The object model

**What:** Every route to drawing a sprite through this module is a `protected` member of a base
class, so the engine's sprite primitives are usable only by deriving from them — the one modelling
grammar PHILOSOPHY says the engine must not impose.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/texture_object.h:13-16, 26-27, 42-43, 65-72
    class TextureObject : public SpriteSheetObject
    {
    public:
            TextureObject() = default;
            TextureObject(...);            // <- the entire public surface

    protected:
            SpriteSheet::frame_handle frame() const;
            ...
            virtual void draw(DirectX::SpriteBatch* sprite_batch,
                    const mattmath::RectangleI& destination_rectangle) const;
            ... (five draw overloads) ...
            void draw_with(DirectX::SpriteBatch* sprite_batch,
                    const mattmath::RectangleF& destination_rectangle,
                    const mattmath::Camera& camera,
                    SpriteSheet::frame_handle frame,
                    ...) const;
    };

`draw_object.h:20`, `sprite_sheet_object.h:30` and `animation_object.h:25` are the same: `protected:`
covers everything but the constructors. (Text is the exception and the counter-proof —
`text_object.h:29-41` puts `draw` and `draw_with` in `public:`, which is exactly why
`samples/minimal` can draw a string with `this->greeting_->draw(sprite_batch)` without inheriting
anything.)

**Why it matters:** PHILOSOPHY/The object model states "The engine imposes no modelling grammar…
what stands behind an interface is the game's business: a class hierarchy, a plain struct, or a
batch", and "A paint-tile grid is one `GameObject`, not ten thousand. Interface granularity is the
user's performance dial." That dial does not exist for sprites. The game shows the consequence:
`structure_paintable.h:59` holds `std::vector<PaintTile> paint_tiles_`, and each `PaintTile`
(`paint_tile.h:55`) is a full `TextureObject` carrying its own `RenderResources*`, `Colour`,
`Vector2F` origin, `SpriteEffects`, `layer_depth`, `frame_handle`, `SpriteSheetHandle` and an entire
`PaintTileSplash` (itself an `AnimationObject` with five more members) — because being one is the
only way to reach `draw_with`. A user who wants the batch shape has to bypass this module and call
`SpriteSheet::draw` through `RenderResources::sprite_sheet(handle)`, which is public
(`render_resources.h:62`, `sprite_sheet.h:48-88`) but is documented nowhere as a supported path.

**Remedy:** Make sprite drawing a free function or small value type over
`(Renderer&, SpriteSheet&, frame_handle, dst, tint, …)` that anything can call, and let
`TextureObject` become one convenience client of it rather than the only door.

#### `const` stops at the object: a const `draw()` still hands out mutable shared state

- **File:** `engine/render/draw_object.cpp:23-26`, `engine/render/sprite_sheet_object.cpp:22-25`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** threading
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Simulation and rendering, T2

**What:** Both accessors return non-`const` pointers from `const` member functions, so every `const`
`draw()` in the tree can reach the mutating API of the two objects that really are shared between
render workers.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/draw_object.cpp:23-26
    RenderResources* DrawObject::render_resources() const
    {
            return this->render_resources_;
    }

    // engine/render/sprite_sheet_object.cpp:22-25
    SpriteSheet* SpriteSheetObject::sprite_sheet() const
    {
            return this->render_resources()->sprite_sheet(this->sheet_);
    }

Both are reached from `TextureObject::draw(...) const` (texture_object.cpp:45, 64, 101) and
`AnimationObject::draw(...) const` (animation_object.cpp:33, 52, 87). Both targets carry public
non-const mutators: `SpriteSheet::set_texture` (sprite_sheet.h:43), and
`RenderResources::add_texture` / `add_sprite_font` / `add_sprite_sheet` / `reset_all_sprite_fonts` /
`reset_all_textures` (render_resources.h:71-84).

**Why it matters:** `i_game_object.h:10-15` states the contract this was bought to install — "draw()
is const, and that is the whole contract that makes parallel rendering sound… const is how the
compiler holds a new object to it instead of a comment nobody reads." That guarantee covers the
drawable's own members and stops there. A `PaintTile::draw` running on four render workers can
legally call `this->sprite_sheet()->set_texture(...)` or
`this->render_resources()->reset_all_textures()` and the compiler will not object — and those two are
precisely the objects *every* worker shares, unlike the per-object members `const` does protect.
Nothing exploits it today: the only callers of those mutators are `resource_loader.cpp:121,150,160`
and `application.cpp:376-377`, all load-time or device-restore. This is a hole in the enforcement,
not a live race — but it is the hole in exactly the mechanism IMPLEMENTED.md #16 records as the
reason the fix "survives someone editing the code".

**Remedy:** Return `const RenderResources*` and `const SpriteSheet*` from the `const` accessors, and
split off non-const overloads for the load-time callers that genuinely mutate. Note this reaches one
level further: `RenderResources::sprite_sheet(handle) const` also returns a mutable `SpriteSheet*`
and needs the same split.
