#### Twenty-one virtuals across the sprite chain, and not one override that changes behaviour

- **File:** `engine/render/draw_object.h:21-32`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T11, T8

**What:** All six accessors and all five setters on the render root are `virtual`, as are all five
`draw` overloads on `TextureObject` and all five on `AnimationObject`. Across the whole codebase
there are exactly two overrides that could be deleted outright, three that exist only to bridge two
unrelated bases, and none that changes what the base does — while `TextureObject::draw` pays six
virtual calls per sprite to read six fields.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/draw_object.h:20-32
    protected:
            virtual RenderResources* render_resources() const;
            virtual const mattmath::Colour& colour() const;
            virtual float draw_rotation() const;
            virtual const mattmath::Vector2F& origin() const;
            virtual DirectX::SpriteEffects effects() const;
            virtual float layer_depth() const;

            virtual void set_colour(const mattmath::Colour& colour);
            virtual void set_draw_rotation(float rotation);
            virtual void set_origin(const mattmath::Vector2F& origin);
            virtual void set_effects(DirectX::SpriteEffects effects);
            virtual void set_layer_depth(float layer_depth);

Grepping `*.h` for an `override` on any of these names across the entire repository returns exactly
one line — `game/objects/weapon.h:141` — plus the five `set_colour` bodies:

    engine/ui/widget.cpp:177-180   MTexture::set_colour        -> SpriteSheetObject::set_colour(colour);
    engine/ui/widget.cpp:270-273   MText::set_colour           -> Text::set_colour(colour);
    engine/ui/widget.cpp:331-334   MTextDropShadow::set_colour -> TextDropShadow::set_colour(colour);
    engine/render/text.cpp:27-30   Text::set_colour            -> TextObject::set_colour(colour);
    game/objects/paint_tile.cpp:160-163  PaintTileSplash::set_colour -> AnimationObject::set_colour(colour);

    // game/objects/weapon.h:141, weapon.h:149, weapon.cpp:518-521
    artattack::RenderResources* render_resources() const override;
    artattack::RenderResources* render_resources_ = nullptr;
    RenderResources* Weapon::render_resources() const { return this->render_resources_; }

The ten virtual `draw` overloads (texture_object.h:42-54, animation_object.h:42-54) have **zero**
overriders anywhere — grep for `override` across `game/**/*.h` finds only `IGameObject::draw`
implementations, which are a different signature.

**Why it matters:** Nine of the eleven `DrawObject` virtuals and all ten virtual `draw` overloads are
paying for dispatch nothing uses. The cost is per sprite: `TextureObject::draw`
(texture_object.cpp:42-55) makes six virtual calls — `render_resources()` via `sprite_sheet()`, then
`colour()`, `draw_rotation()`, `origin()`, `effects()`, `layer_depth()` — each returning a member,
once per sprite per view per frame, over a paint grid whose tiles are 4 world units on their long
axis (`paint_tile_consts::WIDTH = 4.0f`, paint_tile.h:11). T11 names virtual dispatch a tool of last
resort; this is it used as the default for field access, and T8 says indirection must pay for itself.
Separately, `Weapon` now holds two `RenderResources*` members with the same value
(`weapon.cpp:22-25` sets both from the same argument) purely because the base accessor was virtual
and the derived one had the same name — redundant state, not a drift hazard, since neither has a
setter.

*Correction to the reviewer's remedy:* only two of the five `set_colour` bodies are pure re-exports.
`MTexture`, `MText` and `MTextDropShadow` implement `MWidget::set_colour`, which is a **pure virtual
on an unrelated base** (widget.h:73), and a `using DrawObject::set_colour;` declaration cannot
override it — those three classes would stay abstract. Only `Text::set_colour` (text.cpp:27) and
`PaintTileSplash::set_colour` (paint_tile.cpp:160) are access-level changes a `using` would cover.

**Remedy:** Drop `virtual` from the nine accessors/setters that nothing overrides and from all ten
`draw` overloads; keep `set_colour` virtual (or, better, have the widget bridge call the base
non-virtually). Replace `Text::set_colour` and `PaintTileSplash::set_colour` with `using`
declarations, and delete `Weapon::render_resources_` and its override.

#### `draw_with` documents itself as reading no per-draw members, then reads `layer_depth()`

- **File:** `engine/render/texture_object.h:56-58`, `engine/render/texture_object.cpp:92-111`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** docs
- **Tenet:** T4, PHILOSOPHY/Simulation and rendering

**What:** The one function built so callers can pass every per-draw value as a local still reads
`layer_depth` off the shared object, and its own comment says it does not.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/texture_object.h:56-58
    // Draws without reading any of the per-draw members, so callers can compute
    // frame / colour / origin / effects / rotation into locals instead of
    // assigning them to this object first.

    // engine/render/texture_object.cpp:101-110
    SpriteSheet* sprite_sheet = SpriteSheetObject::sprite_sheet();

    sprite_sheet->draw(sprite_batch,
            frame,
            camera.calculate_view_rectangle(destination_rectangle).rectangle_i(),
            colour,
            rotation,
            origin,
            effects,
            this->layer_depth());     // <- a per-draw member, read from the object

**Why it matters:** The comment is the contract a reader will trust when adding the next per-draw
value, and it is false for one of the seven arguments `SpriteSheet::draw` takes. Depth is the one
sprite attribute that legitimately differs per view — the same divider or HUD element drawn into two
viewports at different sort depths cannot be expressed through `draw_with` at all — so the next
person needing it does the thing the comment forbids and assigns the member first, on an object every
render worker is inside. `AnimationObject::draw_with` (animation_object.cpp:81-97) has a wider gap
still: it reads `draw_rotation()`, `origin()` *and* `layer_depth()` off the object, taking only
`colour` and `effects` as parameters. Its comment (animation_object.h:56-57) is at least honest about
that — it claims only colour and effects — so the defect there is capability, not a false contract.

**Remedy:** Add `float layer_depth` to `TextureObject::draw_with`'s parameter list so the signature
matches the comment, and add `rotation`, `origin` and `layer_depth` to `AnimationObject::draw_with`.

#### Every destination rectangle is truncated to `int`, which stripes the paint surface during the zoom-out

- **File:** `engine/render/texture_object.cpp:56-60`, `:76-82`, `:103-106`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T2, T3

**What:** The camera transform is computed in float and then discarded to integers with
truncation-toward-zero, so at any camera scale that is not a clean fraction a sprite's drawn width
shrinks faster than the spacing to its neighbour.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/texture_object.cpp:56-60
    void TextureObject::draw(SpriteBatch* sprite_batch,
            const RectangleF& destination_rectangle)const
    {
            this->draw(sprite_batch, destination_rectangle.rectangle_i());
    }

    // engine/render/texture_object.cpp:103-106 (draw_with)
            camera.calculate_view_rectangle(destination_rectangle).rectangle_i(),

    // engine/math/matt_math.cpp:808-814
    RectangleI RectangleF::rectangle_i() const
    {
            return RectangleI(static_cast<int>(this->x),
                    static_cast<int>(this->y),
                    static_cast<int>(this->width),
                    static_cast<int>(this->height));
    }

`AnimationObject::draw` (animation_object.cpp:47) and `AnimationObject::draw_with` (:91) do the same.

**Why it matters:** `PaintTile::draw` (paint_tile.cpp:51-53) goes through `draw_with`, and paint
tiles are generated 4 world units along the edge they lie on (`paint_tile_consts::WIDTH = 4.0f`,
paint_tile.h:11; `structure_paintable.cpp:96-105` divides the face by it). `Level::update`
(level.cpp:151-160) builds `zoom_out_camera_` by lerping between two cameras whose scale is
`resolution.width / bounds.width` — the three shipped levels all set
`zoom_out_start_bounds.width = 1920` and `zoom_out_finish_bounds.width = 3840`, so at 1920×1080 the
scale runs 1.0 → 0.5 and at 1280×720 (the fallback resolution, resolution_manager.cpp:120) it runs
0.667 → 0.333. At the 1280×720 resting overview scale of 1/3 a tile is drawn `trunc(4/3) = 1` pixel
wide while the next tile's left edge advances 1.333 px, so **25% of the painted surface disappears as
a regular stripe pattern** on the end-of-match screen that shows who won; intermediate scales during
the transition (e.g. 0.7 → `trunc(2.8) = 2` against 2.8 px spacing) lose nearly 30% and the pattern
crawls as the scale changes. The gameplay camera holds scale 1.0 (`camera_tools.cpp:40` copies it
from `prev_camera` and never touches it), which is why this is invisible in play and only shows up on
the results screen — the one frame a player looks at hardest.

**Remedy:** Draw through DirectXTK's float-destination form (position + scale, which
`SpriteSheet::draw` already exposes at sprite_sheet.h:48-57) instead of converting to `RectangleI`;
or at minimum round rather than truncate and derive the width from the difference of two rounded
edges, so adjacent tiles share an edge by construction.

#### `Drawer` is dead engine API built on a camera model the engine replaced

- **File:** `engine/render/drawer.h:14-31`, `engine/render/drawer.cpp:13-43`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T4, PHILOSOPHY/Services and lifetimes, PHILOSOPHY/The public face

**What:** All three of `Drawer`'s protected helpers and its one public method have zero callers
anywhere in the repository; two of the helpers present a `Vector3F` x/y/zoom camera that
`mattmath::Camera` superseded, and the public method reseats a service. The class survives only as a
place for two game types to keep one pointer.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/drawer.h:3, 13-31
    #include "SpriteBatch.h"                     // <- nothing in this header uses SpriteBatch
    ...
            explicit Drawer(RenderResources* render_resources);
            void set_render_resources(RenderResources* render_resources);
    protected:
            RenderResources* render_resources() const;
            mattmath::RectangleI calculate_draw_rectangle(
                    const mattmath::RectangleI& rec,
                    const mattmath::Vector3F& camera) const;
            mattmath::RectangleI calculate_draw_rectangle(
                    const mattmath::Vector2F& position,
                    const mattmath::Vector2F& size,
                    const mattmath::Vector3F& camera) const;
            mattmath::Vector2F calculate_sprite_origin(
                    const mattmath::Vector2F& size,
                    RotationOrigin origin) const;

Grep over every `.h`/`.cpp` in the repo for `calculate_draw_rectangle`, `set_render_resources` and
`calculate_sprite_origin` returns hits in `drawer.{h,cpp}` and — for `calculate_sprite_origin` only —
in `game/objects/weapon.{h,cpp}`, where it is a **separate `static` duplicate**
(weapon.h:127-128, weapon.cpp:93-106) that `Weapon` had to write because it derives from
`TextureObject`, not `Drawer`. So `Drawer::calculate_sprite_origin` is dead too: the reviewer called
it "the one live helper", and it is not. All three are unreachable.

`Drawer`'s only subclasses are `DebugText` (debug_text.h:20) and `InterfaceGameplay`
(interface_gameplay.h:46). Neither calls any helper; both use the base solely for
`render_resources()` (debug_text.cpp:106, interface_gameplay.cpp:75, 119, 156, 186) — they inherit a
class in order to store one pointer.

**Why it matters:** This is shipped engine surface a stranger reads first (PHILOSOPHY/The public
face). It presents a second, obsolete camera concept — `Vector3F` as x/y/zoom — beside
`mattmath::Camera` in the same folder, and it presents `set_render_resources`, a public reseat of a
service, against PHILOSOPHY/Services and lifetimes' "Services are created once, at initialisation,
and never reseated", with no caller to justify it. Delivering a pure function as a `protected` member
of a base class is what forced the duplication in `Weapon`, and the two copies have already diverged
in shape (Drawer's folds `top_left` into `default:`; Weapon's lists it). The `protected:` at
drawer.h:15 also means the two genuinely pure, device-free functions in this module cannot be reached
by a test even today, before any renderer seam exists — a fixture subclass would be required just to
call arithmetic. The header additionally includes `"SpriteBatch.h"` and never uses it, against
PHILOSOPHY/Tests and toolchain's "light headers, disciplined includes". And the name sits one letter
from `DrawObject`, an unrelated class in the same folder with a similar member.

**Remedy:** Delete `Drawer`. `DebugText` and `InterfaceGameplay` can hold a `RenderResources*` member
as they already hold their handles. Move `calculate_sprite_origin` to a free function in
`engine/render/` that `Weapon` and any future caller can call without inheriting — which also makes
it testable today — and delete the `Vector3F`-camera overloads outright.

#### `calculate_sprite_origin` does not say which size it wants, and the live copy is fed the wrong one

- **File:** `engine/render/drawer.cpp:45-57`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T4, PHILOSOPHY/The public face

**What:** DirectXTK interprets `origin` in *source-texture* texels, but this helper's parameter is
undocumented and its game-side copy is fed the *destination* size, so the rotation pivot is off by
the ratio of the two.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/drawer.cpp:45-57
    Vector2F Drawer::calculate_sprite_origin(
        const Vector2F& size, RotationOrigin origin) const
    {
        switch (origin)
        {
        case RotationOrigin::center:
            return Vector2F(size) / 2.0f;
        case RotationOrigin::left_center:
            return { 0.0f, size.y / 2.0f };
        default: // RotationOrigin::top_left
            return Vector2F::ZERO;
        }
    }

    // vcpkg DirectXTK Src/SpriteBatch.cpp:836-843 (verified in the build tree)
    XMVECTOR sourceSize = XMVectorSwizzle<2, 3, 2, 3>(source);
    XMVECTOR destinationSize = XMVectorSwizzle<2, 3, 2, 3>(destination);
    const XMVECTOR isZeroMask = XMVectorEqual(sourceSize, XMVectorZero());
    const XMVECTOR nonZeroSourceSize = XMVectorSelect(sourceSize, g_XMEpsilon, isZeroMask);
    XMVECTOR origin = XMVectorDivide(originRotationDepth, nonZeroSourceSize);

    // game/objects/weapon.cpp:48-49 and :80-81 (the copy, both called with destination sizes)
    Vector2F origin = this->calculate_sprite_origin(
        this->details().size, RotationOrigin::left_center);
    ...
        Vector2F origin_noz = this->calculate_sprite_origin(
            this->nozzle_size(), RotationOrigin::center);

**Why it matters:** `origin` is divided by the *source rectangle's* size and the resulting fraction is
applied to the destination quad, so "centre" requires `sourceSize / 2`. Verified against the content:
`weapon_consts::NOZZLE_SIZE` is `{5.0f, 5.0f}` (weapon_consts.h:11) while the `"nozzle"` frame in
`game/content/textures/sprite_sheet_1.json` is 4×4 texels, so the pivot lands at 2.5/4 = **62.5%** of
the sprite instead of 50%. `DETAILS_SPRAYER.size` is `{70, 30}` (weapon_consts.h:42) against a 72×32
`"sprayer"` frame, so `RotationOrigin::left_center` puts the weapon's rotation pivot at 15/32 =
**46.9%** of its height. Neither is catastrophic on its own — one is debug-only, the other is a
one-pixel-class offset — but the engine helper has no comment saying which size it means, so both
mistakes were invited rather than caught, and every future caller will make the same one.

**Remedy:** Rename the parameter `source_size` and document that it is the frame's texel size; better,
take the `SpriteFrame` (or `frame_handle` plus the sheet) and read the size out of it so a caller
cannot pass the wrong thing.

#### The default constructors build drawables that can never be made valid, and whose first draw is UB

- **File:** `engine/render/draw_object.h:12,37`, `engine/render/sprite_sheet_object.h:22`, `engine/render/texture_object.h:16`, `engine/render/visual.h:12`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T5, T6

**What:** Every type in the chain is default-constructible into a state with `render_resources_ ==
nullptr` and an unresolved element handle; there is no setter for `render_resources_`, so the state
is unrepairable, and the first `draw()` calls a member function through the null pointer.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/draw_object.h:12, 36-37
    DrawObject() = default;
    ...
    private:
            RenderResources* render_resources_ = nullptr;      // no setter anywhere

    // engine/render/sprite_sheet_object.cpp:22-25 — unconditional deref
    SpriteSheet* SpriteSheetObject::sprite_sheet() const
    {
            return this->render_resources()->sprite_sheet(this->sheet_);
    }

Path, verified end to end: `Visual v;` → `v.draw(batch, cam)` (visual.cpp:43-46) →
`TextureObject::draw(batch, rect, camera)` (texture_object.cpp:76-82) → `draw(batch, rect_i)`
(texture_object.cpp:42-45) → `SpriteSheetObject::sprite_sheet()` → `nullptr->sprite_sheet(sheet_)`.
The *constructors* have the same hole one step earlier: `sprite_sheet_object.cpp:17` calls
`render_resources->resolve_sprite_sheet(sheet_name)` in the mem-initialiser list with no null check,
so passing a null `RenderResources*` to any constructor in this group is UB at construction.

**Why it matters:** `Registry::get` is carefully written to throw naming the resource rather than
return null (registry.h:98-115, and the header comment says so), but that safety net is one hop too
far out — the null `RenderResources*` is dereferenced before the registry is ever reached, so the
failure is undefined behaviour rather than the named error T6 promises. Worse, `render_resources_` is
`private` with no setter, so a default-constructed `DrawObject` can *never* be brought to a usable
state: the only legal thing to do with one is assign a fully-constructed object over it. That is
exactly what the game does — `PaintTile`'s constructor assigns over its default-constructed `splash_`
(paint_tile.cpp:24-26) — which means these constructors exist purely to let derived classes write
`= default`, and the pattern is spreading (`PaintTile() = default` paint_tile.h:58,
`PaintTileSplash() = default` :25, `MTexture() = default` widget.h:79,
`StructurePaintable() = default` structure_paintable.h:35). No caller trips it today —
`LevelObjectBuilder` always passes `render_resources_` (level_object_builder.cpp:174-182, 222-227) —
but these are public constructors on public engine types.

**Remedy:** Delete the default constructors and give the derived types real ones. If they must stay
for two-phase construction, have `sprite_sheet()` and the constructors throw naming the class when
`render_resources_` is null, so the failure is loud (T6) instead of undefined.

---

#### `Visual`'s rotated-rectangle constructor throws the rotation away, and the function meant to apply it is an empty TODO

- **File:** `engine/render/visual.cpp:23-36`, `engine/render/draw_object.cpp:67-70`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6, T5, PHILOSOPHY/The public face
- **Origin:** added-by-verifier

**What:** `Visual(…, const RectangleRotated&, …)` converts its rotated rectangle to the *unrotated*
rectangle of the same centre and extents, never applies the angle, and never reports that it dropped
it — and `DrawObject::set_draw_rotation_by_rectangle_rotated`, the one function in the module whose
name says it exists to do exactly this, has an empty body.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/visual.cpp:23-36
    Visual::Visual(const std::string& sheet_name,
            const std::string& frame_name,
            const RectangleRotated& rect_rotated,
            RenderResources* render_resources,
            const Colour& color,
            float rotation, ...) :
            TextureObject(sheet_name, frame_name, render_resources,
                    color, rotation, origin, effects, layer_depth)   // <- the *parameter*, default 0
    {
            this->rectangle_ = rect_rotated.rectangle_rotated_to_axis();
    }

    // engine/math/matt_math.cpp:4469-4472 — returns the axis-aligned rect, angle discarded
    RectangleF RectangleRotated::rectangle_rotated_to_axis() const
    {
            return RectangleF(this->center_, this->hw_extents_.x, this->hw_extents_.y);
    }

    // engine/render/draw_object.cpp:67-70
    void DrawObject::set_draw_rotation_by_rectangle_rotated(const RectangleRotated& /*rect*/)
    {
            // TODO: Implement this function
    }

**Why it matters:** This is a public engine constructor that takes a rotated shape and silently draws
it unrotated — the quiet failure PHILOSOPHY T6 names "the most expensive kind, and doubly so for a
user who didn't write the engine". The angle is available and free: `RectangleRotated::angle()`
already exists (matt_math.cpp:4473-4476). `Visual::bounds()` (visual.cpp:47-50) would be wrong for
the same reason, reporting the unrotated extent to the culler. It is unreachable today — both
`Visual` construction sites use the `RectangleF` overload (level_object_builder.cpp:174-182 and
222-227), and `set_draw_rotation_by_rectangle_rotated` has zero callers repo-wide — which is exactly
why it has survived: an empty stub and a silently-lossy constructor are individually easy to miss and
together look like a working feature from the header.

**Remedy:** Implement `set_draw_rotation_by_rectangle_rotated` as
`this->set_draw_rotation(rect.angle())` and call it from the `Visual(RectangleRotated)` constructor,
or delete both the constructor and the stub. Whichever is chosen, do not leave a declared engine
entry point whose body is a comment.

---

#### `RotationOrigin` mixes "where the pivot is" with "whether to rotate", and the odd value is swallowed

- **File:** `engine/render/rotation_origin.h:5-11`, `engine/render/drawer.cpp:48-56`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T4, T5, T6

**What:** One of the four enumerators is not an origin at all, and the engine's only consumer maps it
to `top_left` through a `default:` label whose comment names a different enumerator.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/rotation_origin.h:5-11
    enum class RotationOrigin
    {
        center,
        top_left,
        left_center,
        no_rotation
    };

    // engine/render/drawer.cpp:48-56
    switch (origin)
    {
    case RotationOrigin::center:
            return Vector2F(size) / 2.0f;
    case RotationOrigin::left_center:
            return { 0.0f, size.y / 2.0f };
    default: // RotationOrigin::top_left
            return Vector2F::ZERO;
    }

**Why it matters:** `no_rotation` means "do not rotate this sprite" — a different question from where
the pivot sits — and it is the value **five** of the six projectile definitions carry
(projectile_consts.h:17, 30, 64, 77, 98; line 51 is `center`). Passing it here returns the top-left
origin with no indication that the caller asked something the function cannot answer, and the
`default:` comment tells the next reader that only `top_left` reaches that branch. Enumerating all
four with no `default:` would have made a future fifth enumerator a `/W4` warning at zero cost (T5),
which matters in a build that runs warnings-as-errors with zero suppressions. *Currently
unreachable:* grep shows `ProjectileDetails::rotat_origin` (projectile_details.h:10) is written by
all six constant tables and **read by nothing**, so `no_rotation` never actually reaches this switch;
the two live calls (weapon.cpp:49, 81) pass `left_center` and `center`. That is a separate dead-data
defect owned by the game-side review, and it is the only reason this one is latent.

**Remedy:** Split the "do not rotate" flag out of the enum, and enumerate all remaining cases
explicitly with no `default:` so the compiler reports an enumerator nothing handles.

---

#### `Visual` exposes a `protected` data member on a `final` class

- **File:** `engine/render/visual.h:9,39-40`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** T4, CONVENTIONS/Variables and members

**What:** `Visual` is `final`, so `protected` on its only data member grants access to nobody and
merely reads as "derive from me".

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/visual.h:9, 39-40
    class Visual final : public IGameObject, public TextureObject
    {
    ...
    protected:
            mattmath::RectangleF rectangle_ = mattmath::RectangleF::ZERO;
    };

**Why it matters:** A reader meeting the header cold has to check `final` against `protected` to work
out that the member is effectively private. Every sibling gets this right — `PaintTile`,
`PaintTileSplash`, `MTexture` and `StructurePaintable` are all `final` with `private:` members. In a
header meant to be the first thing a stranger reads (PHILOSOPHY/The public face), the access specifier
should state the truth.

**Remedy:** Make it `private`.

---

#### `color` and `colour` are both used, in the same declarations, across every render header

- **File:** `engine/render/draw_object.h:14,22,28,38`, `engine/render/visual.h:17,27`, `engine/render/texture_object.h:20`, `engine/render/sprite_sheet_object.h:26`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS (Names are the engine's first API), T4

**What:** The constructor parameter is spelt `color` while the member, accessor and setter on the same
class are `colour_`, `colour()` and `set_colour`.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/draw_object.h:13-38
    DrawObject(RenderResources* render_resources,
            const mattmath::Colour& color = colour_consts::WHITE,   // color
            ...
    virtual const mattmath::Colour& colour() const;                 // colour
    virtual void set_colour(const mattmath::Colour& colour);        // colour
    ...
    mattmath::Colour colour_ = colour_consts::WHITE;                // colour

The same split runs through `Visual` (visual.h:17 and 27 — the reviewer cited line 16, which is the
`render_resources` parameter), `TextureObject` (:20), `SpriteSheetObject` (:26), `TextObject`,
`AnimationObject`, all four `SpriteSheet::draw` overloads (sprite_sheet.h:51, 62, 72, 83) and every
game type that forwards the argument down. `RotationOrigin::center` and `left_center` (rotation_origin.h)
pick the American spelling too, beside `Colour` and `colour_consts`.

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS opens with "Names are the engine's first API… the scheme must be
learnable in one sitting". A user writing a `Visual` subclass has to remember the thing is called
`color` on the way in and `colour` everywhere else, and a grep for one spelling misses the other —
which is how a rename pass leaves half the tree behind.

**Remedy:** Pick one spelling — the type is `Colour`, so British — and rename the parameter
throughout the chain in one pass.

---

#### `Drawer` is a public base class with a public non-virtual destructor

- **File:** `engine/render/drawer.h:10-14`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** lifetime
- **Tenet:** T2, T5

**What:** `Drawer` is designed to be derived from but declares no destructor, so deleting a derived
object through a `Drawer*` is undefined behaviour the type does nothing to prevent.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/drawer.h:10-15
    class Drawer
    {
    public:
            explicit Drawer(RenderResources* render_resources);
            void set_render_resources(RenderResources* render_resources);
    protected:
            ...
    };

Its two subclasses are `DebugText : public artattack::Drawer` (debug_text.h:20) and
`InterfaceGameplay : public artattack::Drawer` (interface_gameplay.h:46).

**Why it matters:** No current owner triggers it — `Level` holds both as
`std::unique_ptr<InterfaceGameplay>` (level.h:125) and `std::unique_ptr<DebugText>` (level.h:152) —
so this is latent. But it is a public engine base class, and the first user who writes
`std::unique_ptr<Drawer>` over their own subclass gets UB with no diagnostic. `DrawObject`
(draw_object.h:11) gets this right with `virtual ~DrawObject() = default;`. This was already reported
in the previous review (docs/review/all-findings.md:11327) and is not recorded as fixed in
IMPLEMENTED.md; it is re-stated here because the code is unchanged.

**Remedy:** Give `Drawer` a `protected` non-virtual destructor — it has no virtual functions, so
polymorphic deletion is not wanted — or delete the class per the finding above.

---

#### `DrawObject` is a copyable polymorphic base, so cross-type assignment slices silently

- **File:** `engine/render/draw_object.h:8-43`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** lifetime
- **Tenet:** T2, T5
- **Origin:** added-by-verifier

**What:** `DrawObject`, `SpriteSheetObject` and `TextureObject` all have virtual functions and a
public virtual destructor, and none of them declares copy control — so the implicit copy constructor
and copy assignment operator are public on classes designed to be inherited from, and object slicing
compiles without a diagnostic.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/draw_object.h:8-12, 36-43 — no copy/move declarations anywhere
    class DrawObject
    {
    public:
            virtual ~DrawObject() = default;
            DrawObject() = default;
            ...
    private:
            RenderResources* render_resources_ = nullptr;
            mattmath::Colour colour_ = colour_consts::WHITE;
            ...
    };

`sprite_sheet_object.h`, `texture_object.h`, `animation_object.h`, `text_object.h` and `drawer.h`
are the same. Copies of these types are genuinely exercised:
`structure_paintable.cpp:121` does `paint_tiles.push_back(paint_tile)` on a `std::vector<PaintTile>`,
and `generate_paint_tiles()` returns that vector by value.

**Why it matters:** Declaring the virtual destructor was the right call, but stopping there leaves
the other half of the rule open: `TextureObject t = somePaintTile;` and
`static_cast<DrawObject&>(a) = b;` both compile and both silently discard the derived state, which is
precisely the class of unfalsifiable corruption T2 says must never be traded for anything. The types
that *are* copied by value in the game are all `final`, so no live slice exists — but nothing in the
headers says only-final-types-may-be-copied, and these are the base classes the engine hands to
strangers to inherit.

**Remedy:** Make the copy and move operations `protected` on `DrawObject`, `SpriteSheetObject`,
`TextureObject`, `AnimationObject` and `TextObject` (the standard shape for a polymorphic base:
public virtual destructor, protected copy/move), leaving `final` leaves fully copyable.

---

#### `draw_with` takes a raw `frame_handle` with no stated contract that it came from this object's sheet

- **File:** `engine/render/texture_object.h:65-72`, `engine/render/texture_object.cpp:92-111`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T4, T6
- **Origin:** added-by-verifier

**What:** `draw_with` resolves the sheet off `this` but takes the frame from the caller, and nothing
in its documentation says the two must match — so an in-range handle resolved against a *different*
sheet draws the wrong frame with no error.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/texture_object.h:65-72 — the comment above it (56-64) is entirely about threading
    void draw_with(DirectX::SpriteBatch* sprite_batch,
            const mattmath::RectangleF& destination_rectangle,
            const mattmath::Camera& camera,
            SpriteSheet::frame_handle frame,      // <- unconstrained
            ...) const;

    // engine/render/texture_object.cpp:101-105
    SpriteSheet* sprite_sheet = SpriteSheetObject::sprite_sheet();   // <- from *this*

    sprite_sheet->draw(sprite_batch,
            frame,                                                   // <- from the caller

**Why it matters:** The invariant is stated carefully everywhere else — `sprite_sheet_object.h:34-37`
("Every element handle a subclass is holding refers to the old sheet and is meaningless against the
new one"), `texture_object.h:29-32` ("a frame handle taken from one sheet indexes nothing meaningful
in another"), `render_resources.h:41-43`, `sprite_sheet.h:31-32`. `draw_with` is the one hole in that
wall: it is the single entry point that accepts an element handle from outside the object, and it is
the only one with no such note. `Registry::get` throws only when the index is out of range
(registry.h:98-115) — an in-range index from the wrong sheet resolves happily to the wrong frame, so
this fails as a wrong picture, not as an error (T6). Both live callers (weapon.cpp:73, 84 and
paint_tile.cpp:52) happen to pass handles from the right sheet.

**Remedy:** State the contract on the parameter — "must have been resolved against this object's
current sheet" — and consider carrying the sheet handle inside `frame_handle` so a mismatch throws
rather than draws.

---

#### Four of this group's six public headers carry no documentation at all

- **File:** `engine/render/draw_object.h:1-44`, `engine/render/drawer.h:1-35`, `engine/render/visual.h:1-42`, `engine/render/rotation_origin.h:1-12`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** docs
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/The public face, T4
- **Origin:** added-by-verifier

**What:** PHILOSOPHY says every public engine header is documented with its contract and intent.
`sprite_sheet_object.h` and `texture_object.h` do this excellently. `draw_object.h`, `visual.h`,
`rotation_origin.h` and `border_thickness.h` have not one word between them, and `drawer.h`'s only
comment explains why three dead functions are `const`.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/draw_object.h — the root of the whole render hierarchy, in full above the class:
    #pragma once

    #include "engine/math/colour.h"
    #include "engine/render/render_resources.h"

    namespace artattack
    {
            class DrawObject                       // <- no comment, here or anywhere in the file

Compare `sprite_sheet_object.h:7-18` and `texture_object.h:7-12`, which each open with a paragraph
naming the type's job, the invariant it holds and why the design is what it is.

    // engine/render/border_thickness.h:5-11 — undocumented, and carrying a stray token
    struct BorderThickness
    {
            float left = 0.0f;
            float top = 0.0f;;                     // <- double semicolon
            float right = 0.0f;
            float bottom = 0.0f;
    };

**Why it matters:** "A stranger starts from the headers, not from reading the implementation"
(PHILOSOPHY/The public face). `DrawObject` is the root every drawable in the engine inherits, and its
header says nothing about what it owns, what `origin` is measured in (see the origin-units finding
above), what `layer_depth` sorts against, or why `draw_rotation` is named differently from
`rotation`. `BorderThickness` gives no units and no statement of whether the four values are pixels,
world units or fractions — the caller (camera_tools.cpp:94-107) treats them as viewport pixels.
The split is informative: the two well-documented headers are the two the recent passes rewrote, so
the gap is not a house style, it is a backlog.

**Remedy:** Give each of the four a header comment in the shape `sprite_sheet_object.h` already
establishes — what the type is for, what it owns, what its contract is — and state the units on
`DrawObject::origin_`, `layer_depth_` and `BorderThickness`. Delete the stray semicolon.

---

### Rejected

- **"`engine/render/` has no tests, and its primitives cannot be given any" (medium)** — rejected as a
  duplicate. Its cause, its evidence (`tests/` has `assets`, `core`, `math` and no `render`) and its
  remedy ("once the `Renderer` seam exists…") are all already inside findings 1 and 2, which both cite
  the missing test folder as their own evidence. The only non-duplicated fragment — that `Drawer`'s two
  pure arithmetic helpers are `protected` and so unreachable by a test *today*, before any seam
  exists — is folded into the `Drawer` finding, where the remedy that fixes it lives.

Claims corrected rather than rejected, recorded so the change is visible:

- **"The entire drawing API is `protected`"** — false for `TextObject`, whose `draw` and `draw_with`
  are public (text_object.h:29-41); narrowed to sprite drawing.
- **"`using DrawObject::set_colour;` does [the access change] for free"** — wrong for three of the five
  overrides: `MTexture`, `MText` and `MTextDropShadow` implement `MWidget::set_colour`, a pure virtual
  on an unrelated base (widget.h:73), which a using-declaration cannot override.
- **"the one live helper [`calculate_sprite_origin`] was copy-pasted into `Weapon`"** — `Drawer`'s copy
  is dead too; all three helpers have zero callers. Strengthened, not weakened.
- **"a *verbatim* copy in the game"** — `Weapon::calculate_sprite_origin` is `static`, non-const, and
  lists `top_left` explicitly where `Drawer`'s folds it into `default:`. Functionally identical, not
  verbatim.
- **"scale 0.4 … ~37% … 4×4 world units"** — the shipped zoom-out runs 1.0 → 0.5 at 1920×1080 and
  0.667 → 0.333 at 1280×720; tiles are 4 × 12 world units. Restated at 25% at the resting overview
  scale, ~30% at the worst transition scale.
- **"`no_rotation` is the value four of six projectile definitions use"** — five of six
  (projectile_consts.h:17, 30, 64, 77, 98). And `rotat_origin` is read by nothing, so the swallowed
  branch is unreachable, not live.
- **"`Weapon` carries two `RenderResources*` … with nothing keeping them in sync"** — neither has a
  setter, so they cannot diverge. Redundant state, not a synchronisation hazard.
- **"`AnimationObject::draw_with` has the same gap"** — it has a wider one (it reads rotation, origin
  *and* depth), but its comment claims only colour and effects, so unlike `TextureObject::draw_with`
  it does not state a false contract.
- **`visual.h:16`** cited for the `color` parameter — it is `visual.h:17` (line 16 is
  `render_resources`).

<a id="g-render-sprites"></a>

## render-sprites — sprite sheets and animation

*Group `render-sprites` · 16 findings (1 high, 10 medium, 5 low) · source `review2/verified/render-sprites.md`, verified report.*

I re-opened all eight assigned files in full and every line the reviewer cited, plus
`engine/core/handle.h`, `name_table.h`, `registry.h`, `engine/render/sprite_sheet_object.{h,cpp}`,
`texture_object.{h,cpp}`, `draw_object.{h,cpp}`, `render_resources.{h,cpp}`,
`engine/assets/sprite_sheet_loader.cpp`, `resource_loader.cpp`, `engine/app/application.{h,cpp}`,
`device_resources.cpp`, `engine/core/i_game_object.h`, `engine/math/matt_math.h`, and the game-side
consumers (`player.{h,cpp}`, `paint_tile.{h,cpp}`, `projectile.h`, all five `projectile_*.cpp`,
`weapon.cpp`, `structure_paintable.cpp`) plus `game/content/textures/sprite_sheet_1.json`.

**Every line number in the raw report is correct.** I checked all fourteen anchors and every
quoted snippet, including the JSON citations (`sprite_sheet_1.json:117-119` and `:136-141` are
both exact) and the count of `engine/render/` (38 files, no `d3d11/` subdirectory). Nothing in
this group appears in IMPLEMENTED.md as fixed; the two animation defects the previous review
filed (`if` not `while`, `reset()` not clearing `paused_`) are genuinely still present and
genuinely absent from IMPLEMENTED.md.

**What I threw out.** Three consequences, none of the observations behind them. (1) The
float-precision tail on the frame-advance finding is arithmetically wrong — at the rate it
describes, `time_elapsed_` would need weeks, not minutes, to reach a magnitude where subtracting
`frame_time` loses a bit; the finding stands on the rate error alone. (2) The `draw_with`
divergence finding claimed Player's two sprite layers "will separate the moment either
subobject's setters are used" — `grep` for `set_origin`/`set_draw_rotation` across
`engine/ game/ samples/` returns *nothing*, and Player passes the same `rotation` and `origin` to
both base constructors (player.cpp:28-32), so the layers cannot currently diverge; worse for the
finding, `TextureObject::draw_with`'s three extra parameters are *earned* — `Weapon::draw`
(weapon.cpp:72-85) draws two different frame handles with computed origins off one object, which
`AnimationObject`'s signature could not express. The duplication in the five plain `draw`
overloads is real and survives; the "already diverged" framing does not. (3) "eleven lines apart"
in the colour/color finding is wrong — it is animation_object.h:20 vs :61, forty-one lines.
I also re-graded the `origin`/`rotated` finding from high to medium: it is dead members plus two
silently-ignored *optional* data fields, with no shipped content that sets them and therefore no
live miscompute.

**What I added.** Three things the reviewer walked past. The const chain that this project treats
as its parallel-render enforcement has a hole exactly here: `sprite_sheet()` and
`render_resources()` are `const` accessors returning *non-const* pointers, so
`sprite_sheet()->set_texture(...)` and `render_resources()->reset_all_textures()` both compile
inside a `draw() const`. `AnimationObject`'s default constructor produces an object on which
every read is a null dereference, which defeats the "inert default" that handle.h's comment
explicitly justifies itself by. And the update/`IGameObject` signature collision is not
hypothetical — `ProjectileRolling::update` (projectile_rolling.cpp:29-35) is a shipped derived
class that overrides both contracts with one declaration and forgets the base call, and nothing
caught it.

### Themes

- The handle discipline is complete on the draw path and absent on the update path: no
  handle-taking clip setter exists on `AnimationObject` at all.
- `RECT` is not at the call boundary, it is the *storage* of both leaf types — which is what puts
  the renderer seam behind a data-model change rather than a signature change.
- The `const` guarantee the project relies on for thread soundness is enforced at the object and
  abandoned at the accessor.
- `SpriteFrame` and `AnimationStrip` are undocumented, untested and unvalidated leaves under a set
  of carefully documented callers, and carry members that nothing reads.
- The animation state machine (`update`/`reset`/`paused_`) has two defects the previous review
  named, both now shipped as engine API, one of which `ApplicationOptions::target_fps` made
  reachable from a client's `main.cpp`.
- One declaration overriding two unrelated contracts is a live failure mode in this tree, not a
  future one.

---

#### Move the Win32 `RECT` out of the sprite data model before cutting the renderer seam

- **File:** `engine/render/sprite_frame.h:20-26`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** boundary
- **Tenet:** ARCHITECTURE/Modules ("render | core, math — D3D11/DirectXTK inside `d3d11/` only")

**What:** `SpriteFrame` and `AnimationStrip` *store* their geometry as Win32 `RECT` and publish
`const RECT*` into the frame loop, so the platform type is the engine's canonical sprite geometry
rather than something a backend converts to at its own boundary.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/sprite_frame.h:20-26
        const RECT* source_rectangle() const;
    private:
        RECT source_rectangle_ = { 0, 0, 0, 0 };

        mattmath::RectangleI source_rectangle2_ = mattmath::RectangleI::ZERO;
        mattmath::Vector2F origin_ = mattmath::Vector2F::ZERO;
        bool rotated_ = false;

    // engine/render/animation_strip.h:14, 20, 26-27
        const RECT* frame_rect(int frame_index) const;
        std::vector<RECT> frame_rects_;
        std::vector<RECT> calculate_all_frame_rects() const;
        RECT calculate_frame(int frame_index) const;

    // engine/render/sprite_sheet.h:7, 23, 48, 70
    #include "SpriteBatch.h"
        SpriteSheet(ID3D11ShaderResourceView* texture,
        void draw(DirectX::SpriteBatch* sprite_batch,
            const RECT* source_rect,

**Why it matters:** `ls engine/render/` is 38 files, all peers — there is no `d3d11/`
subdirectory for the backend to live in. The seam is usually described as "get `SpriteBatch*` out
of the draw signature", which would be a signature change if `RECT` lived only in the backend. It
does not: `SpriteFrame` stores a `RECT`, `AnimationStrip` stores a `std::vector<RECT>`, and both
hand out interior `const RECT*` (animation_object.cpp:157-160, sprite_sheet.cpp:58).
Introducing `draw_sprite(texture, src, dst, tint, rotation, origin, depth)` therefore requires
changing the storage *and* the accessor return type of both leaf types and every caller, not just
the four `SpriteSheet::draw` overloads. `SpriteFrame` already carries the `mattmath::RectangleI`
that would replace it — unused, never assigned, sitting beside the `RECT` under a placeholder
name. Note also that `AnimationStrip`'s `std::vector<RECT>` is a per-strip heap allocation whose
only purpose is to have somewhere to point at: every frame rect is `first_frame_` offset by
`index * width` (animation_strip.cpp:24-26), so the cache exists solely because the accessor
returns a pointer.

**Remedy:** make `mattmath::RectangleI` the stored form in both types — delete
`source_rectangle_`, keep `source_rectangle2_` under a real name, and have `AnimationStrip`
compute its rect and return it by value (which deletes `frame_rects_` and the allocation with it).
Let the eventual D3D11 backend do the one-line conversion to `RECT` at its own edge.

---

#### `SpriteFrame` accepts `origin` and `rotated`, stores them, and never reads them

- **File:** `engine/render/sprite_frame.cpp:7-21`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6 (loud failure over graceful degradation), T7 (data over code)

**What:** the sheet loader parses `origin` and `rotated` out of every frame definition and passes
them to `SpriteFrame`, which stores both in members that no code anywhere reads; a third member,
`source_rectangle2_`, is never even assigned.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/sprite_frame.cpp:7-21
    SpriteFrame::SpriteFrame(const RectangleI& source_rectangle,
        const Vector2F& origin,
        bool rotated)
    {
        this->set_source_rectangle(source_rectangle);
        this->origin_ = origin;
        this->rotated_ = rotated;
    }

    // engine/assets/sprite_sheet_loader.cpp:24-33
                if (frame.HasMember("origin"))
                {
                    origin.x = frame["origin"]["x"].GetFloat();
                    origin.y = frame["origin"]["y"].GetFloat();
                }
                if (frame.HasMember("rotated"))
                {
                    rotated = frame["rotated"].GetBool();
                }
                sprite_frames.add(name, SpriteFrame(source_rectangle, origin, rotated));

    // game/content/textures/sprite_sheet_1.json:136-141
                "origin":
                {
                    "x": 0.0,
                    "y": 0.0
                },
                "rotated": false

**Why it matters:** verified by grep over `engine/ game/ samples/ tests/` — `origin_` and
`rotated_` are written at sprite_frame.cpp:12-13 and 19-20 and read nowhere;
`source_rectangle2_` appears exactly once in the whole tree, at its own declaration
(sprite_frame.h:24). `SpriteFrame`'s only accessor is `source_rectangle()`. So an atlas exported
with packing rotation — what TexturePacker and every comparable tool emits — sets `"rotated":
true` and draws 90° wrong with no diagnostic at load or at draw, and a per-frame pivot is silently
zero. T7's whole claim is that data changes behaviour without a rebuild; here two schema fields
change nothing. MSVC does not warn on an unread private field, so `/W4`-as-errors will not catch
it either.

Severity is medium rather than high because exactly one frame in the shipped content carries these
fields (`square_white_32`, with `origin` 0,0 and `rotated` false), both are optional, and nothing
in the running game is currently drawn wrong. The defect is a trap laid for the engine's first
outside user, not a live bug.

**Remedy:** either implement both — frame pivot folded into the draw origin, atlas rotation folded
into the source rect plus a 90° rotation — or delete the two members, the two constructor
parameters and the two loader branches, so a sheet that sets them fails at load naming the frame
(T6). Delete `source_rectangle2_` either way, or promote it per the finding above.

---

#### `sprite_sheet()` and `render_resources()` are `const` accessors returning non-const pointers, so `draw() const` can mutate the shared sheet

- **File:** `engine/render/sprite_sheet.h:43-47`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T5 (compile-time over run-time), PHILOSOPHY/Simulation and rendering ("`draw()` is `const` all the way down")
- **Origin:** added-by-verifier

**What:** the `const` chain that IMPLEMENTED.md and `i_game_object.h` both describe as the
compiler-enforced guarantee behind parallel rendering stops one hop short: every accessor on the
path from a `const` drawable to the shared `SpriteSheet` is `const` but returns a *mutable*
pointer, so every non-const method on `RenderResources` and `SpriteSheet` — including
`set_texture()` and `reset_all_textures()` — is callable from inside a `draw() const` and compiles.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/sprite_sheet.h:43-47
        void set_texture(ID3D11ShaderResourceView* texture);

        // Every draw overload is const: a single SpriteSheet is shared by every
        // drawable in the level and is entered concurrently by the render workers,
        // so nothing here may mutate the frame or strip tables.

    // engine/render/sprite_sheet_object.h:31   — const in, mutable out
        SpriteSheet* sprite_sheet() const;

    // engine/render/draw_object.h:21           — same
        virtual RenderResources* render_resources() const;

    // engine/render/animation_object.cpp:30-33 — inside a const draw
    void AnimationObject::draw(SpriteBatch* sprite_batch,
        const RectangleI& destination_rectangle) const
    {
        SpriteSheet* sprite_sheet = SpriteSheetObject::sprite_sheet();

**Why it matters:** IMPLEMENTED.md's note on finding #16 says the pure-read contract "is fixed in
the sense that survives someone editing the code: `IGameObject::draw` and every override of it are
`const`, so a `draw()` that assigns a member is now a compile error". That is true of *members*
and false of everything reachable through these two accessors — and the object reachable through
them is the one the header immediately above declares is "shared by every drawable in the level and
is entered concurrently by the render workers". `SpriteSheet::set_texture` is a public mutator on
that object with no stated constraint on when it may be called; the only thing keeping the
guarantee true today is that nobody has written the call. Nothing currently mutates through this
path — I checked every `draw` in `engine/render/` and the game's drawables — so this is a hole in
the enforcement, not a live race.

**Remedy:** return `const SpriteSheet*` from `SpriteSheetObject::sprite_sheet()` and
`const RenderResources*` from `DrawObject::render_resources()`. Every drawable call site already
uses only `const` methods (`draw`, `resolve_*`, `sprite_frame`, `animation_strip`), so this
compiles unchanged; the loader keeps the mutable path through `RenderResources`' by-name
accessors, which is where `set_texture` is actually called from
(resource_loader.cpp:160-161). Document on `set_texture` that it may only be called with the
render workers joined.

#### `AnimationObject` can only change clip by name, so every animation switch is two `std::map<std::string, …>` descents on the update path

- **File:** `engine/render/animation_object.cpp:162-170`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** performance
- **Tenet:** T7/T8 ("Names resolve to handles once, at load. Per-frame code touches no string-keyed map")

**What:** `set_animation_strip_and_reset` is the only clip-switching entry point, it takes two
`std::string`s, and no handle-taking alternative exists anywhere on the class.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/animation_object.cpp:162-170
    void AnimationObject::set_animation_strip_and_reset(const std::string& sprite_sheet,
        const std::string& animation_strip)
    {
        this->set_sprite_sheet(sprite_sheet);
        this->strip_ = this->sprite_sheet()->resolve_animation_strip(
            animation_strip);
        this->set_frame_time_to_default();
        this->reset();
    }

    // engine/render/sprite_sheet_object.cpp:27-31 — descent 1
        this->sheet_ = this->render_resources()->resolve_sprite_sheet(
            sheet_name);
    // engine/core/registry.h:86     const auto it = this->indices_.find(name);
    // engine/core/name_table.h:55   const auto it = this->indices_.find(name);   — descent 2

**Why it matters:** the draw path is clean — I confirmed `SpriteSheetObject::sprite_sheet()`,
`SpriteSheet::sprite_frame`/`animation_strip` and `AnimationObject::source_rectangle` are all
bounds-check-and-index with no string touched. The update path is not. `Player::update_animation_state`
calls this at player.cpp:67, from `Player::update` at player.cpp:734, guarded only by "the state
changed since last frame" (player.cpp:57-60); the adjacent
`TextureObject::set_frame(info.sprite_sheet, info.uniform_texture)` at player.cpp:65 adds two more
descents. Four string-keyed tree walks per player per transition is nothing at four players — the
defect is that the API offers no alternative. `SpriteSheet::resolve_animation_strip` exists and
returns a `strip_handle`; `AnimationObject` exposes no setter that takes one. A client switching
clips per object per frame across the large object counts PHILOSOPHY/Performance sells has no
non-string path at all.

**Remedy:** add `set_animation_strip(SpriteSheet::strip_handle)` (and the `TextureObject`
equivalent) beside the by-name setters, and let game code resolve clip handles once — `Player`'s
`PlayerAnimationInfo` records could hold handles instead of names.

#### `AnimationObject::update(float)` has the same signature as `IGameObject::update(float)`, and a shipped class has already fallen into it

- **File:** `engine/render/animation_object.h:26`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T4 (clarity over cleverness), T11 (virtual dispatch is a last resort)

**What:** `AnimationObject` declares a protected `virtual void update(float dt)` that is
signature-identical to the pure virtual `IGameObject::update(float dt)`, so every class deriving
from both overrides two unrelated contracts with one declaration.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/animation_object.h:26
        virtual void update(float dt);

    // engine/core/i_game_object.h:34
        virtual void update(float dt) = 0;

    // game/objects/projectile.h:19-20, 35 — one declaration, both contracts, made pure
    class Projectile : public artattack::MovingObject,
        public artattack::AnimationObject, public ICollisionGameObject
        void update(float dt) override = 0;

    // game/objects/projectile_rolling.cpp:29-35 — the base call that is not there
    void ProjectileRolling::update(float dt)
    {
        const ProjectileDetails& details = this->details();

        Projectile::update_movement(details.gravity,
            details.wind_resistance, dt);
    }

**Why it matters:** the previous review filed this against the no-argument form; the dt increment
(`c6696af`) changed both signatures in the same direction and re-created the collision exactly,
and `IGameObject::update`'s new comment (i_game_object.h:27-34) explains the change without
noticing it. This is not a bookkeeping worry — the five surviving correct call sites work *only*
because each writes the qualification by hand (paint_tile.cpp:166, projectile_ball.cpp:40,
projectile_jet.cpp:40, projectile_mist.cpp:42, projectile_spray.cpp:42, player.cpp:736), and the
sixth derived class does not. `ProjectileRolling::update` never calls
`AnimationObject::update(dt)`; its animation object is constructed, holds a strip, and is never
advanced, and the compiler said nothing because the one declaration satisfied both bases.
(It happens to be invisible because `ProjectileRolling::draw` is a deliberate no-op, which is
precisely why nobody noticed.) Any future line inside `AnimationObject` that calls `update(dt)`
unqualified would dispatch to the derived game object and recurse. Nothing holds an
`AnimationObject*`, so `virtual` buys nothing here — it only creates the collision.

**Remedy:** rename it to what it does and drop `virtual`: `void advance_animation(float dt);`.
That makes the four correct call sites self-documenting and turns `ProjectileRolling`'s omission
into a visible one.

#### `SpriteSheet` caches a raw, un-AddRef'd `ID3D11ShaderResourceView*` — the one thing the handle/registry design exists to prevent

- **File:** `engine/render/sprite_sheet.h:92`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** lifetime
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Services and lifetimes ("A non-owning pointer is a documented loan")

**What:** the sheet holds its texture as a bare pointer with no reference, no owner named in the
declaration, and no comment — and `RenderResources::reset_all_textures()` destroys the object it
points at.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/sprite_sheet.h:92
        ID3D11ShaderResourceView* texture_ = nullptr;

    // engine/core/registry.h:138-144
        void release_all()
        {
            for (entry& slot : this->entries_)
            {
                slot.resource = Storage{};
            }
        }

    // engine/render/render_resources.h:48-51
        // A handle outlives a device loss. It names a slot, and reload_device_
        // resources() refills slots rather than making new ones, so a drawable
        // resolved before the loss draws the right thing after it - which a cached
        // ID3D11ShaderResourceView* or SpriteFont* would not, both being remade.

**Why it matters:** `Application::OnDeviceLost` calls `render_resources_->reset_all_textures()`
(application.cpp:376), which sets every `ComPtr<ID3D11ShaderResourceView>` slot to `{}`. The
registry holds the only reference — `ResourceLoader::load_texture` releases its local ComPtrs at
resource_loader.cpp:113-121 — so the refcount reaches zero and `texture_` dangles until
`reload_sprite_sheet_texture` re-seats it (resource_loader.cpp:155-162). I traced whether a draw
can land in that window: `DeviceResources::HandleDeviceLost` (device_resources.cpp:427-431) calls
`OnDeviceLost`, recreates, then `OnDeviceRestored` synchronously, so **the dangling read is not
currently reachable**. The live cost is design. `RenderResources`' own header names this exact
caching as the thing handles were introduced to eliminate; I grepped `engine/` and `SpriteSheet`
is the only type left in the engine that still does it (the other survivor, `Level::_sampler_state`,
is game code and is already recorded in IMPLEMENTED.md). The price is a bespoke per-asset-kind
reload hook (resource_loader.cpp:50-60 — the only one of four kinds whose reload differs from its
load) plus a public `set_texture` mutator on an otherwise immutable, concurrently-read object,
neither of which a `TextureHandle` member would need.

**Remedy:** store `RenderResources::TextureHandle` and read the SRV through the registry in
`draw()`. `set_texture`, the sprite-sheet-specific reload hook, and the mutator hole in the
finding above all disappear together.

---

#### Frame advance consumes at most one frame per `update`, and `target_fps` now makes that reachable from a client's `main.cpp`

- **File:** `engine/render/animation_object.cpp:99-125`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T3 ("A simple model still has exact, documented, tested semantics")

**What:** `update` advances at most one frame per call and drains exactly one `frame_time` from
the accumulator, so whenever `dt > frame_time` the clip plays at the tick rate instead of the
authored rate and `time_elapsed_` grows without bound.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/animation_object.cpp:106-124
        this->time_elapsed_ += dt;
        float frame_time = this->frame_time_;
        if (this->time_elapsed_ > frame_time)
        {
            this->frame_index_++;
            ...
            this->time_elapsed_ -= frame_time;
        }

    // engine/app/application.h:41
        int target_fps = 60;

    // engine/app/application.cpp:73-75
        this->timer_.SetFixedTimeStep(true);
        this->timer_.SetTargetElapsedSeconds(
            1.0 / static_cast<double>(this->options_.target_fps));

    // game/content/textures/sprite_sheet_1.json:117-119   (strip "splash_1")
                "frame_count": 5,
                "frame_time": 0.05,
                "looping": false

**Why it matters:** the previous review filed this as latent because dt was pinned at 1/60. It is
no longer only latent: `target_fps` is a public field of `ApplicationOptions` that a client sets
in one line of `main.cpp` (game/main.cpp:37), and `initialize` feeds it straight to
`SetTargetElapsedSeconds`. `target_fps = 15` gives dt ≈ 0.0667 against the shipped `splash_1`
strip's 0.05, so every paint splash plays its five frames at 15 fps of animation instead of the
authored 20, and on any *looping* strip whose `frame_time` is under dt the accumulator gains
`dt - frame_time` every tick forever. `set_frame_time` (animation_object.cpp:171-174) validates
nothing and neither does the loader (sprite_sheet_loader.cpp:50), so a strip authored with
`frame_time: 0` makes `time_elapsed_ -= 0.0f` a no-op with the same result and no diagnostic. This
is engine API now, not game code, and `animation_object.h` states no contract on dt at all.

(The raw report added that the accumulator's growth soon costs float precision. It does not: at the
rate described, `time_elapsed_` would need weeks of continuous running to reach a magnitude where
subtracting `frame_time` loses a bit. The rate error alone is the defect.)

**Remedy:** drain the accumulator — `while (frame_time_ > 0.0f && time_elapsed_ >= frame_time_)` —
and reject `frame_time <= 0` in the loader so a malformed strip fails at load naming itself. State
the dt contract in the header.

#### `reset()` does not clear `paused_`, so the engine's own reset is unusable for any non-looping strip

- **File:** `engine/render/animation_object.cpp:126-130`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6 (loud failure), T4 (names that say what they do)

**What:** `update` latches `paused_ = true` at the end of a non-looping strip, and neither
`reset()` nor `set_animation_strip_and_reset()` clears it, so an object that has finished a
non-looping animation stays frozen through every subsequent reset.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/animation_object.cpp:117-121, 126-130
                else
                {
                    this->frame_index_--;
                    this->paused_ = true;
                }
    ...
    void AnimationObject::reset()
    {
        this->frame_index_ = 0;
        this->time_elapsed_ = 0.0f;
    }

    // game/objects/paint_tile.cpp:155-159 — the workaround, in game code
    void PaintTileSplash::reset_and_play()
    {
        this->reset();
        this->play();
    }

**Why it matters:** the previous review named this and IMPLEMENTED.md does not record it; what is
new is that the method has since moved into the engine library and acquired a doc comment
(animation_object.h:37-40) that documents a *different* invariant — sheet and strip move together
— and still says nothing about `paused_`. I confirmed against the shipped content that `splash_1`
is the only non-looping strip in the sheet (every other strip has `"looping": true`), it belongs
to `PaintTileSplash`, and it latches `paused_` every time a splash finishes; the class survives
only because paint_tile.cpp:118 calls the two-line game-side wrapper above instead of the engine's
`reset()`. `Player::update_animation_state` calls `set_animation_strip_and_reset` (player.cpp:67)
with no `play()`, so adding one non-looping player animation — a death or hit reaction, which the
state enum is plainly heading towards — would freeze that character permanently with no error.

**Remedy:** make `reset()` mean reset (`frame_index_ = 0; time_elapsed_ = 0.0f; paused_ = false;`)
and define `stop()` as `reset(); paused_ = true;`. `PaintTileSplash::reset_and_play` then
collapses to `reset()`.

#### `AnimationObject`'s five `draw` overloads are a line-for-line fork of `TextureObject`'s

- **File:** `engine/render/animation_object.cpp:30-97`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T4 ("Not a licence for: copy-paste in the name of readability — duplication is the opposite of clarity at scale")

**What:** the two sibling classes carry the same five `draw` overloads with bodies that differ in
exactly one argument — `this->source_rectangle()` versus `this->frame_` — and the last two
overloads in each are byte-identical.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/animation_object.cpp:30-42
        SpriteSheet* sprite_sheet = SpriteSheetObject::sprite_sheet();
        sprite_sheet->draw(sprite_batch,
            this->source_rectangle(),
            destination_rectangle,
            this->colour(), this->draw_rotation(), this->origin(),
            this->effects(), this->layer_depth());

    // engine/render/texture_object.cpp:42-54 — the same body
        SpriteSheet* sprite_sheet = SpriteSheetObject::sprite_sheet();
        sprite_sheet->draw(sprite_batch,
                            this->frame_,
                            destination_rectangle,
                            this->colour(), this->draw_rotation(), this->origin(),
                            this->effects(), this->layer_depth());

    // animation_object.cpp:65-79 vs texture_object.cpp:76-90 — identical
        RectangleF rect = camera.calculate_view_rectangle(destination_rectangle);
        this->draw(sprite_batch, rect);

**Why it matters:** roughly a hundred lines of engine API written twice, in two classes a stranger
reads side by side, where every future change to the draw path has to be made in both. The
duplication also drags the documentation apart: `TextureObject::set_frame` carries an eight-line
comment about its non-atomicity ("a bad frame name throws with the sheet already moved… tolerable
only because an unresolvable name is fatal"), and `AnimationObject::set_animation_strip_and_reset`
has exactly the same hazard, in the same order, with no such note.

I rejected the raw report's stronger claim. It said `draw_with` "has already diverged" and that
Player's two sprite layers "will separate the moment either subobject's setters are used" —
`grep` for `set_origin` and `set_draw_rotation` over `engine/ game/ samples/` returns nothing at
all, and Player passes the same `rotation` and `origin` to both base constructors
(player.cpp:28-32), so the layers cannot currently diverge. Nor is the signature difference
accidental: `Weapon::draw` (weapon.cpp:72-85) calls `TextureObject::draw_with` twice with two
different frame handles and two computed origins off one object, which is exactly what the extra
parameters are for and what `AnimationObject`'s signature could not express.

**Remedy:** hoist the five `draw` overloads into `SpriteSheetObject` over one protected hook that
yields the source rectangle to pass to `SpriteSheet::draw`. Leave the two `draw_with` signatures
alone — each matches its callers — but give `set_animation_strip_and_reset` the comment its
sibling already has.

#### `AnimationStrip` and `SpriteFrame` are undocumented and unvalidated, and silently require a single-row atlas layout

- **File:** `engine/render/animation_strip.cpp:18-27`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** docs
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/The public face ("Every public engine header is documented"), T6

**What:** the strip's frame layout — every frame is the first frame offset by `index * width` in x
only — is an unstated, unchecked contract, and neither `animation_strip.h` nor `sprite_frame.h`
carries a single line of documentation.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/animation_strip.cpp:18-27
    RECT AnimationStrip::calculate_frame(int frame_index) const
    {
        if (frame_index < 0 || frame_index >= this->frame_count_)
        {
            throw std::exception("frame_index out of range");
        }
        RectangleI frame = this->first_frame_;
        frame.offset(frame_index * frame.width, 0);
        return frame.win_rect();
    }

    // engine/assets/sprite_sheet_loader.cpp:49-53 — everything straight from JSON
                int frame_count = strip["frame_count"].GetInt();
                float frame_time = strip["frame_time"].GetFloat();
                bool looping = strip["looping"].GetBool();
                animation_strips.add(name, AnimationStrip(
                    first_frame, frame_count, frame_time, looping));

**Why it matters:** every other header in and around this group carries a paragraph of contract —
`sprite_sheet.h`, `texture_object.h`, `animation_object.h`, `sprite_sheet_object.h`,
`name_table.h`, `handle.h`, `registry.h`, `render_resources.h` — and the two files that define
what a *frame* is carry none. A stranger authoring a sheet learns the rules by experiment: strips
must be a single horizontal row (a wrapped grid reads off-atlas pixels with no error, because
`SpriteBatch` clamps), `frame_count` must match what is in the texture (nothing checks the strip's
extent against the atlas), and a negative `frame_count` yields a strip whose `frame_rect` always
throws while a mistyped large one allocates `frame_count` RECTs eagerly in the constructor
(animation_strip.cpp:51-58). All of that is exactly the load-time, name-the-file failure T6 asks
for and none of it happens. Both throws here also use `std::exception("literal")` and name neither
the strip nor the index, while `NameTable::resolve` two files away produces
`no animation strip named 'x'`.

**Remedy:** document both headers — layout rule, coordinate units, the lifetime of the returned
`RECT` — and validate `frame_count > 0` and the strip's extent against the texture in
`sprite_sheet_loader.cpp`, throwing with the strip name and the JSON path. (`frame_time > 0` is
covered by the frame-advance finding above.)

#### `animation_strip.h` compiles only because `matt_math.h` happens to include `<vector>` and `<d3d11.h>`

- **File:** `engine/render/animation_strip.h:3-20`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Files ("own header first — proving every header compiles on its own"), PHILOSOPHY/Tests and toolchain ("light headers, disciplined includes")

**What:** the header uses `std::vector` and `RECT` and includes neither `<vector>` nor anything
that declares `RECT`; the `.cpp` throws `std::exception` without including `<exception>`, and
opens with a `using namespace DirectX;` it never uses.

    // engine/render/animation_strip.h:1-3, 14, 20

    #include "engine/math/matt_math.h"

        std::vector<RECT> frame_rects_;

    using namespace DirectX;
    using namespace mattmath;

#### `stop()`, `pause()`, `is_paused()` and `set_frame_index()` have no callers — including the one the game needs

- **File:** `engine/render/animation_object.h:28-35`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T1 ("Mechanisms are extracted from a real client game in hand")

**What:** four of `AnimationObject`'s eight control methods are called by nothing in `engine/`,
`game/`, `samples/` or `tests/`.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/animation_object.h:28-35
        void stop();
        void play();
        void pause();
        void set_frame_time(float frame_time);
        void set_frame_time_to_default();
        bool is_paused() const;

        void set_frame_index(int frame_index);

**Why it matters:** I grepped each name over `engine/ game/ samples/ tests/`: `stop`, `pause`,
`is_paused` and `set_frame_index` return only their own declaration and definition. `play()` has
exactly one caller (paint_tile.cpp:158) and `set_frame_time*` two (player.cpp:70, :74).
`set_frame_index` is the only one with behaviour worth having, and its behaviour is an untested,
unreached `std::exception("Invalid frame index.")` (animation_object.cpp:149). The sharper point
is `is_paused()`: `PaintTile::draw` (paint_tile.cpp:49) submits its splash sprite on every frame
for every painted tile forever, because the splash latches `paused_` on its last frame and nothing
asks — so the one query with a real client is the one nobody calls. Speculative surface is exactly
what T1's "not a licence for" clause names, and a stranger reads every one of these as supported.

**Remedy:** delete the unreached ones; keep `play`/`pause` only if the `reset()`/`paused_` fix
above leaves them meaningful, and give the splash case a real query (`is_paused()` or
`has_finished()`) with a caller.

#### A default-constructed `AnimationObject` null-dereferences on every read, which is the failure `Handle`'s inert default was designed to prevent

- **File:** `engine/render/animation_object.h:16`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T2 (correctness over speed — "checked access where an invariant can't be proven at the boundary")
- **Origin:** added-by-verifier

**What:** `AnimationObject() = default` leaves `render_resources_` null, `sheet_` and `strip_`
unresolved and `frame_time_` zero; the first `update()` or `draw()` dereferences the null pointer
before any handle is ever checked.

**Evidence:**

    // engine/render/animation_object.h:16
        AnimationObject() = default;

    // engine/render/animation_object.cpp:25-28
    const AnimationStrip& AnimationObject::animation_strip() const
    {
        return this->sprite_sheet()->animation_strip(this->strip_);
    }

    // engine/render/sprite_sheet_object.cpp:22-25 — render_resources() is nullptr here
    SpriteSheet* SpriteSheetObject::sprite_sheet() const
    {
        return this->render_resources()->sprite_sheet(this->sheet_);
    }

    // engine/core/handle.h:20-24 — the invariant this defeats
        // Unresolved. Reading through one is a throw, not a read of slot zero -
        // the default has to be inert, because every draw object is
        // default-constructible and would otherwise start life pointing at
        // whatever happened to load first.
        Handle() = default;

**Why it matters:** `handle.h` reasons explicitly that defaults must be inert *because* every
draw object is default-constructible — and then the level above throws that away: the null
`RenderResources*` is dereferenced one call before the handle's bounds check would have thrown.
The result is undefined behaviour where the design promised a named `std::out_of_range`, and
`DrawObject::render_resources()` (draw_object.h:21) is a `virtual` accessor with no check, so no
subclass can be given one. This is not reachable in the shipped game — I traced every construction
site, and `PaintTile`'s default-constructed `PaintTileSplash` member (paint_tile.h:85) is assigned
a real one in the constructor body before anything touches it, and `structure_paintable.cpp:117-172`
builds every tile through the real constructor — but the pattern `PaintTile` itself uses (default
member, assign later) is the one a client will copy, and `Projectile() = default` and
`ProjectileRolling() = default` are the same shape.

**Remedy:** either delete the default constructors on the drawable hierarchy, or have
`SpriteSheetObject::sprite_sheet()` throw naming the class when `render_resources()` is null — the
same loud, named failure the handle path already gives (T6).

### Rejected

- **"`time_elapsed_` soon grows large enough that `time_elapsed_ -= frame_time` loses precision"**
  (raw finding 7) — rejected. At the accumulation rate the finding itself describes, reaching a
  float magnitude where subtracting 0.05–0.2 loses a bit takes weeks of continuous running, not
  "a few minutes". The finding is kept on the rate error, which is real.
- **"`draw_with` has already diverged … the two layers of one character separate the moment either
  subobject's setters are used"** (raw finding 6) — rejected. `set_origin` and `set_draw_rotation`
  have zero callers anywhere in `engine/`, `game/` or `samples/`, and Player passes the same
  `rotation` and `origin` to both base constructors (player.cpp:28-32). The signature difference is
  also earned, not accidental: `Weapon::draw` (weapon.cpp:72-85) needs the frame, origin and
  rotation parameters that `AnimationObject::draw_with` lacks. The finding survives on the
  duplication in the five plain `draw` overloads, retitled.
- **"AnimationObject uses both spellings eleven lines apart"** (raw finding 13) — rejected as a
  measurement; the two are animation_object.h:20 and :61, forty-one lines apart. Corrected in place.
- **`origin`/`rotated` graded high** (raw finding 2) — re-graded to medium. The observation is
  fully confirmed (both members written and never read; `source_rectangle2_` never even assigned)
  but the consequence is latent: one shipped frame sets the fields, both to their no-op values, and
  nothing in the running game draws wrong.
- No finding was rejected outright, no duplicates were found among the fourteen, and nothing in the
  group is recorded as fixed in IMPLEMENTED.md. The `std::exception("literal")` occurrences at
  animation_strip.cpp:22, :33 and animation_object.cpp:149 were correctly *not* re-filed by the
  reviewer — they belong to the previous review's tree-wide count — and I have kept them out here
  for the same reason, noting them only as evidence inside the documentation finding.
