## render-text — Text rendering

*Group `render-text` · 14 findings (1 critical, 1 high, 8 medium, 4 low) · source `review2/verified/render-text.md`, verified report.*

I re-opened all six assigned files in full and re-checked every line number the reviewer
cited, in this group and in the files they reached into: `draw_object.h/.cpp`,
`texture_object.h`, `animation_object.h`, `visual.h/.cpp`, `render_resources.h/.cpp`,
`core/registry.h`, `core/i_game_object.h`, `ui/widget.h/.cpp`, `game/objects/level.h/.cpp`,
`game/states/menu_page.cpp`, `game/states/main_menu.cpp`,
`samples/minimal/states/hello_state.h/.cpp`, `engine/math/matt_math.h/.cpp`,
`engine/collision/partitioner.cpp`, `engine/core/thread_pool.cpp`,
`engine/app/application.cpp`, and the linked DirectXTK sources
(`out/build/x64-debug/vcpkg_installed/vcpkg/blds/directxtk/src/may2026-a68e548ea6.clean/Src/SpriteFont.cpp`
and `SpriteBatch.cpp`). Every cited line in this group is correct as written; the only line
numbers that were wrong are in the reviewer's supporting narrative for the critical finding
(the countdown draw is at `level.cpp:603`/`759-767`, not `514`/`599-604`), and I have
corrected them.

The critical finding survives and got worse. I confirmed `SpriteFont::Impl::ConvertUTF8` is a
per-font mutable buffer behind every `char const*` overload, and confirmed `Level` really does
run `countdown_text_->draw(...)` from N thread-pool workers concurrently. The reviewer's
use-after-free window was scoped to the `ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER` branch, which needs a
>1024-character string and so never fires in this game — but the *first-allocation* branch
(`if (!utfBuffer) { utfBufferSize = 1024; utfBuffer.reset(new wchar_t[1024]); }`) is equally
unsynchronised and fires on the first concurrent draw of every font. That is a real double-free
/ use-after-free at ordinary string lengths, not an exotic one.

What I threw out or cut back. Finding 3's *observation* is exact — `text_bounds()` is
non-virtual, `TextDropShadow` inherits a box that excludes its own shadow, and the correct
union exists only as a copy in `MTextDropShadow::bounds()` — but its consequence was
overstated: I traced every `bounds()` consumer and nothing culls text today
(`level.cpp:536/545/554` cull `IGameObject`s that are never text; `countdown_text_` is drawn
unconditionally at `level.cpp:600-604`; `MenuPage` does not cull at all). Regraded high →
medium, with a new fact that makes the finding sharper than the reviewer had it: `position()`
is `protected` and `Text` does not widen it, so an external holder of a `TextDropShadow` cannot
even compute the correct union by hand. Finding 4 insinuated the arithmetic in
`text_bounds_at` is probably wrong ("two easy mistakes in it"); I checked it against
`SpriteBatch::Draw`'s origin semantics and `SpriteFont::DrawString`'s `baseOffset` handling and
it is **correct**, including under `SpriteEffects` mirroring — so the finding keeps its coverage
claim and loses the insinuation. Finding 9's "an arbitrary subset of frames" is wrong about
`std::sort`, which is deterministic for a given input; reworded. Finding 5's "indirect call to a
one-line store" was double-counted — `set_position` was already virtual on `TextObject`, and
`Text`'s forward adds a direct call, not a second indirection.

What I added. One new finding: no constructor in this group has a parameter list a beginner can
use — `TextObject` takes ten positional parameters, `TextDropShadow` thirteen, and `scale` moves
from position 6 to position 8 between them with three same-typed floats adjacent, which is a
silent-miscompile shape in the type the sample hands to strangers (T10 is explicit that the
game-facing API must stay teachable). I also widened finding 7 from the `= default` constructors
to *every* constructor — `font_(render_resources->resolve_sprite_font(font_name))` dereferences
the parameter in the member-init list with no check — and widened finding 5 with the fact that
`Text` widens four of nine setters and **zero** getters, so the sample's `Text` is write-only
for four properties and unreadable for the rest.

### Themes

- The pure-read `draw()` contract that `IGameObject`'s header spends fifteen lines defending is
  honoured in ArtAttack's own members and broken one call deeper, inside the shared `SpriteFont`.
- `TextObject`'s drawable chain runs *parallel* to `IGameObject` with identical signatures, so
  every concrete drawable hand-writes the same forwarding stub and no bare text type can enter
  a `Scene`.
- New public API arrived without the contracts the philosophy promises: `text_bounds()` is
  non-virtual and wrong for its only derived class, `draw_with()` is public where both siblings
  are protected, and none of it has a test or a headless way to get one.
- Access is widened by hand and therefore incompletely: four setters widened, five setters and
  every getter left protected, `set_font` stranded with zero callers repo-wide.
- `TextObject`'s header is the best documentation in `engine/render/`; the two classes derived
  from it — the two a user actually names — have no class comment at all.
- Every public entry point in the group takes DirectXTK types from `engine/render/`, and
  `engine/render/d3d11/` does not exist.

#### Draw text through DirectXTK's wide-string overloads: the narrow ones share one buffer per font

- **File:** `engine/render/text_object.cpp:36-45, 53-62, 74-83, 116`
- **Severity:** critical
- **Category:** threading
- **Tenet:** T2

**What:** Every text draw calls `SpriteFont::DrawString(SpriteBatch*, char const*, ...)`, which
converts the string through `SpriteFont::Impl::utfBuffer` — a mutable buffer owned by the shared
`SpriteFont` — so two render workers drawing text in the same font write, and can free, the same
allocation.

**Evidence:**

`engine/render/text_object.cpp:36-45` (identically at `53-62` in the camera-less overload,
`74-83` in `draw_with`, and `116` in `remeasure`):

        sprite_font->DrawString(
            sprite_batch,
            this->text_.c_str(),
            view_pos.xm_vector(),
            this->colour().xm_vector(),
            this->draw_rotation(),
            this->origin().xm_vector(),
            view_scale,
            this->effects(),
            this->layer_depth());

The linked DirectXTK, `Src/SpriteFont.cpp:583` — every narrow overload (583, 589, 595, 601) and
`MeasureString` (607) funnels through the same call:

        DrawString(spriteBatch, pImpl->ConvertUTF8(text), XMLoadFloat2(&position), color, rotation, XMLoadFloat2(&origin), XMVectorReplicate(scale), effects, layerDepth);

`Src/SpriteFont.cpp:365-391`, with `utfBuffer` a `std::unique_ptr<wchar_t[]>` member of `Impl`
at line 67:

        const wchar_t* SpriteFont::Impl::ConvertUTF8(_In_z_ const char *text) noexcept(false)
        {
            if (!utfBuffer)
            {
                utfBufferSize = 1024;
                utfBuffer.reset(new wchar_t[1024]);
            }

            int result = MultiByteToWideChar(CP_UTF8, 0, text, -1, utfBuffer.get(), static_cast<int>(utfBufferSize));
            if (!result && (GetLastError() == ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER))
            {
                ...
                utfBuffer.reset(new wchar_t[utfBufferSize]);
                result = MultiByteToWideChar(CP_UTF8, 0, text, -1, utfBuffer.get(), static_cast<int>(utfBufferSize));
            }

            return utfBuffer.get();
        }

The concurrency, `game/objects/level.cpp:404-415`, one task per player partition:

        for (int i = 0; i < partitioned_players.size(); i++)
        {
            this->thread_pool_->add_task([this, i, partitioned_players,
                deferred_contexts, command_lists, sprite_batches]()
                {
                    this->draw_player_view_level(partitioned_players[i].first,
                    ...

and inside each worker, `game/objects/level.cpp:599-604` → `759-767`:

            // draw countdown text
            if (this->state_ == LevelState::start_countdown ||
                this->start_timer_ > -1.0f)
            {
                this->draw_countdown_text(sprite_batches->at(i), viewport_camera);
            }

        void Level::draw_countdown_text(SpriteBatch* sprite_batch,
            const mattmath::Camera& viewport_camera) const
        {
            sprite_batch->Begin();

            this->countdown_text_->draw(sprite_batch, viewport_camera);

**Why it matters:** `countdown_text_` is one `TextDropShadow` (`game/objects/level.h:122`) and
`render_resources()->sprite_font(font_)` returns the one `DirectX::SpriteFont` held in
`RenderResources::sprite_fonts_`, so N workers call `ConvertUTF8` on the same `Impl`
concurrently, twice per worker because `TextDropShadow::draw` draws shadow then text. Three
distinct failures, in increasing order of how often they fire:

1. **First-allocation double-free.** Two threads both observe `!utfBuffer`, both
   `reset(new wchar_t[1024])`; the second `reset` deletes the array the first thread is about to
   read. This needs no long string — it fires on the first concurrent draw of each font, which is
   the normal case, and the reviewer missed it by scoping the hazard to the resize branch.
2. **Torn conversion.** Both threads `MultiByteToWideChar` into the same `wchar_t[]`. The
   returned pointer may hold either string, or an interleaving. `ForEachGlyph` then calls
   `FindGlyph`, which for a character not in the font and with no default glyph does
   `throw std::runtime_error("Character not in font")` (`Src/SpriteFont.cpp:262`) — from a worker
   thread, i.e. rethrown on the join and fatal, not merely a wrong glyph.
3. **Resize use-after-free**, the reviewer's original case, needing a >1024-character string —
   real but unreachable with this game's content.

The same pattern is live outside the group on the same worker fan-out:
`game/objects/interface_gameplay.cpp:159, 168, 191, 197` (the shared `timer_font_` /
`respawn_timer_font_`, called at `level.cpp:578`) and `game/objects/debug_text.cpp:115, 124`.
The menu path is the same race between *different* objects:
`MenuPage::draw_mobjects_in_viewports` partitions widgets across the same pool
(`game/states/menu_page.cpp:127-152`) and 23 widgets in `main_menu.cpp` share `ITEM_FONT`, so two
`MTextDropShadow`s in different partitions resolve to one `SpriteFont`.

Note the shape of the regression: `IGameObject`'s header (lines 10-22) argues at length that
`const` is what makes the per-view fan-out sound, and `SpriteFont::DrawString` *is* `const` —
`ConvertUTF8` mutates through `pImpl`. Const-correctness in ArtAttack cannot reach past the
library boundary, so the contract stops exactly where the review assumed it held.

**Remedy:** Keep a `std::wstring` beside `text_`, refreshed in `set_text`/`set_font` alongside
`remeasure()`, and call the `wchar_t const*` overloads, which never touch `Impl::utfBuffer`. That
also removes a `MultiByteToWideChar` from `remeasure()`. `debug_text.cpp` and
`interface_gameplay.cpp` need the same treatment, and both build their strings with
`std::to_string(...).c_str()` per draw, so they want a value cached in `update()` anyway.

#### TextObject shadows IGameObject's draw signature from a parallel hierarchy, so no text type can be a scene object without a stub

- **File:** `engine/render/text_object.h:14, 29-31, 57`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/The object model, ARCHITECTURE/The boundary

**What:** `TextObject::draw(SpriteBatch*, const Camera&) const` has byte-for-byte
`IGameObject::draw`'s signature but descends from `DrawObject`, which is not an `IGameObject`,
so a text type can satisfy the interface only by inheriting both and writing a forwarding stub
— and the two widget types that already do this would then carry two non-virtual `IGameObject`
base subobjects.

**Evidence:**

`engine/render/text_object.h:14, 29-31`:

        class TextObject : public DrawObject
        ...
            virtual void draw(DirectX::SpriteBatch* sprite_batch,
                const mattmath::Camera& camera) const;
            virtual void draw(DirectX::SpriteBatch* sprite_batch) const;

`engine/core/i_game_object.h:41-42`:

            virtual void draw(DirectX::SpriteBatch* sprite_batch,
                const mattmath::Camera& camera) const = 0;

The stub this forces is already written three times. `engine/render/visual.cpp:43-46`
(`Visual final : public IGameObject, public TextureObject`, `visual.h:9`):

        void Visual::draw(SpriteBatch* sprite_batch, const Camera& camera) const
        {
            this->TextureObject::draw(sprite_batch, this->rectangle_, camera);
        }

`engine/ui/widget.cpp:250-257`:

        void MText::draw(SpriteBatch* sprite_batch, const Camera& camera) const
        {
            if (this->hidden())
            {
                return;
            }
            this->Text::draw(sprite_batch, camera);
        }

**Why it matters:** This is the mechanism behind "Text is not an `IGameObject`". To make
`Text : public IGameObject, public TextObject` you add exactly three members: a no-op
`update(float)` (`Visual::update` at `visual.cpp:39-42`, `MText::update` at `widget.cpp:258-261`
and `MTextDropShadow::update` at `widget.cpp:317-320` are already empty), `bounds()` — which is
a rename of the existing `text_bounds()` (`text_object.h:57`), and whose name only carries the
`text_` prefix to dodge the collision this finding is about — and a forwarding `draw()`, because
a virtual in one base is never the final overrider of a virtual in an unrelated base. Nothing is
lost. What breaks is `MText : public MWidget, public Text` (`widget.h:114`) and
`MTextDropShadow` (`widget.h:140`): `MWidget → MObject : public IGameObject` (`widget.h:9`)
already supplies one `IGameObject`, so `Text` supplying a second gives every widget two
non-virtual `IGameObject` subobjects — two extra vptrs, and both `IGameObject*` conversion and
`dynamic_cast<IGameObject*>` become ambiguous. It would still compile today only because nothing
converts a widget to `IGameObject*`: the only `IGameObject` containers are `Level`'s
(`level.h:92-93, 101-102`), and `MenuPage` holds widgets as `MObject*`.

Note what is *not* blocked: `MText` and `MTextDropShadow` already are `IGameObject`s, so a
unified `Scene` could hold a widget label today. What it cannot hold is a bare `Text` — the type
the sample hands to strangers (`samples/minimal/states/hello_state.h:31-32`) and the type `Level`
uses (`level.h:122`) — and the only wrapper available is `MWidget`, which forces
`scale_size_and_position(const Vector2F&)` (`widget.h:66`), a resolution-scaling policy, onto
anything that wants to be scene-held (T1).

**Remedy:** Decide the direction once: `DrawObject`'s subtree stops declaring a `draw` carrying
`IGameObject`'s exact signature, and the interface is implemented at exactly one level of each
hierarchy. Making `IGameObject` a virtual base "fixes" the ambiguity by paying indirection on
every widget access, which T8 will not accept.

#### text_bounds() is non-virtual, so TextDropShadow reports a box that excludes the shadow it draws — and no external holder can correct it

- **File:** `engine/render/text_object.h:43-63`, `engine/render/text_object.cpp:120-130`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T2, PHILOSOPHY/Simulation and rendering ("Objects expose bounds; the scene culls")

**What:** `TextObject::text_bounds()` is documented as the box for whoever culls or indexes the
object, but it is non-virtual, and `TextDropShadow` — which draws a second string at
`position + shadow_offset_` with its own `shadow_scale_` — inherits it unchanged and reports only
the text. The correct union exists solely as a copy one layer up, in the UI module.

**Evidence:**

`engine/render/text_object.h:43-57`:

        // The box this string occupies, for whoever has to cull or index it.
        ...
        mattmath::RectangleF text_bounds() const;

`engine/render/text_object.cpp:120-123`:

        RectangleF TextObject::text_bounds() const
        {
            return this->text_bounds_at(this->position_, this->scale_);
        }

`engine/render/text_drop_shadow.cpp:35-40` draws outside that box:

            this->TextObject::draw_with(sprite_batch, camera,
                this->shadow_color_,
                this->position() + this->shadow_offset_,
                this->shadow_scale_);

            this->TextObject::draw(sprite_batch, camera);

and the correct answer lives only in `engine/ui/widget.cpp:321-330`:

        RectangleF MTextDropShadow::bounds() const
        {
            return RectangleF::union_of(
                this->text_bounds(),
                this->text_bounds_at(this->position() + this->shadow_offset(),
                    this->shadow_scale()));
        }

**Why it matters:** The engine's own type answers its own documented query wrongly, the UI
layer's copy is right, and `text_bounds()` being non-virtual is why the fix had to be copied
rather than inherited. Worse than the reviewer noticed: `TextObject::position()` is
`protected` (`text_object.h:68`) and `Text` widens only setters, so a caller holding a
`TextDropShadow` — `Level::countdown_text_` (`level.h:122`) is exactly that — has `text_bounds()`,
`text_bounds_at()`, `shadow_offset()` and `shadow_scale()` all public but no way to obtain the
`position` the union needs. The correct extent of a `TextDropShadow` is not merely wrong by
default, it is unobtainable from outside the class.

Correcting the reviewer on consequence: nothing culls text today. `Level` culls only its
`IGameObject` vectors (`level.cpp:536, 545, 554`); `countdown_text_` is drawn unconditionally
(`level.cpp:600-604`); `MenuPage` draws every widget without a visibility test; the only consumer
of a text `bounds()` anywhere is `MContainer::bounds()`'s recursive union
(`widget.cpp:108-123`), which nothing consumes either. The error is also currently small —
`COUNTDOWN_SHADOW_OFFSET` is `{5, 5}` with equal text and shadow scale (`level.h:38-39`). This is
a latent defect in a documented engine primitive, not a live clipping bug, which is why it is
medium and not high — but `shadow_scale` is a free parameter, so the missing region is bounded
by nothing.

**Remedy:** Fold `text_bounds()` into the eventual `bounds()` and make it virtual there, give
`TextDropShadow` the union, and delete the copy in `MTextDropShadow::bounds()`. Widening
`position()` and `scale()` to public (see the `Text` finding) is needed regardless.

---

#### text_bounds()/text_bounds_at() shipped with no tests and no headless way to write one

- **File:** `engine/render/text_object.cpp:112-130`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** testing
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Tests and toolchain ("A new public primitive ships with behavioural tests in the same commit")

**What:** Two new public geometry primitives were added with zero coverage, and they cannot be
covered headlessly, because the measurement they depend on is taken in `TextObject`'s constructor
from a `SpriteFont` that only exists once a D3D11 device has built one.

**Evidence:**

`engine/render/text_object.cpp:112-130`:

        void TextObject::remeasure()
        {
            const SpriteFont* sprite_font =
                this->render_resources()->sprite_font(this->font_);
            const XMVECTOR size = sprite_font->MeasureString(this->text_.c_str());
            this->measured_size_ =
                Vector2F(XMVectorGetX(size), XMVectorGetY(size));
        }
        ...
        RectangleF TextObject::text_bounds_at(const Vector2F& position,
            float scale) const
        {
            const Vector2F size = this->measured_size_ * scale;
            const Vector2F top_left = position - this->origin() * scale;
            return { top_left, size };
        }

and `engine/render/text_object.cpp:21-25` puts the device dependency on the construction path:

            font_(render_resources->resolve_sprite_font(font_name)),
            ...
            this->remeasure();

`tests/` contains `assets/`, `core/` and `math/` and no `render/`.

**Why it matters:** Correcting the reviewer first: I verified the arithmetic against DirectXTK
rather than assuming it. `SpriteFont::DrawString` sets `baseOffset = origin` and emits each glyph
with `offset = baseOffset - (x, y + YOffset)`, which `SpriteBatch::Draw` then treats as an origin
in source-texture pixels scaled by `scale` — so the drawn top-left is
`position - origin*scale` and the extent is `MeasureString(text) * scale`. `text_bounds_at` is
**correct**, including under `SpriteEffects` mirroring (which offsets `baseOffset` by the measured
size and preserves the box) and for the `RectangleF(position, size)` constructor
(`matt_math.cpp:672-679`). So the finding is not "this is probably wrong" — it is that the
engine cannot demonstrate any of that. Two public primitives on the future culling path, whose
result the `MTextDropShadow` union depends on and whose semantics (origin scales; box is
top-left-anchored; rotation deliberately ignored) are stated only in a comment, have nothing
holding them to it. PHILOSOPHY promises the opposite: "Everything below the platform edge is
testable headlessly."

**Remedy:** Split the arithmetic out — a free function or static taking
`(measured_size, position, origin, scale)` — and test that; leave only the `MeasureString` call
behind the device edge. This is the smallest possible instance of the renderer-seam problem and a
good place to prove the seam pays.

#### Text is 66 lines of forwarding whose only effect is widening four setters, and the widening is arbitrary

- **File:** `engine/render/text.h:7-26`, `engine/render/text.cpp:23-38`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T4, T11

**What:** `Text` adds no state and no behaviour; its four methods each call the base
implementation and exist only because those methods are `protected` on `TextObject`. Because the
widening is done by hand it is incomplete in both directions: five setters and *every* getter
were left behind, and `set_font` — the one method that correctly re-runs `remeasure()` on a font
change — now has zero callers anywhere in the repository.

**Evidence:**

`engine/render/text.cpp:23-38`, the entire body of the class:

        void Text::set_text(const std::string& text)
        {
            this->TextObject::set_text(text);
        }
        void Text::set_colour(const Colour& colour)
        {
            this->TextObject::set_colour(colour);
        }
        void Text::set_scale(float scale)
        {
            this->TextObject::set_scale(scale);
        }
        void Text::set_position(const Vector2F& position)
        {
            this->TextObject::set_position(position);
        }

What is on the other side of the wall — `engine/render/text_object.h:65-74`:

        protected:
            const std::string& text() const;
            RenderResources::FontHandle font() const;
            const mattmath::Vector2F& position() const;
            float scale() const;

            virtual void set_text(const std::string& text);
            void set_font(const std::string& font_name);
            virtual void set_position(const mattmath::Vector2F& position);
            virtual void set_scale(float scale);

plus `DrawObject`'s six protected getters and five protected setters (`draw_object.h:21-32`).

**Why it matters:** Reported against the pre-split code (`docs/review/README.md`, "Other
instances of the same mistake") and not listed in IMPLEMENTED.md, so it survives — worth
restating because the consequences have grown:

- **`set_font` is dead.** Repo-wide grep finds its declaration (`text_object.h:72`), its
  definition (`text_object.cpp:107-111`) and nothing else. A user can change a label's text,
  colour, scale and position but not its font, and `text_bounds()`'s header comment
  (lines 47-49) documents a contract — "it is retaken in exactly those two setters" — whose
  second setter is unreachable.
- **`Text` widens no getters at all.** The type the sample hands to strangers
  (`hello_state.h:31-32`) is write-only for four properties and cannot be read at all: not its
  text, not its position, not its scale, not its colour. `text_bounds()` is the only public read,
  which is why the previous finding's union is uncomputable from outside.
- **The chain is four deep for one string.** `DrawObject → TextObject → Text → TextDropShadow`,
  and `TextDropShadow`'s only two methods qualify straight past the middle class
  (`this->TextObject::draw_with`, `this->TextObject::draw`, `text_drop_shadow.cpp:35, 40`). T11
  calls inheritance a tool of last resort; here a whole level of it contributes nothing to the
  class below it.

**Remedy:** Delete `text.h`/`text.cpp`; make the accessors and setters `public` on `TextObject`
(a text object whose text you cannot set or read is the odd shape here); reparent
`TextDropShadow` and `MText` onto `TextObject`. If a widening layer is ever genuinely wanted,
`using TextObject::set_text;` does it with no code and cannot silently omit a member.

#### The camera-less draw() overload re-introduces the exact overload IGameObject just deleted, in two non-identical copies

- **File:** `engine/render/text_object.h:31`, `engine/render/text_object.cpp:48-63`, `engine/render/text_drop_shadow.cpp:42-45`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T4, PHILOSOPHY/Simulation and rendering

**What:** `TextObject` keeps a camera-less `draw(SpriteBatch*)` that is exactly
`draw(sprite_batch, Camera::DEFAULT_CAMERA)`, written out longhand in one class and delegated in
the other, after the same overload was deleted from `IGameObject` for that reason.

**Evidence:**

`engine/render/text_object.cpp:48-62` hand-inlines the identity:

        void TextObject::draw(SpriteBatch* sprite_batch) const
        {
            const SpriteFont* sprite_font =
                this->render_resources()->sprite_font(this->font_);

            sprite_font->DrawString(
                sprite_batch,
                this->text_.c_str(),
                this->position_.xm_vector(),
                ...
                this->scale_,

`engine/render/text_drop_shadow.cpp:42-45` delegates instead:

        void TextDropShadow::draw(SpriteBatch* sprite_batch) const
        {
            this->draw(sprite_batch, Camera::DEFAULT_CAMERA);
        }

`engine/core/i_game_object.h:35-40` states the rationale for deleting it, and
`engine/math/matt_math.cpp:4163-4173` confirms the two are equivalent only by arithmetic
coincidence:

        Vector2F Camera::calculate_view_position(
            const Vector2F& world_position) const
        {
            return Vector2F((world_position.x - this->translation.x) * this->scale,
                (world_position.y - this->translation.y) * this->scale);
        }
        ...
        const Camera Camera::DEFAULT_CAMERA = { Vector2F::ZERO, 1.0f };

**Why it matters:** Two implementations of one behaviour that agree only because
`(p - 0) * 1 == p`. If `Camera` ever gains a term, the delegating copy follows it and the
longhand copy does not. The sample game — the canonical shape a new project copies — teaches the
overload the interface deliberately removed: `samples/minimal/states/hello_state.cpp:73-74` calls
`greeting_->draw(sprite_batch)`, so the first thing a stranger learns is API that does not exist
on any scene object. It also does not survive one level of derivation: `MText` declares
`draw(SpriteBatch*, const Camera&)` (`widget.h:134-135`), which hides
`TextObject::draw(SpriteBatch*)`, so the same call fails to compile on a widget.

**Remedy:** Delete both camera-less overloads and have the sample pass `Camera::DEFAULT_CAMERA`,
matching what `IGameObject`'s header already tells implementers to do.

#### No constructor in the group validates render_resources, so the first use is a null dereference rather than a loud failure

- **File:** `engine/render/text_object.h:17`, `engine/render/text_object.cpp:21`, `engine/render/text.h:10`, `engine/render/text_drop_shadow.h:10`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** lifetime
- **Tenet:** T6, T5

**What:** All three types expose `= default` constructors that leave the inherited
`render_resources_` at `nullptr` and `font_` unresolved, and every method that does anything
dereferences that pointer before reaching the registry's loud throw. The *full* constructors are
no better: they dereference the parameter in the member-init list with no check.

**Evidence:**

`engine/render/text_object.h:17`, `engine/render/text.h:10`, `engine/render/text_drop_shadow.h:10`:

            TextObject() = default;
            Text() = default;
            TextDropShadow() = default;

`engine/render/draw_object.h:37`:

            RenderResources* render_resources_ = nullptr;

`engine/render/text_object.cpp:21` — the non-default path, before any body runs:

            font_(render_resources->resolve_sprite_font(font_name)),

`engine/render/text_object.cpp:30-31` and `114-115` both start the same way:

            const SpriteFont* sprite_font =
                this->render_resources()->sprite_font(this->font_);

**Why it matters:** `Registry::get` is carefully written to throw naming the resource rather than
return null (`engine/core/registry.h:98-115`), and `RenderResources`' header promises exactly
that (lines 57-59) — but the throw is unreachable from a default-constructed object, because
`nullptr->sprite_font(...)` reads `RenderResources::sprite_fonts_` off a null `this` first.
`draw()`, `draw_with()`, `set_text()` and `set_font()` all take that path. No caller
default-constructs one today, so this is a trap laid for the first stranger who writes
`artattack::Text label;` and fills it in later — which `= default` invites, and which
`MText() = default` / `MTextDropShadow() = default` (`widget.h:117, 143`) extend to the widget
set. T6 says the engine says so immediately, with names and paths; this crashes with neither.

**Remedy:** Delete the defaulted constructors — nothing constructs one — and have the real
constructor throw naming the type if `render_resources` is null, before the member-init list can
dereference it (a small static helper in the init list, or move the resolve into the body).

#### The group takes DirectXTK types in its public API from engine/render/, and its measurement half has no seam to hide behind

- **File:** `engine/render/text_object.h:26, 29-31, 37-41`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** boundary
- **Tenet:** ARCHITECTURE/Modules ("render | core, math — D3D11/DirectXTK inside `d3d11/` only")

**What:** Every public entry point in this group names `DirectX::SpriteBatch` or
`DirectX::SpriteEffects`, and the state names `DirectX::SpriteFont`, in files sitting directly in
`engine/render/`. `engine/render/d3d11/` does not exist.

**Evidence:**

`engine/render/text_object.h:26, 29-31, 37-41`:

                DirectX::SpriteEffects effects = DirectX::SpriteEffects_None,
        ...
            virtual void draw(DirectX::SpriteBatch* sprite_batch,
                const mattmath::Camera& camera) const;
            virtual void draw(DirectX::SpriteBatch* sprite_batch) const;
        ...
            void draw_with(DirectX::SpriteBatch* sprite_batch,
                const mattmath::Camera& camera,
                const mattmath::Colour& colour,
                const mattmath::Vector2F& position,
                float scale) const;

`engine/render/render_resources.h:39`, so even the handle type is DirectXTK:

            using FontHandle = Handle<DirectX::SpriteFont>;

`ls engine/render/` shows 40 files and no `d3d11/` subdirectory.

**Why it matters:** The seam is the known open item and every group will report the general
form, so the increment that belongs to this one is what text specifically demands of the seam
design. Two things. First, `draw_with()` (`text_object.h:37-41`) is a *new* public
`SpriteBatch*` entry point added by the recent data-race work, i.e. after ARCHITECTURE named the
rule — the fourth in this header, added at the moment a first backend-side function could have
been introduced instead. Second, and more useful: `text_bounds()` is nominally pure geometry,
but its input comes from `SpriteFont::MeasureString`, so a renderer interface with only
`draw_sprite(...)` on it — the shape PHILOSOPHY sketches — cannot serve this module. Text needs a
second operation, `measure_text(FontHandle, string_view) -> Vector2F`, and nothing in the design
documents accounts for it. That is also what makes the headless-test finding above structural
rather than incidental.

**Remedy:** When the seam is designed, `draw(Renderer&, const Camera&)` and
`Renderer::measure_text(FontHandle, string_view)` are the two shapes this group needs; add
`measure_text` to the renderer interface's spec now, before the interface is written. Until then,
stop adding public DirectXTK signatures to `engine/render/`.

#### text.h and text_drop_shadow.h carry no class documentation, and the shadow's draw-order contract is unstated

- **File:** `engine/render/text.h:1-27`, `engine/render/text_drop_shadow.h:1-46`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** docs
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/The public face ("Every public engine header is documented")

**What:** The two types a user actually names have no class-level comment at all, and
`TextDropShadow` silently depends on an order-preserving `SpriteBatch` sort mode because it draws
its shadow and its text at the same `layer_depth`.

**Evidence:**

`engine/render/text.h:5-10` — no comment anywhere in the file:

        namespace artattack
        {
            class Text : public TextObject
            {
            public:
                Text() = default;

`engine/render/text_drop_shadow.h:5-10` — the only comment in the file is on `draw`, about
`const`; the class itself has none:

        namespace artattack
        {
            class TextDropShadow : public Text
            {
            public:
                TextDropShadow() = default;

`engine/render/text_drop_shadow.cpp:35-40` — both draws take `this->layer_depth()` from the one
`DrawObject` member (`draw_object.h:42`), so they tie:

            this->TextObject::draw_with(sprite_batch, camera,
                this->shadow_color_, ...);

            this->TextObject::draw(sprite_batch, camera);

DirectXTK breaks depth ties with `std::sort`, not `std::stable_sort`
(`Src/SpriteBatch.cpp:688, 697, 706` — the `Texture`, `BackToFront` and `FrontToBack` modes).

**Why it matters:** `TextObject`'s header is the best documentation in `engine/render/` — the
handle rationale, the measurement cache, the `draw_with` race note — and the two classes derived
from it explain nothing: not what `Text` adds (it adds access), not the shadow's draw order, not
that `shadow_offset` is in position space while `shadow_scale` multiplies the glyphs, not that
`layer_depth` is shared by both draws, not that `shadow_offset` does not track `set_scale`.
Correcting the reviewer on the sort consequence: `std::sort` is deterministic for a given input,
so a `BackToFront` or `FrontToBack` caller does not get a per-frame flicker — it gets an ordering
fixed by introsort's pivot choices, which is silently correct or silently inverted for a given
scene and flips when unrelated sprites are added around it. That is worse to debug, not better.
Every current caller happens to use `SpriteSortMode_Deferred` (`level.cpp:531`,
`menu_page.cpp:113`, `hello_state.cpp:72`) or `Begin()`'s default, which is also Deferred, so the
tie is harmless today.

**Remedy:** Document both classes. State that the shadow is submitted first at the same depth and
therefore requires an order-preserving sort mode — or give the shadow a slightly greater
`layer_depth` so the ordering survives sorting and the constraint disappears.

#### Every constructor in the group is a long positional parameter list, and `scale` changes position between Text and TextDropShadow

- **File:** `engine/render/text_object.h:18-27`, `engine/render/text_drop_shadow.h:11-23`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T10 ("the game-facing API must live in the simple subset of the language and stay teachable to a beginner"), T4, T5
- **Origin:** added-by-verifier

**What:** `TextObject` and `Text` take ten positional parameters, `TextDropShadow` thirteen and
`MTextDropShadow` fifteen, all defaulted, several adjacent and same-typed — and the shadow
constructor inserts two parameters ahead of `scale`, so the same concept is argument 6 on one
class and argument 8 on its direct subclass.

**Evidence:**

`engine/render/text_object.h:18-27`:

            TextObject(const std::string& text,
                const std::string& font_name,
                const mattmath::Vector2F& position,
                RenderResources* render_resources,
                const mattmath::Colour& color = colour_consts::WHITE,
                float scale = 1.0f,
                float rotation = 0.0f,
                const mattmath::Vector2F& origin = mattmath::Vector2F::ZERO,
                DirectX::SpriteEffects effects = DirectX::SpriteEffects_None,
                float layer_depth = 0.0f);

`engine/render/text_drop_shadow.h:11-23`, where `scale` has moved to argument 8 and now has two
same-typed neighbours:

            TextDropShadow(const std::string& text,
                        const std::string& font_name,
                        const mattmath::Vector2F& position,
                        RenderResources* render_resources,
                        const mattmath::Colour& color = colour_consts::WHITE,
                        const mattmath::Colour& shadow_color = colour_consts::BLACK,
                        const mattmath::Vector2F& shadow_offset = { 2.0f, 2.0f },
                        float scale = 1.0f,
                        float shadow_scale = 1.0f,
                        float rotation = 0.0f,
                        ...

and the call it produces, `game/objects/level.cpp:96-105` — nine positional arguments, the last
two identical floats meaning different things:

            this->countdown_text_ = std::make_unique<TextDropShadow>(
                COUNTDOWN_TEXT,
                COUNTDOWN_FONT_NAME,
                position,
                this->render_resources_,
                COUNTDOWN_COLOUR,
                COUNTDOWN_SHADOW_COLOUR,
                COUNTDOWN_SHADOW_OFFSET,
                COUNTDOWN_SCALE,
                COUNTDOWN_SCALE);

**Why it matters:** `scale`, `shadow_scale` and `rotation` are three consecutive `float`s with
defaults: any transposition compiles clean under `/W4` with warnings-as-errors and shows up as a
wrong-looking label, not a diagnostic — which is precisely the class of error T5 exists to move
to the compiler. Converting a `Text` to a `TextDropShadow`, the obvious edit for a user who wants
a shadow, silently shifts `scale`/`rotation`/`origin` by two positions unless every argument is
re-read. The widget subclasses make it worse by inserting `bool hidden` between `shadow_offset`
and `scale` (`widget.h:144-158`), so a float in the scale position binds to `hidden` and the
label disappears. T10 accepts an explicit burden — the game-facing API must be teachable to a
beginner — and a thirteen-argument constructor with four interchangeable trailing floats is the
counter-example to it; this is also the type the sample game and `Level` both construct, so it is
the first constructor a stranger meets.

**Remedy:** Take the optional half as a small aggregate — `TextStyle { colour, scale, rotation,
origin, effects, layer_depth }` and `ShadowStyle { colour, offset, scale }` — so every value is
named at the call site and a transposition is a type error. That also stops the parameter list
being re-declared four times across the group and the widget set.

`engine/render/text_object.h:33-41`, above the `protected:` at line 65:

#### colour and color are spelled both ways inside one class

- **File:** `engine/render/text_drop_shadow.h:15-16, 34, 38, 43`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS ("Names are the engine's first API")

**What:** `TextDropShadow` publishes `shadow_color()` / `set_shadow_color()` / `shadow_color_`
while inheriting `set_colour()` and taking a parameter named `color` of type `Colour`.

`engine/render/text_drop_shadow.h:15-16, 34, 38, 43`:

                const mattmath::Colour& color = colour_consts::WHITE,
                const mattmath::Colour& shadow_color = colour_consts::BLACK,

#### remeasure() dispatches a virtual accessor from inside a constructor

- **File:** `engine/render/text_object.cpp:25, 112-115`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** lifetime
- **Tenet:** T4

**What:** `TextObject`'s constructor calls `remeasure()`, which reads the service through the
virtual `DrawObject::render_resources()`, so a derived override would be silently bypassed during
construction — while the constructor already holds the pointer as a parameter.

**Evidence:**

`engine/render/text_object.cpp:21-25` and `112-115`:

            font_(render_resources->resolve_sprite_font(font_name)),
            position_(position),
            scale_(scale)
        {
            this->remeasure();
        ...
        void TextObject::remeasure()
        {
            const SpriteFont* sprite_font =
                this->render_resources()->sprite_font(this->font_);

`engine/render/draw_object.h:21`:

            virtual RenderResources* render_resources() const;

**Why it matters:** Nothing overrides `render_resources()` today, so nothing misbehaves — but the
accessor is `virtual`, which advertises overriding as supported, and the one call made during
construction cannot honour it, with no diagnostic. The constructor is also inconsistent with

#### set_text() re-measures unconditionally, including when the string is unchanged

- **File:** `engine/render/text_object.cpp:102-106`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** performance
- **Tenet:** T8, PHILOSOPHY/Performance

**What:** The measurement cache exists so `text_bounds()` is not a per-frame string walk, but
`set_text` re-walks on every call whether or not the text changed.

**Evidence:**

`engine/render/text_object.cpp:102-106`:

        void TextObject::set_text(const std::string& text)
        {
            this->text_ = text;
            this->remeasure();
        }

against the justification in `engine/render/text_object.h:45-49`:

            // The measurement is cached rather than taken here, because this is on
            // the culling path and MeasureString walks the string: it would be a
            // per-object, per-view, per-frame walk of every label on screen. Only
            // the text and the font change it, so it is retaken in exactly those
            // two setters; position, scale and origin are arithmetic on top.

**Why it matters:** `Level::update` calls it once per tick for the whole countdown
(`level.cpp:110-116`), where the string is identical for roughly 60 consecutive ticks; each call
re-runs `MeasureString`, which walks the glyph table *and* goes through `ConvertUTF8`'s
`MultiByteToWideChar` — the same shared buffer as the critical finding, though on the update
thread and therefore uncontended. `MainMenuWeaponSelect` does the same for weapon names on every
selection frame (`main_menu.cpp:1560-1602`). The cost is small; it is also the exact cost the
cache was added to remove, and the guard is one comparison.

**Remedy:** `if (text == this->text_) { return; }` at the top of `set_text`.

---

### Rejected

- **"Every drop-shadowed label clips its shadow at a view edge, and any broad-phase index built
  from it under-reports"** (finding 3's consequence) — rejected as stated; nothing culls or
  indexes text today. `Level` culls only its `IGameObject` vectors, `countdown_text_` is drawn
  unconditionally, `MenuPage` does not cull, and `MContainer::bounds()` is the only consumer of a
  text `bounds()` and has no consumer itself. The observation is kept and regraded high → medium.
- **"The arithmetic in `text_bounds_at` has two easy mistakes in it (whether origin scales,
  whether the box is top-left or centred)"** (finding 4) — rejected. Verified against
  `SpriteFont::DrawString`'s `baseOffset` handling, `SpriteBatch::Draw`'s origin semantics and
  `RectangleF(position, size)` (`matt_math.cpp:672-679`): the implementation is correct, including
  under `SpriteEffects` mirroring. The coverage claim survives; the insinuation does not.
- **"A user who picks `SpriteSortMode_BackToFront` gets the shadow drawn on top of the text on an
  arbitrary subset of frames"** (finding 9) — rejected as stated. `std::sort` is deterministic for
  a given input sequence; the ordering is fixed per scene and flips when surrounding sprite counts
  change, which is a different and harder-to-diagnose failure. Reworded in place.
- **"Each forward also keeps the method virtual, so `set_position` is an indirect call to a
  one-line store"** (finding 5) — rejected. `TextObject::set_position` is already `virtual`
  (`text_object.h:73`); `Text`'s forward adds a direct call, not the indirection, so the cost is
  attributed to the wrong line. The rest of finding 5 stands and was expanded.
- **Reviewer's remedy list for the critical finding, "`game/objects/interface_gameplay.cpp:159,
  168, 191`"** — incomplete rather than wrong; `197` is a fourth narrow-string `DrawString` in the
  same file. Corrected in place.
- **Supporting line citations `game/objects/level.cpp:514, 599-604` for the countdown draw** —
  wrong. `514` is the worker's outer `for`; the countdown call is at `603`, dispatching to
  `Level::draw_countdown_text` at `759-767`. Corrected in place; the finding is unaffected.
- **No findings were rejected as duplicates**, and none is recorded as fixed in
  `docs/review/IMPLEMENTED.md`. The `Text`-is-pure-forwarding defect appears in the previous
  review (`docs/review/README.md`, "Other instances of the same mistake") and is *not* in
  IMPLEMENTED.md, so it correctly survives. Note #16's entry in IMPLEMENTED.md claims the
  `TextDropShadow` draw race is fixed; it is fixed in ArtAttack's own members, and the critical
  finding above shows the same race is still live one call deeper in DirectXTK.

## render-viewports — viewports, resolution, cameras

*Group `render-viewports` · 16 findings (4 high, 6 medium, 6 low) · source `review2/verified/render-viewports.md`, verified report.*

I re-opened all ten assigned files in full and re-checked every line the reviewer cited — all thirteen
findings, not a sample. Their citations are unusually accurate: `viewport_manager.cpp:79-93` /
`137-140` / `143-234`, `camera_tools.cpp:91-108`, `render_resources.h:15-22` / `71-78` / `87-88`,
`screen_layout.h:5-11`, `matt_math.cpp:50-60` and `4109-4116`, `menu_page.cpp:104-118`,
`application.cpp:220-223` / `230-237` / `293-302` / `359-362` / `523-531`,
`device_resources.cpp:284-285` / `390`, `texture_object.cpp:99-101`, `resource_loader.cpp:121` and
`level_object_builder.cpp:222-227` all land exactly where they claim. One citation is off by one
(`application.cpp:515` is `:514`), and one range is loose (`render_resources.h:56-69` should be
`57-78` to cover `add_sprite_sheet`, which the evidence block quotes). Both corrected below.

I re-derived the two arithmetic claims rather than trusting them. The camera dead-zone inversion is
real and I confirmed the exact 140 px oscillation — but it is **resolution-dependent** and the
reviewer's own text hedges it correctly while the title does not: at 1920x1080 and above every layout
clamps inside its viewport and the bug vanishes. It fires at `s_1280_720`, which is both the default
(`resolution_manager.h:26`, `application.h:37`) and the value every unrecognised input falls back to,
so it is what ships. The `scale²` cull-rect error is confirmed as an error and confirmed as **latent**:
nothing in the tree writes `Camera::scale`, `calculate_camera` only ever copies it, and the zoom-out
path is commented out (`level.cpp:429-468`) — I regraded the framing, not the severity, and folded in a
second instance the reviewer missed at `camera_tools.cpp:61-63`.

What I threw out is consequence, not observation. The allocation finding claimed "a menu page with 30
widgets performs 30 allocations per frame across 16 threads"; every menu page in the game pushes
exactly **two** top-level containers (`pause_menu.cpp:217-222`, `main_menu.cpp:42-51`, and seven more —
all identical), so it is two calls per frame, and `viewport_dividers()` is not on the draw path at all:
its only caller is `LevelObjectBuilder::build_viewport_dividers`, which runs once at level build. That
finding drops to low. The `RegistryStorage` finding called the ordering hazard "a rule a stranger cannot
see" — `registry.h:13-17` states the split at the primary template, so the claim is corrected, though
the ill-formed-NDR hazard survives. The SCREAMING-constants finding drops to low: it is a naming rule
with no behavioural consequence.

I added four findings. The largest is architectural: `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s module table says
"`render` | core, math — **D3D11/DirectXTK inside `d3d11/` only**", there is no `engine/render/d3d11/`
directory, and this module's public API is `ID3D11DeviceContext*` and `D3D11_VIEWPORT` over what is
otherwise pure `mattmath` rectangle arithmetic — which is the *mechanical* reason the reviewer's
"no tests for this module" finding has never been actionable. I also verified the git claim in the
asset-name finding: `git show 2fa12fe` says in its own message "viewport_consts held four constants
describing how a split-screen divider is drawn, three of which the game reads; they are static members
of `ViewportManager`". The reviewer's reading of that commit is exact.

### Themes

- Two authorities disagree about "the screen": `ResolutionManager` holds a settings enum, `DeviceResources` holds the real client rect, and every viewport is computed from the wrong one — while the `DeviceResources*` that knows the right one sits unread in the class that guesses.
- Out-of-range indices are answered with plausible geometry instead of a diagnosable failure: the fall-through switch, the `player_viewport(4)` call, and every silent fallback in `ResolutionManager` (T6).
- The engine's viewport vocabulary is this game's: `player_num`, `one_player`, four hardcoded arrangements, and two literal asset names out of `game/content/textures/` (T1).
- The module is welded to D3D11 in a directory ARCHITECTURE reserves for backend-free code, which is why none of its pure geometry is — or can be — tested.
- `const` stops at the first pointer: the compiler-enforced pure-read `draw()` the project just bought is escapable through a non-const `RenderResources*` and a mutable `SpriteSheet*`.
- `render_resources.{h,cpp}` is exemplary — resolve-once/read-by-handle, contract written once, device loss documented. The other five headers in this group carry no contract at all, and the undocumented one holds the group's worst bug.

---

#### Fix the camera scroll border, which clamps a minimum above a maximum and inverts the dead zone

- **File:** `engine/render/camera_tools.cpp:91-108`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T3 (simple, but exact)

**What:** `calculate_camera_scroll_border` clamps each border into `[MIN_BORDER_*, viewport/2]`, and at
1280x720 — the default resolution and the fallback for every unrecognised one — the minimum exceeds the
maximum in every split-screen layout. Opposing borders then overlap, the dead zone inverts, and the
camera moves every frame for a completely stationary player.

**Evidence:**

        constexpr float MIN_BORDER_LEFT = 400.0f;
        constexpr float MIN_BORDER_TOP = 250.0f;
        constexpr float MIN_BORDER_RIGHT = 400.0f;
        constexpr float MIN_BORDER_BOTTOM = 250.0f;
        ...
        clamp_ref(result.left, MIN_BORDER_LEFT, viewport_size.x / 2.0f);
        clamp_ref(result.right, MIN_BORDER_RIGHT, viewport_size.x / 2.0f);
        clamp_ref(result.top, MIN_BORDER_TOP, viewport_size.y / 2.0f);
        clamp_ref(result.bottom, MIN_BORDER_BOTTOM, viewport_size.y / 2.0f);

`mattmath::clamp_ref` (`engine/math/matt_math.cpp:50-60`) takes the min branch first, so the max is
never consulted once the min has fired:

        void mattmath::clamp_ref(float& value, float min, float max)
        {
            if (value < min) { value = min; }
            else if (value > max) { value = max; }
        }

**Why it matters:** two-player at 1280x720 gives a 1280x360 viewport (`viewport_manager.cpp:155-169`).
`top = 360*0.2 = 72` clamps up to 250 and `bottom = 360*0.4 = 144` clamps up to 250, against a max of
180 that never runs. In `calculate_camera` (`camera_tools.cpp:36-37`) that makes
`top_edge = T + 250` and `bottom_edge = T + 360 - 250 = T + 110` — the top edge is *below* the bottom
edge, so no `T` fails both tests. Trace a motionless player at world `py`: `py < T+250` sets
`T = py-250`; next frame `py > (py-250)+110` sets `T = py-110`; next frame `py < (py-110)+250` sets
`T = py-250` again. 140 px of vertical judder at 60 Hz, forever. Three- and four-player (640x360) break
both axes: `MIN_BORDER_LEFT/RIGHT` 400 each against a max of 320, adding a 160 px horizontal judder.
Nothing pins it: `close_quarters.json:60-66` gives `camera_bounds` 6100x5350 against a 1280x360 view,
so the bounds clamp in `calculate_camera` never fires. I verified the arithmetic at every supported
resolution — **1280x720 is the only one that breaks**, and at 1920x1080+ every layout clamps inside its
viewport. That is not a mitigation: `s_1280_720` is `ApplicationOptions`' default (`application.h:37`),
`ResolutionManager`'s default (`resolution_manager.h:26`) and the value every unparseable save file
coerces to. This ships inside `ArtAttackEngine`, so a stranger linking the library inherits it.

**Remedy:** clamp the floor against the ceiling first (`min(MIN_BORDER_*, viewport/2)`), or express the
border as a fraction with a floor that is itself capped, and assert `left+right < width` and
`top+bottom < height` as invariants of the returned `BorderThickness`. Pin both with a test:
`calculate_camera_scroll_border({1280,360}).top + .bottom > 360` is one line.

#### Stop asking for viewport index 4, and give the layout switch its missing exits

- **File:** `engine/render/viewport_manager.cpp:79-93, 143-234`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6 (loud failure over graceful degradation)

**What:** `all_viewports()` asks for `player_viewport(4)` to fill the empty quadrant of a three-player
layout. Index 4 falls through every inner switch and lands on the fullscreen `default:`, and the caller
then *applies* a different rectangle from the one it lays the widget out against.

**Evidence:**

        int player_count = this->player_count_from_layout(this->layout_);
        for (int i = 0; i < player_count; i++)
        {
            result.push_back(this->player_viewport(i));
        }
        // Add a 4th viewport if there are 3 players
        if (player_count == 3)
        {
            result.push_back(this->player_viewport(4));
        }

and the missing exits that let it through (`viewport_manager.cpp:194-197` and `224-227`):

            default:
                break;
            }
        case ScreenLayout::four_player:
        ...
            default:
                break;
            }
        default: //1P screen

**Why it matters:** `calculate_viewport(three_player, 4, res)` misses the three-player inner switch,
falls into `case four_player:`, misses again, and lands on `default: //1P screen` at line 227 —
`{0, 0, res.x, res.y}`. `MenuPage::draw_mobject_in_viewports` (`game/states/menu_page.cpp:104-118`)
iterates that vector and, for `i == 3`, calls `apply_player_viewport(3, ...)`, which under
`three_player` falls through to `four_player` case 3 and sets the **bottom-right** quadrant — already
player 1's viewport — then draws the widget through `MObject::draw(sprite_batch, viewports[3])`, which
builds `Camera(viewport)` from the **fullscreen** rect (`engine/ui/widget.cpp:19-22`, translation
`(0,0)`). So every three-player pause menu (`pause_menu.cpp:222`), results menu
(`results_menu.cpp:214`) and end menu (`end_menu.cpp:244`) draws a fourth pass laid out for a full
screen and clipped into player 1's quadrant, while the genuinely blank top-right quadrant is never
drawn. The same missing exit makes `calculate_viewport(two_player, 2, res)` return the three-player
*bottom-left* rect. Note the fix is not "change the 4 to a 1": the empty quadrant is `four_player`
index 1, and `apply_player_viewport` and `viewports[]` would still disagree because they are indexed in
two different spaces (`menu_page.cpp` passes the loop ordinal, `level.cpp:521-523` passes
`player_object->player_num()`) with nothing documenting either. The same gap also means that in
gameplay the halves of both dividers that fall inside the never-drawn top-right quadrant are never
rasterised, so a three-player divider cross is drawn half-width on two of its four arms.

**Remedy:** replace the nested switches with a `[layout][index]` table of normalised rects; make an
out-of-range index throw naming both the layout and the index rather than returning a fullscreen
viewport; and have `all_viewports()` return the layout's own cells, with the caller applying the cell
it was handed rather than re-deriving it from a loop counter.

#### Get this game's sprite-sheet and frame names out of the engine's viewport header

- **File:** `engine/render/viewport_manager.h:15-21`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** boundary
- **Tenet:** T1 (mechanism over policy) / PHILOSOPHY, The boundary

**What:** `ViewportManager` — an engine class — publishes as public API the texture-atlas name, frame
name and colour of an asset that lives in `game/content/`, and the most recent conventions commit
promoted them from a free namespace into the class rather than deleting them.

**Evidence:**

        // How a split-screen divider is drawn. They live on the class that shapes
        // the dividers rather than in a `consts` namespace of strays (CONVENTIONS,
        // Constants and enumerators); a game asks for the rectangles and then for
        // these to fill them.
        static inline const std::string DIVIDER_SHEET_NAME = "sprite_sheet_1";
        static inline const std::string DIVIDER_FRAME_NAME = "pixel";
        static inline const mattmath::Colour DIVIDER_COLOUR = colour_consts::BLACK;

**Why it matters:** PHILOSOPHY, The boundary: "Engine headers contain no game nouns — no team, weapon,
paint, menu or **asset name**. The litmus test for any file: if a game built on the engine — yours or a
stranger's — would need to edit it, it is game code." `sprite_sheet_1` is this game's atlas. The only
consumer is `LevelObjectBuilder::build_viewport_dividers`
(`game/objects/level_object_builder.cpp:222-227`), which reads the engine's constants to decide what
its own dividers are made of — the dependency points backwards. I confirmed the history: `2fa12fe`'s
own commit message reads "viewport_consts held four constants describing how a split-screen divider is
drawn, three of which the game reads; they are static members of `ViewportManager`, which is the class
that shapes the dividers." The placement question was asked and answered from CONVENTIONS; the boundary
question was never asked. Divider *colour* is policy too — a game may want white, or team-coloured.

**Remedy:** delete all three from the engine. `viewport_dividers()` already returns rectangles, which is
the entire mechanism; the game names its own sheet, frame and colour when it fills them.

#### Derive viewport geometry from the render target, not from the resolution setting

- **File:** `engine/render/viewport_manager.cpp:15-19, 43-59, 73-77` (with `engine/render/viewport_manager.h:54-55`)
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T2 (correctness over speed) / ARCHITECTURE, Modules

**What:** every viewport is computed from `ResolutionManager`'s settings enum while the backbuffer is
sized from the window's client rect. The two disagree after any window drag, any resolution change and
any fullscreen toggle — and `ViewportManager` already holds the `DeviceResources*` that knows the right
answer and never reads it once.

**Evidence:**

        ResolutionManager* resolution_manager_ = nullptr;
        DeviceResources* device_resources_ = nullptr;      // never read in the .cpp

        D3D11_VIEWPORT vp = this->calculate_d3d11_viewport(
            this->layout_, player_num, this->resolution_manager_->resolution_vec());
        context->RSSetViewports(1, &vp);

against the frame setup, which uses the real one (`engine/app/application.cpp:293-302`):

        auto const viewport = this->device_resources_->GetScreenViewport();
        context->RSSetViewports(1, &viewport);

**Why it matters:** `GetScreenViewport` is built from `m_outputSize` (`device_resources.cpp:284-285`,
`390`), which `WindowSizeChanged` sets to the client width/height passed by `WM_SIZE`
(`application.cpp:359-362`, `:514`) and `WM_EXITSIZEMOVE` (`application.cpp:523-531`). Three reachable
paths desynchronise them, all of which I traced:

1. The user drags the window edge. `WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW` (`application.cpp:114`) is resizable and
   `WM_GETMINMAXINFO` sets only a *minimum*, so there is no size lock.
2. Options → Apply calls `Application::set_resolution`, which does `SetWindowPos(..., size.x, size.y,
   ...)` with a **window** rect and no `AdjustWindowRect` (`application.cpp:220-223`). `WM_SIZE`'s
   `lParam` carries the *client* size, so `m_outputSize` becomes roughly 16x39 px smaller than the enum
   claims. The same omission is in `create_window` (`application.cpp:112-116`), which passes the
   resolution as a window size and then hands `SetWindow` the resolution again
   (`application.cpp:58-61`).
3. Options → Apply → fullscreen calls `set_fullscreen(true)` → `SW_SHOWMAXIMIZED`
   (`application.cpp:230-237`), giving a monitor-sized backbuffer while `ResolutionManager` still says
   1280x720. The entire game then renders into the top-left 1280x720 of a 1080p or 1440p screen,
   dividers included.

In split-screen the visible symptom is a divider no longer at 50% and a clipped bottom/right strip of
every view. This is a `render`-module defect with the fix site inside `ViewportManager`, which already
holds the authority as an unread member.

**Remedy:** compute from `device_resources_->GetOutputSize()` (or take the target size as a parameter
and delete the member), and demote `ScreenResolution` to a *requested* mode that the window path
converts to a client size via `AdjustWindowRect`.

#### Make screen size a value the game supplies, not a four-mode enum the engine owns — and stop answering unknown modes with 1280x720

- **File:** `engine/render/screen_resolution.h:5-12` (with `engine/render/resolution_manager.cpp:48-64, 95-176`)
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T1 (mechanism over policy) / T6 (loud failure)
- **Origin:** added-by-verifier

**What:** the engine's only notion of screen size is a closed enum of four 16:9 modes, and every
conversion into it answers an unrecognised input with a silent fallback rather than a diagnosis.

**Evidence:**

        enum class ScreenResolution
        {
            s_1280_720,
            s_1920_1080,
            s_2560_1440,
            s_3840_2160,
            max = s_3840_2160
        };

and three of the five converters, each answering the unknown case with a plausible lie:

        default:
            return {-1, -1};            // convert_resolution_to_ivec
        ...
            return std::string("-1x-1"); // convert_resolution_to_string
        ...
        else
        {
            return ScreenResolution::s_1280_720;   // convert_string_to_resolution,
        }                                          // convert_vec_to_resolution,
                                                   // convert_ivec_to_resolution

**Why it matters:** a player on 1366x768, 2560x1080 ultrawide or any non-16:9 panel cannot express
their monitor, and a stranger's game inherits this game's display list — the litmus test in
PHILOSOPHY's The boundary says a file a game would need to edit is game code. The silent half is a
plain T6 breach: `set_resolution("1366x768")` returns having quietly selected 720p, with no name and no
path. It compounds finding #1, because 1280x720 is exactly the resolution at which the camera dead zone
inverts, so the fallback lands on the one broken mode. Three of the four `set_resolution` overloads
(`string`, `Vector2F`, `Vector2I`) and three of the five private converters have **zero callers** in
the tree — this is dead public engine API whose only documented behaviour is a lie — and
`game/save.cpp:134-150` carries a byte-for-byte duplicate of `convert_ivec_to_resolution`, so a save
file naming an unsupported mode is silently rewritten to 720p in two places. The `{-1,-1}` sentinel is
unreachable today (nothing casts into the enum) but would flow straight into `Viewport::width/height`
as a negative extent if it ever fired.

**Remedy:** make the engine's screen size a `Vector2I` the application supplies and the window path
validates; if a menu wants a picker, the *list of offered modes* is game data (T7). Whatever remains of
the enum path should throw naming the requested value instead of substituting one, and `Save` should
call the one converter rather than owning a second.

#### Take D3D11 out of this module's public API, or move the module under render/d3d11/

- **File:** `engine/render/viewport_manager.h:3-8, 34-38, 49, 61-62` (with `engine/render/render_resources.h:5-7`)
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** architecture
- **Tenet:** ARCHITECTURE, Modules / PHILOSOPHY, Tests and toolchain
- **Origin:** added-by-verifier

**What:** ARCHITECTURE's module table reads "`render` | core, math — **D3D11/DirectXTK inside `d3d11/`
only**". There is no `engine/render/d3d11/` directory, and this module's public API — over what is
otherwise pure `mattmath` rectangle arithmetic — is spelled in `ID3D11DeviceContext*` and
`D3D11_VIEWPORT`.

**Evidence:**

        #include "engine/render/screen_layout.h"
        #include "engine/render/resolution_manager.h"
        #include "engine/render/device_resources.h"
        #include "engine/math/matt_math.h"
        #include "engine/math/colour.h"
        #include "SpriteBatch.h"
        ...
        void apply_player_viewport(int player_num,
            ID3D11DeviceContext* context,
            DirectX::SpriteBatch* sprite_batch) const;
        void apply_player_viewport(int player_num,
            ID3D11DeviceContext* context) const;
        ...
        D3D11_VIEWPORT fullscreen_d3d11_viewport() const;
        ...
        D3D11_VIEWPORT calculate_d3d11_viewport(ScreenLayout layout,
            int player_num, const mattmath::Vector2F& screen_size) const;

**Why it matters:** exactly three of the eleven members need a device; the rest are
`mattmath::Viewport`/`RectangleF` in and out. Because the class is welded to D3D11, `tests/render/`
cannot be written without a device — which is the mechanical reason the two one-line assertions that
would have caught this group's two worst bugs have never existed, and why the "no tests for this
module" finding below has never been actionable. PHILOSOPHY: "Everything below the platform edge is
testable headlessly, because the boundary and the seams make it linkable and constructible without a
window." The same include chain is a compile-time cost: every translation unit that includes
`viewport_manager.h` drags in the whole of `device_resources.h` (and with it `d3d11_1.h`, `dxgi1_6.h`
and DirectXTK) for a pointer member that could be forward-declared and is never read — against
"Compile speed is a maintained property — light headers, disciplined includes." (Two smaller cuts in
the same header: it uses `std::string` and `std::vector` without including `<string>` or `<vector>`,
relying on transitive includes, against CONVENTIONS' "own header first — proving every header compiles
on its own"; and neither non-owning member carries the ownership comment PHILOSOPHY, Services and
lifetimes requires of a loan.)

**Remedy:** split the class in two — a device-free `viewport_layout` (free functions over `ScreenLayout`
and `Vector2F`, testable and linkable against MattMath alone) in `engine/render/`, and the
`RSSetViewports`/`SetViewport` application in `engine/render/d3d11/` behind the renderer interface the
project already owes itself. `render_resources.h` is a smaller instance of the same thing and is worth
the same treatment when the seam lands.

#### Divide by camera scale in camera_adjusted_player_viewport_rect, and give Camera an inverse

- **File:** `engine/render/viewport_manager.cpp:27-41` (with `engine/render/camera_tools.cpp:61-63`)
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T4 (clarity over cleverness) — one transform, in one place

**What:** the world-space culling rect multiplies the viewport extent by `camera.scale` where inverting
the view transform requires dividing, so the rect is wrong by `scale²` for any camera not at 1.0. This
is the only hand-rolled camera transform left in the tree, and it exists because `Camera` has no
view→world inverse.

**Evidence:**

        Viewport vp = this->player_viewport(player_num);
        const float scale = camera.scale;
        const Vector2F& translation = camera.translation;

        auto result = RectangleF(
            translation.x,
            translation.y,
            vp.width * scale,
            vp.height * scale);

against the forward transform (`engine/math/matt_math.cpp:4109-4116`):

        return RectangleF((world_rectangle.x - this->translation.x) * this->scale,
            (world_rectangle.y - this->translation.y) * this->scale,
            world_rectangle.width * this->scale,
            world_rectangle.height * this->scale);

**Why it matters:** `view = (world - translation) * scale`, so the world extent behind `vp.width` pixels
is `vp.width / scale`. The result is the world-space cull rect in `Level::draw_player_view_level`
(`game/objects/level.cpp:527-558`), which since the `bounds()` change routes *every* object through
`object->bounds().intersects(camera_view)` — so the error would decide visibility for the whole scene.
**It is latent, not live**, and I verified why: `CameraTools::calculate_camera` only ever copies
`prev_camera.scale`, nothing in the tree writes `Camera::scale`, and the zoom-out path that would is
commented out (`level.cpp:429-468`). The moment any camera zooms, objects vanish exactly when they
should appear. The same assumption is baked in a second place the reviewer did not reach —
`camera_tools.cpp:61-63` builds `camera_rectangle` as `viewport_size.x × viewport_size.y` in world
units for the bounds clamp, which is likewise only true at scale 1 — so a zoom would break the scroll
border and the level-edge clamp too. `Camera` has four forward overloads
(`matt_math.h:1034-1044`) and no inverse at all, which is why both sites hand-rolled one.

**Remedy:** add `Camera::view_to_world(RectangleF)` beside the forward overloads, guard `scale == 0`,
and make both call sites one call to it.

#### Stop expressing the engine's viewport API in players

- **File:** `engine/render/screen_layout.h:5-11` (with `engine/render/viewport_manager.h:34-45, 59`)
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T1 / PHILOSOPHY, Structural types

**What:** the engine's split-screen mechanism is spelled entirely in the game noun "player" and
enumerates exactly four hardcoded arrangements, so no game can ask for a minimap, a picture-in-picture,
a spectator view or a fifth view without editing engine code.

**Evidence:**

        enum class ScreenLayout
        {
            one_player,
            two_player,
            three_player,
            four_player
        };

        void apply_player_viewport(int player_num, ID3D11DeviceContext* context) const;
        mattmath::Viewport player_viewport(int player_num) const;
        int player_count_from_layout(ScreenLayout layout) const;

**Why it matters:** PHILOSOPHY, Structural types: "there is no engine `Player`, `Level`, `Match` or
`Team`. The engine-worthy parts of 'player' already exist as input slots and **views**." Split-screen
itself *is* engine mechanism — The boundary lists it — but "view 2 belongs to player 2" is policy. The
current shape also welds the count to the enum: `player_count_from_layout` and `calculate_viewport`
must both be edited to add a layout, which is precisely why `all_viewports()` reaches for a fifth index
by hand. The enum-rename pass (`dcd8f6f`) touched exactly these names and kept the vocabulary.

**Remedy:** `set_view_count(int)` plus `view(int index)` returning a computed grid cell, with
`ScreenLayout` deleted or reduced to an optional arrangement hint; `player_num` becomes `view_index`.
This is the same edit as the `[layout][index]` table in finding #2 and should be made once.

#### Close the const hole that lets a const draw() mutate RenderResources from a render worker

- **File:** `engine/render/render_resources.h:57-78` (with `engine/render/draw_object.h:21`)
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** threading
- **Tenet:** T2 / PHILOSOPHY, Simulation and rendering

**What:** the `const` accessors hand out non-const `SpriteSheet*` and `SpriteFont*`, and
`DrawObject::render_resources() const` hands out a non-const `RenderResources*`, so the
compiler-enforced pure-read `draw()` does not actually stop a drawable mutating shared render state
from a worker thread.

**Evidence:**

        // Per-draw, and const and non-mutating because they are called from
        // thread-pool workers. ...
        ID3D11ShaderResourceView* texture(TextureHandle texture) const;
        DirectX::SpriteFont* sprite_font(FontHandle font) const;
        SpriteSheet* sprite_sheet(SpriteSheetHandle sprite_sheet) const;
        ...
        void add_sprite_sheet(const std::string& sprite_sheet_name,
            std::unique_ptr<SpriteSheet> sprite_sheet);

and the loan that carries no constness (`engine/render/draw_object.h:21`):

        virtual RenderResources* render_resources() const;

reached from inside a `const` draw (`engine/render/texture_object.cpp:99-101`):

        float rotation) const
        {
            SpriteSheet* sprite_sheet = SpriteSheetObject::sprite_sheet();

**Why it matters:** IMPLEMENTED.md records that `draw()` was made `const` specifically so "a `draw()`
that assigns a member is now a compile error rather than something an audit has to keep catching". That
guarantee stops at the first pointer: from any `const draw()` a game author can legally call
`render_resources()->add_sprite_sheet(...)` — a `std::map::emplace` plus a `vector::push_back` on
`Registry` internals (`registry.h:63-76`) — or `sprite_sheet(handle)->set_texture(...)`
(`sprite_sheet.h:43`), from every task `Level::draw_active_level` submits. **No current caller does
either**, so this is a broken contract rather than a live race — but it is exactly the contract a
stranger writing their first drawable will lean on, and `sprite_sheet.h:45-47` already commits in
writing that "Every draw overload is const … nothing here may mutate the frame or strip tables."

**Remedy:** return `const SpriteSheet*` and `const DirectX::SpriteFont*` from the const accessors —
both types' draw paths are already `const`, and `SpriteFont::DrawString` is const in DirectXTK, so this
compiles — and make `DrawObject` return `const RenderResources*`. `texture()` must stay non-const
because `SpriteBatch::Draw` takes a mutable SRV; say so in a comment.

#### Test the three pure functions in this module

- **File:** `engine/render/viewport_manager.cpp:143-234`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** testing
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY, Tests and toolchain

**What:** `tests/` contains `assets/`, `core/` and `math/` and nothing for `render`, although
`ViewportManager::calculate_viewport`, the whole of `ResolutionManager` and
`CameraTools::calculate_camera` compute pure functions over value types.

**Evidence:** the tree is `tests/assets/{asset_manifest_loader_tests.cpp}`,
`tests/core/{name_table_tests.cpp, registry_tests.cpp}`,
`tests/math/{collision_tools_tests.cpp, math_tests.cpp}`, each with its own `CMakeLists.txt` and
`test_main.cpp`. No file under `tests/` mentions `Viewport`, `ScreenLayout`, `ScreenResolution` or
`Camera` — I grepped. ARCHITECTURE's own directory listing shows `tests/` with exactly those three
folders.

**Why it matters:** "A new public primitive ships with behavioural tests in the same commit", and
"Everything below the platform edge is testable headlessly". The two highest-severity findings in this
group are a single assertion each — `calculate_viewport(three_player, 4, {1280,720})` returning
`{0,0,1280,720}` instead of throwing, and
`calculate_camera_scroll_border({1280,360}).top + .bottom > 360`. Two things stand between them and a
test and both are structural: `calculate_viewport` is `private`, and the class cannot be constructed
without a `DeviceResources` (see the D3D11 finding above) — which is why this is not simply "someone
forgot".

**Remedy:** land the layout split first, then add `tests/render/viewport_layout_tests.cpp` pinning
