#### Sprite-sheet numbers are never range-checked, so `"frame_count": 0` throws namelessly out of a render worker

- **File:** `engine/assets/sprite_sheet_loader.cpp:38-56`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T7 ("Data is read, validated and resolved to handles at load"), T6
- **Origin:** added-by-verifier

**What:** The loader has every animation-strip number in its hands at load and range-checks none
of them. A strip with a zero or negative `frame_count` builds an `AnimationStrip` whose first
read throws — from the draw path, with no file, sheet or strip name in the message.

**Evidence:**

`engine/assets/sprite_sheet_loader.cpp:44-53`:

    auto first_frame = RectangleI(
        strip["first_frame"]["x"].GetInt(),
        strip["first_frame"]["y"].GetInt(),
        strip["first_frame"]["w"].GetInt(),
        strip["first_frame"]["h"].GetInt());
    int frame_count = strip["frame_count"].GetInt();
    float frame_time = strip["frame_time"].GetFloat();
    bool looping = strip["looping"].GetBool();
    animation_strips.add(name, AnimationStrip(
        first_frame, frame_count, frame_time, looping));

`engine/render/animation_strip.cpp:29-36` — what a `frame_count_` of 0 produces:

    const RECT* AnimationStrip::frame_rect(int frame_index) const
    {
        if (frame_index < 0 || frame_index >= this->frame_count_)
        {
            throw std::exception("frame_index out of range");
        }
        return &this->frame_rects_[frame_index];
    }

reached from `engine/render/animation_object.cpp:157-161`:

    const RECT* AnimationObject::source_rectangle() const
    {
        return this->animation_strip().frame_rect(this->frame_index_);
    }

**Why it matters:** `AnimationStrip`'s constructor accepts `frame_count = 0` without complaint
(`animation_strip.cpp:8-16`; `calculate_all_frame_rects` simply produces an empty vector), so the
load walk succeeds, the manifest is kept, and every handle resolves. The first frame that draws
that strip calls `source_rectangle()`, throws, and — because `AnimationObject::draw` runs on the
thread pool — the exception is recorded at `thread_pool.cpp:88-91` and rethrown from
`wait_for_tasks_to_complete` (`thread_pool.cpp:72-75`) into the frame loop, which has no handler.
The process dies with `frame_index out of range`: no file, no sheet, no strip name, and nothing
connecting it to the JSON line that caused it. A negative `w` in `first_frame` is the same shape —
`calculate_frame` offsets by `frame_index * frame.width` and produces overlapping or inverted
`RECT`s that DirectXTK will happily sample. This is the second half of the finding above: guards
fix *presence and type*, and range still gets through. PHILOSOPHY is explicit that data is
"read, validated and resolved to handles at load; the frame loop never sees it".

**Remedy:** Reject `frame_count < 1`, `frame_time <= 0` and non-positive frame dimensions in
`decode_animation_strips`, naming the file and the strip — and reject non-positive `size.w`/`size.h`
in `decode_sprite_frames` the same way.

#### Loading a second manifest silently forfeits the first one's textures at the next device loss

- **File:** `engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:88-106`, `engine/app/application.cpp:376-377`
- **Severity:** medium *(reviewer: high — regraded)*
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T6; PHILOSOPHY/Services and lifetimes

**What:** `ResourceLoader` keeps only the most recent manifest as its device-restore replay list,
while `Application::OnDeviceLost` releases *every* texture and font, so an asset loaded by an
earlier manifest is never rebuilt and its registry slot stays permanently empty.

**Evidence:**

`engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:88-91`:

    // Kept only once the walk has finished, so the loader never holds a
    // manifest it did not load - a restore replaying a half-loaded one would
    // reload assets that were never there.
    this->manifest_ = std::move(manifest);

`engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:94-98`:

    void ResourceLoader::reload_device_resources() const
    {
        // The manifest was walked once already, so every kind in it resolves -
        // load_manifest threw if one did not.
        for (const AssetEntry& entry : this->manifest_.entries)

`engine/app/application.cpp:376-377`:

    this->render_resources_->reset_all_textures();
    this->render_resources_->reset_all_sprite_fonts();

which reach `Registry::release_all()` (`registry.h:138-144`) via `render_resources.cpp:86-89` and
empty **every** slot, not the ones a particular manifest filled.

**Why it matters:** `Application::load_manifest` (`application.h:86`) is public and takes a path,
so calling it twice is the natural way to express "engine content, then level content". After
that, one GPU reset empties both manifests' texture slots and refills only the second's, and every
drawable holding a handle into the first throws `Texture 'x' has been released.` from
`Registry::get` on the render path.

I regraded this from high. The header states the behaviour in the sentence directly above the
declaration (`resource_loader.h:62-65`: "A second manifest replaces the first as the thing a
restore replays, so a game with more than one loads them as one"); both shipped clients call it
exactly once (`game/main.cpp:74`, `samples/minimal/main.cpp:37`); and the trigger needs a device
loss on top of the second call. It is a documented trap with no enforcement — real, latent, and
worth a throw rather than a comment, which is what T6 asks for — but not a live defect.

**Remedy:** Append `manifest.entries` to `manifest_` rather than assigning (keeping each entry's
source path for diagnostics), or make a second `load_manifest` throw naming both files.

#### Make the guarded JSON readers reachable; today they are private to one .cpp and the module's only public JSON API is a raw rapidjson Document

- **File:** `engine/assets/asset_manifest_loader.cpp:10-55`, `engine/assets/json_loader.h:12`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T4 ("duplication is the opposite of clarity at scale"), ARCHITECTURE/Modules

**What:** The module's checked-read layer lives in an anonymous namespace inside
`asset_manifest_loader.cpp`, so the only thing `engine/assets/` offers any other loader — or any
game — is `rapidjson::Document read_json_file(const char*)` with no accessors attached.

**Evidence:**

`engine/assets/asset_manifest_loader.cpp:10-11, 17, 23-24, 34-35, 45-46`:

    namespace
    {
        ...
        [[noreturn]] void fail(const std::string& path, const std::string& what)
        ...
        const Value& require_member(const Value& parent, const char* key,
            const std::string& path, const std::string& context)
        ...
        const Value& require_array(const Value& parent, const char* key,
            const std::string& path, const std::string& context)
        ...
        std::string require_string(const Value& parent, const char* key,
            const std::string& path, const std::string& context)

`engine/assets/json_loader.h:12` — the whole of the module's public JSON surface:

    rapidjson::Document read_json_file(const char* path);

**Why it matters:** This is the structural cause of the critical finding and of everything
downstream of it. The two sibling loaders in the same folder could not use the guards if their
authors wanted to. On the game side, `game/objects/level_loaded_info.h:30-31, 38` exposes
`const rapidjson::Value&` accessors and a `rapidjson::Document json_doc_` member, and its own
header admits the consequence at `:41-46` — "The rest of this class still reaches into the
document unchecked — that is the loaders' standing validation debt, and it is not paid here."
PHILOSOPHY's boundary table promises the game "Asset loading, registries, JSON parsing"; what it
actually hands over is a parser handle. Every game that reads its own content will either rewrite
these four functions or, like this one, skip them.

**Remedy:** Promote the guards to `engine/assets/json_read.h` as a documented, tested part of the
module's public surface, taking the file path so each throw can name it.

#### Path strings are widened byte-by-byte, so any non-ASCII content path fails to open

- **File:** `engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:117, 133, 173-174`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T2; PHILOSOPHY/The public face

**What:** All three file-opening sites convert `std::string` to `std::wstring` with the
iterator-range constructor, which widens each byte independently rather than decoding UTF-8, so
any path containing a non-ASCII character becomes a different, non-existent path.

**Evidence:**

`engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:115-119`:

    ThrowIfFailed(
        CreateDDSTextureFromFile(this->device_,
            std::wstring(texture_path.begin(), texture_path.end()).c_str(),
            resource.GetAddressOf(),
            texture_view.ReleaseAndGetAddressOf()));

`engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:131-133`:

    this->render_resources_->add_sprite_font(name,
        std::make_unique<SpriteFont>(this->device_,
            std::wstring(font_path.begin(), font_path.end()).c_str()));

`engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:172-174`:

    wave_bank = std::make_unique<WaveBank>(this->audio_engine_,
        std::wstring(wave_bank_path.begin(),
            wave_bank_path.end()).c_str());

**Why it matters:** The manifest is hand-authored data and both halves of every path come straight
out of it (`asset_manifest.h:19-24`). A developer who writes `"directory": "./texturen_grün/"` or
names a font `menü_24` gets two `wchar_t` of mojibake per multi-byte character — and because
MSVC's `char` is signed, byte `0xC3` sign-extends to `wchar_t` `0xFFC3` rather than `0x00C3`, so
even a Latin-1-style single-byte guess would not accidentally work. The open fails, and for the
texture kind the failure does not even say which file (finding above). This costs nothing in the
shipped content, which is entirely ASCII; it is a defect specifically against "intended,
eventually, for developers other than its author".

**Remedy:** Convert with `MultiByteToWideChar(CP_UTF8, …)` in one small helper in this file, or
hold paths as `std::filesystem::path` and pass `.c_str()`.

#### State what `directory` is relative to, and reject a directory with no trailing separator

- **File:** `engine/assets/asset_manifest.h:19-24`, `engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:111, 127, 151, 167, 184`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** docs
- **Tenet:** T6; CONVENTIONS/Data

**What:** Nothing in the module says whether `AssetEntry::directory` is relative to the process
working directory or to the manifest, nothing normalises the separator, and
`AssetManifest::source_path` — captured precisely so a bad entry can name its file — is never used
to root the paths it describes.

**Evidence:**

`engine/assets/asset_manifest.h:19-24` — the whole documented contract for the field:

    struct AssetEntry
    {
        std::string kind;
        std::string directory;
        std::string name;
    };

`engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:111` and its four siblings — the entire path construction:

    const std::string texture_path = directory + name + ".dds";

`engine/assets/asset_manifest.h:34-36` — what `source_path` is for, and the only thing it is used for:

    // Where it was read from, so a bad entry can name the file it came out of
    // and not just itself (T6).
    std::string source_path;

**Why it matters:** The answer is "relative to the process working directory", discoverable only
by reading `game/CMakeLists.txt:74-76`'s comment and noticing that both `main.cpp` files pass a
relative path. A stranger who does the obvious thing —
`app.load_manifest("C:/games/mine/content/manifest.json")` — gets a manifest that parses
perfectly and then a failure naming `./fonts/x.spritefont`, a path that appears nowhere in what
they wrote, because the manifest's own location was thrown away for path purposes while sitting
right there in `source_path`. Separately, `"directory": "./textures"` without the trailing slash —
an easy hand-edit — concatenates to `./texturessprite_sheet_1.dds`; three of the four kinds at
least put the mangled path in the message, and the texture kind prints an HRESULT.

**Remedy:** Document the rule in `asset_manifest.h` and enforce it at parse time: either resolve
`directory` against `source_path`'s parent, or reject a `directory` that does not end in a
separator, naming the group.

#### Duplicate asset names overwrite silently, and `sprite_sheet` shares the texture namespace with `texture`

- **File:** `engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:143-153`, `engine/assets/sprite_sheet_loader.cpp:33`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6

**What:** Both stores the loaders write into replace on a repeated name rather than rejecting it,
so a manifest naming the same asset twice — or naming a `texture` and a `sprite_sheet` the same
thing — resolves quietly to "last one wins", and in the cross-kind case leaves a live
`SpriteSheet` pointing at a freed texture.

**Evidence:**

`engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:146-152` — the sheet's texture is deliberately filed under the
*sheet's* name, in the same registry `kind: "texture"` writes to:

    // The sheet's texture is loaded under the sheet's own name: they are one
    // asset with two files, and the manifest names it once.
    this->load_texture(directory, name);

    this->render_resources_->add_sprite_sheet(name,
        read_sprite_sheet((directory + name + ".json").c_str(),
            this->render_resources_->texture(name)));

`engine/core/registry.h:63-71` — what `add` does with a repeat:

    void add(const std::string& name, Storage resource)
    {
        const auto it = this->indices_.find(name);
        if (it != this->indices_.end())
        {
            this->entries_[static_cast<size_t>(it->second)].resource =
                std::move(resource);
            return;
        }

`engine/render/sprite_sheet.h:92` — and what the sheet holds:

    ID3D11ShaderResourceView* texture_ = nullptr;

`engine/assets/sprite_sheet_loader.cpp:33` writes frames into a `NameTable` with the same
replace-on-repeat semantics (`name_table.h:36-48`), so two frames called `"paint"` in
`sprite_sheet_1.json` silently become one.

**Why it matters:** The manifest is the one file a person edits to add an asset, and a
copy-pasted line with an unchanged name is the likeliest mistake they will make. Nothing reports
it. The cross-kind case is worse than "wrong sprite", which is how it reads at first: the texture
registry's storage is a `ComPtr`, so a later `texture` entry with the same name as an earlier
`sprite_sheet` *assigns over the ComPtr*, drops the last reference, destroys the
`ID3D11ShaderResourceView` — and `SpriteSheet::texture_` is a bare pointer that nobody updates.
The next frame samples freed memory from every render worker. Neither case is live in the shipped
manifest (there is no `texture` group, and `sprite_sheet_1.json` has no duplicate `"name"` values
— I checked), so this is latent. Note also that the sound-bank loader *does* reject duplicates
explicitly (`sound_bank_loader.cpp:56-63`), with a comment explaining why: one of the three
loaders has the right behaviour and the module has no shared rule.

**Remedy:** Have `ResourceLoader::load_manifest` reject a `(namespace, name)` pair it has already
seen in this walk, naming both groups and the manifest file — and say in `resource_loader.h` that
`sprite_sheet` and `texture` share one namespace.

#### Tests compile engine translation units instead of linking the engine library

- **File:** `tests/assets/CMakeLists.txt:3-15` *(reviewer cited 3-19)*
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Targets and layout ("Tests link libraries, never `#include` implementation files")

**What:** The assets test target compiles `asset_manifest_loader.cpp` and `json_loader.cpp` a
second time into its own executable rather than linking `ArtAttackEngine`, and re-declares the
engine's include paths by hand.

**Evidence:**

`tests/assets/CMakeLists.txt:3-15`:

    # The manifest loader reads a file and parses JSON, and that is all it does -
    # no device, no DirectXTK - so this target compiles the two translation units
    # directly rather than linking the engine and everything the engine drags in.
    add_executable(AssetsTests
        asset_manifest_loader_tests.cpp
        test_main.cpp
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/engine/assets/asset_manifest_loader.cpp"
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/engine/assets/json_loader.cpp"
    )
    target_include_directories(AssetsTests PRIVATE
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}"
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/external/rapidjson/include"
    )

`engine/CMakeLists.txt:50-53` is what it is dodging:

    target_link_libraries(ArtAttackEngine
        PUBLIC MattMath Microsoft::DirectXTK d3d11 dxgi dxguid
        PRIVATE artattack_settings
    )

`tests/math/CMakeLists.txt` links `MattMath`, as the target table says tests do.

**Why it matters:** Two costs, both structural. It masks the real problem it was written to dodge:
`ArtAttackEngine` exports `Microsoft::DirectXTK d3d11 dxgi dxguid` as **PUBLIC** link
dependencies, so "everything below the platform edge is … linkable and constructible without a
window" is not true of the engine target as it stands, and every future headless test will copy
this workaround rather than fix the seam. And the source list is maintained by hand: the moment
`asset_manifest_loader.cpp` calls into anything else in `engine/`, this target stops linking and
the cheap fix will be to add another source path.

I dropped the reviewer's lead claim that "what is tested is not what ships: the two objects can
diverge". Both builds link `artattack_settings` and the engine keeps it `PRIVATE`, so today the
two objects compile under identical flags; the divergence risk is confined to the hand-copied
include directories and to any `PUBLIC` compile property the engine gains later.

**Remedy:** Link `ArtAttackEngine` (a static library contributes only the objects the test
references), or, if the platform link deps genuinely must stay `PUBLIC`, split the pure-data
loaders into a small library that both the engine and the tests link.

#### `load_sprite_font` reports every failure as "not found", including four kinds of corrupt file

- **File:** `engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:129-141`, `engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:169-181`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6
- **Origin:** added-by-verifier

**What:** The two loaders that do satisfy T6's "name the file" both catch `std::exception` and
throw a new message without `e.what()`, so every failure mode — corrupt file, wrong format, null
device, out of memory — is reported as the one failure mode the message names.

**Evidence:**

`engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:129-141`:

    {
        this->render_resources_->add_sprite_font(name,
            std::make_unique<SpriteFont>(this->device_,
                std::wstring(font_path.begin(), font_path.end()).c_str()));
    }
    catch (const std::exception&)

#### A UTF-8 BOM makes any content file fail as "Invalid value (offset 0)"

- **File:** `engine/assets/json_loader.cpp:63-72`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6
- **Origin:** added-by-verifier

**What:** `read_json_file` hands the raw bytes to `Document::Parse`, which has no BOM handling, so
a content file saved as "UTF-8 with BOM" fails with a message that names the file but describes
the wrong problem and points at the wrong place.

**Evidence:**

`engine/assets/json_loader.cpp:63-72`:

    rapidjson::Document document;
    document.Parse(text.c_str(), text.size());
    if (document.HasParseError())
    {
        throw std::runtime_error(
            std::string("read_json_file - '") + path +
            "' is not valid JSON: " +
            rapidjson::GetParseError_En(document.GetParseError()) +
            " (offset " + std::to_string(document.GetErrorOffset()) + ")");
    }

`external/rapidjson/include/rapidjson/reader.h:266-272` — the whole of what the parser will skip
before the first value:

    void SkipWhitespace(InputStream& is) {
        internal::StreamLocalCopy<InputStream> copy(is);
        InputStream& s(copy.s);

        typename InputStream::Ch c;
        while ((c = s.Peek()) == ' ' || c == '\n' || c == '\r' || c == '\t')
            s.Take();

**Why it matters:** rapidjson deliberately leaves BOM handling to `EncodedInputStream` /
`AutoUTFInputStream`, which this path does not use, so a leading `EF BB BF` is an ordinary
invalid character: the loader reports `is not valid JSON: Invalid value (offset 0)` for a file
that a person looking at it in an editor can see is perfectly good JSON. The trigger is not
exotic on this project — Windows PowerShell's `Out-File`/`>` write UTF-8 *with* BOM by default,
"Save as UTF-8 with BOM" is one click in most editors, and every file this module reads is
hand-authored. The failure is loud, which T6 asks for; it just blames the wrong thing, which is
the expensive half.

**Remedy:** Skip a leading `\xEF\xBB\xBF` before `Parse`, in the one place all four schemas go
through.

#### `const` on the loading methods carries no information

- **File:** `engine/assets/resource_loader.h:84, 103-116`, `engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:94, 108-186`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T5 ("`const`, `noexcept` and `[[nodiscard]]` carry information the compiler enforces")
- **Origin:** added-by-verifier

**What:** `reload_device_resources` and all five `load_*`/`reload_*` helpers are declared `const`
while destroying and rebuilding every texture, font, sprite sheet and sound bank in the process.
The `const` binds only to the raw member pointers, so it constrains nothing a reader cares about.

**Evidence:**

`engine/assets/resource_loader.h:84`:

    void reload_device_resources() const;

`engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:108-121`:

    void ResourceLoader::load_texture(const std::string& directory,
        const std::string& name) const
    {
        ...
        this->render_resources_->add_texture(name, texture_view.Get());

**Why it matters:** The engine has just spent a commit (`ca4d228`) making `draw()` `const` all
the way down precisely so that the keyword means "this is a pure read" and the compiler enforces
it. Here it means "this mutates everything, through a pointer" — the one place in the codebase
where a `const` member function is the most destructive call in the API. A stranger reading
`reload_device_resources() const` has to open the implementation to learn it reloads the world,
which is exactly the cost PHILOSOPHY's "a stranger starts from the headers" is meant to avoid,
and it devalues the signal everywhere else it is used correctly. `load_manifest` is
(correctly) non-const, so the class is already inconsistent with itself.

**Remedy:** Drop `const` from the six methods that write into `RenderResources` or
`AudioResources`. Nothing calls them through a `const ResourceLoader&`.

    sounds/sound_bank_1.xwb    148M   the only file the loader opens
    textures/old textures      8.3M
    textures/sprite_sheet_1.png 8.7M
    textures/sprite_sheet_1.xcf 176K
    textures/texconv.exe       924K
    textures/sprite_sheet_1.dds 2.2M  the only texture the loader opens

**Why it matters:** Adding a `"directory": "./ui/"` group to `manifest.json` — the edit the
manifest exists to make cheap — produces a runtime `cannot open './ui/…'` because CMake never
copied the folder, four directories away from where the change was made. The sample, which is
the template a new project copies (`samples/minimal/CMakeLists.txt:38-43` hardcodes `fonts`),
teaches the same pattern. The comment above the block is thoughtful about *when* the copy runs
and silent about *what* it copies: a clean build writes ~316 MB per configuration where ~150 MB
is needed, and `content/textures` ships an executable (`texconv.exe`) into the build output.

Regraded to low: the directory list is arguably the honest, boring thing for a build file that
ARCHITECTURE wants to stay "a dozen honest lines", the failure it produces is loud, and the rest
is disk rather than correctness. `asset_manifest.h`'s claim is narrowly true — the *loader* does
not change — and misleading only if read as "and nothing else does either".

**Remedy:** Say in `asset_manifest.h` that a new `directory` needs a line in the project's build
file, and give the copy an explicit source list (or an exclusion list) so the authoring tree stops
shipping.

---

#### Conventions breaches in the new `json_loader.cpp`

- **File:** `engine/assets/json_loader.cpp:1-28`, `engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:5-7`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Types, CONVENTIONS/Never, CONVENTIONS/Files

**What:** Two types are named in snake_case, a constant is SCREAMING_SNAKE, and two files order
their includes with the standard library before external headers.

**Evidence:**

`engine/assets/json_loader.cpp:14-28`:

    struct file_closer
    {
        void operator()(FILE* fp) const noexcept
    ...
    using unique_file = std::unique_ptr<FILE, file_closer>;

    // Big enough that every asset in the project is read in one or two calls,
    // small enough to sit comfortably on the stack.
    constexpr size_t READ_CHUNK_SIZE = 64 * 1024;

`engine/assets/json_loader.cpp:1-8`:

    #include "engine/assets/json_loader.h"

    #include <cstdio>
    #include <memory>
    #include <stdexcept>
    #include <string>

    #include <rapidjson/error/en.h>

`engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:5-7` — external, standard, external:

    #include <DDSTextureLoader.h>
    #include <stdexcept>
    #include <wrl/client.h>

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS is explicit on all three. Types, aliases included, are
PascalCase. "SCREAMING constants — screaming means macro, nothing else" is in the `Never` list,
and the stated rationale is that a screaming name must always signal preprocessor danger, so
`READ_CHUNK_SIZE` costs every reader a check. Include order is "own header first … then engine
headers, then external, then standard library". This is brand-new code written after four
conventions passes, in a folder whose other four files get all three right, which is the
argument that it is an oversight rather than a disagreement.

**Remedy:** `FileCloser`, `UniqueFile`, `read_chunk_size`; move `<rapidjson/error/en.h>` and
`<wrl/client.h>` above the standard-library block.

---

#### One class of failure, three exception types

- **File:** `engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:81-83, 138-139, 179-180`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T4

**What:** "The content names something that is not there" is reported as `std::out_of_range` in
two places and `std::runtime_error` in a third, within one hundred lines of one file.

**Evidence:**

`engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:81-83` — an unregistered kind:

    throw std::out_of_range("Asset '" + entry.name + "' in '" +
        manifest.source_path + "' is of kind '" + entry.kind +
        "', which nothing registered.");

`engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:138-139` — a missing font *file*:

    throw std::out_of_range(
        "SpriteFont " + name + " not found at " + font_path + ".");

`engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:179-180` — a missing wave-bank *file*:

    throw std::runtime_error(
        "Failed to load wave bank: " + wave_bank_path);

**Why it matters:** `std::out_of_range` is the standard's "argument outside the valid range" — a
`.at()` failure — so using it for "this file is not on disk" means a caller cannot distinguish a
content-authoring error from a filesystem error, and a `catch (const std::out_of_range&)` around
a resource lookup will swallow an I/O failure. `read_json_file` and `read_asset_manifest` both
use `std::runtime_error` for the same class of thing (`json_loader.cpp:41`,
`asset_manifest_loader.cpp:19-20`), so the module already has a convention and two of its five
throw sites break it. Everything is caught as `std::exception` today (`game/main.cpp:93`), so
nothing misbehaves — this is about the API a stranger reads.

**Remedy:** `std::runtime_error` for "the file is not there or will not load"; reserve
`std::out_of_range` for handle and index failures, as `Registry` and `NameTable` already do.

### Rejected

- **"What is tested is not what ships: the two objects can diverge" (tests/assets finding, lead
  claim)** — wrong today. `ArtAttackEngine` links `artattack_settings` `PRIVATE` and
  `AssetsTests` links it directly, so both compile under identical flags; the finding survives on
  its other two legs (hand-kept source list, masked `PUBLIC` platform deps).
- **"`read_json_file` … nothing exercises it" (severity kept, claim trimmed)** — two of its five
  branches *are* exercised, by `asset_manifest_loader_tests.cpp:130-135` (cannot open) and
  `:142-145` (parse error). The finding now claims only the three genuinely unreached branches.
- **"Loading a second manifest … permanently loses" at high** — regraded to medium. The behaviour
  is documented one line above the declaration, neither shipped client calls `load_manifest`
  twice, and it additionally requires a device loss to become visible.
- **"The manifest can only name directories the build file already knows about" at medium** —
  regraded to low and merged with its own trailing note, which is the larger half. A hand-kept
  list in a build file that ARCHITECTURE wants to stay a dozen lines is a defensible design, and
  its failure is a loud runtime error.
- **"`sprite_sheet_loader.h` … the header that documents this as safe"** — reworded. The header
  does not claim safety; it claims rapidjson throws, which is a different and equally wrong
  statement, and saying so is the sharper point.
- **"the same catch misses `WaveBank::CreateInstance(index, …)`'s real throw" as a live knock-on**
  — verified as a line (`WaveBank.cpp:334`) but demoted to a parenthetical: it fires only for a
  wave bank built as *streaming*, and this project's `.xwb` is in-memory.
- **"the other three parsers are the pre-split code moved into new files … and nothing else"
  (theme)** — half checked, half restated. `git log --follow` confirms the two unguarded loaders
  arrived in `7cea2df` ("Move JSON parsing into the loaders") and the guarded one was written
  fresh in `b045a2c`; I dropped the "nothing else changed" flourish, which I did not verify
  line by line.
- **`com_exception`'s `static char[64]` and its snake_case name** — kept as a secondary note
  inside the `load_texture` finding rather than raised separately: `engine/core/throw_if_failed.h`
  belongs to the core group's file list, not this one.

<a id="g-audio"></a>

## audio — Audio

*Group `audio` · 14 findings (4 high, 6 medium, 4 low) · source `review2/verified/audio.md`, verified report.*

I re-opened every cited line in all six files of `engine/audio/`, plus every out-of-module
line the reviewer leaned on: `engine/assets/sound_bank_loader.cpp`,
`asset_manifest_loader.cpp`, `sprite_sheet_loader.cpp`, `json_loader.cpp`,
`resource_loader.{h,cpp}`, `engine/core/registry.h`, `engine/core/handle.h`,
`engine/app/application.{h,cpp}`, `engine/CMakeLists.txt`, `CMakePresets.json`,
`cmake/settings.cmake`, and the game call sites in `player`, `weapon`, `level`,
`structure_paintable` and the four menu pages. I re-derived the rapidjson union layout from
`external/rapidjson/include/rapidjson/document.h` rather than taking the reviewer's word for
it, and re-read the vendored DirectXTK (`Audio/WaveBank.cpp`, `Audio/AudioEngine.cpp`,
`Audio/SoundEffectInstance.cpp`, `Audio/SoundCommon.h`, `Inc/Audio.h`) in
`out/build/x64-debug/vcpkg_installed/…/directxtk/src/may2026-a68e548ea6.clean/`. I also
dumped the name table out of `sound_bank_1.xwb` to check whether the null-instance path is
live or latent.

The report holds up better than most. Every quoted source line matched the file, and the two
claims most likely to have been invented — that `WaveBank::CreateInstance(name)` returns an
empty `unique_ptr` instead of throwing, and that DirectXTK's audio path contains no lock —
are both exactly true (`WaveBank.cpp:356-363`; zero hits for `mutex|CRITICAL_SECTION|
lock_guard` in `AudioEngine.cpp` and `WaveBank.cpp`). What I moved is severity, and one
structural claim. I regraded four findings down. The raw JSON indexing goes critical → high:
the undefined behaviour is real, but it is gated behind a malformed content file, and the
identical defect sits in `sprite_sheet_loader.cpp`, so it is an assets-layer gap rather than
an audio catastrophe. The `const` hole and the missing voice model go high → medium: neither
misbehaves today — I checked that collision response and `Level::update` are single-threaded
(the thread pool is used only by `draw_active_level`), so the const hole is latent exactly as
the reviewer hedged, and "no mixer" is a feature that has not been built rather than a defect.
`CoUninitialize` goes medium → low: I traced every COM object that outlives the destructor
body and none of them is a `CoCreateInstance` server — DirectXTK's `IMMDeviceEnumerator`
uses are function locals at `AudioEngine.cpp:1834` and `:1880`, `IXAudio2` comes from a DLL
export, and D3D11/DXGI do not need an initialised apartment. The rule is broken; nothing
observable depends on it.

I rejected one finding outright: "give the audio module tests" is the same defect as "put the
DirectXTK types behind an interface" — same root cause, same remedy, same paragraph — so I
merged its evidence into the boundary finding rather than let the module carry two entries for
one problem. I corrected several off-by-one line citations against the DirectXTK and rapidjson
sources, and one factual error: the reviewer wrote that "`render/` at least has the `d3d11/`
folder reserved" — it does not. `engine/render/` is flat; `d3d11/` exists only in
ARCHITECTURE's tree diagram, which makes the boundary finding stronger, not weaker.

I added one finding the reviewer missed while looking straight at it: `engine/audio/` contains
no reference to `AudioEngine` at all. The audio *device* — the object that owns silent mode,
critical-error recovery, master volume and the voice pool — lives as a naked
`DirectX::AudioEngine` in `Application`, and `ResourceLoader` in the `assets` module holds a
`DirectX::AudioEngine*` member to build wave banks. ARCHITECTURE's module table lets `assets`
depend on `audio`; it does not let `assets` name the audio backend. That single missing type
is why the device-recovery finding has nowhere to live and why the mixer has nowhere to go.
I also sharpened three surviving findings: the loader's *missing-key* case is silent rather
than UB in Release (a different T6 failure the reviewer did not separate from the wrong-type
case); `SoundBankObject`'s default constructor is reachable by *omission* from a
mem-initializer list, not only by explicit call, which is what makes it worth fixing; and the
cross-bank handle problem applies to `EffectHandle` as well as `WaveHandle`.

### Themes

- **The DirectXTK edge is not at the edge.** It is in the public type vocabulary of
  `sound_bank.h` and `sound_bank_object.h` (forcing `PUBLIC` toolkit linkage), and it has
  leaked sideways into `assets` as well. No engine-owned audio type exists anywhere.
- **Load-time validation is claimed in the comments and absent in the code.** Three header
  comments promise a throw naming the offending name; the loader that would have to produce it
  neither validates its JSON nor checks what DirectXTK hands back.
- **`const` carries no information in this module.** Every mutating call is `const`, which
  punches an audio-shaped hole in the one compiler-enforced wall the project bought outright
  in `ca4d228`.
- **There is no notion of a voice, and no notion of a device.** One name is one
  `SoundEffectInstance` forever, so concurrency is a content-authoring decision — already paid
  for in 24 JSON records and eight `WeaponDetails` fields — and there is no object anywhere
  that could hold a bus, a master volume, or a recovery retry.
- **Failure modes are inherited from the backend rather than chosen.** DirectXTK's
  trace-and-continue habit shows through `play_wave`, `CreateInstance` and `AudioEngine::Update`
  unconverted.
- **Nothing here is tested and nothing here can be tested**, because `SoundBank`'s only
  constructor demands a live `DirectX::WaveBank`, which demands a live `AudioEngine`.

#### Validate the sound-bank JSON instead of indexing it raw

- **File:** `engine/assets/sound_bank_loader.cpp:14-22,51-54,73-78`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6

**What:** `read_sound_bank` reads six JSON members with rapidjson's unchecked
`operator[]`/`GetArray()`/`GetString()`/`GetBool()`. In the Release build a wrong-typed key is
undefined behaviour and a missing key is silence — the exact pair of hazards the sibling
manifest loader documents and guards against, one file away.

**Evidence:**

    // sound_bank_loader.cpp:73-78
    const Document doc = read_json_file(json_path);

    auto instances = decode_instances(*wave_bank,
        doc["waves"],
        doc["sound_effect_instances"],
        doc["create_effect_instance_for_each_wave"].GetBool());

    // sound_bank_loader.cpp:14-22
    std::vector<std::string> decode_wave_names(const Value& json)
    {
        std::vector<std::string> wave_names;
        for (auto& wave : json.GetArray())
        {
            wave_names.push_back(wave.GetString());
        }
        return wave_names;
    }

    // sound_bank_loader.cpp:51-54
    for (auto& effect : instances_json.GetArray())
    {
        std::string name = effect["name"].GetString();
        std::string wave = effect["wave"].GetString();

The standard the project already set, one file away (`asset_manifest_loader.cpp:12-16`):

    // rapidjson's operator[] asserts on a missing member and GetArray() asserts
    // on the wrong type - a crash in debug and undefined behaviour in release.
    // The manifest is the one file a person edits by hand to add an asset, so
    // every read below goes through these instead and a typo comes back as a
    // sentence naming the file and the group it was in (T6).

**Why it matters:** `RAPIDJSON_ASSERT` is `assert` (`rapidjson.h:437`) and the `x64-release`
preset sets `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release`, whose MSVC defaults define `NDEBUG` — nothing in
`cmake/settings.cmake` overrides it — so every one of those asserts is compiled out of the
shipping build. Two distinct failures follow, and they are worth separating:

*Wrong type is undefined behaviour.* Change `"waves"` from an array to a string.
`GetArray()` (`document.h:1810`) loses its assert and constructs a `ConstArray` over a
`String`. The union at `document.h:2036-2098` lays `String { SizeType length; SizeType
hashcode; const Ch* str; }` over `ArrayData { SizeType size; SizeType capacity; GenericValue*
elements; }`, so `a.size` aliases the string length and `a.elements` aliases the character
pointer. `Begin()`/`End()` (`document.h:1677-1680`) then hand the range-for `length`
`GenericValue` objects starting at character data, and `wave.GetString()` dereferences
whatever it finds. That is a wild-pointer read reachable from a one-character content edit, on
the path `Application::load_manifest` → `ResourceLoader::load_sound_bank` → `read_sound_bank`.

*Missing key is silence.* In `NDEBUG`, `operator[]` on a missing member
(`document.h:1226-1256`) returns a thread-local default-constructed null `GenericValue` whose
`data_` is zeroed, so `GetArray()` yields `Begin() == End() == nullptr` and the loop simply
never runs. Delete `"waves"` and you get a bank with no instances and no message; delete
`"create_effect_instance_for_each_wave"` and `GetBool()` (`document.h:1176`) returns `false`
without complaint. Quiet degradation is precisely what T6 rules out.

Regraded from critical: the undefined behaviour is real but requires an authoring error, and
the identical pattern is in `sprite_sheet_loader.cpp:14-66`, so the durable fix is an
assets-layer one rather than an audio emergency.

**Remedy:** Promote `require_member`/`require_array`/`require_string` out of
`asset_manifest_loader.cpp`'s anonymous namespace into a shared header and route every read in
this loader — and in `sprite_sheet_loader.cpp` — through them.

#### Recover the audio engine after a device change instead of discarding the signal

- **File:** `engine/app/application.cpp:257-262`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6

**What:** `Application::update` discards the return value of `AudioEngine::Update()`, and the
tree contains no call to `IsCriticalError()` or `AudioEngine::Reset()`, so the first
default-device change silences the game permanently and says nothing.

**Evidence:**

    void Application::update()
    {
        *this->dt_ = static_cast<float>(this->timer_.GetElapsedSeconds());
        StateContext::update();
        std::ignore = this->audio_engine_->Update();
    }

DirectXTK's contract (`Inc/Audio.h:243-248`):

    DIRECTX_TOOLKIT_API bool __cdecl Update();
        // Performs per-frame processing for the audio engine, returns false if in 'silent mode'
    DIRECTX_TOOLKIT_API bool __cdecl Reset(
        _In_opt_ const WAVEFORMATEX* wfx = nullptr,
        _In_opt_z_ const wchar_t* deviceId = nullptr);

and the implementation that produces it (`Audio/AudioEngine.cpp:720-724`):

    case WAIT_OBJECT_0:     // OnCritialError
        mCriticalError = true;

        SetSilentMode();
        return false;

`grep -rn "IsCriticalError" engine/ game/ samples/` returns nothing; the only `Reset()` calls
in `engine/` are D3D `ComPtr::Reset` in `device_resources.cpp`.

**Why it matters:** Unplug a USB headset, or let Windows re-enumerate the endpoint, and
XAudio2 raises its critical-error event. `Update()` sets silent mode and returns false
forever; `AllocateVoice` then hands back null, so `WaveBank::Impl::Play` returns early at
`Audio/WaveBank.cpp:187-191` and every `play_wave`/`play_effect` in the match becomes a no-op.
The game runs on with no sound and no message for the rest of the session. This was reported
twice in the previous review — `docs/review/all-findings.md` items 8 ("Audio device loss is
explicitly caught and discarded", high) and 18 (medium) — and appears nowhere in
`IMPLEMENTED.md`'s fixed list. The only change since is that the empty `if` body became an
explicit `std::ignore`, which documents the discard rather than fixing it.

**Remedy:** On `!Update() && IsCriticalError()`, set a retry flag and attempt `Reset()` on
subsequent frames. Note in the engine API that a successful reset leaves every
`SoundEffectInstance` stopped, so looping music has to be restarted. This belongs on the
engine-owned audio device type that does not yet exist (see the module-boundary finding below),
not permanently in `Application::update`.

---

#### Fail at load when a wave name is not in the bank, as the header promises

- **File:** `engine/assets/sound_bank_loader.cpp:24-35`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6

**What:** `create_instance` catches an exception DirectXTK never throws. A misspelt wave name
produces a null `SoundEffectInstance` that is stored in the registry under its name, so the
load-time throw this module documents never happens and the failure surfaces mid-match with a
message that blames device loss.

**Evidence:**

    // sound_bank_loader.cpp:24-35
    std::unique_ptr<SoundEffectInstance> create_instance(
        WaveBank& wave_bank, const std::string& wave_name)
    {
        try
        {
            return wave_bank.CreateInstance(wave_name.c_str());
        }
        catch (const std::out_of_range&)
        {
            throw std::out_of_range("Wave with name " + wave_name + " not found");
        }
    }

What `CreateInstance` actually does on a miss (`Audio/WaveBank.cpp:356-363`):

    std::unique_ptr<SoundEffectInstance> WaveBank::CreateInstance(_In_z_ const char* name, ...)
    {
        const unsigned int index = pImpl->mReader.Find(name);
        if (index == unsigned(-1))
        {
            // We don't throw an exception here as titles often simply ignore missing assets rather than fail
            return std::unique_ptr<SoundEffectInstance>();
        }

The promise this breaks (`engine/audio/sound_bank.h:13-17`):

    // Names resolve once and are never seen again (PHILOSOPHY T7, T8). That is
    // worth more here than it looks: ... so a misspelt wave was silence with no
    // error at all. Resolved up front, the same typo throws at load, naming the
    // wave (T6).

**Why it matters:** The null goes into `Registry<SoundEffectInstance>` under its name —
`Registry::add` (`registry.h:63-76`) accepts a null `Storage` without comment.
`resolve_effect` consults only `indices_`, so it succeeds and hands back a valid-looking
handle; the throw does not arrive until `Registry::get`'s null check at `registry.h:109-113`,
i.e. at the first `play_effect`, in the middle of a match. The message it produces is
`"SoundEffectInstance 'sprayer_a0' has been released."`, which sends the reader hunting a
device-loss bug that does not exist. `game/main.cpp:24-100` wraps `app.run()` in the try, so
the whole game exits to a message box. Two further consequences of the same null:
`Registry::contains` reports the name as absent (`registry.h:125-132`), so the duplicate-name
guard at `sound_bank_loader.cpp:56-63` cannot see it; and `create_effect_instance_for_each_wave`
would silently produce a bank of nulls if the JSON `waves` list drifted from the `.xwb`. I
checked: it has not drifted — the 24 names in `sound_bank_1.json` match the bank's name table
exactly — so this is latent today, not live.

**Remedy:** Test the returned `unique_ptr` for null and throw naming the wave and the JSON
path; delete the dead `catch`. `WaveBank::CreateInstance(index)` also throws
`std::runtime_error("WaveBank::CreateInstance")` for a streaming bank
(`Audio/WaveBank.cpp:331-335`), which the current `catch` would also miss. The durable fix one
level down is for `Registry::add` to reject a null resource, since the registry's own header
promises it "never returns nullptr and never inserts on a miss" while enforcing that only on
read.

#### Put the DirectXTK types behind an engine-owned audio interface

- **File:** `engine/audio/sound_bank.h:3,26,30-31,59`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** boundary
- **Tenet:** ARCHITECTURE/Modules ("audio | core, math — the audio backend at its edge only")

**What:** DirectXTK is in the public vocabulary of the audio module rather than behind a seam:
the effect handle is parameterised on `DirectX::SoundEffectInstance`, the constructor takes a
`DirectX::WaveBank`, and `effect_state()` returns a `DirectX::SoundState` to game code. The
module therefore cannot be constructed, linked or tested without the backend.

**Evidence:**

    // sound_bank.h
    #include <Audio.h>                                                    // :3
    using EffectHandle = Registry<DirectX::SoundEffectInstance>::handle;  // :26
    SoundBank(std::unique_ptr<DirectX::WaveBank> wave_bank,               // :30
        Registry<DirectX::SoundEffectInstance> instances);                // :31
    DirectX::SoundState effect_state(EffectHandle effect) const;          // :59

    // sound_bank_object.h:44 - re-exported to every game type that makes noise
    DirectX::SoundState effect_state(SoundBank::EffectHandle effect) const;

    // engine/CMakeLists.txt - PUBLIC, because the headers above require it
    target_link_libraries(ArtAttackEngine
        PUBLIC MattMath Microsoft::DirectXTK d3d11 dxgi dxguid
        PRIVATE artattack_settings)

**Why it matters:** PHILOSOPHY (Targets and layout) says platform code "lives at the edge
behind engine-owned interfaces, so that a second platform is an addition, not a rewrite", and
ARCHITECTURE's module table allows the audio backend "at its edge only". Four concrete costs
today.

1. A game file that plays a sound compiles `<Audio.h>` and names `DirectX::SoundState`, so a
   second backend is a rewrite of every call site rather than an addition.
2. `SoundBank` cannot be constructed without a real `DirectX::WaveBank`, whose only public
   constructor is `WaveBank(AudioEngine*, const wchar_t* wbFileName)` (`Inc/Audio.h`, ending
   `:355`) — so it needs a live device and a real `.xwb` on disk. That is why `tests/` contains
   `assets`, `core` and `math` and nothing else, and why every documented contract in these
   headers is currently only a claim: that `resolve_wave` throws naming the wave
   (`sound_bank.cpp:23-28`), that a play through an unresolved handle throws
   (`sound_bank.cpp:41-45`), that `clamp_levels` maps out-of-range levels
   (`sound_bank.cpp:104-109`). `tests/core/registry_tests.cpp` covers the handle machinery
   underneath, which makes the gap here more visible, not less. PHILOSOPHY's "everything below
   the platform edge is testable headlessly" is false for this module.
3. The `PUBLIC` link puts DirectXTK on the include and link line of every engine consumer
   whether it makes a noise or not.
4. There is nowhere for a backend to go: `engine/` on disk is
   `app assets audio collision core input math render ui` and `engine/render/` is flat —
   contrary to the raw report, `render/d3d11/` does **not** exist. The `d3d11/` and `xinput/`
   folders live only in ARCHITECTURE's tree diagram, and `audio/` is not given one even there,
   though the module table demands the backend sit at its edge.

**Remedy:** Give the module an engine-owned `SoundState` enum and an internal handle tag, move
the `DirectX::*` types into an `audio/xaudio2/` implementation folder the public headers do not
include, and drop DirectXTK to `PRIVATE` linkage. Then pin `resolve_*`, the unresolved-handle
throws and the clamping in `tests/audio/sound_bank_tests.cpp` against a null backend, and
amend ARCHITECTURE's tree to name the audio backend folder alongside `render/d3d11/`.

---

#### Make the mutating audio calls non-const

- **File:** `engine/audio/sound_bank.h:45-60`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T5

**What:** Every state-changing method on `SoundBank`, `SoundBankObject` and `AudioResources` is
`const`, so a `const` object can start, stop and re-level voices and the compiler cannot
object.

**Evidence:**

    // sound_bank.h:45-58
    void play_wave(WaveHandle wave, float volume = 1.0f,
        float pitch = 0.0f, float pan = 0.0f) const;
    void play_effect(EffectHandle effect, bool loop = false, float volume = 1.0f,
        float pitch = 0.0f, float pan = 0.0f) const;
    void stop_effect(EffectHandle effect, bool immediate = false) const;
    void set_effect_volume(EffectHandle effect, float volume) const;

    // sound_bank.cpp:62-65 - mutation through a const method
    void SoundBank::stop_effect(EffectHandle effect, bool immediate) const
    {
        this->sound_effect_instance(effect)->Stop(immediate);
    }

    // audio_resources.h:26-28 - the const method that hands out the mutable bank,
    // under a comment that calls itself non-mutating
    // Const and non-mutating, like every other registry getter: throws
    // std::out_of_range naming the bank if it is absent or released.
    SoundBank* sound_bank(SoundBankHandle sound_bank) const;

It compiles because `const std::unique_ptr<T>::operator->` still yields a non-const `T*`. Game
code already leans on it — `game/objects/level.cpp:341-347`:

    void Level::stop_player_sounds() const
    {
        for (const auto& player : *this->player_objects_)
        {
            player->stop_sounds();
        }
    }

**Why it matters:** `IMPLEMENTED.md` records that making `draw()` `const` everywhere
(`ca4d228`) was bought specifically so "a `draw()` that assigns a member is now a compile error
rather than something an audit has to keep catching", and PHILOSOPHY leans on the same wall for
parallel rendering. That wall has an audio-shaped hole: `Player::draw` is
`const override` (`player.h:88-89`) and `Player` holds `artattack::SoundBank* sound_bank_`
(`player.h:168`), so `this->sound_bank_->play_wave(...)` inside a `const draw()` compiles
cleanly. `Level::draw_active_level` (`level.cpp:393-417`) fans that path out over the thread
pool, and DirectXTK's audio contains no `mutex`, `CRITICAL_SECTION` or `lock_guard` anywhere in
`Audio/AudioEngine.cpp` or `Audio/WaveBank.cpp` — I grepped both, zero hits.

Regraded from high, because no current `draw()` does it and nothing else is concurrent: the
thread pool is used in `level.cpp` only at lines 397-417, so collision response
(`structure_paintable.cpp:86`) and `Level::update` are single-threaded. This is a latent hole
whose closing cost rises with every game written against the const signatures, not a live race.

**Remedy:** Drop `const` from every call that starts, stops or re-levels a voice (keep it on
`resolve_*`, `effect_state`, `is_effect_looping`), and let `AudioResources::sound_bank()` return
a mutable bank only from a non-const overload — and fix the header comment above it, which
currently tells the reader the opposite of what the function enables.

---

#### Model a voice, not a name: one effect name is one instance forever

- **File:** `engine/audio/sound_bank.h:26,41,51`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T9 ("Build the mixer, buy the audio backend")

**What:** A persistent sound is addressed by the name of a pre-created `SoundEffectInstance`,
so the number of simultaneous copies of a sound is fixed at content-authoring time, and the
module supplies none of the mixing machinery T9 names as the engine's to build — no buses or
categories, no master or group volume, no voice pool.

**Evidence:**

    // sound_bank.h:26,41,51
    using EffectHandle = Registry<DirectX::SoundEffectInstance>::handle;
    EffectHandle resolve_effect(const std::string& effect_name) const;
    void play_effect(EffectHandle effect, bool loop = false, float volume = 1.0f, ...) const;

The price, already paid in the game's data (`game/content/sounds/sound_bank_1.json:31-64`,
then the same again for `roller_*` at `:63-96` and `mister_*` at `:95-128`):

    { "name": "sprayer_a0", "wave": "WaterSprayIntoBucket" },
    { "name": "sprayer_a1", "wave": "WaterSprayIntoBucket" },
    ... eight of these, then eight roller_*, then eight mister_* — 24 records

and in the game's types (`game/objects/weapon_details.h:22-29`):

    std::string shoot_sound_name_a0 = "";
    ... through shoot_sound_name_b3

which `Weapon::resolve_loop_sound` (`game/objects/weapon.cpp:269-303`) selects between by
`(team, player_num)`.

**Why it matters:** Twenty-four JSON records and eight struct fields exist only because two
players cannot play the same looping sound — they would share one `SoundEffectInstance`, so the
first player to stop firing would silence the second. That is the engine pushing its own missing
mechanism into the client's content and type definitions, the inverse of T1. It also caps what
the engine can offer: with no bus or category there is no way to build the options-menu
music/SFX sliders any game will want, and `AudioEngine::SetMasterVolume` (`Inc/Audio.h:258`) is
never surfaced at all.

Regraded from high: nothing here misbehaves. This is a mechanism that has not been built yet,
correctly identified, and its cost is real but currently paid in content rather than in bugs.

**Remedy:** Make `play_effect` return a voice handle drawn from an engine-sized pool, and add a
small bus/category layer with per-bus volume — the mixer T9 asks for. It deletes the `_a0`…`_b3`
naming scheme from both the JSON and `WeaponDetails`.

---

#### The audio module owns no audio device, so the backend leaks into `app` and `assets`

- **File:** `engine/assets/resource_loader.h:49,93`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** boundary
- **Tenet:** ARCHITECTURE/Modules
- **Origin:** added by verifier

**What:** `engine/audio/` contains no reference to `AudioEngine` of any kind. The audio device —
the object that owns silent mode, critical-error recovery, master volume, output-format and the
voice pool — exists only as a naked `DirectX::AudioEngine` held by `Application`, and a second
raw pointer to it is a member of `ResourceLoader` in the `assets` module.

**Evidence:**

    $ grep -rn "AudioEngine" engine/ | grep -v "^engine/app/"
    engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:16:   DirectX::AudioEngine* audio_engine) :
    engine/assets/resource_loader.h:49:         DirectX::AudioEngine* audio_engine);
    engine/assets/resource_loader.h:93:      DirectX::AudioEngine* audio_engine_ = nullptr;

    // engine/app/application.h:144 - the device, owned by the shell
    std::unique_ptr<DirectX::AudioEngine> audio_engine_ = nullptr;

    // engine/app/application.cpp:261 - and driven by it, per frame
    std::ignore = this->audio_engine_->Update();

ARCHITECTURE's module table:

    | `audio`  | core, math — the audio backend at its edge only |
    | `assets` | core, math, render, audio, rapidjson            |

**Why it matters:** `assets` is permitted to depend on `audio`; it is not permitted to name the
audio backend, and `render`'s row makes the distinction explicit by confining DirectXTK to
`d3d11/`. More importantly this is the root cause of two other findings on this page rather than
a separate stylistic complaint: the device-change recovery has nowhere in `engine/audio/` to
live, so it sits unwritten in `Application::update`; and the missing mixer has no object to hang
a master volume or a bus off. A module described in ARCHITECTURE as "playback, mixing" currently
contains a handle cache and nothing else. It also means `Application` — the shell, whose job is
assembly — knows the backend's per-frame contract, which is a thing a shell should be told about
through an engine interface, not something it should be responsible for calling correctly.

**Remedy:** Introduce an engine-owned audio device type in `engine/audio/` that owns the backend
engine, exposes `update()`, a device-recovery path, and master volume, and hands `assets` an
engine-typed factory for wave banks instead of a `DirectX::AudioEngine*`. `Application` then
constructs it once like every other service and calls one engine method per frame.

#### Replace the SoundBankObject base class with a plain SoundBank borrow

- **File:** `engine/audio/sound_bank_object.h:17-57`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T11 ("Inheritance and virtual dispatch are tools of last resort")

**What:** `SoundBankObject` is inheritance used purely to reuse implementation: it stores two
members and forwards eleven methods verbatim, and the engine asks game types to derive from it to
get them.

**Evidence:**

    // sound_bank_object.cpp:31-40 - the whole class is this, eleven times
    void SoundBankObject::play_wave(SoundBank::WaveHandle wave, float volume,
        float pitch, float pan) const
    {
        this->sound_bank()->play_wave(wave, volume, pitch, pan);
    }
    void SoundBankObject::play_effect(SoundBank::EffectHandle effect,
        bool loop, float volume, float pitch, float pan) const
    {
        this->sound_bank()->play_effect(effect, loop, volume, pitch, pan);
    }

What deriving costs the client (`game/states/main_menu.cpp:10-15`):

    MainMenuPage::MainMenuPage(MainMenuData* data) :
        MenuPage(data),
        SoundBankObject(main_menu_consts::SOUND_BANK,
            this->audio_resources()),
        data_(data)

**Why it matters:** That mem-initializer calls a member function on a *different* base
subobject to feed this one. `MenuPage::audio_resources()` (`menu_page.cpp:81-83`) reads
`this->data_`, which `MenuPage`'s own constructor sets, so the call is well-defined only because
`MenuPage` is listed first in
`class MainMenuPage : public MenuPage, public artattack::SoundBankObject` (`main_menu.h:108`).
Reorder the base list and it reads an uninitialised member with no diagnostic. The same shape
appears in `end_menu.h:41`/`end_menu.cpp:11`, `pause_menu.h:43`/`.cpp:12` and
`results_menu.h:61`/`.cpp:12`, all with three bases. T10 says the game-facing API must stay in
the simple subset of the language; an initialisation whose correctness depends on base-list
ordering is not that. The class also has a public non-virtual destructor while being documented
as a base ("inherited for the plumbing", `sound_bank_object.h:9`), which is the classic unsafe
combination — harmless here only because nothing ever holds a `SoundBankObject*`.

The engine's own client already votes against the class: `Player` (`player.h:168`), `Weapon`
(`weapon.h:55`), `Level` (`level.h:104`) and `StructurePaintable` (`structure_paintable.h:66`)
all just hold `artattack::SoundBank*` obtained once at construction (`player.cpp:44`) and are
simpler for it. Only the four menu pages derive.

**Remedy:** Delete the class and let objects hold a `SoundBank*` from
`AudioResources::sound_bank(handle)`, which is what most of the game already does. If the
forwarding is wanted, make it a member `SoundBankRef` value rather than a base class — which
also removes the mem-initializer ordering hazard entirely, because a member is initialised after
every base.

---

#### Reject a null AudioResources instead of dereferencing it

- **File:** `engine/audio/sound_bank_object.h:20,55-56` and `engine/audio/sound_bank_object.cpp:7-18`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** lifetime
- **Tenet:** T6

**What:** The defaulted constructor leaves `audio_resources_` null and every protected method
then dereferences it without a check; the two-argument constructor dereferences its pointer
parameter in the mem-initializer list, before any body could validate it.

**Evidence:**

    // sound_bank_object.h:20,55-56
    SoundBankObject() = default;
    ...
    AudioResources::SoundBankHandle sound_bank_;
    const AudioResources* audio_resources_ = nullptr;

    // sound_bank_object.cpp:7-18
    SoundBankObject::SoundBankObject(const std::string& sound_bank_name,
                                     const AudioResources* audio_resources) :
        sound_bank_(audio_resources->resolve_sound_bank(sound_bank_name)),
        audio_resources_(audio_resources)
    { }
    SoundBank* SoundBankObject::sound_bank() const
    {
        return this->audio_resources_->sound_bank(this->sound_bank_);
    }

**Why it matters:** A default-constructed `SoundBankObject` is a loaded gun: `sound_bank()`,
every `play_*`, `resolve_*` and `set_sound_bank` null-dereference with no diagnostic, in a module
whose every other error path is a named throw. The reviewer called this unreachable because no
in-tree caller writes `SoundBankObject()` — but that understates it, and the understatement is
what makes the finding worth keeping. Because the class is a *base*, the default constructor is
selected by **omission**: a subclass author who leaves `SoundBankObject(...)` out of the
mem-initializer list — easy to do in the three-base menu pages — gets it silently, compiles
clean, and null-dereferences on the first sound. That is exactly the trap T5 exists to close, in
public engine API, for a default constructor that serves no stated purpose.

**Remedy:** Delete the default constructor — nothing needs it, and its absence turns the
omission case into a compile error. Have the remaining constructor throw `std::invalid_argument`
naming the bank if `audio_resources` is null, via a small private helper that validates and
returns the pointer so it can stay in the initializer list.

---

#### Bind a handle to the bank that produced it

- **File:** `engine/audio/sound_bank.cpp:38-50`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T6

**What:** `play_wave` checks only that the handle is not the default-constructed one, so a handle
resolved against a different bank either plays the wrong wave or is silently dropped by DirectXTK
— the failure the header says this design eliminated. `play_effect` has the same hole with a
better-behaved out-of-range case.

**Evidence:**

    void SoundBank::play_wave(WaveHandle wave, float volume, float pitch,
        float pan) const
    {
        if (!wave.valid())
        {
            throw std::out_of_range(
                "A wave was played through an unresolved handle.");
        }

        clamp_levels(volume, pitch, pan);
        this->wave_bank_->Play(static_cast<unsigned int>(wave.index()),
            volume, pitch, pan);
    }

What DirectXTK does with an out-of-range index (`Audio/WaveBank.cpp:169-174`):

    if (index >= mReader.Count())
    {
        DebugTrace("WARNING: Index %u not found in wave bank with only %u entries, "
            "one-shot not triggered\n", index, mReader.Count());
        return;
    }

The API that invites it (`sound_bank_object.h:47-50`):

    // Points this object at a different bank. Every handle resolved from the
    // old one is meaningless against the new one, so a caller doing this
    // re-resolves everything it holds.
    void set_sound_bank(const std::string& sound_bank_name);

**Why it matters:** `Handle::valid()` is only `index_ >= 0` (`engine/core/handle.h:30`), and
`Handle<Wave>` is the same type for every bank, so the phantom-type protection the header
describes catches wave-vs-effect confusion but not bank-vs-bank. Out of range gives silence with
a debug trace — precisely "a misspelt wave was silence with no error at all", which
`sound_bank.h:13-17` claims to have fixed. In range gives the wrong sound, which is worse because
it looks like it worked. The same applies to `EffectHandle`, which the raw report did not cover:
it is `Handle<DirectX::SoundEffectInstance>` for every bank alike, so a cross-bank effect handle
either throws the wrong message via `Registry::get` or plays the wrong instance. `set_sound_bank`
has no caller in the tree and the game ships one bank, so nothing triggers this today —
`Player`, `Weapon`, `Level` and `StructurePaintable` each independently call
`audio_resources->sound_bank("sound_bank_1")`, and a second bank is one manifest line away.

**Remedy:** Bounds-check the wave index against the bank before calling `Play` and throw naming
the bank, or carry a small bank id inside the handle and check it on both paths — one integer
compare, off the hot path either way.

---

#### Release COM objects before CoUninitialize, not after

- **File:** `engine/app/application.cpp:21-31`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** lifetime
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Services and lifetimes ("Construction and destruction order are designed")

**What:** `~Application` calls `CoUninitialize()` in the destructor body, which runs before any
member is destroyed — so the `AudioEngine`'s `IXAudio2`, and every D3D/DXGI `ComPtr` below it, is
released after the COM library has been shut down on that thread.

**Evidence:**

    Application::~Application()
    {
        if (this->audio_engine_)
        {
            this->audio_engine_->Suspend();
        }
        if (this->com_initialized_)
        {
            CoUninitialize();
        }
    }

The ordering the class does document (`application.h:137-144`):

    // DECLARATION ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING BELOW THIS LINE.
    // ... So audio_engine_ is declared FIRST and dies LAST.
    std::unique_ptr<DirectX::AudioEngine> audio_engine_ = nullptr;

**Why it matters:** C++ runs the destructor body first, then members in reverse declaration
order, so `audio_engine_` — declared first, deliberately — is destroyed strictly after
`CoUninitialize()`, as are `device_resources_`, `common_states_` and `sprite_batches_`. COM's
documented rule is that all interface pointers are released before `CoUninitialize`. It is a
second ordering hazard in the same destructor that finding #10 of the previous review fixed, and
it runs on every clean exit.

Regraded from medium: I traced what actually survives the destructor body, and none of it is a
`CoCreateInstance` server. DirectXTK's `IMMDeviceEnumerator` uses are function locals released
during initialisation (`Audio/AudioEngine.cpp:1834`, `:1880`); `IXAudio2` comes from the
`XAudio2Create` DLL export (`:415`); D3D11 and DXGI do not require an initialised apartment. So
this is a violation of a documented contract with nothing observable depending on it here — worth
fixing because a stranger's game will add a COM service, not because it breaks today.

**Remedy:** Reset the members explicitly, in the intended order, at the top of the destructor
body, and call `CoUninitialize()` last — which also makes the ordering readable instead of
implied by declaration position.

---

#### Reject a duplicate sound-bank name instead of silently replacing it

- **File:** `engine/audio/audio_resources.cpp:22-26`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6

**What:** `add_sound_bank` forwards to `Registry::add`, which refills an existing name's slot and
destroys the `SoundBank` that was there, so two manifest entries naming one bank leave the second
silently winning.

**Evidence:**

    void AudioResources::add_sound_bank(const std::string& sound_bank_name,
        std::unique_ptr<SoundBank> sound_bank)
    {
        this->sound_banks_.add(sound_bank_name, std::move(sound_bank));
    }

`Registry::add` (`engine/core/registry.h:63-71`):

    void add(const std::string& name, Storage resource)
    {
        const auto it = this->indices_.find(name);
        if (it != this->indices_.end())
        {
            this->entries_[static_cast<size_t>(it->second)].resource =
                std::move(resource);
            return;
        }

The same case one level down *is* guarded (`sound_bank_loader.cpp:56-63`):

    // Registry::add refills a name's slot rather than rejecting it, so
    // the duplicate check has to happen here: two definitions claiming
    // one name is a content bug, not an overwrite.
    if (instances.contains(name))

**Why it matters:** The reasoning quoted for effect instances applies verbatim to banks and was
not applied. Today the damage is contained: `Application::load_manifest` runs before any state is
constructed, so no game object holds a `SoundBank*` when an overwrite frees one, and the
sound-bank kind is skipped on a device restore (`resource_loader.cpp:62-71`). But
`ResourceLoader::load_manifest` is documented as callable more than once, and a second manifest
naming an already-loaded bank would free a `SoundBank` that `Player::sound_bank_`,
`Level::sound_bank_`, `Weapon::sound_bank_` and every `StructurePaintable` point at.

**Remedy:** Have `add_sound_bank` throw naming the bank if the registry already contains it,
matching the guard the effect-instance loader already carries.

---

#### Fix the include block in sound_bank.h

- **File:** `engine/audio/sound_bank.h:1-7`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Files

**What:** The header lists external and standard includes before engine ones, against the stated
order, and pulls in `matt_math.h`, which it does not use.

**Evidence:**

    #pragma once

    #include <Audio.h>
    #include <memory>
    #include <string>
    #include "engine/core/registry.h"
    #include "engine/math/matt_math.h"

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS/Files fixes the order as "own header first … then engine headers,
then external, then standard library", and the module's other two headers (`audio_resources.h:3-6`,
`sound_bank_object.h:3-5`) both follow it, so this file is the outlier a reader trips on. The
`matt_math.h` include is worse than cosmetic: nothing in `sound_bank.h` names anything from
`mattmath` — `clamp` (`matt_math.h:52`) is used only in the `.cpp`, which has its own
`using namespace mattmath;` — and `matt_math.h` is 1150 lines that itself pulls in `SimpleMath.h`
and `<d3d11.h>`. Since `audio_resources.h` includes this header and `application.h` includes that,
the unused include rides into most of the tree. PHILOSOPHY makes compile speed "a maintained
property — light headers, disciplined includes".

**Remedy:** Reorder to engine-then-external-then-standard, and move the `matt_math.h` include into
`sound_bank.cpp`, which is the only file in the module that needs it.

---

#### Stop silently clamping levels, and stop writing the ranges four times

- **File:** `engine/audio/sound_bank.cpp:74-88,104-109`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T1

**What:** Volume is silently capped at 1.0 where the backend accepts far more, and the same three
ranges are written out in four separate places.

**Evidence:**

    void SoundBank::set_effect_volume(EffectHandle effect, float volume) const
    {
        volume = clamp(volume, 0.0f, 1.0f);
        ...
    void SoundBank::set_effect_pitch(EffectHandle effect, float pitch) const
    {
        pitch = clamp(pitch, -1.0f, 1.0f);
        ...
    void SoundBank::set_effect_pan(EffectHandle effect, float pan) const
    {
        pan = clamp(pan, -1.0f, 1.0f);
        ...
    void SoundBank::clamp_levels(float& volume, float& pitch, float& pan)
    {
        volume = clamp(volume, 0.0f, 1.0f);
        pitch = clamp(pitch, -1.0f, 1.0f);
        pan = clamp(pan, -1.0f, 1.0f);
    }

What the backend actually accepts (`Audio/SoundCommon.h:256-258`, and the same bound at
`Audio/WaveBank.cpp:159`):

    void SetVolume(float volume)
    {
        assert(volume >= -XAUDIO2_MAX_VOLUME_LEVEL && volume <= XAUDIO2_MAX_VOLUME_LEVEL);

**Why it matters:** Capping at 1.0 is an engine policy that removes a capability from the game — a
quiet source asset cannot be boosted — and removes it silently, which is the graceful degradation
T6 rules out for a broken contract. Neither the cap nor the accepted ranges appear in
`sound_bank.h`, so a caller passing 1.5 has no way to learn what happened. The four-way
duplication is small now and is exactly the kind that diverges: pitch and pan already have their
bounds stated twice each.

**Remedy:** State the accepted ranges in the header, have the three setters call `clamp_levels`
rather than repeat it, and either raise the volume ceiling to the backend's or document the 1.0
cap as a deliberate engine decision with its reason.

---

### Rejected

- **"Give the audio module tests, and a seam that makes them possible"** (`sound_bank.h:30-31`,
  medium) — rejected as a duplicate. It is the same defect and the same remedy as the DirectXTK
  boundary finding: nothing here can be tested *because* the constructor demands a live
  `DirectX::WaveBank`. Its evidence (the contents of `tests/`, the list of unpinned contracts,
  `WaveBank`'s only public constructor) has been merged into that finding rather than discarded.
- **"critical" on the raw JSON indexing** — rejected as a grade, kept as a finding at high. The
  undefined behaviour is real and I re-derived it from the rapidjson union layout, but it is
  gated behind an authoring error in a content file, and `sprite_sheet_loader.cpp` has the
  identical defect, which makes it an assets-layer gap rather than an audio emergency.
- **"high" on the const hole** — rejected as a grade, kept at medium. Verified there is no live
  race: the thread pool is entered only from `Level::draw_active_level`, and no `draw()` on that
  path touches audio. The reviewer's own text said "latent", and the grade should have matched.
- **"high" on the missing voice model** — rejected as a grade, kept at medium. Nothing
  misbehaves; this is a mechanism that has not been built, priced accurately in content.
- **"medium" on CoUninitialize ordering** — rejected as a grade, kept at low. I checked every COM
  object that outlives the destructor body: DirectXTK's device enumerators are function locals,
  `IXAudio2` is a DLL export, D3D11/DXGI need no apartment. Contract violated, nothing observable
  behind it.
- **"`render/` at least has the `d3d11/` folder reserved for this"** — rejected as a factual
  error inside the boundary finding. `engine/render/` is flat on disk; `d3d11/` exists only in
  ARCHITECTURE's tree diagram. Corrected in place, and it strengthens the finding.
- **Line-number corrections applied silently** — `asset_manifest_loader.cpp:11-14` → `12-16`;
  `WaveBank.cpp:167-172` → `169-174`; `WaveBank.cpp:186-190` → `187-191`; `WaveBank.cpp:158` →
  `159`; `AudioEngine.cpp:1834` (enumerator) is the `ComPtr` declaration, the
  `CoCreateInstance` is at `:1835`; `registry.h:63-72` → `63-71` for the refill branch;
  `sound_bank.h:1-8` → `1-7`; `sound_bank_1.json:32-63` → `31-64`; `level.cpp:341-348` →
  `341-347`; `sound_bank.h:14-17` → `13-17`.
