#### The engine hardcodes the icon resource name only the paint-shooter defines

- **File:** `game/resource.rc:1`, `engine/app/application.cpp:85-89`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** boundary
- **Tenet:** T1; T6

**What:** `Application` looks up a fixed resource string `IDI_ICON` that only
`game/resource.rc` provides, `ApplicationOptions` has no field for it, and
`samples/minimal` ships no `.rc` — so the template a stranger copies gets the default
Windows icon and no indication why.

**Evidence:**

`game/resource.rc` (UTF-16, one line):

    IDI_ICON                ICON                "directx.ico"

`engine/app/application.cpp:85-89`

    		window_class.hIcon = LoadIconW(instance, L"IDI_ICON");
    		window_class.hCursor = LoadCursorW(nullptr, IDC_ARROW);
    		window_class.hbrBackground = reinterpret_cast<HBRUSH>(COLOR_WINDOW + 1);
    		window_class.lpszClassName = this->options_.window_class_name.c_str();
    		window_class.hIconSm = LoadIconW(instance, L"IDI_ICON");

`samples/minimal/` contains `CMakeLists.txt`, `content`, `main.cpp`, `states` — no `.rc`,
no `.ico`, and its `add_executable` lists only two sources. `ApplicationOptions`
(`application.h:30-52`) carries `window_class_name`, `window_title`, `resolution`,
`fullscreen`, thread counts and minimum window size, and nothing for an icon.

**Why it matters:** `ApplicationOptions`' own comment says it holds "a decision only the
game can make … which is exactly why none of it is compiled into the engine (T1)" — and
then the icon, unambiguously a game decision, is compiled into the engine as a magic
string. `LoadIconW` returning `nullptr` is not an error, so the sample fails silently: a
stranger following ARCHITECTURE's "starting a game is copying `samples/minimal/`" has no
way to discover that an icon means naming a resource `IDI_ICON` in a `.rc` nobody told
them to create. The name works only because `resource.rc` `#include`s nothing that would
`#define` it, so `rc.exe` records it as a string and the string lookup happens to match.

**Remedy:** Add an icon field to `ApplicationOptions` — an `HICON`, or the resource name
to look up — default it to none, and set it in `game/main.cpp`.

#### `game/pch.h` is compiled at warning level 0, and hides a would-be `/WX` error

- **File:** `game/pch.h:14-31`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Tests and toolchain ("warnings are errors with zero suppressions")

**What:** `pch.h` re-`#define`s `NOMINMAX` and `WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN`, which
`artattack_settings` already supplies on the command line. That is C4005 — an error under
`/WX` — and the only reason the build is green is that CMake's generated PCH wrapper
carries `#pragma system_header` and the game is compiled with `-external:W0`, so `pch.h`
and everything it includes are inspected at warning level 0.

**Evidence:**

`game/pch.h:14-15` and `:31`

    // Use the C++ standard templated min/max
    #define NOMINMAX
    ...
    #define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN

`cmake/settings.cmake` already has them:

    target_compile_definitions(artattack_settings INTERFACE
        UNICODE _UNICODE
        WIN32 _WINDOWS
        NOMINMAX             # std::min/max, never the Windows.h macros
        WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
    )

and the generated command line carries `-DNOMINMAX -DWIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN` on every game
TU alongside `/W4 /WX`. I verified the mechanism rather than assuming it. Compiling a
file that redefines `NOMINMAX` with `cl /W4 /WX /DNOMINMAX`:

    warning C4005: 'NOMINMAX': macro redefinition
    note: 'NOMINMAX' previously declared on the command line

Compiling the same thing behind a wrapper holding `#pragma system_header`, with
`-external:W0` added — which is exactly what
`out/build/x64-debug/game/CMakeFiles/ArtAttackGame.dir/cmake_pch.hxx` is and exactly what
the game's `INCLUDES` line ends with — succeeds silently, and swallows an unreferenced
local in the same header for good measure.

**Why it matters:** PHILOSOPHY promises "warnings are errors with zero suppressions", and
here is a blanket suppression over an authored game header and one engine header
(`engine/core/throw_if_failed.h`), arrived at by accident rather than decision. Nothing is
currently hidden except these two redefinitions — the engine target compiles
`throw_if_failed.h` normally — but the exemption is permanent and invisible, and anything
added to `pch.h` from now on is uninspected.

**Remedy:** Delete both `#define`s from `pch.h` and let the shared settings target own
them alone, which is the point of having one. If the version block above goes too, `pch.h`
becomes a pure include list and the exemption stops mattering.

#### `ctime_s` returns an error code, not the string, so the save log prints "0"

- **File:** `game/save.cpp:109-112`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** —

**What:** The timestamp line streams `ctime_s`'s `errno_t` return value instead of the
buffer it filled, so the line reads `0 Saving...` and `buffer` is written and never read.

**Evidence:**

    	auto start = std::chrono::system_clock::now();
    	auto legacy_start = std::chrono::system_clock::to_time_t(start);
    	char buffer[30];
    	std::cout << ctime_s(buffer, sizeof(buffer), &legacy_start) << " Saving...\n";

The CRT declares `errno_t __cdecl ctime_s(char* _Buffer, size_t _SizeInBytes, const
__time64_t* _Time);` — the formatted time goes into `_Buffer` and the return is a status
code. `/W4` does not object, because the value *is* used: it is streamed as an `int`.

**Why it matters:** Regraded down from medium. The defect is real and unambiguous, but its
consequence is not: this line writes to `std::cout` in a `/SUBSYSTEM:WINDOWS` process, so
nobody has ever read the wrong value either. It matters as a latent bug that will bite the
moment the first finding gives this code a channel that works — not as a live diagnostic
failure today.

**Remedy:** Check the return, then print `buffer`; or drop `<ctime>` and format with
`<chrono>`, which `save.h` already drags in.

#### A repeated level name in the manifest silently doubles a stage in the menu

- **File:** `game/main.cpp:60-72`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6

**What:** The `level` loader pushes a `Stage` before calling `Registry::add`, and `add`
merges a repeated name into its existing slot and returns, so a manifest naming a level
twice yields two identical stage-select tiles backed by one registry slot.

**Evidence:**

`game/main.cpp:60-72`

    		app.resource_loader()->register_kind("level",
    			{
    				[&level_infos, &stages](const std::string& directory,
    					const std::string& name)
    				{
    					auto info = std::make_unique<LevelLoadedInfo>(
    						(directory + name + ".json").c_str());
    					stages.push_back(Stage{ name, info->display_name(),
    						info->icon_frame() });
    					level_infos.add(name, std::move(info));
    				},
    				nullptr
    			});

`engine/core/registry.h:63-76`

    		void add(const std::string& name, Storage resource)
    		{
    			const auto it = this->indices_.find(name);
    			if (it != this->indices_.end())
    			{
    				this->entries_[static_cast<size_t>(it->second)].resource =
    					std::move(resource);
    				return;
    			}
    			...
    		}

`game/content/manifest.json` names levels as a flat array of three strings under one
`"names"` key — exactly the shape a copy-paste duplicates.

**Why it matters:** Regraded down from medium. The mechanism is exactly as described and
the registry genuinely cannot report it — re-adding a name is its documented
device-restore behaviour, so this lambda is the only place a check can live. But it needs
a content-authoring mistake to reach, and its symptom is two visibly identical tiles that
both play the same level, not a crash or a corruption. It is worth fixing because four
lines below, `main.cpp` already refuses to start with *zero* levels "rather than discover
that by dividing by zero three screens later (T6)" — the same instinct, one case over.

**Remedy:** Check `level_infos.contains(name)` first and throw naming the level and the
manifest, matching the empty-stage-list throw below it. (The `nullptr` reload half is
correct and intentional — `reload_device_resources` skips empty kinds, verified at
`resource_loader.cpp:101`.)

#### Applying settings writes the save file twice

- **File:** `game/save.cpp:123-133`, `game/states/main_menu.cpp:334-342`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T4

**What:** `set_resolution_and_save` and `set_full_screen_and_save` each perform a full
serialise-and-write, so one "apply" in the options menu does two complete file writes.

**Evidence:**

    void Save::set_resolution_and_save(ScreenResolution resolution)
    {
        this->save_data_.resolution = resolution;
        this->save_to_file();
    }

    void Save::set_full_screen_and_save(bool full_screen)
    {
        this->save_data_.fullscreen = full_screen;
    	this->save_to_file();
    }

and the caller invokes both inside one apply — `main_menu.cpp:334` and `:342`.

**Why it matters:** Two synchronous `fopen`/serialise/`fclose` cycles on the thread
running the frame loop for one button press, and the count grows with the number of
settings. A crash or power loss between them leaves the file holding a new resolution and
an old fullscreen flag. Neither is severe with two fields; both scale badly, and the shape
is the defect.

**Remedy:** Split into `set_resolution` / `set_fullscreen` plus an explicit
`save_to_file()` the menu calls once.

#### The sample has no hybrid-GPU export, so a copied project runs on the integrated part

- **File:** `game/main.cpp:14-19`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** performance
- **Tenet:** T8; PHILOSOPHY/The public face

**What:** The two exported symbols that ask a hybrid-graphics laptop for the discrete GPU
exist only in the paint-shooter's `main.cpp`; `samples/minimal/main.cpp` — the file
ARCHITECTURE says a new project is copied from — does not have them.

**Evidence:**

    // Indicates to hybrid graphics systems to prefer the discrete part by default.
    extern "C"
    {
    	__declspec(dllexport) DWORD NvOptimusEnablement = 0x00000001;
    	__declspec(dllexport) int AmdPowerXpressRequestHighPerformance = 1;
    }

`grep -rn "NvOptimus" --include=*.cpp .` returns exactly one file: `game/main.cpp`.

**Why it matters:** These symbols must be exported from the *executable*, so the engine
cannot supply them from a static library — which makes them required boilerplate that
exists only in the one file a new project does not start from. A game built by copying
`samples/minimal` runs on integrated graphics on every hybrid laptop, and the author's
first impression of an engine whose headline value is speed is formed on the wrong GPU.

**Remedy:** Copy the block into `samples/minimal/main.cpp` with the same comment, or ship
it as an engine-provided `.cpp` that ARCHITECTURE's "a dozen honest lines" tells every
project to add to its target.

(Line corrected from the reviewer's `:35`, which is `options.resolution`.)

#### `max_threads = 16` is hardcoded and restates the engine default

- **File:** `game/main.cpp:37-38`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** performance
- **Tenet:** T8

**What:** Two of the option lines under a comment promising "everything the shell cannot
decide for itself" set values identical to `ApplicationOptions`' defaults, and the thread
count ignores the machine.

**Evidence:**

`game/main.cpp:32-38`

    		ApplicationOptions options;
    		options.window_class_name = L"ArtAttackWindowClass";
    		options.window_title = L"Colour Wars";
    		options.resolution = save.resolution();
    		options.fullscreen = save.fullscreen();
    		options.target_fps = 60;
    		options.max_threads = 16;

against `engine/app/application.h:41-46`

    		int target_fps = 60;
    		...
    		int min_threads = 1;
    		int max_threads = 16;

**Why it matters:** `max_threads` also sizes the deferred contexts
(`application.cpp:63-64`) and the sprite batches (`application.cpp:156-167`), so sixteen
of each are constructed at startup regardless of core count — on a quad-core machine,
twelve of each are created and never used. `std::thread::hardware_concurrency()` appears
nowhere in the repository. The two redundant lines also weaken the comment above them,
which is otherwise the clearest statement in the codebase of where the engine/game line
runs.

**Remedy:** Delete the two lines that restate defaults, and derive `max_threads` from
`hardware_concurrency()` in `ApplicationOptions`' default.

#### Dead API on both types this group owns

- **File:** `game/game_data.h:58`, `game/save.h:22`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T4

**What:** `GameData::game_data()` returns `this` and `Save::save_data()` returns the whole
struct by value; neither has a caller anywhere in `game/`.

**Evidence:**

`game/game_data.cpp:116-119`

    GameData* GameData::game_data()
    {
    	return this;
    }

`grep -rn "game_data()" game/` matches only its own declaration and definition;
`grep -rn "save_data()" game/` matches only `save.h:22` and `save.cpp:176`.

**Why it matters:** `game_data()` exists only to let a `MenuData` — which *is-a*
`GameData`, `menu_data.h:6` — hand out a base pointer it already is, mirroring
`MenuData::menu_data()` (`menu_data.cpp:27-30`), which by contrast has 79 uses. Together
they are the visible symptom of the inheritance-for-field-concatenation the `*MenuData`
hierarchy is built on. (I checked the obvious hazard that pattern invites: nothing ever
deletes a `GameData*`, so the missing virtual destructor is not live UB.)

#### `game/content/save/save_data.txt` is a dead file from a previous save format

- **File:** `game/CMakeLists.txt:101-107`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** T7

**What:** The seeded save directory contains a `save_data.txt` in an older line-oriented
format that no code reads, and the build copies the whole directory beside the exe.

**Evidence:**

`game/CMakeLists.txt:101-107`

    add_custom_command(TARGET ArtAttackGame POST_BUILD
        COMMAND "${CMAKE_COMMAND}"
            "-Dsrc=${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/content/save"
            "-Ddst_parent=$<TARGET_FILE_DIR:ArtAttackGame>"
            -P "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/seed_save.cmake"
        VERBATIM
    )

`game/content/save/` holds `save_data.json`
(`{"resolution":{"x":1920,"y":1080},"fullscreen":false}`) and `save_data.txt`
(`1920x1080` / `false`). A grep for `save_data.txt` and for any `".txt"` literal across
`game/` and `engine/` returns nothing.

**Why it matters:** Corrected from the reviewer's "shipped and installed": `seed_save.cmake`
copies only when `${dst_parent}/save` does not exist, and the project has no `install()`
rule anywhere, so this is one stale file seeded once beside the exe rather than something
shipped on every build. It still means the next person debugging a settings problem finds
two save files in two formats and no way to tell which one the game reads.

**Remedy:** Delete `game/content/save/save_data.txt`.

#### `save.cpp` hand-rolls file handling the engine already solved

- **File:** `game/save.cpp:40-49`, `game/save.cpp:82-104`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** lifetime
- **Tenet:** T2

**What:** Existence is tested by opening the file with `fopen_s` in a file that already
includes `<filesystem>`, and the write path holds a raw `FILE*` across two operations that
can throw.

**Evidence:**

    bool Save::check_if_save_file_exists()
    {
        FILE* fp = nullptr;
        if (fopen_s(&fp, SAVE_FILE_PATH.c_str(), "rb") != 0 || fp == nullptr)
        {
    		return false;
    	}
    	fclose(fp);
    	return true;
    }

and, thirty lines later, `<filesystem>` in use for the directory (`save.cpp:75-76`):

        const std::filesystem::path save_path(SAVE_FILE_PATH);
        if (save_path.has_parent_path())

The write path:

        FILE* fp = nullptr;
        if (fopen_s(&fp, SAVE_FILE_PATH.c_str(), "wb") != 0 || fp == nullptr)
        {
            return false;
        }
        // Allocate buffer on the heap
        auto write_buffer = std::make_unique<char[]>(65536);
        FileWriteStream os(fp, write_buffer.get(), 65536);
        ...
        fclose(fp);

**Why it matters:** `std::make_unique<char[]>(65536)` and rapidjson's `AddMember` calls
can both throw `std::bad_alloc`, and either leaks `fp` — a low-probability leak, but the
engine already has the fix and cannot share it: `json_loader.cpp:12-24` defines a
`file_closer`/`unique_file` pair inside an anonymous namespace, so the game had to write
raw `FILE*` code. The existence check is a second, gratuitous open of the same path when
`std::filesystem::exists` is one line and already available, and 64 KB is an odd buffer
for a 53-byte document. I confirmed the reviewer's disproved hypothesis independently:
the buffered write *does* reach disk before `fclose`, because `Writer::EndValue` flushes
the top-level value, so this is a leak and a duplication finding, not a
use-after-close one.

**Remedy:** Use `std::filesystem::exists` for the check, and promote the engine's
`unique_file` out of the anonymous namespace into a small `engine/core` header the game
can use — which also gives the checked `fclose` the third finding asks for.

### Rejected

No finding was rejected outright; every one of the reviewer's 23 survived verification.
The claims below were struck from the findings that carried them, and the surviving text
above is corrected accordingly.

- **"the resolution the save file persists is not the resolution the game renders at",
  attributed to DPI virtualisation** (finding 1) — wrong mechanism: the swap chain does
  render at the saved resolution and is then composited scaled. The true causes are
  blurring on scaled displays, an unreachable 4K option, and separately the missing
  `AdjustWindowRect`, now filed on its own.
- **DPI finding graded high** — regraded medium: real and common, but the game runs and
  the setting is honoured in logical pixels; no data loss, no crash.
- **"twelve of GameData's sixteen accessors" forward** (findings 5, 6) — there are
  eleven; `application()` returns the member and `game_data()` returns `this`.
- **"screen_resolution.h exposes the enum with no way to size it"** (finding 14) — it
  carries `max = s_3840_2160`. What is missing is a public pixel-pair conversion, which is
  what the finding now says.
- **"Fifteen of the twenty headers … plus the one engine header"** (finding 10) — sixteen
  of twenty are unreferenced, and the remedy's proposal to keep `SimpleMath.h` is wrong:
  it is one of the unused ones (`XMFLOAT2` comes from `<DirectXMath.h>` at `pch.h:39`).
- **"~20 including translation units" for `directory_consts.h`** (finding 12) — measured:
  fourteen of forty-six.
- **"`menu_data.h` by fourteen further files"** (finding 11) — six files include it
  directly; the defensible numbers are 18 of 46 TUs reaching rapidjson and 13 reaching
  `game_data.h`.
- **`ctime_s` graded medium, with "a maintainer chasing a save-corruption report reads a
  timestampless log"** (finding 7) — regraded low: there is no log, by the same finding's
  own argument two entries above it.
- **Duplicate level name graded medium** (finding 15) — regraded low: requires a content
  authoring error and its symptom is two visibly identical tiles, not a failure.
- **"shipped and installed" for `save_data.txt`** (finding 22) — `seed_save.cmake` copies
  only when the destination `save/` is absent, and the project declares no `install()`
  rule at all.
- **Window title at `main.cpp:35`** (finding 19) — it is line 34; 35 is
  `options.resolution`.
- **"pch.h:1-80"** (finding 9) — the file is 79 lines.

<a id="g-game-states-flow"></a>

## game-states-flow — Game states and secondary menus

*Group `game-states-flow` · 19 findings (3 high, 9 medium, 7 low) · source `review2/verified/game-states-flow.md`, verified report.*

I re-opened all eighteen assigned files and every line the reviewer cited, plus
`engine/core/state.h`, `engine/core/state_context.{h,cpp}`, `engine/app/application.cpp`,
`engine/core/step_timer.h`, `engine/render/viewport_manager.{h,cpp}`,
`engine/audio/sound_bank_object.{h,cpp}`, `game/states/menu_page.{h,cpp}`, `menu_data.{h,cpp}`,
`menu_input.{h,cpp}`, `game/objects/player_input.{h,cpp}`, `level_builder.{h,cpp}`,
`level.{h,cpp}`, `weapon.cpp`, `game/game_data.h`, `game/main.cpp`, `cmake/settings.cmake`,
`game/CMakeLists.txt`, `engine/CMakeLists.txt`, `tests/*/CMakeLists.txt` and
`samples/minimal/`. Every line number in the raw report was checked against the file; three
were off by one or two and are corrected here. The load-bearing facts all hold:
`ViewportManager::set_layout` really does have exactly one call site in the whole repository
(`game_states.cpp:134`; `level.cpp:641` is a comment saying the second one was removed);
`level_builder_` really is built once in `init()` and never rebuilt, so the stale
`PointClamp()` sampler that IMPLEMENTED.md lists as "known remaining" genuinely cannot be
cleared by restarting; `StateContext::transition_to` really does destroy the calling state at
`state_context.cpp:23`; and no test binary constructs a `State` — nor could one, because the
whole flow layer lives in `ArtAttackGame`, a WIN32 *executable*, while every test links
`ArtAttackEngine` or nothing.

What I threw out is mostly consequence, not observation. The two-frame warm-up finding was
argued from "the huge `dt` produced by `build_and_enter_level()`" — but `StepTimer` is in
fixed-step mode (`application.cpp:71`), so `m_elapsedTicks = m_targetElapsedTicks` on every
single update and `dt` is *always* exactly 1/60; the catch-up after a long build is bounded to
six updates by `m_qpcMaxDelta` and the warm-up does not prevent it. The same finding claimed
`update()` skips one frame while `draw()` skips two: `Application::tick()` runs update before
render, so both skip exactly one. The "previous frame may be minutes old" claim in the
menu-input finding is also wrong as stated — a menu always exits on a release edge, which
stores an all-false `prev_inputs_` — but the finding survives because the two frames *after* a
menu opens are a real, reproducible way to close the pause menu with an input the player never
made in it. I re-graded four findings down (self-destroying `transition_to`, the sub-menu
rebuild order, the base-initialiser call, and the warm-up) because each is latent: I traced
every one of the ten self-transition sites and none touches `this` after the call, and no
destructor in the menu-page family dereferences the data object destroyed two statements
earlier. I also confirmed with the actual toolchain that `/W4 /WX` does *not* diagnose the
default-less switch (C4062 does not fire) or the `int i < v.size()` loops, so nothing in this
group is being caught by the build.

Added three findings the reviewer missed: pausing never silences a weapon's looping shoot
sound, because `Weapon::handle_shoot_sound` is only reached from `Level::update` and the pause
state stops calling it; `game_states.h` includes three page headers it does not need; and the
level draw and the menu draw disagree on `ExecuteCommandList`'s `RestoreContextState` flag with
no comment either way.

### Themes

- The engine's `State`/`StateContext` pair supplies one replace-transition and nothing else —
  no stack, no return channel, no `dt` — so `GameLevel` reinvents all three by hand: an enum,
  three nested contexts, three heap-allocated enums used as out-parameters, and a 173-line
  `update()`.
- Global presentation state owned by the engine (`ViewportManager::layout_`) is written on the
  way *into* a level and never restored on the way out. The one fixed half of old critical #12
  is the entry side.
- Lifetime here is correct by luck rather than by construction: `transition_to` destroys the
  state that called it, and the sub-menu trio is rebuilt owner-last. Nothing dereferences in
  either window today, and nothing in the code says why not.
- The `*_action` / `*_data` / `*_menu` cartridge is one idea instantiated four times. It has
  already drifted (`ResultsMenuData` takes `const GameData*`, the other two take `GameData*`,
  and the base takes `const` regardless), and every `*Data` inherits the whole `GameData`
  service bag to add one or two pointers — with a `set_action()` and, in two cases, a second
  setter that nothing calls.
- Input is read per pad slot with no reference to who is in the match, and the two input pumps
  are alternated rather than run every frame, so edge detection compares against a frame that
  belongs to a different mode.
- Menu tuning — positions, colours, timings, font and sound names — is SCREAMING_SNAKE
  constants in `*_consts` namespaces inside headers, which CONVENTIONS forbids by casing *and*
  by grouping and T7 says should be data. Seven of them are dead.
- The const-draw discipline the project just bought stops at the state boundary: `State::draw()`
  is non-`const`, and `ResultsMenuInitial` has three `const` methods whose entire job is mutation
  through `unique_ptr` members.

- **File:** `game/states/game_states.cpp:131-137` (and the five exits at `216-223`, `256-265`, `266-275`, `276-285`, `293-302`)

applied and the whole main menu is then drawn once per player viewport, scaled into a quadrant.

`game/states/game_states.cpp:131-137` — the only writer of the layout, anywhere:

and the same omission in all four end-menu exits — `change_teams` (256-265),

`engine/render/viewport_manager.cpp:79-93` — what the menu then loops over:

        for (size_t i = 0; i < num_viewports; i++)

            this->viewport_manager()->apply_player_viewport(
                static_cast<int>(i), deferred_context, sprite_batch);

**Why it matters:** play a two-to-four-player match, open the end menu and choose "Change
Weapons" (or "Exit to Main Menu", or Quit from the pause menu). `GameMenu` is pushed with
`ViewportManager::layout_` still `four_player`, so `MainMenuPage::draw` renders the entire main
menu four times, each scaled into a quarter of the screen, for the rest of the menu session —
until the player happens to start another level and `build_and_enter_level()` sets the layout
again. Grep confirms the only `set_layout` call in code is `game_states.cpp:134`. This is
exactly the class of bug review #12 named, fixed on the entry side and untouched on the exit
side. (A three-player match makes it worse still: `all_viewports()` appends a *fifth* viewport
for `player_viewport(4)`, which falls through `calculate_viewport`'s switch to the fullscreen
default — but that defect belongs to `engine/render`.)

**Remedy:** set the layout on the way out too — `set_layout(ScreenLayout::one_player)` beside
`stop_music()` in the five exit branches — or better, make the layout something `GameMenu` and
`GameLevel` each assert on entry, so neither inherits the other's.

#### The level builder snapshots `CommonStates::PointClamp()`, and no restart can clear it

- **File:** `game/states/game_states.cpp:106-125`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** lifetime
- **Tenet:** T2

**What:** `GameLevel::init()` reads `common_states()->PointClamp()` once and passes the raw
`ID3D11SamplerState*` into a `LevelBuilder` that is constructed there and never rebuilt, so
every `Level` — including every restarted one — draws through a pointer into the `CommonStates`
object that device loss destroys.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/game_states.cpp:114-124`:

            this->level_builder_ = std::make_unique<LevelBuilder>(
                this->data()->viewport_manager(),
                this->data()->render_resources(),
                this->data()->audio_resources(),
                this->data()->level_infos(),
                this->data()->common_states()->PointClamp(),
                this->data()->resolution_manager(),
                this->data()->thread_pool(),
                this->data()->partitioner());

            this->build_and_enter_level();

`game/game_data.h:53-55` states the contract this violates:

            // Recreated on device loss, so unlike the rest these change identity
            // across one and must be read through this each time they are needed.
            DirectX::CommonStates* common_states() const;

The pointer lands in `LevelBuilder::sampler_state_` (`game/objects/level_builder.h:39`), is
handed to every `Level` at `game/objects/level_builder.cpp:77`, stored as
`Level::sampler_state_` (`game/objects/level.h:149`, `level.cpp:45`) and dereferenced from
render workers at `level.cpp:531`, `:585` and `:650`:

        sprite_batches->at(i)->Begin(SpriteSortMode_Deferred, nullptr, this->sampler_state_);

**Why it matters:** IMPLEMENTED.md already lists "`Level::_sampler_state` caches a pointer into
the `CommonStates` that device loss destroys" under *Known remaining issues*, so the defect is
not new — but two facts are, and they change the fix. First, the single line that creates the
stale copy is `game_states.cpp:119`; nothing else in the game snapshots a `CommonStates`
member. Second, `level_builder_` is built in `init()` and is *not* rebuilt by
`build_and_enter_level()` (`131-137`), so restarting the match after a device-lost event
re-seeds the new `Level` with the same dead pointer — the "restart and it recovers" escape
hatch does not exist. The correct pattern is three files away in the same group:
`MenuPage::point_clamp_sampler_state()` (`menu_page.cpp:185-188`) reads `PointClamp()` fresh
every draw.

**Remedy:** hand `LevelBuilder`/`Level` the `GameData*` and read `PointClamp()` at draw time,
exactly as `MenuPage` already does. At minimum, rebuild `level_builder_` inside
`build_and_enter_level()` so a restart clears it.

#### Give the engine a state stack instead of making each game state build one

- **File:** `game/states/game_states.h:35-69`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T1; PHILOSOPHY/Structural types and ARCHITECTURE/Modules both say the shell "owns the state stack"

**What:** `StateContext` holds one `unique_ptr<State>` and `transition_to` replaces it, so there
is no push/pop and no way for a pushed state to return a result. `GameLevel` therefore
reimplements a three-deep stack out of an enum, three nested `StateContext` members, three
heap-allocated enums used as out-parameters, and a 173-line `update()`.

**Evidence:**

`engine/core/state_context.h:8-18` — the entire mechanism:

        class StateContext
        {
        public:
            virtual ~StateContext() = default;
            StateContext() = default;
            void update() const;
            void draw() const;
            void transition_to(std::unique_ptr<State> state);
        private:
            std::unique_ptr<State> state_ = nullptr;
        };

`game/states/game_states.h:35-43` and `:59-69` — the game's replacement for it:

        enum class GameLevelState
        {
            first_update,
            second_update,
            active,
            pause_menu,
            results,
            end_menu,
        };
        ...
            std::unique_ptr<artattack::StateContext> pause_menu_ = nullptr;
            std::unique_ptr<PauseMenuAction> pause_menu_action_ = nullptr;
            std::unique_ptr<PauseMenuData> pause_menu_data_ = nullptr;
            std::unique_ptr<MenuInput> menu_input_ = nullptr;
            std::unique_ptr<artattack::StateContext> results_menu_ = nullptr;
            std::unique_ptr<ResultsMenuAction> results_menu_action_ = nullptr;
            std::unique_ptr<ResultsMenuData> results_menu_data_ = nullptr;
            std::unique_ptr<artattack::StateContext> end_menu_ = nullptr;
            std::unique_ptr<EndMenuAction> end_menu_action_ = nullptr;
            std::unique_ptr<EndMenuData> end_menu_data_ = nullptr;
            GameLevelState state_ = GameLevelState::first_update;

and `game_states.cpp:341-354`, where the missing stack forces the parent to hand-dispatch its
children's draws:

            switch (this->state_)
            {
            case GameLevelState::active:
                break;
            case GameLevelState::pause_menu:
                this->pause_menu_->draw();

**Why it matters:** the *forward* channel already exists as a value —
`MainMenuMidwayLoadSettings`, passed to `GameMenu`'s constructor at `game_states.cpp:11-19`.
Only the backward channel is missing, and its absence is the entire reason three heap-allocated
enums exist. A stranger writing the most ordinary thing in a game — a pause overlay above a
running level — must copy all 173 lines of `GameLevel::update()` before they can begin, and
`samples/minimal/` (one `HelloState`, 50-line `main.cpp`) does not demonstrate it. Documented
behaviour and shipped behaviour disagree: two design documents assert a state stack that does
not exist. This is the single largest piece of engine mechanism this group is missing, and it
has to exist before the engine can be handed to anyone.

**Remedy:** add `push`/`pop` to `StateContext` (a `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<State>>`, top
updated, whole stack drawn bottom-up) plus a typed result the popped state hands back.
`GameLevelState`, the three nested contexts and the three action pointers all delete with it.

#### `transition_to` destroys the running state; ten self-transitions in this group call it from their own `update()`

- **File:** `game/states/game_states.cpp:80-85` (also `221-222`, `262-263`, `272-273`, `282-283`, `299-300`; `game/states/pause_menu.cpp:87-89`, `94-96`, `242-244`, `267-269`)
- **Severity:** medium *(re-graded down from high — latent, see below)*
- **Category:** lifetime
- **Tenet:** T11 (ownership is explicit and lexical), T2

**What:** `StateContext::transition_to` destroys the state that called it before it returns, so
every self-transition in this group is a member function that keeps executing on an object whose
lifetime has ended.

**Evidence:**

`engine/core/state_context.cpp:21-26` — line 23 is where the caller dies:

        void StateContext::transition_to(std::unique_ptr<State> state)
        {
            this->state_ = std::move(state);
            this->state_->set_context(this);
            this->state_->init();
        }

`game/states/game_states.cpp:80-85` — `GameMenu` destroys itself from inside its own `update()`
(`update()` at `:72-79` calls `order_level_creation()` at `:77`):

        void GameMenu::order_level_creation()
        {
            this->context()->transition_to(
                std::make_unique<GameLevel>(this->game_data_,
                    *this->menu_data_->level_settings()));
        }

`game/states/game_states.cpp:299-302` — and `GameLevel` does the same, five branches deep
inside two nested switches:

                    this->context()->transition_to(
                        std::make_unique<GameMenu>(this->data(), settings));
                    break;
                }

**Why it matters:** I traced all ten sites (the reviewer said eight; the actual count is six in
`game_states.cpp` and four in `pause_menu.cpp`). **None of them is a live use-after-free
today** — every one either returns immediately or executes only `break`/`}` afterwards, and the
locals destroyed on the way out (`MainMenuMidwayLoadSettings settings`, the `std::string`
highlight name) live in the still-valid stack frame, not in `*this`. That is why this is graded
medium rather than high. What makes it worth fixing anyway is that the safety is invisible and
unwritable-down: adding one line after any of the ten — a log, a `stop_music()`, an assignment
to `state_` — is an immediate use-after-free of a `GameLevel` that owns an entire `Level`, and
neither the compiler nor a reviewer reading only the `.cpp` can see it. The discipline is not
even uniform within one file: `pause_menu.cpp:242-244` and `:267-269` end with `return;`,
`:87-89` and `:94-96` do not.

**Remedy:** make the transition a *request* — have `transition_to` record a pending state that
`StateContext::update()` applies after `state_->update()` returns — so a state can never be
destroyed inside its own call. This falls out naturally of the state-stack work above.

#### Do not let a controller outside the match pause, quit, or advance the menus

- **File:** `game/states/game_states.cpp:357-368`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T2

**What:** `check_for_pause_input` scans all four XInput slots with no reference to
`settings_.player_count()`, so a connected pad that is not in the match can open the pause menu
and drive it to Quit. `EndMenuInitial::update` and `ResultsMenuInitial::check_for_continue_input`
have the same hole.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/game_states.cpp:357-368`:

        int GameLevel::check_for_pause_input(
            const std::vector<PlayerInputData>& player_inputs)
        {
            for (int i = 0; i < static_cast<int>(player_inputs.size()); i++)
            {
                if (player_inputs[i].toggle_pause_menu)
                {
                    return i;
                }
            }
            return -1;
        }

`game/objects/player_input.h:36-38` confirms the vector is always four entries, one per slot,
regardless of how many players are playing:

            // Returns exactly player_input_consts::MAX_PAD_COUNT entries, indexed by
            // XInput pad slot. Absent pads carry ConnectionState::disconnected and
            // neutral input rather than being omitted.

`game/states/end_menu.cpp:35` and `game/states/results_menu.cpp:269` loop the same four slots
with the same absent bound:

            for (int i = 0; i < inputs.size(); i++)

Players are bound to slots one-for-one at `game/states/main_menu.cpp:1203-1212`
(`set_player_num(i, i)` for `i < player_count()`), so slots at and above `player_count()` belong
to nobody. `PauseMenuPage::pausing_player_input` (`pause_menu.cpp:44-55`) bound-checks only
against `inputs.size()`, which is 4 — so slot 2 in a two-player match passes.

**Why it matters:** three pads plugged in, a two-player match. The idle third pad presses Start;
the pause menu opens over both players' screens headed "Pause Menu P3"
(`pause_menu.cpp:30` maps slot 2 to that string), and that pad can then confirm Quit and end the
match for everyone. The results and end menus are worse, because they take input from *any* of
the four slots: an idle pad can skip the results screen and pick "Change Level" while the actual
players are still reading their scores.

**Remedy:** pass `settings_.player_count()` into the pause check and into the two menu loops and
ignore slots at or above it. `pausing_player_input`'s comment already says it is "the only menu
page that reads a single player's input rather than looping every slot" — that is the shape the
other two want.

#### Pump the menu input every frame, not only while a menu is open

- **File:** `game/states/game_states.cpp:111-112` (pumps at `:202`, `:229`, `:252`)
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T2

**What:** `menu_input_` is polled only while a menu state is running, so on the first two frames
after a menu opens its edge detector is comparing against gameplay input; a player holding A
when the pause menu opens releases it two frames later and the synthesised `proceed` confirms
the default highlight, "Resume", closing the menu on its own.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/game_states.cpp:111-112` creates it; the only pumps are inside the three menu
branches (`this->pause_menu_->update();` at `:202`, `this->results_menu_->update();` at `:229`,
`this->end_menu_->update();` at `:252`), each of which reaches
`MenuPage::menu_inputs()` (`game/states/menu_page.cpp:190-193`):

        std::vector<ProcessedMenuInput> MenuPage::menu_inputs() const
        {
            return this->data()->input()->update_and_get_menu_inputs();
        }

`game/states/menu_input.cpp:42-48` — every menu action is a release edge against `prev_inputs_`:

            bool no_press_current = !current.proceed && !current.back && !current.pause;
            bool prev_proceed = previous.proceed && !previous.back && !previous.pause;
            ...
            bool proceed = prev_proceed && no_press_current;

`game/states/menu_input.cpp:145-152` writes `prev_inputs_` only when the function is called:

            for (int i = 0; i < MAX_PAD_COUNT; i++)
            {
                if (current[i].connected)
                {
                    result[i] = calculate_menu_input(current[i], this->prev_inputs_[i]);
                }
                this->prev_inputs_[i] = current[i];
            }

**Why it matters:** the pause menu opens on the *release* of Start
(`player_input.cpp:54`, `!current.pause_menu && previous.pause_menu`). A player holding A —
jump, `player_input.cpp:28` — at that moment gets: frame N+1, the menu's first pump records
`prev.proceed = true`; frame N+2, they release A, `proceed` fires against a press made during
gameplay, and `PauseMenuInitial::update` confirms the highlight `set_highlighted_widget` left
on "Resume" (`pause_menu.cpp:78-83`, `:191`). The menu closes two frames after opening with no
input the player made in it. The same stale diff applies to the D-pad edges and to the analogue
stick edges at `menu_input.cpp:74-97`. (I checked and rejected the stronger version of this
claim: because a menu always exits on a release edge, `prev_inputs_` is left all-false, so the
stale state is *not* "minutes old" — the exposure is precisely the two frames after a menu
opens. It is still reproducible on every pause where a face button is held.) The mirror image
exists on the other pump: `player_input_` is not polled during a pause, so a button first
pressed inside the pause menu registers as a fresh press on the frame the level resumes.

**Remedy:** call `update_and_get_menu_inputs()` and `update_and_get_player_inputs()` once per
frame from `GameLevel::update()` regardless of state and pass the results down, or re-seed
`prev_inputs_` from live pad state when a menu opens.

#### Stop heap-allocating a `bool` and three enums to carry flow decisions

- **File:** `game/states/game_states.h:28`, `:60`, `:64`, `:67`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T11 (the stack over the heap)

**What:** four scalars — one `bool` and three four-to-six-value `enum class`es — are
individually `make_unique`'d so that a raw pointer to each can be stored in a `*MenuData`.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/game_states.h:28`:

            std::unique_ptr<bool> is_ready_to_load_level_ = nullptr;

`game/states/game_states.h:60`, `:64`, `:67`:

            std::unique_ptr<PauseMenuAction> pause_menu_action_ = nullptr;
            ...
            std::unique_ptr<ResultsMenuAction> results_menu_action_ = nullptr;
            ...
            std::unique_ptr<EndMenuAction> end_menu_action_ = nullptr;

`game/states/game_states.cpp:24` allocates the bool:

            this->is_ready_to_load_level_ = std::make_unique<bool>(false);

It is dereferenced at `game_states.cpp:75` (`if (*this->is_ready_to_load_level_)`), and the enum
pattern at `:204`, `:230`, `:253`, written from the menu side at `pause_menu.cpp:74`,
`end_menu.cpp:42`, `results_menu.cpp:66`.

**Why it matters:** T11 opens "Objects are values… There is no garbage collector, and there
never will be", and `new bool` is the most literal violation available. The allocation exists
only because `PauseMenuData` wants a `PauseMenuAction*` member, and it wants that only because
`State` has no return channel (see the state-stack finding). It buys nothing even on its own
terms: the four objects are already owned by `GameLevel`/`GameMenu`, which already outlive every
page that points at them. The cost is not four allocations — it is that this is the shape a
stranger will copy, because it is the only shape the flow layer demonstrates.

**Remedy:** make them plain value members
(`PauseMenuAction pause_menu_action_ = PauseMenuAction::none;`) and hand out
`&pause_menu_action_` — or delete them together with the out-parameter protocol when the state
stack lands.

#### Pass `dt` to `State::update()` instead of reading it out of the service bag

- **File:** `game/states/results_menu.cpp:34`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Services and lifetimes — "Frame time is a parameter — `update(float dt)` — not shared state"

**What:** the "pass `dt` to `update()`" work did not reach the `State` interface, so states
dereference a `float*` borrowed from `GameData`.

**Evidence:**

`engine/core/state.h:12`:

            virtual void update() = 0;

`game/states/results_menu.cpp:34`:

            const float dt = *this->data()->dt();

`game/states/game_states.cpp:195-196` — `GameLevel` receives it the same way and immediately
dereferences it to hand a `float` down:

                    this->level_->update(player_inputs,
                        *this->game_data_->dt());

`game/game_data.h:44`:

            float* dt() const;

**Why it matters:** the conversion stopped exactly one level short of the interface the
philosophy names. `ResultsMenuInitial`, whose entire behaviour is three timers (`delay_timer_`,
`fill_timer_`, `show_results_timer_`, `results_menu.h:102-104`), can only ever be stepped by a
live `Application` — there is no way to drive it from a harness. It also keeps a mutable
`float*` in the service bag that every object in the game can write through, and
`Application::update()` (`application.cpp:257`) writes it every frame.

**Remedy:** change `State::update()` to `update(float dt)` and drop `GameData::dt()`.

#### `update_fill_box()` and friends are `const` and do nothing but mutate

- **File:** `game/states/results_menu.h:109-111`, `game/states/results_menu.cpp:217-255`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T5

**What:** three `const` member functions change widget geometry through `unique_ptr` members,
which `const` does not reach — the same hole IMPLEMENTED.md documented for `Level`'s
`unique_ptr`-held drawables, reintroduced in code written since.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/results_menu.h:109-111`:

            void update_fill_box() const;
            void update_team_a_fill() const;
            void update_team_b_fill() const;

`game/states/results_menu.cpp:242-255`:

        void ResultsMenuInitial::update_team_b_fill() const
        {
            float score = this->level_end_info().team_b_ratio();
            float max_width = RESULTS_MENU_TEAM_FILL_SIZE.x * score;
            float fill = this->fill_time_ratio();
            if (fill > 1.0f)
            {
                fill = 1.0f;
            }
            float width = fill * max_width;
            this->team_b_fill_->set_width(width);
            this->team_b_fill_->set_position_from_top_right_origin(
                this->calculate_team_b_fill_top_right_position());

**Why it matters:** IMPLEMENTED.md's note on #16 says the const pass was worth doing precisely
because it "survives someone editing the code" — a `draw()` that assigns is now a compile
error. That guarantee is void for anything reached through a `unique_ptr`, and these three are a
worked example: a reader who sees `const` on `update_team_b_fill` will reasonably conclude it is
safe to call from a draw path, and `State::draw()` (`engine/core/state.h:13`) is not `const`
either, so nothing would stop them. The mutation is not a race today — the only caller is
`update()` at `results_menu.cpp:44` — but the label is a lie in the one place the project
decided labels would be enforced.

**Remedy:** drop `const` from the three, and make `State::draw()` `const` so the enforcement the
project already bought extends to the states.

#### Collapse the `*MenuData` classes; they are one idea that has already diverged

- **File:** `game/states/pause_menu_data.h:6-19`, `game/states/end_menu_data.h:6-16`, `game/states/results_menu_data.h:7-21`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T4 — "duplication is the opposite of clarity at scale"

**What:** four types derive from `MenuData` — which itself derives from the entire `GameData`
service bag — to add one or two pointers each; their constructors have already drifted on the
constness of that bag, and each ships setters nothing calls.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/menu_data.h:6-16` — the base takes a `const GameData*` in both constructors:

        class MenuData : public GameData
        {
        public:
            explicit MenuData(const GameData* game_data);
            MenuData(const GameData* game_data, MenuInput* input);

`game/states/results_menu_data.h:10-11` matches it:

            ResultsMenuData(const GameData* game_data, MenuInput* input,
                const LevelEndInfo& info, ResultsMenuAction* action);

`game/states/pause_menu_data.h:9-10` and `game/states/end_menu_data.h:9` do not, for no reason —
they demand a mutable bag and then pass it to a `const` parameter:

            PauseMenuData(GameData* game_data, MenuInput* input, int player_num,
                PauseMenuAction* action);
            EndMenuData(GameData* game_data, MenuInput* input, EndMenuAction* action);

Dead API, confirmed by grepping the whole tree: `PauseMenuData::set_action`
(`pause_menu_data.cpp:29-32`), `PauseMenuData::set_player_num` (`:19-22`),
`EndMenuData::set_action` (`end_menu_data.cpp:18-21`), `ResultsMenuData::set_action`
(`results_menu_data.cpp:29-32`) and `ResultsMenuData::set_level_end_info` (`:19-22`) have no
callers anywhere. Neither do `MenuData::menu_data()` or `GameData::game_data()`, both of which
just `return this`.

**Why it matters:** `PauseMenuData` *is a* `GameData`, which is false — a pause menu is not a
service bag — and the inheritance means every pause copies the whole bag to attach two fields.
The already-diverged constness is the evidence that this is copy-paste rather than design: it
means `ResultsMenuData` can be built from a `const GameData*` and the other two cannot, for a
reason nobody chose. Counting `menu_data.{h,cpp}`, the three `*_data.{h,cpp}` pairs and the
three `*_action.h` files, eleven files implement "pass the page a context and let it set a
result".

**Remedy:** one `MenuContext` value type holding `const GameData*` and `MenuInput*`, *composed*
into each page rather than inherited, with the result returned by the state-stack pop instead of
written through a pointer. Delete the six uncalled setters on the way past.

#### Move menu tuning out of SCREAMING_SNAKE header constants

- **File:** `game/states/pause_menu.h:10-41`, `game/states/end_menu.h:10-39`, `game/states/results_menu.h:8-59`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Never ("SCREAMING constants — screaming means macro, nothing else"), CONVENTIONS/Constants, T7

**What:** all three menu headers open with a `*_consts` namespace of SCREAMING_SNAKE constants
covering positions, sizes, colours, timings, font names and sound names. Seven are dead, and the
same values are maintained in four places.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/pause_menu.h:22-40`:

            const static mattmath::Vector2F PAUSE_MENU_INITIAL_WIDGET_SIZE = { 100.0f, 50.0f };
            const static mattmath::Vector2F PAUSE_MENU_INITIAL_WIDGET_POSITION = { 610.0f, 300.0f };
            ...
            const std::string SOUND_BANK = "sound_bank_1";
            const std::string DIRECTION_SOUND = "UI_Clicks14";

CONVENTIONS forbids both the casing and the grouping:

            - SCREAMING constants — screaming means macro, nothing else.
            ...
            Constants that stay in code live next to the one thing they configure,
            not in a `consts` namespace collecting strays.

Dead entries, each verified by grepping the name against the only `.cpp` whose
`using namespace` can see it: `pause_menu.h:31` (`TITLE_SHADOW_OFFSET`), `end_menu.h:30`
(`TITLE_SHADOW_OFFSET`), `end_menu.h:33` (`DETAIL_SHADOW_OFFSET`), `results_menu.h:24`
(`RESULTS_MENU_TEAM_FILL_Y_OFFSET`), `results_menu.h:31` (`RESULTS_MENU_TITLE_Y_OFFSET`),
`results_menu.h:33` (`WINNER_TEXT_Y_OFFSET`), `results_menu.h:48` (`TITLE_SHADOW_OFFSET`).

**Why it matters:** four headers — these three plus `main_menu.h` — each declare their own
`SOUND_BANK = "sound_bank_1"`, `CONFIRM_SOUND = "UI_Clicks01"` and
`DEFAULT_RESOLUTION = {1920, 1080}`, so the same values are maintained in four places and a
fifth menu makes it five. Because `const` at namespace scope has internal linkage, every
translation unit that pulls these headers in gets its own dynamically-initialised copy of a
dozen `std::string` statics — `game_states.h:7-10` pulls all three into `main.cpp` and
`game_states.cpp`, which never name most of them. And T7 says this content — box sizes, fill
durations, the winner sound — is exactly what should be data a designer can retune without a
rebuild. `ViewportManager` (`viewport_manager.h:19-21`) already shows the shape the engine
prefers: `static inline const` members on the class the values configure, with a comment saying
why they are not in a `consts` namespace.

**Remedy:** `inline constexpr` snake_case members on the class each one configures for the
genuinely structural values, and JSON for the tuning — colours, offsets, timings, asset names.

#### The state layer has no tests, and no test binary could reach it

- **File:** `game/states/pause_menu.cpp:132-212`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** testing
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Tests and toolchain; UI ("menus are headlessly testable")

**What:** nothing under `tests/` constructs a `State`, and nothing could — twice over: the flow
logic lives in an executable target, and every page's flow decisions are keyed off widgets that
only exist because a D3D-backed construction succeeded.

**Evidence:**

`tests/` holds `assets/asset_manifest_loader_tests.cpp`, `core/name_table_tests.cpp`,
`core/registry_tests.cpp`, `math/collision_tools_tests.cpp`, `math/math_tests.cpp`; grepping all
of them for `state`, `menu`, `pause`, `end_menu` or `results` returns nothing.

`game/CMakeLists.txt:` `add_executable(ArtAttackGame WIN32 …)` — the entire flow layer is in an
**executable**, so no test target can link it even in principle. `engine/CMakeLists.txt:12` is
`add_library(ArtAttackEngine STATIC …)`; `tests/core/CMakeLists.txt` links `doctest` and
`artattack_settings` and nothing else.

`game/states/pause_menu.cpp:137-143` is the second wall:

            this->box_ = std::make_unique<MTexture>(
                "box",
                "sprite_sheet_1",
                "pixel",
                RectangleF(Vector2F::ZERO, PAUSE_MENU_BOX_SIZE),
                this->render_resources(),
                PAUSE_MENU_BOX_COLOUR);

and `game/states/pause_menu.cpp:67-68`, where the flow decision is keyed off a widget that only
exists because that construction succeeded:

            std::string highlighted_element =
                this->highlighted_widget()->name();

**Why it matters:** the behaviour worth testing here is pure logic — "down from quit wraps to
resume", "Yes on the quit confirmation sets `PauseMenuAction::quit`", "the results screen
accepts proceed only after the fill completes" — and every bit of it is unreachable from a test
binary. PHILOSOPHY promises menus are headlessly testable; the whole menu flow, which is what a
stranger will copy, has zero behavioural coverage. It is also the reason the input-edge and
viewport-layout defects above are findable only by reading.

**Remedy:** key navigation off an index into a widget list rather than off `name()` string
compares, so the wrap-around table is a pure function a test can call. Longer term the flow
layer needs to sit somewhere a test can link — which is the same structural work as
IMPLEMENTED.md's outstanding #1/#2, applied to the game side.

#### Rebuild a sub-menu's context before its data, not after

- **File:** `game/states/game_states.cpp:160-172` (also `:179-191`, `:235-246`)
- **Severity:** low *(re-graded down from medium — latent)*
- **Category:** lifetime
- **Tenet:** T11

**What:** each sub-menu is rebuilt action-first, data-second, context-last, so on the second and
later opens the still-owned previous page holds pointers to a `*MenuData` and a `*MenuAction`
that were destroyed two statements earlier.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/game_states.cpp:160-172`:

                    this->pause_menu_action_ = std::make_unique<PauseMenuAction>(
                        PauseMenuAction::none);

                    this->pause_menu_data_ = std::make_unique<PauseMenuData>(
                        this->data(),
                        this->menu_input_.get(),
                        pause_menu_player,
                        this->pause_menu_action_.get());

                    this->pause_menu_ = std::make_unique<StateContext>();
                    this->pause_menu_->transition_to(
                        std::make_unique<PauseMenuInitial>(
                            this->pause_menu_data_.get()));

`game/states/pause_menu.h:74-75` is what is left dangling for the duration:

        private:
            PauseMenuData* data_ = nullptr;

**Why it matters:** pause, resume, play on, pause again. Line 160 destroys the
`PauseMenuAction` that the still-live `PauseMenuInitial`'s `PauseMenuData::action_` points at;
line 163 destroys the `PauseMenuData` that the page's `data_` points at; only line 169 destroys
the page. For two statements the object graph is invalid. I checked every destructor on that
path — `~PauseMenuInitial`, `~PauseMenuPage`, `~MenuPage`, `~MenuHighlight`, `~SoundBankObject`
are all defaulted and none reads `data_` — so this is latent, not a live crash, which is why it
drops to low. It is still backwards, and the reason it is safe is written down nowhere. The
identical shape is at `:179-191` (results, on the second match end) and `:235-246` (end menu).

**Remedy:** reset the context first — one extra `this->pause_menu_.reset();` before line 160, or
simply assign the three in the reverse order — so the owner dies before the things it points at.

#### Document, or delete, the two-frame warm-up before a level starts

- **File:** `game/states/game_states.cpp:138-149`, `:312-318`
- **Severity:** low *(re-graded down from medium; the reviewer's mechanism was wrong)*
- **Category:** docs
- **Tenet:** T4

**What:** `GameLevelState::first_update` and `second_update` skip one frame of simulation and one
frame of drawing on entry and on every restart, with no comment saying what they are for.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/game_states.cpp:141-149`:

            switch (this->state_)
            {
            case GameLevelState::first_update:
                this->state_ = GameLevelState::second_update;
                return;
            case GameLevelState::second_update:
                this->state_ = GameLevelState::active;
                //no break here so it goes to active
            case GameLevelState::active:

`game/states/game_states.cpp:314-318`:

            if (this->state_ == GameLevelState::first_update ||
                this->state_ == GameLevelState::second_update)
            {
                return;
            }

**Why it matters:** the only comment in the region explains the missing `break`, not the
mechanism, and the mechanism cannot be reconstructed from the code. I checked the two
explanations that suggest themselves and both are false. It does **not** absorb a large `dt`
from the seconds spent inside `build_and_enter_level()`: `application.cpp:71` puts `StepTimer`
in fixed-step mode, so `m_elapsedTicks = m_targetElapsedTicks` on every update
(`step_timer.h:129-136`) and `dt` is *always* exactly 1/60 — what a long build actually produces
is up to six catch-up `update()` calls (bounded by `m_qpcMaxDelta`, `step_timer.h:38`), which
the warm-up consumes one of and does nothing about. And `update()` and `draw()` do **not**
disagree about the length: `Application::tick()` runs `update()` before `render()`, so both skip
exactly one frame. What is left is one guaranteed blank frame on entry and on every restart
(`:214`, `:290`), for a reason no reader can recover.

**Remedy:** one comment saying what the warm-up absorbs — or, if the answer is "nothing", delete
both states and the early return in `draw()`.

#### Do not call a member function of a half-built object in a base-class initialiser

- **File:** `game/states/pause_menu.cpp:10-15` (also `end_menu.cpp:9-17`, `results_menu.cpp:10-19`)
- **Severity:** low *(re-graded down from medium — well-defined today, fragile to one edit)*
- **Category:** maintainability
- **Tenet:** T4, T2

**What:** all three page base classes initialise `SoundBankObject` with the result of
`this->audio_resources()`, a `MenuPage` member function, whose correctness depends silently on
`MenuPage` appearing before `SoundBankObject` in the base-specifier list.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/pause_menu.cpp:10-15`:

        PauseMenuPage::PauseMenuPage(PauseMenuData* data) :
            MenuPage(data),
            SoundBankObject(pause_menu_consts::SOUND_BANK,
                this->audio_resources()),
            data_(data)

`game/states/pause_menu.h:43` is the only thing making that legal:

        class PauseMenuPage : public MenuPage, public MenuHighlight, public artattack::SoundBankObject

and `game/states/menu_page.cpp:81-84` shows what is being read:

        const AudioResources* MenuPage::audio_resources() const
        {
            return this->data_->audio_resources();
        }

**Why it matters:** bases are initialised in declaration order, so `MenuPage::data_` is set
before `audio_resources()` runs and the call is well-defined as written — this is not a live
bug, which is why it drops to low. Reorder the base list, though — the most innocuous refactor
imaginable, and one a reader might do to group the two engine bases together — and
`audio_resources()` dereferences an uninitialised `MenuPage::data_`: undefined behaviour at the
construction of every menu page, with no diagnostic. The dependency is invisible in the `.cpp`
where the call is written and repeated in three files.

**Remedy:** use the constructor parameter, which depends on nothing:
`SoundBankObject(SOUND_BANK, data->audio_resources())`.

#### Close the state switches: a missing `break` and two `default`-less switches

- **File:** `game/states/game_states.cpp:200-309` (also `:29-63`)
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6

**What:** `case GameLevelState::end_menu` has no `break` and falls into `default:`; the
pause-action switch has no `default:` (and declares a non-trivially-constructed local inside an
unbraced case); and `GameMenu::init()`'s screen switch has no `default:` either.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/game_states.cpp:303-309` — the end-menu case block simply ends:

                default:
                    break;
                }
            }
            default:
                break;
            }

`game/states/game_states.cpp:206-224` — the pause switch, with `PauseMenuAction::none`
unhandled, no `default`, and a `MainMenuMidwayLoadSettings` (which holds a `std::string` and a
`std::vector<MenuPlayerSettings>`) declared in an unbraced case body, while the three end-menu
cases twenty lines below *are* braced:

                switch (action)
                {
                case PauseMenuAction::resume:
                ...
                case PauseMenuAction::quit:
                    this->level_->stop_music();
                    MainMenuMidwayLoadSettings settings;

`game/states/game_states.cpp:29-63` — the third instance, and the worst-behaved one: eight cases,
no `default`. A `screen_` outside the set leaves `menu_` an empty `StateContext`, whose
`update()` and `draw()` both return silently (`state_context.cpp:5-20`) — a black screen that
accepts no input and reports nothing.

**Why it matters:** all three are harmless today, and — checked against the actual toolchain —
the build will not tell you when they stop being: I compiled the exact shapes with
`cl /W4 /WX /permissive- /std:c++20` and neither C4062 (unhandled enumerator, no `default`) nor
C4018 on the `int i < v.size()` loops fires, so `/WX` is not a backstop here. Adding a
`GameLevelState` after `end_menu` silently runs the end-menu handler for it; adding any label
after `PauseMenuAction::quit` makes the file fail to compile with a jump-past-initialisation
error that will read as mysterious; adding a `MainMenuScreen` produces a dead black screen.

**Remedy:** add the `break`, brace the `quit` case like its neighbours, and give all three
switches a `default:` that is loud rather than silent (T6).

#### Pausing does not silence a weapon's looping shoot sound

- **File:** `game/states/game_states.cpp:155-173`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T4 — *(added by verifier)*

**What:** entering `GameLevelState::pause_menu` stops calling `Level::update`, and stopping a
looping weapon sound is something only `Level::update` ever does — so a player holding the
trigger when they press Start leaves the spray/roller loop playing under the pause menu until
they resume.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/game_states.cpp:155-158` — the frame the pause is detected, `level_->update()` is
not reached at all (the `else` at `:193-197` is skipped), and it is not reached again until the
state returns to `active`:

            int pause_menu_player = this->check_for_pause_input(player_inputs);
            if (pause_menu_player != -1)
            {
                this->state_ = GameLevelState::pause_menu;

`game/objects/weapon.cpp:242-260` — the only thing that ever stops the loop, reached only from
the weapon's update path:

        void Weapon::handle_shoot_sound(bool shooting_this_update, bool holding_shoot)
        {
            if (!this->loop_sound_.valid())
            {
                return;
            }

            if (holding_shoot || shooting_this_update)
            {
                this->sound_bank_->play_effect(
                    this->loop_sound_,
                    true,
                    this->details_.shoot_sound_volume);
            }
            else
            {
                this->sound_bank_->stop_effect(this->loop_sound_, true);
            }
        }

`game/objects/level.cpp:134` shows `Level` already has the call this needs
(`this->stop_player_sounds();`), used when the match timer expires — but it is private
(`level.h:174`) and `GameLevel` never calls it.

**Why it matters:** it is trivially reproducible — hold the right trigger with the sprayer,
press Start — and it is audible for as long as the pause lasts, because nothing on the pause
path will ever run the branch that stops the loop. It is also the kind of defect the missing
state stack causes: a real `push`/`pop` would give a level an obvious place to hang "quiet down
while something is above me".

**Remedy:** make `Level::stop_player_sounds()` public (or add `Level::pause()`), and call it in
the branch that sets `GameLevelState::pause_menu`.

#### The level draw and the menu draw disagree on `ExecuteCommandList`'s restore flag

- **File:** `game/states/game_states.cpp:330-339`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T4 — *(added by verifier)*

**What:** `GameLevel::draw()` executes its command lists with `RestoreContextState = TRUE`,
while `MenuPage::draw_mobjects_in_viewports` — which runs immediately afterwards, in the same
frame, onto the same immediate context — uses `FALSE`. Neither says why.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/game_states.cpp:330-339`:

            for (int i = 0; i < command_lists.size(); i++)
            {
                if (command_lists[i] == nullptr)
                {
                    continue;
                }

                immediate_context->ExecuteCommandList(command_lists[i], TRUE);
                command_lists[i]->Release();
            }

`game/states/menu_page.cpp:157-166`, reached one statement later via
`this->pause_menu_->draw()` (`game_states.cpp:346`):

            for (size_t i = 0; i < command_lists.size(); i++)
            {
                if (command_lists[i] == nullptr)
                {
                    continue;
                }

                immediate_context->ExecuteCommandList(command_lists[i], FALSE);

**Why it matters:** the two flags mean opposite things — `TRUE` saves and restores the immediate
context's state around the execution, `FALSE` leaves it reset to defaults — and one frame
performs both, in that order, whenever a menu overlays a level. It happens not to matter today
because `Application::clear()` (`application.cpp:281-300`) re-binds the render target and
viewport on the immediate context at the top of every frame, and `Present()` needs neither. But
this is exactly the kind of divergence that becomes a "why is the render target unbound"
afternoon after one unrelated change, and `TRUE` is the more expensive of the two for no stated
benefit.

**Remedy:** pick one — `FALSE` on both, given `clear()` re-binds everything each frame — and say
in a comment why.

### Rejected

- **"The warm-up absorbs the huge `dt` produced by `build_and_enter_level()`"** — rejected as
  the mechanism. `StepTimer` is in fixed-step mode (`application.cpp:71`), so
  `m_elapsedTicks = m_targetElapsedTicks` unconditionally (`step_timer.h:129-136`) and `dt` is
  always exactly 1/60; a long build produces up to six catch-up `update()` calls, which the
  warm-up does not prevent. The finding survives as a docs issue at low.
- **"`update()` skips one frame of simulation while `draw()` skips two states' worth of frames"**
  — rejected. `Application::tick()` runs `update()` before `render()`, so both skip exactly one
  frame.
- **"Eight call sites call `transition_to` from their own `update()`"** — corrected to ten (six
  in `game_states.cpp`, four in `pause_menu.cpp`).
- **"`transition_to` … high severity"** — re-graded to medium. I traced all ten sites; none
  touches `*this` after the call, so there is no live use-after-free, only a one-edit-away one.
- **"`menu_input_`'s previous frame is the last menu frame — potentially minutes earlier"** —
  rejected as stated. Every menu exit fires on a release edge, which stores an all-false
  `prev_inputs_`, so the stale window is the two frames after a menu *opens*, not an arbitrary
  gap. The finding survives at medium on the corrected mechanism.
- **"Rebuild a sub-menu's context before its data … medium"** — re-graded to low: every
  destructor on that path is defaulted and none reads the destroyed object, so it is latent.
- **"Base-class initialiser … medium"** — re-graded to low: the call is well-defined as written
  ([class.cdtor]/3 — `MenuPage` is fully constructed), so this is fragility, not a defect.
- **"CONVENTIONS forbids … six of them are dead"** — corrected to seven; the reviewer's own list
  named seven.
- **"Three separate headers each declare their own `SOUND_BANK` / `CONFIRM_SOUND` /
  `DEFAULT_RESOLUTION`"** — corrected to four (`main_menu.h:15`, `:73`, `:75` is the fourth).
- **"`MenuData::menu_data()` / `GameData::game_data()` are hand-written upcasts"** — imprecise;
  they return `this` unchanged. Kept as evidence of dead API, not as a casting problem.
- Line-number corrections, all otherwise-accurate findings: `game_data.h:53-56` → `53-55`;
  `pause_menu.cpp:66-68` → `67-68`; `menu_input.cpp:42-52` → `42-48`;
  `main_menu.cpp:1205-1212` → `1203-1212`; `player_input.h:36-39` → `36-38`.
- Not rejected but worth recording so nobody expects the compiler to help: I verified with
  `cl /W4 /WX /permissive- /std:c++20` (MSVC 14.44) that neither C4062 (unhandled enumerator with
  no `default`) nor C4018 on `int i < v.size()` fires, so the switch-hygiene and
  signed/unsigned patterns in this group are invisible to the warnings-as-errors build.
- **`ViewportManager::all_viewports()` pushing `player_viewport(4)` for a three-player layout**
  (`viewport_manager.cpp:88-91`), which falls through `calculate_viewport` to the fullscreen
  default — a real defect, but in `engine/render`, outside this group's files. Noted inside the
  viewport-layout finding rather than filed here.

<a id="g-game-level"></a>

## game-level — Level

*Group `game-level` · 18 findings (1 critical, 2 high, 5 medium, 10 low) · source `review2/verified/game-level.md`, verified report.*

**Verdict.** I re-opened every cited line in `game/objects/level.{h,cpp}`,
`level_builder.{h,cpp}`, `level_mode.h` and `stage.h`, and re-checked every off-file citation
the reviewer leaned on: `game/game_data.h:53-56`, `game/states/game_states.cpp:114-137` and
`:312-355`, `engine/app/application.cpp:152-178` and `:364-378`, `engine/core/thread_pool.cpp`,
`engine/collision/partitioner.cpp`, `engine/render/viewport_manager.{h,cpp}`,
`engine/core/registry.h`, `engine/core/i_game_object.h`,
`game/objects/{player,structure,projectile,projectile_spray,structure_paintable,interface_gameplay,debug_text}.cpp`,
`game/objects/player_builder.cpp`, `game/states/main_menu.cpp` and the three level JSONs. The
critical finding holds and is worse than `IMPLEMENTED.md` records: `CommonStates` is destroyed at
`application.cpp:374`, and the freed `ID3D11SamplerState*` is cached in *two* objects, the second
of which outlives every level it builds. I threw out one finding: the command-list leak on a
throwing render worker is real but inert — `main.cpp:93` catches, message-boxes and returns 1, so
the process is already dying and the leak costs nothing; its only durable content, the
undocumented `Release` obligation on the output parameter, is already stated inside the
"D3D11 in the signature" finding, where I folded it. I regraded three: `update_level_logic
const` from high to medium (it is an enforcement gap with no runtime consequence, not a defect);
the first-update camera loop from medium to low (`main_menu.cpp:1211` sets `player_num == ordinal`,
so the divergence is unreachable, and even if reached it costs a wrong camera *size* for the
three-second countdown, not a crash); and `count_projectiles` from medium to low (its per-view
repetition is gated on `showing_debug_`, which defaults `false` — `player.h:149` — so the walk is
not on the normal frame path at all). I checked and cleared four things the reviewer flagged as
uncertain or that looked wrong to me: the swap-and-pop unsigned wraparound at `:320-329` is
correct; `for (int i = 0; i < vec.size(); …)` does **not** warn under this project's `/W4 /WX`
(I compiled a reduction with `cl /W4 /WX /std:c++20 /permissive-` — clean), so the build is not
stale; every `SpriteBatch` is constructed on its *own* deferred context (`application.cpp:162-164`),
so the render fan-out has no hidden race; and `Registry::get(name)` throws naming the resource
(`registry.h:117-120`), so the level's sound-bank and stage lookups fail loudly rather than
null-dereferencing. I added five findings the reviewer missed: a 21-parameter constructor with four
adjacent `RectangleF` parameters that a transposition passes silently; `level_mode.h` — a group
file the reviewer touched only for its namespace — holding a type that is written once and never
read; seven borrowed pointers with no documented loan, in a file whose author documents loans
carefully everywhere else; three draw-path throws that discard the `HRESULT` and the view index;
and music whose lifetime is a seven-call-site convention rather than the level's.

### Themes

- **`const` on `Level` is decorative.** Every object list sits behind an outer `unique_ptr`,
  which does not propagate `const`, so the function that assigns input, spawns projectiles and
  deletes objects compiles as a `const` member. The compiler-enforced `draw()` contract that
  `ca4d228` bought stops at the `IGameObject` boundary and does not cover the scene.
- **The engine/game seam runs *through* this file, not around it.** Engine-shaped machinery —
  culling, dispatch, per-view fan-out, compaction — is written in the game's vocabulary
  (`Player`, `CollisionObjectType`, `PlayerInputData`, `TeamColour`), and the view count, each
  view's viewport and each view's camera are all read off `Player`.
- **The renderer backend is in the public signature, not behind it.** Three raw D3D11/DirectXTK
  vector parameters, one an output parameter carrying three obligations stated nowhere.
- **Raw D3D pointers are cached across device loss, in two objects**, contradicting the contract
  `game_data.h:53-56` states in its own header — and the caching object with the longer life is
  the one that re-injects the dangling pointer on restart.
- **Collision is unfiltered, unindexed and order-sensitive**: every ordered pair is tested twice,
  and both objects' responses fire off one object's predicate, so correctness rests on exactly
  one side of each pair having a permissive filter.
- **Lifetimes are documented by exception, not by rule.** Two members carry careful ownership
  comments; the seven borrowed pointers beside them carry none — including the one whose owner
  does not outlive it.
- **Dead surface persists and has started to cost twice**: two spawn vectors duplicating what
  `PlayerBuilder` already reads, an unused input vector, two uncalled methods, 112 commented-out
  lines, and a whole enum written once and never read.
