#### All eight `.cpp` files include `game/pch.h` before their own header

- **File:** `game/objects/weapon.cpp:1-2`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Files (include order)
- **Origin:** added-by-verifier

**What:** CONVENTIONS fixes the include order as "own header first — proving every header compiles on
its own". Every `.cpp` in this group puts a 79-line precompiled header carrying `Windows.h`,
`d3d11_1.h` and eighteen DirectXTK headers ahead of it, so no weapon header is ever compiled on its
own.

**Evidence:** `weapon.cpp:1-2`, and identically `weapon_builder.cpp`, `weapon_details.cpp`,
`weapon_sprayer.cpp`, `weapon_sniper.cpp`, `weapon_roller.cpp`, `weapon_mister.cpp` and
`weapon_bucket.cpp` —

    #include "game/pch.h"
    #include "game/objects/weapon.h"

**Why it matters:** The rule is not stylistic — CONVENTIONS states its purpose in the same sentence,
and that purpose is defeated here in all eight files. `weapon.h` uses `std::vector` (`:40`) and
`std::unique_ptr` (`:148`) without including `<vector>` or `<memory>`, and reaches DirectXTK's
`SpriteEffects` and `SpriteBatch` transitively; whether it stands alone is currently unknown and
untested, because nothing ever compiles it first. The include is also redundant:
`game/CMakeLists.txt:72` uses `target_precompile_headers(ArtAttackGame PRIVATE pch.h)`, which
force-includes it into every TU already.

**Remedy:** Drop the explicit `#include "game/pch.h"` from all eight files and let the own header
come first, so a header that has quietly grown a dependency on the PCH fails the build that
introduces it (T5).

---

### Rejected

No finding was rejected in full — every citation, quotation and line number in the raw report checked
out against the files. What was thrown out are sub-claims and severities:

- **"Weapon is six inheritance levels deep"** (summary) — rejected as stated: `Weapon` is four
  (`Weapon` → `TextureObject` → `SpriteSheetObject` → `DrawObject`). The concrete weapons are six.
- **"recompiles most of the game"** (finding 2) — rejected as overstated: measured at ~13 of ~40 game
  translation units. Corrected to "roughly a third", which is still the point.
- **Fire-loop finding tagged T6** — rejected as the wrong tenet. Nothing here fails quietly where it
  should be loud; a resource has no owner. Re-tagged to Services and lifetimes / T11.
- **"each is a namespace-scope `static` object"** (finding 10) — rejected for the three
  `constexpr float`s, which cost nothing at runtime. The claim holds for `NOZZLE_SIZE`,
  `NOZZLE_FRAME` and the nine `DETAILS_*` / `*_SOUND_DETAILS` objects, which is where the 48 string
  constructions come from.
- **"The base's early return exists only so these two can override it"** (finding 5) — rejected as
  inverted. The early return exists so a weapon with no loop does nothing; the overrides exist to add
  a one-shot wave on top of it. The remedy is unaffected.
- **"the same twenty lines apart from one call"** (finding 9) — rejected as too generous to the code.
  Three calls differ, and two of them (`weapon.cpp:600,603`) are explicitly qualified where the base
  is not, which devirtualises two hooks. Finding strengthened rather than trimmed.
- **"Two members now shadow each other by name"** (finding 8) — rejected as imprecise:
  `DrawObject::render_resources_` is private, so this is name hiding within `Weapon`'s scope, not
  access shadowing. Consequence unchanged; two further instances of the same pattern added.
- **Severity of the sprite-origin finding** — medium rejected, re-graded **low**: the current error
  is ~0.94 world units on a 30-unit sprite, sub-pixel at 1:1. The units coupling is the defect, not
  the present appearance.
- **Severity of the `WeaponType`-parameter finding** — medium rejected, re-graded **low**: the
  mismatch is unreachable from the single construction site, which uses its own switch selector as
  the argument.
- **Severity of the `resolve_loop_sound` finding** — medium rejected, re-graded **low**: both guards
  are provably unreachable given the four-player cap and the two-team enum.
- **Severity of the per-frame-allocation finding** — medium rejected, re-graded **low**: the carrier
  vector is one allocation among N+1, and removing it leaves the polymorphic per-projectile
  allocations that dominate. The finding now says so.
- Considered and **not** filed: a frame-rate dependence in the sprayer's rate of fire and ammo drain.
  It looks live from `weapon.cpp:208-233` alone, but `application.cpp:73` calls
  `SetFixedTimeStep(true)`, so `dt` is fixed and the behaviour is stable. Rejected before filing.
- Considered and **not** filed: `play_effect` being called on an already-playing instance every
  firing frame. DirectXTK's `SoundEffectInstance::Impl::Play` returns early when the voice is already
  playing (`SoundEffectInstance.cpp:144-145`), so this is three parameter sets per frame, not a
  retrigger. Rejected before filing.

<a id="g-game-projectile"></a>

## game-projectile — Projectiles

*Group `game-projectile` · 17 findings (4 high, 8 medium, 5 low) · source `review2/verified/game-projectile.md`, verified report.*

I re-opened every line the reviewer cited, in all sixteen assigned files, and re-derived every
number: the 60 Hz fixed step (`engine/app/application.cpp:73-75`, `game/main.cpp:37`), the shipped
weapon tuning (`weapon_consts.h`), the three level JSONs, `Vector2F(float)`'s splatting constructor
(`matt_math.h:406`, `matt_math.cpp:1514-1518`), `RectangleF::inflate_to_size`
(`matt_math.cpp:942-948`), `NameTable::resolve` and `Registry::resolve` (both
`std::map<std::string,int>::find`), and the four collision loops in `level.cpp:185-329`. All
fourteen findings have a real basis in the code and none is a duplicate of anything in
`docs/review/IMPLEMENTED.md` — that file's projectile entries are the out-of-bounds throw (fixed,
and the fix is visible at `level.cpp:307-317`) and the `default: throw` pattern (recorded as a known
remaining issue, and correctly not re-filed here). So nothing was rejected outright.

What I did throw out is a layer of consequence sitting on top of true observations. Five sub-claims
are wrong and are corrected in place: ramps are not paintable (`level_object_builder.cpp:130-163`
builds `StructureRamp` as a plain `Structure`, so "without painting" is not a consequence of the ramp
bug); `spawn_a_ceiling` in `close_quarters.json` is `STRUCTURE_JUMP_THROUGH`, not `STRUCTURE`
(it is still inside the projectile's filter, so the tunnelling point survives intact); the spray and
mist `delete_timer`s are at `projectile_consts.h:31` and `:78`, not `:35` and `:78`; `ProjectileSpray`
and `ProjectileMist` *cannot* declare `= default` because `DiffusingProjectile` has no default
constructor, so that is not an arbitrary divergence; and scoping an enum does not change MSVC's
switch-exhaustiveness diagnostics — the `default:` label is what suppresses C4062, on scoped and
unscoped enums alike. I regraded one finding down (the dead-data bundle: every item in it is dead
code or a latent mismatch with no runtime effect today, which is a low, not a medium).

I strengthened three findings with evidence the reviewer did not have — the drag dead zone is
narrower in practice than claimed because the sprayer adds the player's x velocity
(`weapon.cpp:559-562`); the tunnelling case is *worse* than claimed because gravity alone puts a
spray or ball projectile at the 5000 px/s cap after two seconds, which is 83 px per step against a
15 px collider; and adding a projectile type edits eleven places, not five. And I added three
findings: `Projectile::update(float)` silently overrides `artattack::AnimationObject::update(float)`
as well as `IGameObject::update(float)`, which is the mechanism behind the rolling divergence the
reviewer noticed; the roller's `delete_timer = 0.000001f` is a "live for exactly one collision pass"
sentinel with a hidden dependency on `Level` spawning projectiles *after* its collision-object update
loop; and `projectile.h` includes `projectile_consts.h` when it only needs `projectile_details.h`.

### Themes

- The same list written twice by hand, four lines from the header that already holds the correct
  helper — and both copies miss the same two enumerators.
- Tuning as positionally-initialised aggregates in a header, whose only field labels are comments.
  Every identity defect in this group (mist tagged `SPRAY`, `end_scale` filled from a bare `1.5f`)
  is a direct product of that shape.
- Five leaf classes encoding four bits of variation, with three demonstrated divergences and 150
  lines of byte-identical `is_colliding`.
- Data authored and never read: `player_damage`, `rotat_origin`, `DiffusionType`, `team_colour_`,
  `player_num_` — while the numbers actually applied live in `player_consts.h` with opposite signs.
- The philosophy's stated price for simplicity (T3's speed cap) is a round number derived from
  nothing, and shipped geometry is already thinner than one frame of travel.
- One heap-allocated, three-vtable `GameObject` per pellet, with a by-value ~100-byte details copy,
  at counts around 1000 — the exact grammar PHILOSOPHY's object-model section rules out for shipped
  code.
- Two string-keyed map lookups per pellet constructed, on the simulation path, in a codebase that
  built `Registry`/`NameTable` expressly to stop that.
- None of the arithmetic is constructible without a live `RenderResources`, so none of it is tested
  and none of it could be.

---

#### Add ramps to the projectile's structure filter

- **File:** `game/objects/projectile.cpp:96-99,122-125`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T4

**What:** Both hand-written copies of the "is this a structure" test omit `structure_ramp_left` and
`structure_ramp_right`, so projectiles pass through ramps without colliding and without being
deleted, while the correct helper sits in a header `projectile.h` already includes.

**Evidence:** `projectile.cpp:94-104`, inside `is_matching_collision_object_type`:

    CollisionObjectType other_type = other->collision_object_type();

    bool structure_collision =
        other_type == CollisionObjectType::structure ||
        other_type == CollisionObjectType::structure_paintable ||
        other_type == CollisionObjectType::structure_jump_through;

    if (structure_collision)
	{
		return true;
	}

and again verbatim at `projectile.cpp:120-125` inside `on_collision`. `collision_object_type.h:73-80`
— reached from `projectile.h:7` via `i_collision_game_object.h` — already defines the correct test:

    inline bool is_structure(CollisionObjectType type)
    {
    	return type == CollisionObjectType::structure ||
    		type == CollisionObjectType::structure_paintable ||
    		type == CollisionObjectType::structure_jump_through ||
    		type == CollisionObjectType::structure_ramp_left ||
    		type == CollisionObjectType::structure_ramp_right;
    }

`Level` calls that helper correctly at `level.cpp:250`, and `Player` at `player.cpp:155`.

**Why it matters:** The path is reachable and the projectile is the only initiator —
`Structure::is_colliding` returns `false` unconditionally (`structure.cpp:39-42`), so if the
projectile's filter says no, nothing else says yes. `king_of_the_hill.json:258-274` declares
`mountain_level_1_ramp_east` as `"type": "StructureRamp"` with
`"collision_type": "STRUCTURE_RAMP_RIGHT"`, a 1400 x 450 triangle;
`level_object_builder.cpp:130-163` builds it as a `Structure` whose `collision_object_type()`
returns `structure_ramp_right`. `king_of_the_hill` is in the shipped manifest
(`content/manifest.json:23-31`). Shots aimed at that ramp face pass through it and carry on to
whatever is behind, instead of stopping there.

*Correction to the raw finding:* ramps are **not** paintable — `StructureRamp` builds a plain
`Structure`, not a `StructurePaintable` — so lost paint is not a consequence here. Nor does "every
shot flies through the mountain" hold: `mountain_level_1_centre` and the rest of the massif are
ordinary `Structure` records and do stop projectiles. The defect is the ramp face specifically. The
same two copies also stop projectiles at jump-through platforms while letting players pass upward
through them; that asymmetry is a policy call, not a bug, and is left alone.

**Remedy:** Delete both copies and call `is_structure(other_type)`. `on_collision` then reduces to
`if (is_structure(t) || is_enemy_player(t)) { set_for_deletion(true); }`.

#### Fix the diffusion interpolation so it is continuous at end_time

- **File:** `game/objects/projectile.cpp:59-87`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T3

**What:** The in-range branch computes `1 + end_scale * ratio` while the past-the-end branch returns
`end_scale`, so at `end_time` the sprite and the collision rectangle jump discontinuously — the
spray shrinks 40% in one frame and stays shrunk for the rest of its life.

**Evidence:** `projectile.cpp:59-87`:

    Vector2F DiffusingProjectile::calculate_diffusion_size() const
    {
        const float time = this->timer();
        const DiffusionDetails& details = this->diffusion_details_;
        const Vector2F& base_size = this->base_size();
        Vector2F multiple;
        if (time < details.start_time)
        {
            multiple = Vector2F::ONE;
        }
        else if (time >= details.end_time)
        {
            multiple = details.end_scale;
        }
        else
        {
            float diff_length = details.end_time -
                details.start_time;
            float diff_time = time -
                details.start_time;

            float ratio = diff_time / diff_length;

            multiple = Vector2F::ONE +
                Vector2F(details.end_scale.x * ratio,
    			details.end_scale.y * ratio);
        }
        return base_size * multiple;
    }

With `DIFFUSION_DETAILS_SPRAY = { 0.2f, 1.0f, 1.5f, ... }` (`projectile_consts.h:39-45`) and
`DETAILS_SPRAY.size == (15, 15)` (`projectile_consts.h:33`): at `t → 1.0⁻`, `multiple → 2.5`, giving
37.5 px; at `t == 1.0` it becomes `1.5`, giving 22.5 px. Mist (`projectile_consts.h:86-92`, base
size 5 at `:80`) grows to 30 px by `t → 2.0⁻` and snaps to 25 px. The `time < start_time` branch *is*
continuous with the formula (ratio 0 → multiple 1), which identifies the terminal branch as the
intended endpoint and the lerp as the error.

**Why it matters:** `ProjectileSpray::update` and `ProjectileMist::update` feed this straight into
`rectangle_.inflate_to_size(...)` (`projectile_spray.cpp:37`, `projectile_mist.cpp:37`), and
`rectangle_` is both the draw destination (`shape()` returns `&rectangle_`) and the collision shape.
`inflate_to_size` preserves the centre (`matt_math.cpp:942-948`), so the whole 40% comes off the hit
area. Spray's `delete_timer` is 5.0 s against a 1.0 s `end_time` (`projectile_consts.h:31`) and
mist's is 5.0 s against a 2.0 s `end_time` (`:78`, `:89`), so four fifths of every spray
projectile's life is spent at the wrong size, on the default weapon, with a visible pop at the
transition.

**Remedy:** Make the in-range branch `Vector2F::ONE + (details.end_scale - Vector2F::ONE) * ratio`,
and pin it with a test at `t = start_time`, mid-range, and `t = end_time`.

#### Derive the projectile speed cap from the collider and the timestep, or amend T3

- **File:** `game/objects/projectile_consts.h:11`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T3

**What:** The cap PHILOSOPHY names as the accepted price for having no CCD is a round constant with
no relationship to any collider or to the fixed timestep, and it permits more travel per step than
the thinnest shipped collidable.

**Evidence:** `projectile_consts.h:11`:

    const mattmath::Vector2F MAX_VELOCITY = { 5000.0f, 5000.0f };

enforced per-axis in `projectile.cpp:231-238` and `:258-265`:

        if (MovingObject::velocity_y() > projectile_consts::MAX_VELOCITY.y)
    	{
            MovingObject::set_velocity_y(projectile_consts::MAX_VELOCITY.y);
    	}

The step is fixed at 1/60 s (`application.cpp:73-75`, `main.cpp:37`), so the cap permits 83.3 px of
travel per axis per update and 117.9 px on the diagonal. Nothing compares that to any collider.
Two reachable cases:

- **The sniper.** `DETAILS_SNIPER.starting_vel_length` is 2000 (`weapon_consts.h:79`) firing `JET`
  (`:83`); `DETAILS_JET` has zero gravity and zero drag with a 20 x 20 collider
  (`projectile_consts.h:47-58`). 2000/60 = 33.3 px per step against a 20 px extent leaves a 13.3 px
  band per step that is never sampled. `close_quarters.json:164-178` declares `spawn_a_ceiling`, 300
  x 10 — thinner than that band. (It is `"collision_type": "STRUCTURE_JUMP_THROUGH"`, not
  `"STRUCTURE"` as the raw finding said; jump-through is inside the projectile's filter at
  `projectile.cpp:99`, so it is a collidable the projectile is supposed to stop at.)
- **Gravity alone, on the default weapon.** `DETAILS_SPRAY.gravity` is 2500 (`:28`) applied as
  `alter_velocity_y(gravity * dt)` (`projectile.cpp:230`), so a spray projectile in free fall
  reaches the 5000 cap after 2.0 s of its 5.0 s life and then travels 83.3 px per step with a 15 px
  collider — a 68 px untested band, wider than most thin geometry in any of the three shipped
  levels. The bucket's `BALL` is the same gravity with a 100 px collider.

**Why it matters:** Collision is a discrete per-frame test with no swept form anywhere
(`projectile_*.cpp` `is_colliding`, `level.cpp:271-305`). T3 explicitly trades CCD away *in exchange
for* the cap, and 5000 does not buy what was traded for it. A stranger building on this engine
inherits a documented guarantee the code does not keep.

**Remedy:** Derive the cap as `min_collider_extent / dt` and assert at load that no collidable in a
level is thinner than `max_speed * dt`; or amend T3 to state the real contract and check level
geometry against it at load (T6 wants that as a named load-time error, not a silently missed shot).

#### Stop modelling every pellet as its own heap-allocated, triple-vtable GameObject

- **File:** `game/objects/projectile_builder.cpp:9-191`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T11 / T8

**What:** `build_projectiles` returns a `vector<unique_ptr<ICollisionGameObject>>` — one separate
heap allocation, three vtable pointers and a by-value copy of a 100-byte details record per pellet —
and shipped tuning puts around a thousand of them live at once.

**Evidence:** `projectile_builder.cpp:126-137`, one of six such blocks:

    	projectiles.push_back(
    		std::make_unique<ProjectileMist>(
    			RectangleF(position, DETAILS_MIST.col_rect_size),
    			velocity,
    			team,
    			player_num,
    			team_colour,
    			render_resources,
    			rotation,
    			origin,
    			effects,
    			layer_depth));

`Projectile` inherits three independently polymorphic bases (`projectile.h:18-19`):

    class Projectile : public artattack::MovingObject,
    	public artattack::AnimationObject, public ICollisionGameObject

`MovingObject`, `DrawObject` (under `AnimationObject`) and `IGameObject` (under
`ICollisionGameObject`) each declare a virtual destructor, so each contributes its own vptr — three,
24 bytes, before any state. `projectile.h:67-73` then stores by value:

    	ProjectileDetails details_ = ProjectileDetails();
    	float timer_ = 0.0f;
    	int player_num_ = -1;
    	mattmath::Colour team_colour_ = colour_consts::GRAY;
    	projectile_type type_ = SPRAY;

`ProjectileDetails` (`projectile_details.h:6-17`) is exactly 100 bytes on x64 (5 floats + an enum +
two `Vector2F` + two 32-byte `std::string`s). Both strings are read once, in the `AnimationObject`
base's constructor, and carried for life. (They are 14 and 12 characters, so MSVC's SSO means the
copy itself allocates nothing — the cost is footprint and a non-trivial copy constructor, not a
malloc.) `player_num_` and `team_colour_` are never read at all: their only accessors,
`Projectile::player_num()` and `Projectile::team_colour()` (`projectile.h:58-59`), have no callers
anywhere, and the team colour is stored a second time in `DrawObject::colour_` because every leaf
passes it as both the `team_colour` and the `color` argument (`projectile_spray.cpp:19-22`).

The counts are computable from shipped tuning. The mister fires every 0.1 s
(`weapon_consts.h:122`) and each shot makes five pellets (`projectile_builder.cpp:126-189`); pellets
have zero gravity and a 5 s `delete_timer` (`projectile_consts.h:75,78`); ammo does not bind for the
first ten seconds of a burst (usage 0.01/shot at 10 shots/s against 1.0 starting ammo,
`weapon.cpp:209-232`). That is 250 live objects per player, 1000 in a four-player match, before a
single spray projectile — and the sprayer's `shoot_interval` is `0.0f` (`weapon_consts.h:44`), so it
adds 60 more per second per player.

**Why it matters:** `Level::update_level_logic` walks `collision_objects_` against itself pairwise
(`level.cpp:289-304`) with a virtual `is_colliding` per ordered pair; each of those calls
`other->collision_object_type()`, itself a virtual returning the result of a two-level switch
(`projectile.cpp:153-193`). At 1000 objects that is on the order of 10⁶ pair tests and several
million nested switches per frame. PHILOSOPHY's object model says the engine's own internals *and
everything it ships* are value-first — "A paint-tile grid is one `GameObject`, not ten thousand" —
and throughput is named as the engine's identity (T8). This is also the item that will be most
expensive to undo, because `ICollisionGameObject` is the seam the whole game is written against.

**Remedy:** Model the pellets as one registered batch object over contiguous POD state (position,
velocity, timer, team, type index), with the immutable per-type record referenced by handle rather
than copied into each instance. Drop `player_num_` and `team_colour_` while doing it.

#### Give ProjectileMist its own projectile_type

- **File:** `game/objects/projectile_mist.cpp:19-22`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T5

**What:** `ProjectileMist` passes `SPRAY` as its type tag, so every mist pellet reports
`projectile_spray_team_*` and the two `projectile_mist_team_*` enumerators are unreachable.

**Evidence:** `projectile_mist.cpp:19-22`:

    	DiffusingProjectile(velocity, team, player_num, team_colour,
    		SPRAY, render_resources,
    		DETAILS_MIST, DIFFUSION_DETAILS_MIST,
    		team_colour, rotation, origin, effects, layer_depth),

against `projectile_spray.cpp:19-22`, which is character-for-character the same but for
`DETAILS_SPRAY, DIFFUSION_DETAILS_SPRAY`. That argument reaches `Projectile::type_`, which
`Projectile::collision_object_type()` (`projectile.cpp:153-193`) switches on to produce
`CollisionObjectType::projectile_spray_team_a` / `_b`.

**Why it matters:** The mislabel is masked *only* by a coincidence in tuning.
`Player::on_projectile_collision` (`player.cpp:675-712`) charges `SPRAY_DAMAGE` where it should
charge `MIST_DAMAGE`, and `player_consts.h:64,68` happen to set both to `0.01f`. The instant either
is retuned, the mister silently deals the sprayer's damage. Everything else that classifies —
`structure_paintable.cpp:56-67`, `paint_tile.cpp:97-112`, `collision_object_type.h:41-71`,
`player.cpp:212-228` — lists both enumerators, so all of that carries live branches for a value
nothing can produce.

**Remedy:** Pass `MIST`. The underlying cause is twelve same-typed positional parameters
(`projectile.h:81-93`) plus an unscoped enum whose enumerators are interchangeable `int`s; scoping
the enum (below) makes this class of mistake a compile error.

#### The wind-resistance dead zone is 240x too wide — it means `wind_resistance * dt`

- **File:** `game/objects/projectile.cpp:241-257`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T3

**What:** The guard that stops drag overshooting zero compares horizontal speed against
`wind_resistance * 4.0f` instead of the per-step decrement `wind_resistance * dt`, creating an
80 px/s snap-to-zero dead zone for the sprayer and the bucket.

**Evidence:** `projectile.cpp:240-257`:

        //wind resistance
        if (std::fabs(MovingObject::velocity_x()) > wind_resistance * 4.0f)
        {
            //right
            if (MovingObject::velocity_x() > 0.0f)
            {
                MovingObject::alter_velocity_x(-wind_resistance * dt);
            }
            //left
            else
            {
                MovingObject::alter_velocity_x(wind_resistance * dt);
            }
        }
    	else
    	{
            MovingObject::set_velocity_x(0.0f);
    	}

The step actually applied in both arms is `wind_resistance * dt`. With `wind_resistance = 20`
(`projectile_consts.h:29` for spray, `:97` for ball) and `dt = 1/60`, the step is 0.333 px/s and the
threshold is 80 px/s — 240 times the quantity the guard exists to protect against.

**Why it matters:** Reachable on the default weapon. The sprayer launches at 1100 px/s
(`weapon_consts.h:45`) along the aim direction, so a shot fired within `asin(80/1100)` ≈ 4.2° of
vertical has `|vx| <= 80` and has its entire horizontal velocity zeroed on its first update, with no
visual or audible cue. *Narrowing the raw finding:* the sprayer and bucket are
`RelativeVelocityWeapon`s with `AddPlayerVelocity::x_only`
(`weapon_consts.h:55-59,167-171`, applied at `weapon.cpp:559-562`), so a moving player's x velocity
is added to the launch and usually carries the shot out of the dead zone — the snap bites a
stationary player, or one whose motion happens to cancel the aim. The magic `4.0f` appears nowhere
else and is undocumented, so a reader cannot tell intent from typo; the drag model is also constant
deceleration, not resistance proportional to speed, which is fine under T3 but means the name lies.

**Remedy:** Compare against `wind_resistance * dt` — the amount about to be subtracted — or clamp
the result rather than branching on the input.

#### Five leaf classes encode four bits of variation and have already diverged three times

- **File:** `game/objects/projectile_spray.cpp:52-83`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T4

**What:** `projectile_spray/jet/ball/mist/rolling` (.h + .cpp, ~430 lines) are the same file five
times; the diff is four decisions, and each place where the copies differ by accident is a defect.

**Evidence:** the complete diff of the five `.cpp` files:

- **Constructor** — differs only in the `projectile_type` tag, the `DETAILS_*` constant, and (spray,
  mist) an extra `DIFFUSION_DETAILS_*`. The local is spelled `size` in ball/mist/spray
  (`projectile_ball.cpp:25`) and `col_size` in jet/rolling (`projectile_jet.cpp:25`).
- **`update`** — ball (`projectile_ball.cpp:30-41`) and jet (`projectile_jet.cpp:30-41`) are
  byte-identical; spray and mist add one line,
  `this->rectangle_.inflate_to_size(calculate_diffusion_size());`; rolling omits *both* the
  `rectangle_.offset(dx)` and the `AnimationObject::update(dt)` (`projectile_rolling.cpp:29-35`).
- **`draw`** — four are byte-identical
  `this->AnimationObject::draw(sprite_batch, this->rectangle_, camera);`; rolling is a no-op.
- **`bounds`**, **`shape`** — identical in all five.
- **`is_colliding`** — byte-identical in all five, 30 lines each, 150 lines total
  (`projectile_spray.cpp:52-83`, `projectile_jet.cpp:50-81`, `projectile_ball.cpp:51-82`,
  `projectile_mist.cpp:52-83`, `projectile_rolling.cpp:48-79`), including the same comments:

    	// aabb check
    	if (!this->shape()->AABB_intersects(other->shape()))
    	{
    		return false;
    	}
    	else // AABBs are intersecting
    	{
    		// if the other object is a rectangle, then we have a collision
    		// since the AABB check passed
    		ShapeType other_shape_type = other->shape()->shape_type();
    		if (other_shape_type == ShapeType::rectangle)
    		{
    			return true;
    		}
    	}

- **Headers** — identical but for the class name and base.

Two accidental divergences: mist's `SPRAY` tag, and rolling's missing `offset`/animation tick
(inert today only because the roller's `starting_vel_length` is `0.0f`, `weapon_consts.h:95`, and its
`draw` is a no-op — nothing states that dependency).

*Correction to the raw finding:* the third "divergence" it named — spray and mist declaring
`= delete` where ball, jet and rolling declare `= default` — is not arbitrary. `DiffusingProjectile`
declares no default constructor (`projectile.h:81-93` is its only one), so `= default` on
`ProjectileSpray` would be implicitly deleted anyway. The real defect is on the base and is filed
separately below.

**Why it matters:** The behaviour that varies is data (which details, diffuse or not, visible or
not), so the class-per-variant split buys nothing and costs a guaranteed divergence per edit. The
copied `is_colliding` also propagates an unstated invariant five times — the
`ShapeType::rectangle` early-out is sound only because `this->shape()` is always an axis-aligned
`RectangleF`, which nothing states and nothing enforces. (It is sound today:
`ShapeType::rectangle_rotated` is a separate enumerator, `shape_type.h:5-13`.)

**Remedy:** One concrete `Projectile` type parameterised by its details record plus a
diffusion/visible flag; the five headers and five `is_colliding` bodies collapse to one.

#### Move projectile tuning out of a header of positional aggregates

- **File:** `game/objects/projectile_consts.h:13-105`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T7

**What:** Every projectile definition is a `static const` aggregate in a header, positionally
initialised with `//comment` labels, in a namespace six `.cpp` files pull in wholesale.

**Evidence:** `projectile_consts.h:26-37`:

    static const ProjectileDetails DETAILS_SPRAY =
    {
        2500.0f,                        //gravity
        20.0f,                          //wind_resistance
        artattack::RotationOrigin::no_rotation,   //rotat_origin
        5.0f,                           //delete_timer
        -0.1f,                           //player_damage
        mattmath::Vector2F(15.0f, 15.0f),        //size
        mattmath::Vector2F(15.0f, 15.0f),         //col_rect_size
        "sprite_sheet_1",               //sheet_name
        "projectile_3",                        //animation_strip_name
    };

`DIFFUSION_DETAILS_SPRAY` (`:39-45`) fills the `Vector2F end_scale` field from a bare `1.5f`, which
compiles because `Vector2F(float)` is a non-explicit converting constructor (`matt_math.h:406`,
`matt_math.cpp:1514-1518`) that splats to both components — and the comment says `//end_size`, not
`end_scale`. `static` at namespace scope gives each of the eight aggregates internal linkage, so
every translation unit that includes this header gets its own dynamically-initialised copy,
twelve `std::string` constructions included.

**Why it matters:** *Strengthening the raw finding, which counted five edit sites.* Adding one
projectile type today edits **eleven** places:

1. the `projectile_type` enumerator (`projectile.h:9-16`)
2. a `DETAILS_*` blob here
3. a new leaf `.h` and `.cpp` (~86 lines, mostly copied)
4. a `case` in `ProjectileBuilder::build_projectiles` (`projectile_builder.cpp:23-108`)
5. two enumerators in `CollisionObjectType` (`collision_object_type.h:14-23`)
6. three classification helpers (`collision_object_type.h:41-71`)
7. two branches in `Projectile::collision_object_type` (`projectile.cpp:159-189`)
8. two team lists in `Player::on_collision` (`player.cpp:212-228`)
9. a branch in `Player::on_projectile_collision` (`player.cpp:679-712`)
10. two lists in `PaintTile::on_collision` (`paint_tile.cpp:97-112`)
11. the offensive-projectile list in `StructurePaintable::on_collision`
    (`structure_paintable.cpp:57-67`)

plus a damage constant in `player_consts.h:64-68` — and a rebuild that reaches `player.h`,
`level.h`, `level_builder.h` and `game_states.h` through `weapon_details.h:4` → `projectile.h` and
`weapon.h:10` → `projectile_builder.h`. (The raw finding said "most of the game parses it"; the
measured fan-out is the object/level/state layer, roughly a third of the 46 game `.cpp` files, not
all of it.) T7's promise is that adding a type edits JSON and a registration line and rebuilds
nothing. Positional aggregates with comment labels are also exactly what let mist be tagged `SPRAY`.

**Remedy:** Move the definitions to `content/*.json` read into a registry at load, as T7 prescribes;
until then, C++20 designated initialisers (`.gravity = 2500.0f, ...`) at least make the field names
compiler-checked, and `inline constexpr` removes the per-TU copies.

#### `Projectile::update` silently overrides two unrelated virtuals

- **File:** `game/objects/projectile.h:36`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T5

**What:** `Projectile` inherits both `artattack::AnimationObject` and `ICollisionGameObject`, and
both declare `virtual void update(float)`. The single declaration in `Projectile` overrides both, so
the animation tick can never be dispatched and every leaf has to remember to call the base by hand —
which is the mechanism behind the rolling divergence above.

**Evidence:** `engine/core/i_game_object.h`:

    		virtual void update(float dt) = 0;

`engine/render/animation_object.h:26`, in the `protected:` section:

    		virtual void update(float dt);

`game/objects/projectile.h:36` declares one function that satisfies both:

    	void update(float dt) override = 0;

`override` compiles and says nothing about which base is meant. Every leaf then has to reach past its
own override with an explicit qualification — `projectile_spray.cpp:42`:

    	AnimationObject::update(dt);

and `ProjectileRolling::update` (`projectile_rolling.cpp:29-35`) does not.

**Why it matters:** No live symptom today — nothing calls `AnimationObject::update` polymorphically,
because it is protected. But the collision is invisible at every one of its declaration sites: a
reader of `projectile.h:36` cannot tell that this line also disables the engine's animation tick,
and the compiler will never warn, because both overrides are legitimate. T5 wants the wall to be a
compile error; here the wall is a convention that one of the five leaves has already broken. It also
publicly exposes what `AnimationObject` deliberately made protected.

**Remedy:** Rename the engine-side tick — `AnimationObject::advance_animation(float dt)` — so the
two virtuals are distinct, and let the leaf call it explicitly because it means to, not because it
must. This applies to `PaintTileSplash` and every other `AnimationObject` client too.

#### The roller's one-frame lifetime is a magic epsilon with a hidden ordering dependency

- **File:** `game/objects/projectile_consts.h:60-71`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T3 / T7

**What:** `DETAILS_ROLLING.delete_timer = 0.000001f` encodes "exist for exactly one collision pass"
as a number smaller than any `dt`. It works only because `Level` happens to append new projectiles
*after* its collision-object update loop; reordering those two loops silently deletes every roller
shot before it can ever collide.

**Evidence:** `projectile_consts.h:60-71`:

    static const ProjectileDetails DETAILS_ROLLING =
    {
        0.0f,                           //gravity
        0.0f,                           //wind_resistance
        artattack::RotationOrigin::no_rotation,   //rotat_origin
        0.000001f,                           //delete_timer
        -1000.0f,                        //player_damage
        mattmath::Vector2F(50.0f, 50.0f),        //size
        mattmath::Vector2F(50.0f, 50.0f),         //col_rect_size
        "sprite_sheet_1",               //sheet_name
        "projectile_3",                        //animation_strip_name
    };

`projectile.cpp:271-278` ages then tests:

        this->alter_timer(dt);

        if (this->timer() > this->delete_timer())
    	{
    		this->set_for_deletion(true);
    	}

`ProjectileRolling` also never draws (`projectile_rolling.cpp:36-40`) and never applies its
displacement (`:29-35`), and `WeaponRoller`'s `starting_vel_length` is `0.0f`
(`weapon_consts.h:95`). So the whole roller weapon is: stamp an invisible, immobile 50 x 50 collider
at the nozzle, let it live for exactly one collision pass, delete it. The ordering that makes that
true is `level.cpp:185-188` (update existing collision objects) → `:218-224` (append the new ones) →
`:271-305` (collision) → `:320-329` (delete). Nothing at any of those four sites says so.

**Why it matters:** T3 permits a simple model but requires exact, documented semantics; T7 says data
carries *how much*, not *how*. `0.000001f` is control flow written as a tuning number, and its
correctness rests on a spawn/update order stated nowhere — exactly the load-bearing ordering
PHILOSOPHY's Services and lifetimes section says must be designed away or written down. The
`-1000.0f` damage in the same record is dead (see below), so a reader has no way to tell which of
these two numbers is load-bearing.

**Remedy:** Give the roller an explicit `lifetime_frames = 1` (or a `one_shot` flag on the details
record) so the intent is legible, and state the spawn-then-collide ordering as a comment at
`level.cpp:218`. A test that the roller paints on its spawn frame would pin it.

#### Resolve sheet and strip names once, not once per projectile fired

- **File:** `game/objects/projectile.cpp:20-22`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** performance
- **Tenet:** T7 / T8

**What:** Constructing a projectile performs two `std::map<std::string, int>` lookups, and
projectiles are constructed dozens of times a second per player on the simulation path.

**Evidence:** `projectile.cpp:20-22`:

        MovingObject(velocity, rotation),
        AnimationObject(details.sheet_name, details.animation_strip_name,
                        render_resources, color, rotation, origin, effects, layer_depth),

`AnimationObject`'s constructor (`animation_object.cpp:8-23`) calls
`SpriteSheetObject(sheet_name, ...)`, which does
`render_resources->resolve_sprite_sheet(sheet_name)` (`sprite_sheet_object.cpp:17`), and then
`resolve_animation_strip(animation_strip_name)`. Those bottom out in `Registry::resolve` and
`NameTable::resolve` (`engine/core/name_table.h:53-62`), both
`std::map<std::string, int>::find` plus an `std::out_of_range` throw on miss. `NameTable`'s own
header states the contract being broken:

    	//     resolve(name) -> Handle       once, at load
    	//     get(handle)   -> Resource*    per frame - no string, no map, no compare

**Why it matters:** `Level::update_level_logic` spawns projectiles inside the per-frame update
(`level.cpp:218-224`). The sprayer's `shoot_interval` is `0.0f` (`weapon_consts.h:44`), so it fires
every frame while it has ammo, and the mister builds five pellets ten times a second — 120+
string-keyed map probes per second per player, in a codebase that introduced `Registry`/`NameTable`
for the express purpose of not doing this. Both `Content and assets` and `Performance` in PHILOSOPHY
state the rule flatly. The throw is also on the firing path with no catch above it, so a content
rename turns pulling the trigger into a process kill rather than the load-time error T6 wants.

**Remedy:** Resolve the sheet and strip handles once when the projectile definitions are loaded and
store the handles in the details record, so construction copies two ints.

#### Rename `enum projectile_type` — it is the last unscoped enum in the repository

- **File:** `game/objects/projectile.h:9-16`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS (Types, Constants and enumerators, Never, Files)

**What:** `projectile_type` is unscoped, snake_case-named and SCREAMING-enumerated, and it rides
inside `projectile.h` instead of its own header.

**Evidence:** `projectile.h:9-16`:

    enum projectile_type
    {
    	SPRAY,
    	JET,
    	ROLLING,
    	MIST,
    	BALL
    };

`grep -rn "^\s*enum [A-Za-z_]" --include=*.h --include=*.cpp game/ engine/ | grep -v "enum class"`
returns exactly one line: this one. Every other enum in the repository is `enum class` with a
PascalCase type and snake_case enumerators — `CollisionObjectType`, `PlayerTeam`, `WeaponType`,
`DiffusionType`, `RotationOrigin`, `ShapeType`, `LevelMode`, `AddPlayerVelocity` and the rest. The
siblings also each own a header named for them (`weapon_type.h`, `player_team.h`,
`collision_object_type.h`, `level_mode.h`); this one does not.

**Why it matters:** This is one file the conversion pass skipped, not a general backlog item, and
the fan-out makes it expensive: `weapon_details.h:4` includes `projectile.h` and `weapon.h:10`
includes `projectile_builder.h`, so `SPRAY`, `JET`, `MIST`, `BALL` and `ROLLING` are
global-namespace `int`s wherever `player.h` or `level.h` reach. Being implicitly convertible `int`s
is precisely what let `ProjectileMist` be constructed with `SPRAY` without a diagnostic, in a
constructor call with twelve same-typed positional arguments. CONVENTIONS/Never also reserves
SCREAMING names for macros so that a screaming name always signals preprocessor danger.

*Correction to the raw finding:* its claim that unscoped-ness is "why they carry `default: throw`
arms" is wrong — scoping does not change MSVC's switch-exhaustiveness diagnostics; the `default:`
label is what suppresses C4062, on scoped and unscoped enums alike. Converting the enum will not by
itself make those arms unreachable.

**Remedy:** `enum class ProjectileType : std::uint8_t` in `game/objects/projectile_type.h`, and
qualify the ~25 use sites (`projectile.cpp:161-186`, `projectile_builder.cpp:25-89`, the five leaf
constructors, `weapon_consts.h:27,49,83,99,127,161`).

#### Delete or wire up the projectile data nothing reads

- **File:** `game/objects/projectile.cpp:286-294`
- **Severity:** low *(regraded down from medium — every item here is dead code or a latent
  mismatch with no runtime effect today)*
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T7

**What:** Four authored fields and four public/protected accessors have zero readers, one accessor
returns the wrong member, and the damage numbers that *are* applied live in a different header with
opposite signs.

**Evidence:** `projectile.cpp:286-294`:

    Vector2F Projectile::col_rect_size() const
    {
    	return this->details().size;
    }

    float Projectile::player_damage() const
    {
    	return this->details().player_damage;
    }

`col_rect_size()` returns `size`, not `col_rect_size` (`projectile_details.h:13-14`). A repo-wide
grep finds no caller of `Projectile::col_rect_size()` or `player_damage()` (`projectile.h:49-50`),
nor of `Projectile::player_num()` or `team_colour()` (`projectile.h:58-59`). The same confusion
appears once more in `DiffusingProjectile::base_size()` (`projectile.cpp:54-57`), which returns
`details().size` while the rectangle it scales was built from `col_rect_size`
(`projectile_builder.cpp:30`) — latent only because the shipped records set the two equal in all six.

Also dead: `ProjectileDetails::rotat_origin` (`projectile_details.h:10`) — grep finds its
declaration and the six sites that set it, and nothing that reads it, so `DETAILS_JET`'s
`RotationOrigin::center` (`projectile_consts.h:51`) does nothing; and the whole `DiffusionType` enum
(`projectile_details.h:19-24`) — `calculate_diffusion_size` never reads
`diffusion_details_.type`, so `linear_size` and `linear_size_and_col_rect` are indistinguishable
(and `linear_size` is unimplementable, since one `rectangle_` serves as both sprite destination and
collider).

The damage actually applied comes from `player_consts.h:64-68`:

        constexpr float SPRAY_DAMAGE = 0.01f;
        constexpr float JET_DAMAGE = 0.334f;
        constexpr float ROLLING_DAMAGE = 0.015f;
        constexpr float BALL_DAMAGE = 0.201f;
        constexpr float MIST_DAMAGE = 0.01f;

against `projectile_consts.h`'s `-0.1f`, `-0.5f`, `-1000.0f`, `-0.1f`, `-0.05f`.

**Why it matters:** Two contradictory sets of damage numbers, one signed the wrong way and one
66000x out (`-1000.0f` against `0.015f`), is a trap for whoever next tunes the roller — they will
edit the wrong file and see nothing change, which is the quiet failure T6 exists to prevent. Dead
enums and dead fields also tell a reader the system supports options it does not.

*Note on a raw-finding claim:* it says the dead `rotat_origin` is why "the sniper's bolt never
rotates to face its travel". True that it does not rotate, but wiring `rotat_origin` up would not
fix it on its own — `Weapon::shoot` (`weapon.cpp:340-354`) never passes a `rotation` argument at all,
so every projectile is built with the default `0.0f`.

**Remedy:** Delete `player_damage()`, `player_num()`, `team_colour()`, `rotat_origin` and
`DiffusionType`, or make the details record the single source of truth and delete the
`player_consts` copies; fix `col_rect_size()` and `base_size()` to return `col_rect_size`.

#### The ballistics cannot be unit tested at all

- **File:** `game/objects/projectile.cpp:226-279`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** testing
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY (Tests and toolchain)

**What:** Every behaviour worth pinning in this group — gravity, drag, the speed cap, lifetime,
diffusion — sits on a type that cannot be constructed without a `RenderResources` holding a loaded
sprite sheet and animation strip, so none of it has or can have a test.

**Evidence:** `Projectile::update_movement` (`projectile.cpp:226-279`) is pure arithmetic on
`MovingObject` state, and so is `calculate_diffusion_size` (`:59-87`). But `Projectile`'s constructor
runs `AnimationObject(details.sheet_name, details.animation_strip_name, render_resources, ...)`
(`:21-22`), whose own constructor immediately resolves and dereferences the sheet
(`animation_object.cpp:16-22`). `tests/` contains only `assets/`, `core/` and `math/` — eight `.cpp`
files, none of them game code — so there is no game test target and no projectile test anywhere.

**Why it matters:** Two of the confirmed defects above (the diffusion discontinuity, the drag dead
zone) are three-line arithmetic errors that a five-line test would have caught the day the code was
written. This is also the engine/game boundary argument in miniature: the moment the ballistics stop
inheriting from a render type, they become constructible and assertable without a window — which is
what PHILOSOPHY means by "Everything below the platform edge is testable headlessly".

**Remedy:** Separate the ballistic state from the render object — a plain value struct updated by a
free function — so the arithmetic is constructible and assertable on its own.

#### Delete `Projectile() = default` and the defaulted leaf constructors it enables

- **File:** `game/objects/projectile.h:22`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T5

**What:** `Projectile` defaults its default constructor, which lets `ProjectileBall`,
`ProjectileJet` and `ProjectileRolling` default theirs — producing an object whose first `update()`
dereferences a null `RenderResources`.

**Evidence:** `projectile.h:22`:

    	Projectile() = default;

`projectile_ball.h:8`, `projectile_jet.h:8` and `projectile_rolling.h:8` each read
`ProjectileX() = default;`. A default-constructed leaf leaves `details_ = ProjectileDetails()` —
`delete_timer = -1.0f` (`projectile_details.h:11`) so it dies on its first tick — `team_ =
PlayerTeam::none` so `collision_object_type()` throws (`projectile.cpp:190-191`), and a
default-constructed `AnimationObject` whose `DrawObject::render_resources_` is `nullptr`.
`AnimationObject::update` then calls `animation_strip()`, which is
`this->sprite_sheet()->animation_strip(...)` (`animation_object.cpp:25-28`) on that null pointer.

`ProjectileSpray` and `ProjectileMist` say `= delete` instead (`projectile_spray.h:8`,
`projectile_mist.h:8`), but that is not a stylistic choice: `DiffusingProjectile` declares no default
constructor (`projectile.h:81-93`), so `= default` there would be implicitly deleted anyway. The
divergence is a symptom of the base, not of the leaves.

**Why it matters:** No caller default-constructs one today, so this is not currently reachable — it
is a loaded gun left on the table in a family PHILOSOPHY says the sample game exists to hand over as
starter code to copy. T5 wants the compiler to be the one saying no.

**Remedy:** Delete `Projectile() = default` and the three leaf `= default` declarations; the
`DiffusingProjectile` branch already has no default constructor and needs no change.

#### `projectile.h` drags the whole tuning table into everything that includes it

- **File:** `game/objects/projectile.h:4`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS (Files) / PHILOSOPHY (Tests and toolchain)

**What:** `projectile.h` includes `projectile_consts.h` but uses nothing from it; the types it
actually needs, `ProjectileDetails` and `DiffusionDetails`, come from `projectile_details.h` one
level down.

**Evidence:** `projectile.h:1-7`:

    #pragma once

    #include "game/objects/player_team.h"
    #include "game/objects/projectile_consts.h"
    #include "engine/render/animation_object.h"
    #include "engine/core/moving_object.h"
    #include "game/objects/i_collision_game_object.h"

Nothing in `projectile.h` names `projectile_consts`. `projectile_consts.h:3` is
`#include "game/objects/projectile_details.h"`, which is the only thing `projectile.h` needs.
`projectile.cpp` does use `projectile_consts::MAX_VELOCITY` (`:231-264`), and the six leaf `.cpp`
files each open with `using namespace projectile_consts;` — all of them relying on this transitive
include rather than saying so.

**Why it matters:** `weapon_details.h:4` includes `projectile.h` and `weapon.h:10` includes
`projectile_builder.h`, so this one line pushes eight `static const` aggregates — six of them
carrying two `std::string`s each, all of them internally linked and therefore dynamically
initialised once per translation unit — into `player.h`, `level.h`, `level_builder.h` and
`game_states.h` and everything that includes those. CONVENTIONS calls compile speed a maintained
property kept by light headers and disciplined includes, and PHILOSOPHY calls a build-time
regression a defect.

**Remedy:** Change `projectile.h:4` to `#include "game/objects/projectile_details.h"` and add an
explicit `#include "game/objects/projectile_consts.h"` to `projectile.cpp` and to each leaf `.cpp`
that opens the namespace.

#### Remove the unused constants that shadow `player_consts`

- **File:** `game/objects/projectile_consts.h:7-24`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS (Constants and enumerators)

**What:** Five constants in `projectile_consts` have no readers, and four collide by name with
differently-valued constants in `player_consts`.

**Evidence:** `projectile_consts.h:7-10` and `:13-24`:

        const mattmath::Vector2F DEFAULT_STARTING_POSITION = { 0.0f, 0.0f };
        const mattmath::Vector2F DEFAULT_SIZE = { 10.0f, 10.0f };
        const mattmath::Vector2F STARTING_DX = { 0.0f, 0.0f };
        const mattmath::Vector2F STARTING_VELOCITY = { 0.0f, 0.0f };

        static const ProjectileDetails DETAILS_DEFAULT = ...

`player_consts.h:19-24` declares `DEFAULT_STARTING_POSITION`, `DEFAULT_SIZE` (`{52, 120}`, not
`{10, 10}`), `STARTING_DX` and `STARTING_VELOCITY`. Grepping `game/` finds one use of `DEFAULT_SIZE`
(`player_builder.cpp:39`, which does `using namespace player_consts;` and not the projectile one),
no use of any projectile copy, and no use of `projectile_consts::DETAILS_DEFAULT` —
`weapon.h:56` uses `weapon_consts::DETAILS_DEFAULT`, a different symbol.

**Why it matters:** `projectile_builder.cpp:6` and all five leaf `.cpp` files already do
`using namespace projectile_consts;`; the day one of them also needs `player_consts`, four names
become ambiguous. It is a compile error rather than a silent wrong value, so the cost is confusion,
not corruption — but it is dead weight in a header with a wide include fan-out, and CONVENTIONS says
constants that stay in code live next to the one thing they configure, not in a `consts` namespace
collecting strays.

**Remedy:** Delete the five unused constants; they are not tuning anything.

---

### Rejected

No whole finding was rejected — all fourteen have a verified basis in the code, and none duplicates
an entry in `IMPLEMENTED.md`. The following sub-claims inside otherwise-valid findings were rejected
or corrected, and the finding text above reflects the correction:

- *"projectiles pass through ramps ... without painting"* (finding 1) — **rejected.**
  `level_object_builder.cpp:130-163` builds `StructureRamp` as a plain `Structure`, not a
  `StructurePaintable`, so there is no paint to lose on a ramp.
- *"on `king_of_the_hill` every shot flies through the mountain"* (summary) — **rejected.** One
  ramp face is affected; `mountain_level_1_centre` and the other massif records are ordinary
  `Structure`s that do stop projectiles.
- *"`close_quarters.json:164-174` ... a 300 x 10 `Structure`"* (finding 3) — **corrected.** Its
  `collision_type` is `STRUCTURE_JUMP_THROUGH`. It is still inside the projectile's filter
  (`projectile.cpp:99`), so the tunnelling argument is unaffected.
- *"`projectile_consts.h:35,78`" cited for the spray and mist lifetimes* (finding 2) —
  **corrected.** Line 35 is the spray's `sheet_name`; the `delete_timer`s are at `:31` and `:78`.
- *"spray and mist declare `= delete` while ball, jet and rolling declare `= default`"* framed as an
  accidental divergence (finding 7) — **rejected as a divergence.** `DiffusingProjectile` has no
  default constructor, so `= default` on spray or mist would be implicitly deleted. The defect is
  `Projectile() = default` on the base, filed separately.
- *"being unscoped means `/W4` cannot check exhaustiveness ... which is why they carry `default:
  throw` arms"* (finding 11) — **rejected.** `enum class` does not change MSVC's switch
  diagnostics; the `default:` label is what suppresses C4062 either way. The implicit-`int`
  conversion argument in the same finding stands.
- *"the sniper's bolt never rotates to face its travel"* attributed to the dead `rotat_origin`
  (finding 9) — **corrected.** True but not sufficient: `Weapon::shoot` (`weapon.cpp:340-354`)
  never passes a `rotation` argument, so the projectile is built with `0.0f` regardless.
- *"a by-value copy ... including two `std::string`s"* implying per-pellet allocation (finding 4) —
  **narrowed.** Both strings are 14 and 12 characters and fit MSVC's small-string buffer, so the
  copy allocates nothing; the cost is footprint and a non-trivial copy constructor.
- *"any shot fired within about 4.2 degrees of vertical"* (finding 6) — **narrowed.** The sprayer
  and bucket add the player's x velocity (`weapon.cpp:559-562`), so the dead zone bites a
  stationary player, not every near-vertical shot.
- *"a header most of the game parses"* (finding 8) — **narrowed.** The measured fan-out is the
  object/level/state layer, roughly a third of the 46 game `.cpp` files.

## game-world-objects — Structures, paint tiles, collision interfaces

*Group `game-world-objects` · 14 findings (2 high, 7 medium, 5 low) · source `review2/verified/game-world-objects.md`, verified report.*

I re-opened all eleven assigned files in full and every line the reviewer cited, plus
`game/objects/level.cpp`, `player.cpp`, `projectile.cpp`, the engine bases
(`i_game_object.h`, `draw_object.h`, `sprite_sheet_object.h`, `texture_object.h`,
`animation_object.h`, `sound_bank.h`, `audio_resources.h`), `engine/collision/`,
`game/CMakeLists.txt`, `game/pch.h`, `tests/`, `game/content/manifest.json`,
`game/content/sounds/sound_bank_1.json` and the three shipped level JSONs. I re-derived
the tile counts from the level data with the builder's own arithmetic and got exactly the
reviewer's numbers (close_quarters 1,898 / king_of_the_hill 4,116 / turbulence 5,230), and
I re-ran every "this is dead" and "this is never called" claim as a tree-wide grep.

Every finding survived as an observation; four had a consequence or a count that did not.
**Finding 4 is regraded medium → low**: `PaintTile::bounds()` is unreachable — no
`ICollisionGameObject*` or `IGameObject*` ever points at a `PaintTile`, so the scene never
culls on it. The live half of that finding is the *missing* `bounds()` override on
`StructurePaintable`, whose worst case is a 10-unit fringe on a structure hundreds of units
wide, and the splash overhang itself is already on record from the previous review. I
re-anchored the finding to the missing override and corrected the consequence.
**Finding 7's** claim that `"WaterSplashing"` is "the one asset name in the tree that is
neither snake_case" is false: all twenty-four wave names in `sound_bank_1.json` are the
source `.wav` filenames baked into the `.xwb` name table, so this is a content-pipeline
item, not a string edit — corrected, and the remedy changed accordingly.
**Finding 12's** claim that `on_collision` mutates through the pointer the `const` fails to
protect is wrong — `SoundBank::play_wave` is `const`; the real T5 point is that
`AudioResources::sound_bank() const` hands back a non-const `SoundBank*`, so the `const`
propagates nothing. Corrected. Three counts were off and are fixed inline: 155
`CollisionObjectType` occurrences across 14 files (not 120 across 8), sixteen `*_consts`
namespaces (not eleven), six header-scope `std::string`s (not five), and `engine/collision/`
holds two files (`partitioner.h`, `partitioner.cpp`), not one.

Nothing was rejected outright, but two findings substantially re-file items the previous
review already carries as Outstanding, and I have said so in each: finding 2 **is** critical
`#13`, and finding 3's header half is `LevelObjectBuilder.cpp` finding 4. They are kept
because the new material — that `#13` is now entirely game-local, and that the CMake
conversion added a `game -> rapidjson` target arrow ARCHITECTURE's graph does not have — is
real and postdates that review. I added two findings of my own: the `set_for_deletion`
no-op default, which is new code carrying a silent-refusal contract, and the game-type name
sitting in an engine header's documentation.

### Themes

- The group is the worked example PHILOSOPHY uses twice and inverts both times: thousands of
  individually polymorphic paint tiles where "a paint-tile grid is one `GameObject`", and a
  22-enumerator flat type tag where "collidability is layer/mask filtering plus an opaque
  game tag".
- The interface tax is paid and none of the flexibility is bought — four of `PaintTile`'s
  eight interface members, and three of `PaintTileSplash`'s four, are unreachable, because
  no pointer of either interface type ever points at one.
- Conventions work stopped at the engine boundary: `game/` still owns the global namespace,
  still `I`-prefixes its interfaces, still SCREAMs its constants, and still writes its
  registry keys in PascalCase and SCREAMING_SNAKE.
- Tuning numbers T7 puts in JSON — tile pitch, band thickness, mix level, sheet and frame
  names — live in `*_consts` namespaces in headers, the one place CONVENTIONS names as wrong.
- The one piece of real logic in the group has had two shipped face-mapping bugs and still
  cannot be reached by a headless test, because its constructor resolves a live wave bank.
- Include discipline runs on different rules in the two halves of the repo: the engine puts
  its own header first, the game puts a force-included PCH first and orders nothing.
- Extent contracts are stated nowhere: `Structure` carries a sprite rectangle and a cloned
  collision shape with no invariant tying them, and `StructurePaintable` reports neither the
  extent it draws nor the one it collides on.

#### Store the paint grid as values, not as thousands of interface implementations

- **File:** `game/objects/paint_tile.h:22-86`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/The object model (also T8, T11)

**What:** Each paint tile is a separate polymorphic object implementing
`ICollisionGameObject`, containing a second polymorphic object implementing `IGameObject`,
but no pointer of either interface type ever points at one — so the shipped levels build
1,898–5,230 tiles' worth of vtables, duplicated resource pointers and duplicated
`TeamColour` copies to buy dispatch that is never exercised.

**Evidence:**

    class PaintTileSplash final : public artattack::AnimationObject, public artattack::IGameObject
    ...
    class PaintTile final : public artattack::TextureObject, public ICollisionGameObject
    ...
    private:
        mattmath::RectangleF rectangle_ = mattmath::RectangleF::ZERO;
        PlayerTeam team_ = PlayerTeam::none;
        TeamColour team_colours_ = TeamColour();
        PaintTileSplash splash_;

`structure_paintable.h:59` is the only thing that holds them, and it holds them by value:

    std::vector<PaintTile> paint_tiles_ = std::vector<PaintTile>();

**Why it matters:** PHILOSOPHY (The object model) names this exact case as the wrong side of
the dial: "A paint-tile grid is one `GameObject`, not ten thousand. Interface granularity is
the user's performance dial." I grepped `PaintTile` across `game/`, `engine/`, `samples/`
and `tests/`: it appears in its own definition and in `StructurePaintable`'s by-value vector,
and nowhere else. Nothing takes a `PaintTile*`, an `ICollisionGameObject*` or an
`IGameObject*` to one, and the consequence is measurable in dead members. On `PaintTile`,
four of the eight interface members are unreachable — `bounds()` (`paint_tile.cpp:128-131`),
`collision_object_type()` (`:120-123`, and `CollisionObjectType::paint_tile` occurs nowhere
else in the tree), `for_deletion()` (`:124-127`, a constant `false`), and the inherited
`set_for_deletion` no-op. On `PaintTileSplash`, three of four are — `draw()` (`:168-171`,
never called; `draw_with_colour` is what `PaintTile::draw` uses), `bounds()` (`:178-181`) and
`set_colour()` (`:160-163`). Counted against the shipped level JSONs with the builder's own
arithmetic (`nx = int(|w| / 4)`, `ny = int(|h| / 4)`, one band per enabled face) I get
king_of_the_hill 4,116 tiles across 13 paintables, turbulence 5,230 across 9, close_quarters
1,898 across 2 — so turbulence constructs 10,460 polymorphic objects at load. Each tile pays
four vtable pointers (two for itself, two for the embedded splash), two copies of the same
`RenderResources*`, and a private `TeamColour` copy of a value identical for the whole level.
This is not "the game chose OOP behind the interface" that T11 explicitly permits — nothing
behind the interface is polymorphic. It is the shipped sample the engine's own philosophy
says must be value-first.

Note this substantially re-states an outstanding finding from the previous review
(`PaintTile.h`: "PaintTile is a heavyweight polymorphic object … instantiated thousands of
times"). What is new is the authority — PHILOSOPHY now names this grid by name — and the
proof that the polymorphism is not merely heavy but entirely unused.

**Remedy:** Make the grid data: per structure, a `std::vector<PlayerTeam>` plus origin,
pitch and counts, with `StructurePaintable` remaining the single registered object that
updates and draws it, and a short list of *active* splashes rather than one per cell. Delete
`PaintTile` and `PaintTileSplash` as object types.

#### Split CollisionObjectType into a layer/mask and an opaque tag while it is still game-local

- **File:** `game/objects/collision_object_type.h:3-27`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** boundary
- **Tenet:** T1 (also PHILOSOPHY/Collision)

**What:** The enum fuses object kind with team identity into 22 flat enumerators, so two
`switch` towers encode it and six consumers hand-decode it back, while five of the seven
helper predicates written for exactly that job have zero call sites and three enumerators
are never read at all.

**Evidence:**

    enum class CollisionObjectType
    {
        structure,
        structure_paintable,
        ...
        projectile_spray_team_a,
        projectile_spray_team_b,
        projectile_jet_team_a,
        projectile_jet_team_b,
        ...
        paint_tile,
        power_up,
        none
    };

Encoded by a 2x5 tower in `projectile.cpp:153-192` and a 2x2 tower in `player.cpp:105-134`,
both of which `throw std::exception` on `default`. Decoded by hand at:

- `structure_paintable.cpp:56-67` — ten comparisons, byte-for-byte `is_projectile()` from
  this very header
- `paint_tile.cpp:95-116` — `is_team_a_projectile()` and `is_team_b_projectile()` from this
  header, split in two, with a `throw` between
- `level.cpp:687-699` — `is_projectile()` again
- `player.cpp:210-231` — the per-team half again
- `player.cpp:679-701` — kind again, as a damage table
- `level.cpp:733-741` — the `structure_paintable` tag used as a substitute for the type
  system, then recovered by `dynamic_cast<IPaintableGameObject*>`

**Why it matters:** This **is** critical finding `#13`, still Outstanding in IMPLEMENTED.md.
The new information is where it now stands. Post-split it does **not** cross into engine
code: grepping `engine/` for `CollisionObjectType` and `ICollisionGameObject` yields exactly
one hit, a comment in `engine/core/i_game_object.h:55`, which names a game type but creates
no dependency; and `engine/collision/` holds only `partitioner.h`/`partitioner.cpp`, whose
entire content is `partition(num_elements, num_partitions)` — a thread-range splitter, not
collision. So the whole collision system is game-side, and the fix is currently game-local:
replace the enum with a layer/mask bitfield the dispatcher filters on plus an opaque tag the
game packs `(kind, team)` into, then edit the two encoders, the six decoders and this header.
`CollisionObjectType` occurs 155 times across 14 files (115 of them outside its own header),
and every one of those sites is in `game/`. No engine change, no behaviour change if the
packing is faithful. The day an engine `CollisionObject` interface lands, the same edit costs
those files *plus* the engine seam — and until then every new collidable in this game, and
in anyone else's, has to declare itself as one of these 22 values. The enum is already
rotting from disuse: `power_up` and `none` have zero references anywhere in the tree,
`paint_tile` is produced by `PaintTile::collision_object_type()` and read by nothing, and
`is_player`, `is_dead_player`, `is_projectile`, `is_team_a_projectile` and
`is_team_b_projectile` all have zero call sites while their bodies are re-typed by hand at
four of the six decode sites above. Only `is_structure` (`level.cpp:250`, `player.cpp:155`)
and `is_structure_ramp` (`player.cpp:206`) are called.

**Remedy:** Replace with `layer` + `mask` bits plus a game-owned opaque tag, and give
`ICollisionGameObject` a `team()` so `PaintTile::on_collision` becomes
`team_ = other->team();` with no chain and no throw.

#### Stop the game target from depending on rapidjson, and get it out of game public headers

- **File:** `game/CMakeLists.txt:64-66` (with `game/objects/level_object_builder.h:5,18`)
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** boundary
- **Tenet:** ARCHITECTURE/The targets

**What:** `game/CMakeLists.txt` puts rapidjson on the game target's include path, and
`level_object_builder.h` includes `rapidjson/document.h` and names `const rapidjson::Value&`
in its public signatures — a `game -> rapidjson` arrow ARCHITECTURE's target graph does not
have.

**Evidence:**

    target_include_directories(ArtAttackGame PRIVATE
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/external/rapidjson/include"
    )

and in `level_object_builder.h`:

    #include "rapidjson/document.h"
    ...
    std::unique_ptr<std::vector<std::unique_ptr<ICollisionGameObject>>>
        build_collision_objects(const rapidjson::Value& json,
            const TeamColour& team_colours) const;

**Why it matters:** ARCHITECTURE's graph has exactly one arrow into rapidjson
(`engine --> rapidjson`) and states the reason: "Nothing points back at `assets`, and that
is what keeps its arrows from closing into a cycle … so `rapidjson` reaches `assets` and
stops there — drawing a sprite does not compile a JSON parser." PHILOSOPHY's boundary table
puts "JSON parsing" on the engine side and "the content: definitions, levels, tuning data"
on the game side. Four game headers name rapidjson today — `level_object_builder.h:5`,
`level_builder.h:13`, `level_loaded_info.h:4` and `save.h:6` — so a stranger who copies
`samples/minimal/` as ARCHITECTURE instructs inherits either a JSON parser dependency they
were told the engine owned, or a level pipeline they cannot reuse. `engine/assets/` already
exists and is where this belongs.

The header half of this is already on record from the previous review
(`LevelObjectBuilder.cpp` finding 4, "…and rapidjson in the public API", still Outstanding).
What is new is the target: the CMake conversion (`6a15785`) made the dependency a build-graph
edge, and ARCHITECTURE now names the graph that edge violates.

**Remedy:** Have the engine hand the builder already-decoded records (or an engine-owned
JSON view type), so no game header includes rapidjson and
`target_include_directories(ArtAttackGame … rapidjson)` can be deleted outright.

#### Make the tile-layout geometry constructible without the audio stack so it can be tested

- **File:** `game/objects/structure_paintable.cpp:31-33`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** testing
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Tests and toolchain

**What:** `generate_paint_tiles()` — the only non-trivial logic in this group, and the site
of two separate shipped face-mapping bugs — cannot be exercised by a headless test, because
the same constructor resolves a live XAudio2 wave bank.

**Evidence:**

    this->paint_tiles_ = this->generate_paint_tiles();
    this->sound_bank_ = audio_resources->sound_bank(SOUND_BANK_NAME);
    this->paint_sound_ = this->sound_bank_->resolve_wave(SOUND_NAME);

`SoundBank` (`engine/audio/sound_bank.h:30`) takes `std::unique_ptr<DirectX::WaveBank>`, and
`AudioResources::sound_bank` is documented to throw `std::out_of_range` naming the bank if
nothing loaded it (`engine/audio/audio_resources.h:26-29`), so there is no headless path to a
constructed `StructurePaintable`. The layout loop itself needs none of that — it is arithmetic
over `this->rectangle()`, four booleans and two constants (`structure_paintable.cpp:93-181`).

**Why it matters:** PHILOSOPHY says "Everything below the platform edge is testable
headlessly" and "A new public primitive ships with behavioural tests in the same commit."
`tests/` has three folders — `assets`, `core`, `math` — and grepping all three for `game/`
returns nothing, so no file in this group has any coverage at all. The `PaintableFaces`
rewrite that fixed critical `#32` (three of four faces painting on the wrong side) and
critical `#20` (a dangling reference to a builder local) both landed here with no regression
test, and the corner-overlap and zero-tile-count defects the previous review filed against
this same function are still Outstanding and still unpinned. I confirmed from the shipped
JSONs that no current paintable is small enough to trip the zero-tile-count divide, so that
defect is latent — which is exactly the condition under which a test is the only thing that
would catch it coming back.

**Remedy:** Extract the band layout into a free function over
`(RectangleF, PaintableFaces, tile size, thickness)` returning the tile rectangles, and cover
it with behavioural tests — the corner overlap and the `w < 4` / `h < 4` cases first. Leave
object construction stacked on top of it.

#### Drop the I prefix from the two game interfaces and their filenames

- **File:** `game/objects/i_collision_game_object.h:7`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Never

**What:** `ICollisionGameObject` and `IPaintableGameObject`, and the filenames
`i_collision_game_object.h` / `i_paintable_game_object.h`, carry the `I` type prefix that
CONVENTIONS/Never forbids outright and that four consecutive conventions passes did not
remove.

**Evidence:**

    class ICollisionGameObject : public artattack::IGameObject

and `i_paintable_game_object.h:9`:

    class IPaintableGameObject

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS/Never lists "`I`, `C`, `F`, `U` or any other type prefix",
and CONVENTIONS/Types spells out why: "Interfaces are just types — `GameObject`, not
`IGameObject`; whether a type is abstract is visible in its header, not encoded in its name."
T12 reinforces it, citing Unreal's prefixes as the anti-example and noting the prefix exists
there "to tell you which dialect you are currently in". Four commits (`6175c6b`, `52fe513`,
`a36544f`/`dcd8f6f`, `54db795`) were spent on conventions and this rule reached none of the
three `I`-prefixed types in the tree — I grepped for `class I[A-Z]` across `engine/`, `game/`
and `samples/` and there are exactly three: `artattack::IGameObject`, `ICollisionGameObject`
and `IPaintableGameObject`. Because these names are load-bearing in every game object header
and in `Level`'s member types, the rename gets more expensive with every file added, and the
sample a stranger is told to copy currently demonstrates the forbidden form.

**Remedy:** Rename to `CollisionGameObject` / `PaintableGameObject` with matching filenames,
in the same pass as the engine's `IGameObject`.

#### Move the paint tuning constants into level data and stop SCREAMing them

- **File:** `game/objects/paint_tile.h:9-20`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Constants and enumerators (also T7)

**What:** `paint_tile_consts` and `structure_paintable_consts` are SCREAMING-cased constant
namespaces in headers holding exactly the "how much" values T7 puts in JSON, and their
header-scope `std::string`s get an internally-linked, dynamically initialised copy in every
translation unit that includes them.

**Evidence:**

    namespace paint_tile_consts
    {
        constexpr float WIDTH = 4.0f;
        constexpr float HEIGHT = 4.0f;
        constexpr float THICKNESS = 12.0f;
        const static std::string SHEET_NAME = "sprite_sheet_1";
        const static std::string FRAME_NAME = "pixel";

        const static std::string SPLASH_SPRITE_SHEET_NAME = "sprite_sheet_1";
        const static std::string SPLASH_ANIMATION_STRIP_NAME = "splash_1";
        const static mattmath::RectangleF SPLASH_RECTANGLE = { 0.0f, 0.0f, THICKNESS * 2.0f, THICKNESS * 2.0f };
    }

and `structure_paintable.h:10-15`:

    namespace structure_paintable_consts
    {
        const std::string SOUND_BANK_NAME = "sound_bank_1";
        const std::string SOUND_NAME = "WaterSplashing";
        constexpr float SOUND_VOLUME = 0.1f;
    }

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS/Never says "SCREAMING constants — screaming means macro,
nothing else"; CONVENTIONS/Constants adds "A header full of numeric constants is usually
tuning data in the wrong place — *which* and *how much* belong in JSON (T7). Constants that
stay in code live next to the one thing they configure, not in a `consts` namespace
collecting strays." Both namespaces are that namespace. `WIDTH`, `HEIGHT`, `THICKNESS` and
`SOUND_VOLUME` are the paint resolution and mix level for one game, and changing any of them
today rebuilds everything that transitively includes `paint_tile.h` —
`structure_paintable.h` -> `level_object_builder.h` -> `level_builder.h` — which is precisely
the rebuild T7 exists to remove. `"sound_bank_1"` and `"sprite_sheet_1"` are already in the
level JSON and the manifest, hardcoded here a second time. Separately, `const` and
`const static` at namespace scope in a header give each including TU its own copy of these
six `std::string`s plus one `RectangleF`, dynamically initialised at static-init time.

One correction to the reviewer's version: `"WaterSplashing"` is **not** the only non-snake_case
asset name in the tree. All twenty-four wave names in
`game/content/sounds/sound_bank_1.json` are non-snake_case, because they are the source `.wav`
filenames baked into the `.xwb` name table by `XWBTool` (`content/sounds/sound_bank_1/cmd.txt`).
Renaming them is a content-pipeline change — rename the wavs, rebuild the bank, update the
JSON — not a string edit, so it should be scheduled separately from the code half.

**Remedy:** Move the four numbers and the sheet/frame/bank names into the level or structure
JSON records the builder already reads, and delete both `*_consts` namespaces. Handle the
wave-name casing as its own content-pipeline task.

#### Give the game its own namespace

- **File:** `game/objects/structure.h:6`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Namespaces

**What:** Every type in `game/` is declared in the global namespace — including names as
generic as `Structure`, `PaintTile` and `CollisionObjectType` — while commit `2fa12fe`
wrapped the engine in `artattack`.

**Evidence:**

    class Structure : public artattack::TextureObject, public ICollisionGameObject

and `collision_object_type.h:3`:

    enum class CollisionObjectType

Grepping `game/**/*.h` for namespace declarations returns sixteen, and every one of them is
a `*_consts` namespace (`paint_tile_consts`, `structure_paintable_consts`, `player_consts`,
`weapon_consts`, `level_consts`, `directory_consts`, …). No game *type* is in a namespace.

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS/Namespaces states "The engine never claims the global
namespace. Game code owns its own namespace and never reopens the engine's." `2fa12fe` did
the engine half — its message calls it "the last conventions rule" — and left the game half
undone, so the rule holds in one direction only. The concrete risk is at the seam:
`structure_paintable.cpp:4-8` opens with `using namespace artattack;` alongside four other
directives, which drops the entire engine into the same global scope the game already
occupies. Any name the engine adds later that collides with a game type is a build break in
game code that did nothing wrong — and `Structure`, `Visual`, `Level` and `PaintTile` are
exactly the sort of names an engine grows. The sample a new user copies shows the wrong
pattern.

**Remedy:** Wrap `game/` in a single namespace (the game's own name, not `artattack`), in
one mechanical pass like `2fa12fe`.
