#### A button held when a menu opens is delivered to that menu as a fresh action

- **File:** `game/states/menu_input.cpp:42-48, 145-152`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T2 (correctness over speed)

**What:** Menu actions fire on the *release* edge computed against `prev_inputs_`, but
`prev_inputs_` only advances on frames where `update_and_get_menu_inputs()` is called — which
is only while a menu is on screen. A button already held when the menu opens is therefore seen
as a press the menu itself received, and its release is delivered as an action.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/menu_input.cpp:42-48`

        bool no_press_current = !current.proceed && !current.back && !current.pause;
        bool prev_proceed = previous.proceed && !previous.back && !previous.pause;
        bool prev_back = previous.back && !previous.proceed && !previous.pause;
        bool prev_pause = previous.pause && !previous.proceed && !previous.back;
        bool proceed = prev_proceed && no_press_current;
        bool back = prev_back && no_press_current;
        bool pause = prev_pause && no_press_current;

`game/states/menu_input.cpp:145-152` — the only place `prev_inputs_` moves forward:

        for (int i = 0; i < MAX_PAD_COUNT; i++)
        {
            if (current[i].connected)
            {
                result[i] = calculate_menu_input(current[i], this->prev_inputs_[i]);
            }
            this->prev_inputs_[i] = current[i];
        }

**Why it matters:** Reachable in one sitting, and I traced every hop. `A` is jump
(`player_input.cpp:28`). Hold `A` and tap Start. `PlayerInput` fires `toggle_pause_menu` on
Start's *release* (`player_input.cpp:53-58`), so Start is already up; `GameLevel::update`
switches to `GameLevelState::pause_menu` and `StateContext::transition_to`
(`state_context.cpp:22-27`) runs `PauseMenuInitial::init()` (`game_states.cpp:158-173`). The
pause menu's first `update()` runs the following frame, against the `MenuInput` created in
`GameLevel::init` (`game_states.cpp:111-112`) whose `prev_inputs_` is all-default. On that
frame `current.proceed == true` (A still held) against `previous.proceed == false`, so no
action fires — but `prev_inputs_` records `proceed`. The player lets go of jump; the next
frame `prev_proceed && no_press_current` is true, `MenuInputAction::proceed` is delivered, and
`PauseMenuInitial::update` (`pause_menu.cpp:76-83`) confirms the default highlight, `"resume"`
(`pause_menu.cpp:191`). The pause menu closes itself the instant the player releases a button
they were already holding.

The same defect has a mirror image that confirms the diagnosis: while the pause menu is up,
`GameLevel::update` never calls `player_input_->update_and_get_player_inputs()`, so
`PlayerInput::prev_inputs_` is frozen at the pause frame. A player who paused mid-jump resumes
with `previous.jump_button == true`, and `jump_pressed = current.jump_button &&
!previous.jump_button` swallows their first jump. Two classes, one bug: an edge detector whose
"previous" is only advanced on frames its owner happens to be running.

**Remedy:** Give `MenuInput` (and `PlayerInput`) an explicit `prime()` that seeds
`prev_inputs_` from the current pad state, and call it when the owning state is entered, so a
button held across a transition must be released *and pressed again* to count. State the
release-edge contract in the header while you are there — it is written down nowhere.

---

#### Move the deferred-context render submission out of the menu base class

- **File:** `game/states/menu_page.h:38-50`, `game/states/menu_page.cpp:94-183`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** boundary
- **Tenet:** T1 (mechanism over policy), ARCHITECTURE/The boundary

**What:** `MenuPage` — a game state base class — owns the whole multi-viewport,
multi-threaded D3D11 command-list submission path, so the engine's headline rendering
mechanism is duplicated in `game/` and unavailable to any other client.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/menu_page.h:38-50`

        void draw_mobject_in_viewports(ID3D11DeviceContext* deferred_context,
            ID3D11CommandList*& command_list,
            DirectX::SpriteBatch* sprite_batch, artattack::MObject* widget,
            ID3D11SamplerState* sampler_state = nullptr);

        void draw_mobjects_in_viewports(std::vector<std::pair<artattack::MObject*,
            ID3D11SamplerState*>>* mobjects);

        void draw_range_of_mobjects_in_viewports(int start, int end,
            std::vector<std::pair<artattack::MObject*, ID3D11SamplerState*>>*mobjects,
            std::vector<ID3D11DeviceContext*>* deferred_contexts,
            std::vector<ID3D11CommandList*>* command_lists,
            std::vector<DirectX::SpriteBatch*>* sprite_batches);

`game/states/menu_page.cpp:130-166` — partitioner, thread pool, command-list execution and
manual COM `Release()`, all in game code:

        auto deferred_contexts = this->data()->device_resources()->deferred_contexts();
        std::vector<ID3D11CommandList*> command_lists(deferred_contexts->size(), nullptr);
        auto sprite_batches = this->data()->sprite_batches();
        auto partitioner = this->data()->partitioner();
        int num_threads = this->data()->thread_pool()->max_num_threads();
        ...
            immediate_context->ExecuteCommandList(command_lists[i], FALSE);
            command_lists[i]->Release();

**Why it matters:** Not one identifier in those ninety lines is a paint-shooter noun — no
team, weapon, paint or menu content anywhere in them — so by PHILOSOPHY's own litmus test this
is engine mechanism sitting on the wrong side of the boundary. Three costs today:

- `samples/minimal/` cannot draw a menu without copying the file. It is a declared target in
  `CMakeLists.txt` already.
- PHILOSOPHY/UI's "widgets draw through the renderer interface like everything else, so menus
  are headlessly testable" is false: drawing a menu requires a live `ID3D11Device`, sixteen
  deferred contexts and a thread pool.
- `Level::draw_active_level` (`game/objects/level.cpp:392-417`) is the second copy of the same
  partition-then-thread-pool-then-execute dance, and the two have already diverged:
  `game_states.cpp:337` executes level command lists with `RestoreContextState = TRUE` while
  `menu_page.cpp:164` passes `FALSE`; `level.cpp:606` finishes with `RestoreDeferredContextState
  = TRUE` while `menu_page.cpp:120` passes `FALSE`; `level.cpp:405` captures its partition
  vector by value while `menu_page.cpp:145` captures it by reference. Nothing today depends on
  either choice — `Application::clear` (`application.cpp:296-302`) rebinds the render target on
  all sixteen deferred contexts every frame, which is the only reason the `FALSE` path renders
  at all — but two copies drifting on D3D11 state-restore flags is precisely the failure mode
  duplication produces.

**Remedy:** Lift the whole "record N objects across M deferred contexts, once per view, then
execute" loop into `engine/render/` behind a renderer-facing call that both `Level` and
`MenuPage` use, and leave `MenuPage` holding a widget list.

#### Pull focus and controller navigation into engine/ui; per-viewport focus does not exist

- **File:** `game/states/menu_highlight.h:13-28`, `game/states/menu_input.h:30-44`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** boundary
- **Tenet:** T1 (mechanism over policy), PHILOSOPHY/UI

**What:** The two mechanisms PHILOSOPHY says the engine ships — focus, and navigation between
widgets — are implemented, are entirely game-agnostic, and live in `game/states/`. The third,
per-viewport focus for split-screen, is not implemented anywhere and is hand-rolled per page.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/menu_highlight.h:13-28` — focus, with no game noun in it:

        artattack::MWidget* highlighted_widget() const;
        void set_highlighted_widget(artattack::MWidget* widget);
        void highlight_widget(artattack::MWidget* widget) const;
        void unhighlight_widget(artattack::MWidget* widget) const;
        void change_highlight(artattack::MWidget* next_highlight);
        ...
        artattack::MWidget* highlighted_widget_ = nullptr;
        mattmath::Colour highlight_colour_ = colour_consts::WHITE;
        mattmath::Colour unhighlight_colour_ = colour_consts::GRAY;

`game/states/menu_input.h:30-44` — stick/d-pad navigation, likewise:

        enum class MenuDirection
        {
            up, down, left, right, none
        };

        struct ProcessedMenuInput
        {
            MenuDirection direction = MenuDirection::none;
            MenuInputAction action = MenuInputAction::none;
            artattack::ConnectionState connection = artattack::ConnectionState::disconnected;
        };

Per-viewport focus, in its absence — `main_menu.h:240-258` re-invents it per page:

        struct TeamSelectState
        {
            PlayerTeam team = PlayerTeam::none;
            ConfirmationState state = ConfirmationState::unconfirmed;
        };
        ...
        std::vector<std::unique_ptr<PlayerWidgets>> player_widgets_;
        std::vector<TeamSelectState> select_states_;

**Why it matters:** This is the spec for `engine/ui/`, and it is precise. Engine-owed
mechanism, all of it currently in `game/states/`:

| Belongs in `engine/ui` or `engine/input` | Where it is now |
|---|---|
| Focus: which widget has it, how focus is shown, moving it | `menu_highlight.h/.cpp` (whole file) |
| Directional navigation: analog→digital direction, edge detection, `MenuDirection` | `menu_input.cpp:74-128`, `menu_input.h:30-37` |
| Pad polling and per-slot previous-state bookkeeping | `menu_input.cpp:18-36, 133-154` |
| Per-viewport / per-pad focus for split-screen | **nowhere** — `main_menu.h:257-258`, `291-292` re-do it per page |

Game content that is correctly game-side and must **not** follow it: the action set
(`MenuInputAction::proceed/back/pause`) and its A/B/Start bindings, `MenuElement`,
`MenuLevelSettings`, `MenuPlayerSettings`, `MainMenuData::is_ready_to_load_level`, and every
colour, font, string and offset in `main_menu_consts` / `pause_menu_consts`. (I dropped the raw
report's claim on `calculate_center_position`: PHILOSOPHY/UI explicitly says layout is manual
and there is no autolayout engine, so a centring helper is defensible on either side.)

Until the first column moves, `engine/ui/widget.h` is a set of drawables with no interaction
model, and PHILOSOPHY/UI's "the two things every controller game needs solved once" is solved
zero times in the engine. Note also *how* `MenuHighlight` is consumed: its entire API is
`protected`, so inheritance is the only way to use it, and six pages take it as a second base
(`main_menu.h:148, 165, 191, 211`, `pause_menu.h:43`, `end_menu.h:41`). A plain member would
do the same work; T11 names inheritance a tool of last resort.

**Remedy:** Move `MenuHighlight` and the direction/edge half of `MenuInput` into `engine/ui/`,
parameterised by an opaque game-owned action enum, hold focus as a value rather than a base
class, and give it a per-slot dimension from the start rather than retrofitting one.

#### The render worker indexes contexts by MObject ordinal, capping every menu at sixteen objects

- **File:** `game/states/menu_page.cpp:169-183`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T2 (correctness over speed)

**What:** The worker subscripts `deferred_contexts`, `command_lists` and `sprite_batches` with
the *MObject* index, so the helper silently caps any menu at sixteen top-level draw objects and
throws `std::out_of_range` out of a render worker past that.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/menu_page.cpp:175-182`

        for (int i = start; i < end; i++)
        {
            // Use the contexts passed in rather than re-fetching the same ones
            // through GameData from a worker thread.
            this->draw_mobject_in_viewports(
                deferred_contexts->at(i),
                command_lists->at(i), sprite_batches->at(i), mobjects->at(i).first, mobjects->at(i).second);
        }

`start`/`end` come from `partitioner->partition(mobjects->size(), num_threads)`
(`menu_page.cpp:137-138`), i.e. they range over the *mobject* list, while `command_lists` is
sized `deferred_contexts->size()` (`menu_page.cpp:131`), which is `options.max_threads` = 16
(`main.cpp:38`, `application.cpp:68-69`, `application.cpp:156-167`).

**Why it matters:** This is the unfixed half of `all-findings.md:6087`. `IMPLEMENTED.md:144-146`
records only that the function stopped re-fetching contexts through `GameData` from a worker
thread — the comment above documents exactly that change — and the index confusion it was
reported alongside is still here. The path is **currently unreachable**: every call site
(`main_menu.cpp:51, 134, 303, 621, 856, 1130, 1413, 1760`, `pause_menu.cpp:222, 376`,
`results_menu.cpp:214`, `end_menu.cpp:244`) pushes exactly two containers, and
`Partitioner::partition(2, 16)` returns two single-element ranges whose indices happen to
coincide with the context slots. It becomes reachable the day a page pushes a seventeenth
object; the failure is a `std::out_of_range` recorded by the thread pool
(`thread_pool.cpp:84-92`), rethrown out of `wait_for_tasks_to_complete`
(`thread_pool.cpp:66-75`) inside `draw()`, with no handler between there and `wWinMain`.

The cap is structural, not incidental, and that constrains the fix: `draw_mobject_in_viewports`
calls `FinishCommandList` once per MObject (`menu_page.cpp:120`), so the design needs one
deferred context per object. Simply switching to the partition ordinal would put two MObjects
on one context and overwrite — and leak — the first one's command list. Note also that
`sprite_batches[i]` was constructed on `deferred_context(i)` (`application.cpp:162-164`), so
whatever index is chosen, the two must stay the same index.

**Remedy:** Either state and check the one-context-per-MObject limit at the top of
`draw_mobjects_in_viewports` (T6: fail loudly, in the caller's frame, naming the limit), or
record several MObjects into one context per partition and finish the command list once per
partition. Do not simply swap the index.

#### The const-`draw()` contract stops at `State`: MenuPage's draw helpers are non-const and run on sixteen threads

- **File:** `game/states/menu_page.h:38-50`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T2 (correctness over speed), PHILOSOPHY/Simulation and rendering
- **Origin:** added-by-verifier

**What:** `draw_mobject_in_viewports`, `draw_mobjects_in_viewports` and
`draw_range_of_mobjects_in_viewports` are all non-`const` members, and the last two fan out
over the thread pool with `this` captured. The compiler-enforced pure-read guarantee that
`ca4d228` established for every `IGameObject` does not reach here, because `State::draw()`
itself is not `const`.

**Evidence:**

`engine/core/state.h:12-14` — the interface the const pass never reached:

        virtual void update() = 0;
        virtual void draw() = 0;
        virtual void init() = 0;

`game/states/menu_page.h:38-50` — no `const` on any of the three:

        void draw_mobject_in_viewports(ID3D11DeviceContext* deferred_context, ...);
        void draw_mobjects_in_viewports(std::vector<std::pair<artattack::MObject*,
            ID3D11SamplerState*>>* mobjects);
        void draw_range_of_mobjects_in_viewports(int start, int end, ...);

`game/states/menu_page.cpp:145-151` — `this` captured into sixteen worker tasks:

        thread_pool->add_task([this, i, &partitioned_mobjects, mobjects, deferred_contexts,
            &command_lists, sprite_batches]()
            {
                this->draw_range_of_mobjects_in_viewports(
                    partitioned_mobjects[i].first, partitioned_mobjects[i].second,
                    mobjects, deferred_contexts, &command_lists, sprite_batches);
            });

By contrast `Level::draw_active_level` and `Level::draw_player_view_level`
(`level.cpp:392`, `509`) are both `const`, doing the same job on the same thread pool.

**Why it matters:** `IMPLEMENTED.md:70-78` is explicit that the value of the const pass is that
it "survives someone editing the code" — a `draw()` that assigns a member is a compile error
rather than something an audit has to keep catching. That guarantee has a hole exactly the size
of the state stack: a `MenuPage` subclass can cache anything it likes into a member from inside
these helpers and the build will not say a word, while sixteen workers execute the enclosing
lambda concurrently. Nothing mutates today — I checked the whole call chain, and
`ViewportManager::apply_player_viewport` and `MObject::draw` are both `const` — so this is a
missing wall, not a live race. It is also the cheapest remaining piece of the const pass, and
the fix has to land before `Scene` inherits this shape.

**Remedy:** Make `State::draw()` const (it is the same one-line change that was made to
`IGameObject::draw`), and const-qualify all three `MenuPage` helpers. Anything that genuinely
must be written during a draw is state that belongs in `update()`.

#### `menu_inputs()` reads as an accessor but polls the pads and consumes the frame's edges

- **File:** `game/states/menu_page.h:53`, `game/states/menu_page.cpp:190-193`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Functions

**What:** A bare-noun, `const` accessor calls hardware and advances the edge detector, so
calling it twice in one `update()` silently discards that frame's input, and nothing in the
name, the signature or a comment says so.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/menu_page.h:53`

        std::vector<ProcessedMenuInput> menu_inputs() const;

`game/states/menu_page.cpp:190-193`

        std::vector<ProcessedMenuInput> MenuPage::menu_inputs() const
        {
            return this->data()->input()->update_and_get_menu_inputs();
        }

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS/Functions reserves the bare noun for reads ("`bounds()`, not
`get_bounds()` … reads are frequent and should read like the thing itself") and verbs for
actions; the wrapped function is honestly named `update_and_get_menu_inputs` and the wrapper
throws that away. The `const` is a second lie — it holds only because `data_` is a pointer, and
the call it makes writes `prev_inputs_[0..3]`. Every page today calls it once per `update()` and
stores the result (twelve call sites, all of the form `std::vector<ProcessedMenuInput> inputs =
this->menu_inputs();`), so nothing is broken. The trap is that the obvious-looking
`if (this->menu_inputs()[i].action == …)` inside a per-player loop — the exact shape
`MainMenuTeamSelect::update` uses (`main_menu.cpp:1135-1140`) — would re-poll and destroy the
edges for every player after the first, because the second call compares the pad against a
`prev_inputs_` the first call already advanced to match it.

**Remedy:** Name it `update_and_get_menu_inputs()` like the thing it forwards to, drop the
`const`, and state the once-per-frame contract in the header.

#### `MenuElement` is dead code; widget identity is done with per-frame string comparison

- **File:** `game/states/menu_element.h:3-29`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T5 (compile-time over run-time)

**What:** The enum that exists to identify menu widgets is referenced only by two private static
converter functions that nothing calls, while the pages identify widgets by copying
`MWidget::name()` into a `std::string` and comparing it against literals every frame.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/menu_element.h:3-29` — twenty-one enumerators plus `none`, including five
`pause_menu_*` that no translation unit mentions.

`grep -rn "MenuElement\|convert_.*_to_element" game/ engine/` — every reference in the tree:

        game/states/main_menu.h:208:	static MenuElement convert_mode_to_element(LevelMode mode);
        game/states/main_menu.h:228:	static MenuElement convert_player_count_to_element(int player_count);
        game/states/main_menu.cpp:722:MenuElement MainMenuModeSelect::convert_mode_to_element(LevelMode mode)
        game/states/main_menu.cpp:988:MenuElement MainMenuPlayerCount::convert_player_count_to_element(

Neither converter is called from anywhere. What the pages do instead — `pause_menu.cpp:67-68`,
and the same two lines at `main_menu.cpp:627-628` and five more sites:

        std::string highlighted_element =
            this->highlighted_widget()->name();

followed by chains of `if (highlighted_element == "resume")`, `== "restart"`, `== "quit"`.

**Why it matters:** `/W4` with warnings-as-errors does not flag unused private static member
functions, so this is invisible dead weight that a reader of `menu_element.h` will reasonably
assume is load-bearing — and `menu_element.h` is included by `main_menu.h`, so it is on the
include path of every menu translation unit. Meanwhile navigation dispatches on string equality
in `update()` every frame, against PHILOSOPHY/Performance ("per-frame code performs no heap
allocation and no string-keyed lookups") — `name()` returns a `const std::string&` and every one
of those sites copies it into a fresh `std::string` first. It is fragile in a way an enum would
not be: a typo in `"restart"` compiles and silently makes a menu item inert.

**Remedy:** Pick one. Either make widget identity the enum (or a handle resolved once at
`init()`) and route navigation through it, or delete `menu_element.h` and both converters and
admit that names are the identity — in which case at least stop copying the string.

#### `menu_input.h` compiles only because the game's PCH is force-included

- **File:** `game/states/menu_input.h:1-7, 49`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Files

**What:** The header names `DirectX::GamePad` without including anything that declares it, and
its `.cpp` includes `game/pch.h` *before* its own header, so the "every header compiles on its
own" check CONVENTIONS gets from include order never runs here.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/menu_input.h:1-7` and `:49`

        #pragma once

        #include <vector>
        #include "game/states/menu_input_action.h"
        #include "engine/input/connection_state.h"
        #include "engine/math/matt_math.h"
        #include "game/objects/player_input.h"
        ...
            explicit MenuInput(DirectX::GamePad* gamepad);

`grep -rn "GamePad.h" engine/ game/` finds two includes of it in the whole tree, and neither is
reachable from that list (`connection_state.h` is a bare enum, `matt_math.h` pulls
`SimpleMath.h` and `d3d11.h`, `player_input.h` has the identical defect):

        engine/app/application.h:17:#include <GamePad.h>
        game/pch.h:64:#include "GamePad.h"

`game/CMakeLists.txt` force-includes the PCH into every TU:

        target_precompile_headers(ArtAttackGame PRIVATE pch.h)

and `game/states/menu_input.cpp:1-2` — like all six `.cpp` files in this group — puts it ahead
of the header under test:

        #include "game/pch.h"
        #include "game/states/menu_input.h"

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS/Files is explicit — "Include order: own header first — proving
every header compiles on its own" — and the point of the rule is that the build catches a
missing include. It cannot here: `menu_input.h` has never been compiled without `pch.h` in front
of it. This is not academic for this group. The navigation half of `MenuInput` belongs in
`engine/input`/`engine/ui` (see above), and `ArtAttackEngine` has no PCH
(`engine/CMakeLists.txt` sets none), so the move fails to compile on day one for a reason that
has nothing to do with the move. `menu_page.h` is clean by luck rather than discipline — it gets
`SpriteBatch.h` transitively through `engine/ui/widget.h` → `engine/core/i_game_object.h`.

**Remedy:** Include `<GamePad.h>` where `GamePad` is named, and put the own-header include
first — the PCH arrives via `/FI` regardless, so the explicit `#include "game/pch.h"` line can
simply go.

#### `MenuData` inherits and copies the service bag instead of holding it

- **File:** `game/states/menu_data.h:6-16`, `game/states/main_menu_data.h:7-21`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T11 (the stack over the heap — inheritance as a last resort)

**What:** `MenuData : GameData` and `MainMenuData : MenuData` use inheritance to bolt
menu-scoped members onto a service bag, and each construction *copies* the bag rather than
referring to it, giving the process several independently-mutable snapshots of the same four
pointers.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/menu_data.h:6-16`

        class MenuData : public GameData
        {
        public:
            explicit MenuData(const GameData* game_data);
            MenuData(const GameData* game_data, MenuInput* input);
            MenuInput* input() const;
            void set_input(MenuInput* input);
            MenuData* menu_data();
        private:
            MenuInput* input_ = nullptr;
        };

`game/game_data.cpp:5-12` — the "constructor" is a copy:

        GameData::GameData(const GameData* game_data) :
            application_(game_data->application()),
            save_(game_data->save()),
            level_infos_(game_data->level_infos()),
            stages_(game_data->stages())

`game/states/menu_data.cpp:27-30` and `game/game_data.cpp:116-119` are the same function twice:

        MenuData* MenuData::menu_data()
        {
            return this;
        }

**Why it matters:** `GameData`'s own header (`game_data.h:9-20`) says it is "the service bag
every state, object and drawable in this game is handed at construction" — a thing you are
*given*, not a base you *become* — and warns that a cached copy "would be a second place for a
service pointer to be wrong" (`game_data.cpp:54-55`) while this hierarchy makes four of them.
`GameData::set_save` called after `GameMenu`'s constructor (`game_states.cpp:5-10`) would leave
the menu's copy stale with no diagnostic. The seam is const-inconsistent —
`MenuData(const GameData*)` versus `MainMenuData(GameData*)` — and the two-phase initialisation
it forces (`GameMenu::init` calls `set_main_menu_data_ptrs()`, `game_states.cpp:65-71`) leaves
`input_`, `menu_level_settings_` and `is_ready_to_load_level_` null between construction and
`init()`. Nothing here needs polymorphism: no `MenuData` is ever handled through a `GameData&`,
and `GameData` has no virtual destructor, so the whole family is a slicing accident waiting for
someone to hold one by base pointer.

**Remedy:** Make `MenuData` hold a `GameData*` (or `const GameData&`) member rather than derive
from it, forward what it needs, and delete the self-returning `menu_data()`/`game_data()` pair.

#### `MenuHighlight`'s "seed me in `init()`" precondition is unstated and unenforced

- **File:** `game/states/menu_highlight.h:26-28`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T6 (loud failure over graceful degradation)

**What:** `highlighted_widget_` starts null and every consumer dereferences the result of
`highlighted_widget()` without a check, so a page that omits one line in `init()` null-derefs on
its first `update()`.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/menu_highlight.h:26-28`

        artattack::MWidget* highlighted_widget_ = nullptr;
        mattmath::Colour highlight_colour_ = colour_consts::WHITE;
        mattmath::Colour unhighlight_colour_ = colour_consts::GRAY;

`game/states/menu_highlight.cpp:7-14` carefully null-guards the *arguments*:

        void MenuHighlight::highlight_widget(MWidget* widget) const
        {
            if (widget == nullptr)
            {
                return;
            }
            widget->set_colour(this->highlight_colour_);
        }

but the member is handed straight out, and every caller does this (`pause_menu.cpp:67-68`,
`pause_menu.cpp:236-237`, `main_menu.cpp:627-628`, `end_menu.cpp:32-33` and three more):

        std::string highlighted_element =
            this->highlighted_widget()->name();

**Why it matters:** Graded down from the raw report's medium because there is no live defect: I
checked all seven concrete pages that inherit `MenuHighlight` and all seven seed it
(`main_menu.cpp:279, 542, 833, 1100`, `pause_menu.cpp:191, 347`, `end_menu.cpp:213`). What
remains is a trap for the next page. The class documents nothing, and the null-guards inside
`highlight_widget`/`unhighlight_widget` actively suggest null is a supported state, so the first
thing a new page author learns is wrong. The seed line sits sixty lines into an `init()` that is
otherwise pure widget construction, and the payoff for omitting it is a null dereference on the
first frame rather than a diagnostic.

**Remedy:** Require the initial focus at construction, or make the "nothing focused" case
explicit in the return type so callers must handle it.

#### `MenuLevelSettings` exposes unchecked indices and keeps two sources of truth for its size

- **File:** `game/states/menu_level_settings.cpp:10-26, 63-86`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T2 (correctness over speed)

**What:** Six public functions subscript `player_settings_` with a caller-supplied `int` and no
bounds check or documented precondition, while the vector's size and `player_count_` are
separate state kept in step by a single setter.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/menu_level_settings.cpp:63-74`

        void MenuLevelSettings::set_player_setting(int player_index, MenuPlayerSettings player_settings)
        {
            this->player_settings_[player_index] = player_settings;
        }
        void MenuLevelSettings::set_player_team(int player_index, PlayerTeam team)
        {
            this->player_settings_[player_index].team = team;
        }
        PlayerTeam MenuLevelSettings::player_team(int player_index) const
        {
            return this->player_settings_[player_index].team;
        }

`game/states/menu_level_settings.cpp:10-26` — the size lives in two places, and the fill loop
re-does what `resize` already did:

        void MenuLevelSettings::set_player_count(int player_count)
        {
            this->player_count_ = player_count;
            int vector_size = static_cast<int>(this->player_settings_.size());
            if (vector_size < player_count)
            {
                this->player_settings_.resize(player_count);
                for (int i = vector_size; i < player_count; i++)
                {
                    this->player_settings_[i] = MenuPlayerSettings();
                }
            }
            else if (vector_size > player_count)
            {
                this->player_settings_.resize(player_count);
            }
        }

**Why it matters:** Graded down from the raw report's medium: there is no live out-of-bounds
access. Every caller bounds its loop with `player_count()`
(`main_menu.cpp:1205, 1216, 1227, 1240, 1271, 1323, 1475, 1491, …`), which
`MainMenuPage::player_count` (`main_menu.cpp:28-32`) forwards to this object, and the copy
constructor carries both members together across the midway-load path
(`game_states.cpp:259-260`, `game_states.cpp:16-17`), so the invariant survives copying too.
What is left is an API that proves nothing at its boundary while T2's stated price is "checked
access where an invariant can't be proven at the boundary" — a negative or too-large index is
silent undefined behaviour on a type that is copied by value into `GameLevel::settings_`
(`game_states.cpp:96-97`). Separately, `player_settings()` (`:5-8`) returns the whole vector by
value; the one caller (`player_builder.cpp:28`) binds it in a range-for, copying the vector to
walk it once.

**Remedy:** Derive `player_count()` from `player_settings_.size()` and delete `player_count_`,
make the indexed accessors use `at()`, drop the redundant fill loop (`resize` value-initialises
already), and return the settings by `const&`.

---

#### Two `throw new std::exception` statements, in provably unreachable arms

- **File:** `game/states/menu_input.cpp:62-68, 116-124`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6 (loud failure over graceful degradation)

**What:** Both guards throw a *pointer* to a heap-allocated exception, from `else if` arms whose
conditions are false whenever control reaches them.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/menu_input.cpp:50-68`

        if (proceed)
        {
            result.action = MenuInputAction::proceed;
        }
        else if (back)
        ...
        else if ((proceed && back) ||
            (proceed && pause) ||
            (pause && back))
        {
            throw new std::exception(
                "2 or more of proceed, back or pause pressed at same time");
        }

`game/states/menu_input.cpp:116-124` has the same shape:

        else if (right)
        {
            result.direction = MenuDirection::right;
        }
        else if (up && down && left && right)
        {
            throw new std::exception(
                "up, down, left, and right pressed at same time");
        }

**Why it matters:** Graded down from the raw report's medium, because the arms are dead twice
over and the reviewer's own analysis says so. Reaching the fourth action arm requires `proceed`,
`back` and `pause` to all be false — each is tested individually above it — which makes every
disjunct in its condition false; and `prev_proceed`/`prev_back`/`prev_pause` are constructed
mutually exclusive two lines earlier (`:43-45`), so the state it claims to detect cannot arise
either. The direction guard is dead the same way. That is the only thing keeping the real defect
harmless: `throw new std::exception(...)` throws a `std::exception*`, which `wWinMain`'s
`catch (const std::exception& e)` (`main.cpp:93`) cannot match, so if either arm were ever
reached the process would `std::terminate` — with the exception object leaked — rather than show
the message box T6 asks for. (`std::exception(const char*)` is also an MSVC extension, not
standard.)

**Remedy:** Delete both arms; the conditions they guard cannot occur. If any invariant here is
worth stating, assert it. And never `throw new` — search the tree for the pattern while you are
in there.

---

#### Constants here are SCREAMING and live in a `_consts` namespace

- **File:** `game/states/menu_input.h:9-15`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Never, CONVENTIONS/Constants, CONVENTIONS/Namespaces

**What:** Two `constexpr float`s are SCREAMING_SNAKE inside a namespace whose whole purpose is
to collect constants — both explicitly ruled out — and the namespace name is three words where
CONVENTIONS says one.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/menu_input.h:9-15`

        namespace menu_input_consts
        {
        	constexpr float DIGITAL_PRESENCE_THRESHOLD = 0.8f;
        	constexpr float DIGITAL_ABSENCE_THRESHOLD = 0.8f;

        	using player_input_consts::MAX_PAD_COUNT;
        }

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS/Never lists "SCREAMING constants — screaming means macro,
nothing else"; CONVENTIONS/Constants says "Constants that stay in code live next to the one
thing they configure, not in a `consts` namespace collecting strays"; CONVENTIONS/Namespaces
says "one lowercase word". Three breaches in six lines, in the first menu header a new reader
opens — and in a file this review says should become engine code, where the rule is not
negotiable. The `using` on line 14 compounds it by re-exporting another `*_consts` namespace's
member. `ViewportManager` (`engine/render/viewport_manager.h`) already shows the target shape.

**Remedy:** Rename to `presence_threshold` / `absence_threshold` and make them private static
members of `MenuInput`, next to the one function that reads them; take `MAX_PAD_COUNT` from its
own header at the point of use.

---

#### The named hysteresis band between the analog thresholds is zero wide

- **File:** `game/states/menu_input.cpp:74-89`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T3 (simplicity over accuracy — "a simple model still has exact, documented, tested semantics")

**What:** `DIGITAL_PRESENCE_THRESHOLD` and `DIGITAL_ABSENCE_THRESHOLD` are both `0.8f`, so the
two-threshold scheme the names promise degenerates to a single crossing test at `0.8`, on a
stick read with `DEAD_ZONE_NONE`.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/menu_input.cpp:74-81`

        bool analog_down = previous.left_analog_stick.y >
            menu_input_consts::DIGITAL_PRESENCE_THRESHOLD &&
                current.left_analog_stick.y <
                menu_input_consts::DIGITAL_ABSENCE_THRESHOLD;
        bool analog_up = previous.left_analog_stick.y <
            -menu_input_consts::DIGITAL_PRESENCE_THRESHOLD &&
                current.left_analog_stick.y >
                -menu_input_consts::DIGITAL_ABSENCE_THRESHOLD;

with `menu_input.h:11-12` setting both to `0.8f`, and `menu_input.cpp:21` reading the pad raw:

        const auto pad = this->gamepad_->GetState(gamepad_num, GamePad::DEAD_ZONE_NONE);

**Why it matters:** Two differently-named thresholds exist so a stick resting near the boundary
cannot chatter. Equal values mean any frame-to-frame jitter downward across `0.8` — which
`DEAD_ZONE_NONE` does nothing to suppress — emits a fresh navigation event, so a player resting
the stick at roughly 80% deflection can walk the highlight on their own. The names are then
misinformation: a reader assumes a band and there is none. The same lines pin semantics that are
documented nowhere: navigation fires on the *release* edge, in both the analog half here and the
d-pad half at `:92-97`, which is an unusual choice for a menu and deserves a sentence in the
header.

**Remedy:** *Not* simply separating the two values — with only `previous` and `current` to work
from, an absence threshold below the presence threshold makes a slow release
(0.85 → 0.7 → 0.4) match no frame pair at all and emit nothing. Real hysteresis needs a latched
per-slot "currently deflected" flag beside `prev_inputs_`: set it above the presence threshold,
clear it below the absence threshold, and emit on the clear. If that is more machinery than the
menu deserves (T3), collapse to one honestly-named threshold and delete the second name.

---

#### The menu frame path allocates on the heap several times a frame, including inside render workers

- **File:** `game/states/menu_page.cpp:104-105, 131`, `game/states/menu_input.cpp:144`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** performance
- **Tenet:** T8 (performance over customisability), PHILOSOPHY/Performance
- **Origin:** added-by-verifier

**What:** Every menu frame allocates: a `std::vector<Viewport>` per MObject on a worker thread, a
sixteen-element command-list vector, a four-element input vector, and the caller's MObject list —
against a rule that says per-frame code allocates nothing.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/menu_page.cpp:104-105`, inside `draw_mobject_in_viewports`, which runs once per
MObject on a thread-pool worker:

        std::vector<Viewport> viewports =
         	this->viewport_manager()->all_viewports();

`engine/render/viewport_manager.cpp:79-93` builds that vector with `push_back` from scratch every
call, recomputing the identical list for every MObject in the frame.

`game/states/menu_page.cpp:131`

        std::vector<ID3D11CommandList*> command_lists(deferred_contexts->size(), nullptr);

`game/states/menu_input.cpp:144`, once per frame on the update path:

        std::vector<ProcessedMenuInput> result(MAX_PAD_COUNT);

and each page's `draw()` builds its own (`pause_menu.cpp:215-221`, and eleven more sites):

        std::vector<std::pair<MObject*, ID3D11SamplerState*>> mobjects;

**Why it matters:** PHILOSOPHY/Performance is unambiguous — "Per-frame code performs no heap
allocation and no string-keyed lookups; fixed-size geometry returns fixed-size containers" — and
every one of these is fixed-size and known at load: at most four viewports, exactly
`max_threads` command lists, exactly `MAX_PAD_COUNT` inputs, a handful of MObjects. The
`all_viewports()` call is the worst of them because it is inside the parallel section, so the
allocator is contended by up to sixteen workers to rebuild a list that did not change. Menus are
the cheapest screen in the game, so nothing is visibly slow; the point is that this is the shape
`Scene` will inherit, and the rule exists to stop it.

**Remedy:** Compute the viewport list once in `draw_mobjects_in_viewports` and pass it down by
`const&`; give the fixed-size ones a fixed-size container (`std::array`, or a small inline
vector) or hoist them to members initialised at load.

#### Clear the dead weight out of `MenuPage`

- **File:** `game/states/menu_page.h:13-15, 58-60`, `game/states/menu_page.cpp:85-88`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** T4 (clarity over cleverness)

**What:** The class carries a commented-out member function, three redundant re-declarations of
already-pure base virtuals, and three magic layout vectors that are load-bearing for some derived
pages and dead for others.

**Evidence:**

`game/states/menu_page.cpp:85-88`

        //SpriteBatch* MenuPage::sprite_batch() const
        //{
        //	return this->data_->sprite_batches()->at(0);
        //}

`game/states/menu_page.h:13-15` — `State` already declares all three as `= 0`
(`engine/core/state.h:12-14`):

        void update() override = 0;
        void draw() override = 0;
        void init() override = 0;

`game/states/menu_page.h:58-60`

        mattmath::Vector2F widget_position_ = { 150.0f, 150.0f };
        mattmath::Vector2F widget_size_ = { 300.0f, 75.0f };
        mattmath::Vector2F widget_spacing_ = { 250.0f, 150.0f };

**Why it matters:** Small individually, but this is the header a new page author reads first. The
commented-out accessor is a fossil of a pre-`sprite_batches()` API and tells a reader something
that is no longer true. The re-declared pure virtuals imply `MenuPage` adds a contract it does
not. And the three defaults are tuning numbers with no unit, no comment and no owner:
`PauseMenuInitial::init` overwrites all three (`pause_menu.cpp:146-148`) while
`MainMenuModeSelect::init` overwrites one and leaves a commented-out line for another
(`main_menu.cpp:743-744`), so they are load-bearing for some pages and dead for others and no
reader can tell which.

**Remedy:** Delete the commented-out function and the three re-declarations, and either comment

#### `calculate_menu_input` is a pure function with no tests, and it is the piece most in need of them

- **File:** `game/states/menu_input.cpp:38-131`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** testing
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Tests and toolchain

**What:** The one function in this group whose semantics are subtle — edge detection,
analog-to-direction conversion, mutual exclusion between actions — is a `static` function over two
plain structs, needs no device, no window and no pad, and has zero coverage.

**Evidence:** `game/states/menu_input.h:57-58`

        static ProcessedMenuInput calculate_menu_input(const RawMenuInput& current,
                                                       const RawMenuInput& previous);

`ls tests/` gives `assets/`, `core/`, `math/`; `grep -rli menu tests/` returns nothing; the root
`CMakeLists.txt` adds exactly those three test directories.

**Why it matters:** Four of the findings above are behavioural claims about this function — the
release-edge semantics, the stale-`previous` bug, the dead throw arms, the zero-width band — and
a table-driven test over `(previous, current)` pairs would have caught all four, including the
one that is shipping today. It is also the exact thing PHILOSOPHY says the engine must ship with
tests ("A new public primitive ships with behavioural tests in the same commit"), and it becomes
a public engine primitive the moment navigation moves to `engine/ui`. The usual excuse does not
apply: `RawMenuInput` and `ProcessedMenuInput` are POD, and the function is a pure map between
them.

**Remedy:** Add a `tests/` case over `calculate_menu_input` pinning the release edge, the analog
band and the action mutual exclusion, before the function changes modules — the tests are the
thing that makes the move safe.

### Rejected

- **Raw #6, "Menus are screen-space but are drawn once per player viewport"** — merged into raw
  #1. Same eighteen lines (`menu_page.cpp:104-118`), same fix (draw menus once with the
  fullscreen viewport); reporting them separately would have the author fix one and re-read the
  other. The performance argument and the stale-layout leak are preserved in the merged finding.
- **Raw #4's claim that `calculate_center_position` is engine-owed mechanism** — dropped from the
  table. PHILOSOPHY/UI says layout is manual and there is no autolayout engine, so a screen-space
  centring helper is defensible on the game side; the rest of the table stands.
- **Raw #4's "Multi-viewport widget draw submission" table row** — dropped as a duplicate of raw
  #3, which the row itself points at.
- **Raw #15's remedy ("separate the two values, e.g. presence 0.8, absence 0.5")** — rejected and
  replaced. With only `previous` and `current` in hand, a lower absence threshold makes a slow
  stick release match no frame pair at all and emit no navigation event; real hysteresis needs a
  latched flag. The finding itself is confirmed.
- **Raw #7's severity (medium → low)**, **raw #10's (medium → low)** and **raw #11's (medium →
  low)** — all three are true observations attached to consequences no reachable input produces:
  both `throw` arms are dead twice over, all seven pages that inherit `MenuHighlight` seed it, and
  every `MenuLevelSettings` index is bounded by a `player_count()` its own setter keeps in step.
  Kept as latent traps at the severity the observation deserves.
- **Considered and not raised: `for (int i = 0; i < partitioned_mobjects.size(); i++)`
  (`menu_page.cpp:143`) as a `/W4 /WX` signed/unsigned violation** — `cmake/settings.cmake` does
  set `/W4 /WX` with no suppressions, but `menu_page.cpp.obj` is newer than its source and
  `ArtAttackGame.exe` links from it, so the file demonstrably compiles clean. No finding.
- **Considered and not raised: the render target is never bound on the deferred contexts the menu
  records into, and `ExecuteCommandList(…, FALSE)` resets the immediate context** — checked to a
  conclusion: `Application::clear` (`application.cpp:296-302`) binds the target and viewport on
  all sixteen deferred contexts at the top of every frame, so each command list carries its own
  binding. The `TRUE`/`FALSE` divergence against `level.cpp` is recorded inside raw #3 as
  duplication drift, not as a rendering bug.

<a id="g-game-main-menu"></a>

## game-main-menu — Main menu

*Group `game-main-menu` · 19 findings (3 high, 7 medium, 9 low) · source `review2/verified/game-main-menu.md`, verified report.*

I re-opened both files end to end (`main_menu.h`, 340 lines; `main_menu.cpp`, 1977 lines) and every line the reviewer cited, plus the types they lean on: `MenuPage`, `MenuHighlight`, `MenuInput`/`ProcessedMenuInput`, `MenuLevelSettings`, `MenuPlayerSettings`, `Stage`/`StageList`, `LevelLoadedInfo`, `engine/ui/widget.{h,cpp}`, `engine/render/texture_object.cpp`, `engine/render/sprite_sheet.cpp`, `engine/render/text_object.cpp`, `engine/core/registry.h`, `engine/core/state_context.cpp`, `engine/audio/sound_bank_object.{h,cpp}`, `engine/render/{resolution_manager,viewport_manager}.{h,cpp}`, `engine/app/application.cpp`, `game/game_data.h`, `game/main.cpp` and `game/states/game_states.cpp`.

**Every cited line number is correct.** That is unusual at this scale and worth saying: I checked all 51 `highlighted_element ==` comparisons (9 / 12 / 15 / 15 across the four pages — the reviewer's per-function split is exact), all 34 `change_highlight` calls, all 16 `#pragma region` lines, all eight `draw()` bodies, and all 21 `transition_to` sites. Four counting claims were wrong and I corrected them in place: the constant namespace holds **54** constants, not 48; the weapon roster is **two** switches, not three; the file pair is **2,317** lines, not 2,316; and the dead commented-out statements sit at **five** sites, not four. The empty-stage-list guard in `main.cpp` is at 79-84, not 76-83.

**What I threw out.** One sub-claim inside finding 1: that `#pragma region` violates ARCHITECTURE's "Nothing IDE-specific is committed". That sentence is about build files ("a solution file... is generated output"), and the engine itself uses the same pragma in `engine/ui/widget.cpp` and `engine/math/matt_math.cpp` — so it is house style, not a boundary breach. The observation survives (the regions are the author's own map of a file too large to navigate); the citation does not. I also rewrote finding 6's title: the six sound handles are resolved in the constructor **body**, which is not the hazard; only the base's mem-initializer is.

**What I re-graded.** Four moves. The weapon-roster finding drops high→medium (real T7 debt, but no runtime defect and it is the tail of a structural item IMPLEMENTED.md already lists as outstanding). The mem-initializer finding drops medium→low: I confirmed it is *currently well-defined* — `MenuPage` genuinely precedes `SoundBankObject` in the base clause, so `MenuPage::data_` is live when line 13 reads it — which makes it latent, not live. Back-out-to-mode-select drops medium→low: reachable and wrong, but one press to recover.

**What I checked and cleared.** No critical survives, and I verified the reviewer's three negative claims myself rather than taking them: all 21 `transition_to` sites are followed by `return` (I listed and walked each), which matters more than they said — `StateContext::transition_to` assigns into the owning `unique_ptr`, so the running page is destroyed *inside* the call and any member access after it would be use-after-free; `main.cpp:79-84` does prove the stage list non-empty; `WeaponType::max_prim_wep = random_primary` and `ScreenResolution::max = s_3840_2160` are inclusive aliases, so all three wrap functions are exact. I also ran down a suspicion of my own — `for (int i = 0; i < inputs.size(); i++)` at line 56 under `/W4 /WX` — by compiling the pattern with this toolchain's `cl.exe` (19.51): no diagnostic, and the object file is newer than the source, so the file does build clean. `PlayerTeam` has exactly three enumerators, so the un-defaulted `switch` at 1243 cannot leave `selected_widget` null. `ViewportManager` recomputes from `ResolutionManager` on every call, so nothing goes stale after Apply.

**What I added.** Three findings, all local to these two files. A load-time validation gap that turns a mistyped `icon_frame` in a level JSON into a process kill from `update()` under a dialog titled "startup failure" — and which contradicts the comment in `stage.h` written alongside it. The two presses a player is most likely to make on Team Select being silent no-ops. And Home's Exit calling `quit()` with no `return`, destroying the window from inside `update()` while the same tick still renders and Presents.

### Themes

- The menu re-implements, four to eight times each, machinery PHILOSOPHY assigns to `engine/ui`: focus, navigation, and a page's draw plumbing.
- Game policy and platform detail are welded together — a menu page names `ID3D11SamplerState`, so no menu in this engine can be constructed without a device.
- Content lives in C++: fonts, colours, spacings, weapon names and six description sentences are compile-time constants in a header, which T7 exists to prevent.
- The per-frame path allocates and does string-keyed map lookups, in direct contradiction of the contract written on `Registry` itself — and the same lookup is the only validation some content ever gets.
- Duplication has diverged: the three per-player confirm pages disagree about whether `proceed` is guarded, what "unconfirm all" means, and where `back` goes.
- Several presses do nothing and say nothing — the failure mode T6 names as the most expensive kind.
- The conventions passes stopped at the door of this file: 54 SCREAMING constants and four leading-underscore members remain.

#### Split MainMenu into its eight pages; it is nine types and ten jobs in one translation unit

- **File:** `game/states/main_menu.h:1-340`, `game/states/main_menu.cpp:1-1977`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Files ("One primary type per header", "No huge files")

**What:** 2,317 lines hold nine classes, an enum, a struct and a 54-entry constant namespace. `main_menu.h` alone declares nine types, against a rule that admits only one plus its small helpers.

**Evidence:**

    34:#pragma region MainMenuTitle
    115:#pragma endregion MainMenuTitle
    117:#pragma region MainMenuHome
    284:#pragma endregion MainMenuHome
    286:#pragma region MainMenuOptions
    602:#pragma endregion MainMenuOptions
    604:#pragma region MainMenuModeSelect
    838:#pragma endregion MainMenuModeSelect
    840:#pragma region MainMenuPlayerCount
    1105:#pragma endregion MainMenuPlayerCount
    1107:#pragma region MainMenuTeamSelect
    1388:#pragma endregion MainMenuTeamSelect
    1390:#pragma region MainMenuWeaponSelect
    1735:#pragma endregion MainMenuWeaponSelect
    1737:#pragma region MainMenuStageSelect
    1977:#pragma endregion MainMenuStageSelect

The distinct jobs, enumerated as the guideline asks:

1. **Theme** — fonts, colours, shadow offsets, widget spacings, icon sizes (`main_menu.h:15-71`).
2. **Copy and content** — six weapon descriptions, six sound names, the music track (`main_menu.h:73-87`).
3. **Flow resume points** — `MainMenuScreen`, `MainMenuMidwayLoadSettings` (`main_menu.h:90-106`), needed only by `game_states.{h,cpp}`, which today drags all eight page classes in to reach them.
4. **Page-family plumbing** — `MainMenuPage`: six sound handles plus `player_count()` (`main_menu.cpp:10-32`).
5. **Eight screens**, each owning widget construction, layout, input handling and its outgoing transitions.
6. **A vertical-list focus/navigation machine**, hand-written four times: 51 `highlighted_element ==` comparisons and 34 `change_highlight` calls, split `MainMenuHome::update` 9, `MainMenuOptions::update` 12, `MainMenuModeSelect::update` 15, `MainMenuPlayerCount::update` 15.
7. **A per-player confirm/cancel machine**, hand-written three times (`1132-1287`, `1415-1614`, `1762-1867`), and the three disagree — see the divergences named in findings below.
8. **A wrap-around cursor**, hand-written three times: `cycle_resolution` (`547-578`), `cycle_weapons` (`1502-1532`), `cycle_stages` (`1961-1975`).
9. **Display-settings application and persistence** (`main_menu.cpp:323-352`, `426-429`).
10. **Authoring `MenuLevelSettings`** — five pages write into the shared settings object.

**Why it matters:** the guideline's own diagnosis applies literally — "the cause is almost always a type that grew past one job, so the fix is usually to split the type, not the file". Jobs 6, 7 and 8 are why the eight pages cannot be separated today: each page reimplements them, so each page is a full-size type, and splitting the file first would only produce eight medium files. The `#pragma region` markers are not themselves a violation (the engine uses them too, in `engine/ui/widget.cpp` and `engine/math/matt_math.cpp`) — they are the author's own admission that the file needs a table of contents.

**Remedy:** extract job 6 as an engine-side `MenuList` (PHILOSOPHY/UI already promises focus and navigation solved once), job 7 as a game-side `PlayerConfirmations` value type, job 8 as one free `wrap()`; then one file pair per page, `main_menu_page.*` for the base, `main_menu_screen.h` for job 3, and jobs 1-2 to JSON (T7), which deletes `main_menu_consts` outright.

#### Team and weapon select cannot be completed with fewer pads than players — and the field that fixes it is now populated and read nowhere

- **File:** `game/states/main_menu.cpp:1132-1235`, `1415-1554`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6 (loud failure over graceful degradation)

**What:** the input loop is bounded by pad slot, while the advance condition scans every player slot, so with four players selected and one pad connected the page's forward edge is inert and nothing on screen says why.

**Evidence:**

    1134:	std::vector<ProcessedMenuInput> inputs = this->menu_inputs();
    1135:	int num_inputs = static_cast<int>(inputs.size());
    1136:	int player_count = this->player_count();
    1137:
    1138:	for (int i = 0; i < num_inputs && i < player_count; i++)

and

    1214:bool MainMenuTeamSelect::all_players_confirmed() const
    1215:{
    1216:		for (int i = 0; i < this->player_count(); i++)
    1217:		{
    1218:			if (this->select_states_[i].state != ConfirmationState::confirmed)
    1219:			{
    1220:				return false;
    1221:			}
    1222:		}
    1223:		return true;
    1224:}

**Why it matters:** this was finding #9 of the first review and its stated mechanism is now *wrong*, which would cost the author time to re-derive. `MenuInput::update_and_get_menu_inputs` no longer compacts by connection — `menu_input.cpp:144` builds `std::vector<ProcessedMenuInput> result(MAX_PAD_COUNT);` and returns exactly four entries, so `num_inputs` is always 4 and the loop bound is no longer the blocker. The blocker is that slots 2 and 3 carry the default `ProcessedMenuInput` (`direction none, action none, connection disconnected`) forever, so `select_states_[2]` and `[3]` never leave `unconfirmed`. `MainMenuPlayerCount::update` (`858-987`) still offers 1-4 with no reference to pads present. The path: connect one pad, choose "4 Players", pick a team, confirm — the page never advances, and the only way out is B to unconfirm followed by B to leave. Meanwhile `menu_input.cpp:129` sets `result.connection = ConnectionState::connected` honestly and `main_menu.h:43` declares the field — and I grepped the whole of `game/`: `.connection` is **written** in two places and **read** in zero. The engine landed the data and the menu ignores it.

**Remedy:** read `inputs[i].connection`; treat a disconnected slot as absent in `all_players_confirmed()` and mark it on screen, or reject player counts above the connected-pad count in `MainMenuPlayerCount` with a visible reason rather than a silent dead end.

    51:	this->draw_mobjects_in_viewports(&mobjects);
    52:}

**Why it matters:** ARCHITECTURE states platform-specific code "lives only in the backend subfolders (`render/d3d11/`, `input/xinput/`), behind engine-owned interfaces, so a second platform is an addition, not a rewrite", and PHILOSOPHY/UI promises "Widgets draw through the renderer interface like everything else, so menus are headlessly testable". Neither holds: the sampler state is chosen by the *game*, and the seam it passes through — `MenuPage::draw_mobject_in_viewports` (`menu_page.h:38-50`) — takes `ID3D11DeviceContext*`, `ID3D11CommandList*&` and `DirectX::SpriteBatch*` in its signature. The consequence is measurable rather than theoretical: `tests/` contains `assets/`, `core/` and `math/` and nothing else, and no test can construct a `MainMenuStageSelect` to exercise `slot_of`, `cycle_stages` or `all_players_confirmed`, because constructing one requires a device. The eight identical bodies exist only because the type they name is not the engine's; behind a renderer interface, `MenuPage` could own both containers and all eight overrides would delete themselves.

**Remedy:** make the sampler choice a renderer-interface parameter (`draw_sprite(..., Filter)` or a small `DrawOptions`) rather than a game-visible COM pointer. This is the renderer-seam decision the project already has open; the menu is its loudest client.

#### The resolution is written to `ResolutionManager` twice, and the container rescale silently depends on the first write

- **File:** `game/states/main_menu.cpp:327-350`

- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Services and lifetimes ("If an ordering is load-bearing, it is either designed away or stated where it lives")

**What:** `Application::set_resolution` already repoints the resolution manager, but the apply path also does it by hand five lines earlier and reads the manager in between — so deleting the apparently-redundant line turns the widget rescale into a silent no-op.

**Evidence:**

    327:				auto prev_resolution = this->resolution_manager()->resolution_vec();
    328:
    329:				this->resolution_manager()->set_resolution(
    330:					this->resolution_selection_);
    336:				auto res_f = this->float_resolution();
    337:
    338:				this->data()->application()->set_resolution(
    339:					this->resolution_selection_);
    346:				this->texture_container_->scale_objects_to_new_resolution(
    347:					prev_resolution, res_f);

`engine/app/application.cpp:215-218`:

    void Application::set_resolution(ScreenResolution resolution)
    {
    	this->options_.resolution = resolution;
    	this->resolution_manager_->set_resolution(resolution);

and `MenuPage::float_resolution()` (`menu_page.cpp:195-198`) is `data()->resolution_manager()->resolution_vec()` — the same object, since `GameData::resolution_manager()` forwards to the shell's.

**Remedy:** call `application()->set_resolution()` first and read `float_resolution()` after it; delete 329-330.

#### Menu `update()` allocates and does string-keyed map lookups every frame, contradicting the contract written on `Registry` itself

- **File:** `game/states/main_menu.cpp:1236-1287`, `1555-1604`, `1831-1859`, `44`, `140-141`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** performance
- **Tenet:** T7/T8 ("Per-frame code performs no heap allocation and no string-keyed lookups")

**What:** all three per-player select pages re-resolve every sprite frame by name and re-set every string on every frame, and every page allocates a `std::vector` per frame to pass two elements to the draw path.

**Evidence:** `MainMenuTeamSelect::deselect_and_unconfirm_all_widgets` runs unconditionally from `update()` each frame —

    1273:		this->player_widgets_[i]->player_a->set_sprite_frame(
    1274:			"team_select_a");
    1275:		this->player_widgets_[i]->player_center->set_sprite_frame(
    1276:			"team_select_center");
    1277:		this->player_widgets_[i]->player_b->set_sprite_frame(
    1278:			"team_select_b");

I followed the call: `MTexture::set_sprite_frame` (`widget.cpp:173`) → `TextureObject::set_frame` (`texture_object.cpp:37-40`) → `SpriteSheet::resolve_sprite_frame` (`sprite_sheet.cpp:23-27`) → `Registry::resolve`, which is a `std::map<std::string,int>::find`. The registry's own header (`engine/core/registry.h:32-37`) says:

    //     resolve(name) -> Handle       once, at load
    //     get(handle)   -> Resource*    per frame - no string, no map, no compare
    //
    // Per-frame code touches no string-keyed map (PHILOSOPHY T7, T8), so per-frame
    // code never sees a name.

**Why it matters:** at four players the team page performs sixteen `std::map::find` calls per frame (twelve in the reset, four in the re-apply). The weapon page adds four more frame resolves plus eight `TextObject::remeasure()` calls — `set_text` unconditionally re-measures (`text_object.cpp:102-106`), and `MeasureString` walks the string glyph by glyph, on descriptions up to 100 characters (`1601-1602`, and `weapon_description` returns by value, so each is copied twice per player per frame). The stage page does one more at `1847`. `MainMenuOptions::update` adds a guaranteed heap allocation of its own: `std::string highlighted_element = this->highlighted_widget()->name();` (`309-310`) copies `"resolution_element"` — 18 characters, past MSVC's 15-character small-string buffer — every frame the page is open. All of it recomputes values that changed on no frame but the one where a button was pressed, and the engine documents the rule on the very type being misused.

**Remedy:** resolve the frame handles once in `init()`, touch a widget only when its state actually changed, and take `name()` by `const&`.

#### A mistyped `icon_frame` in a level file is first detected from `update()`, three screens into the menu, by killing the process

- **File:** `game/states/main_menu.cpp:1844-1849`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6 (loud failure — "a missing texture is a launch-time error naming the file"); T5
- **Origin:** added-by-verifier

**What:** the stage list is built at load and its `icon_frame` string is carried along, but nothing checks the frame exists until the stage-select page displays it — from `update()`, every frame, through a call that throws.

**Evidence:**

    1844:	else if (slot >= 0 && slot < static_cast<int>(stages->size()))
    1845:	{
    1846:		const Stage& stage = stages->at(static_cast<size_t>(slot));
    1847:		this->stage_icon_->set_sprite_frame(stage.icon_frame);
    1848:		this->stage_name_->set_text(stage.display_name);
    1849:	}

`Registry::resolve` (`engine/core/registry.h:84-93`) throws `std::out_of_range` naming the frame. There is no handler between `State::update()` and `wWinMain`, whose catch (`game/main.cpp:93-101`) reports it as:

    MessageBoxA(nullptr, e.what(), "ArtAttack - startup failure",

**Why it matters:** `LevelLoadedInfo::icon_frame()` is deliberately a `required_string`, and its header explains why — "these two are checked because they are the keys a person adding a stage has to write by hand, so getting one wrong is the likely mistake" (`level_loaded_info.h:41-46`). That check confirms the key is *present*, never that it *resolves*. So the likely mistake — a typo in the frame name — survives load, survives the manifest, survives four menu screens, and then terminates the game the instant Stage Select opens, under a dialog that says "startup failure" about something that is not startup. `stage.h:15-17` states the opposite as the design: "display_name and icon_frame are copied out of the level file at load rather than read back through the registry each time the menu redraws — the menu holds no handle and does no lookup for its own text (T8)." That is true of the text and false of the icon, in the same struct.

**Remedy:** resolve the frame to a handle in the loader that builds the `StageList` (`main.cpp:60-72`), so a bad name fails at load naming the level file; store the handle on `Stage` and let the menu hold it, which fixes the per-frame lookup at 1847 at the same time.

- **File:** `game/states/main_menu.cpp:138-141`, `307-310`, `625-628`, `860-863`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T2 (correctness over speed)

**What:** all four pad slots are processed against a focus name read once, while `change_highlight` mutates the focus inside the loop.

**Evidence:**

    138:	std::vector<ProcessedMenuInput> inputs = this->menu_inputs();
    139:	int num_inputs = static_cast<int>(inputs.size());
    140:	std::string highlighted_element =
    141:		this->highlighted_widget()->name();
    142:
    143:	for (int i = 0; i < num_inputs; i++)

**Why it matters:** finding #18 of the first review, still live, and now on a loop whose bound is fixed at 4 rather than the connected-pad count, so every page walks all four slots every frame. Two concrete consequences on `MainMenuHome`. Pad 0 releases Down (focus moves Play → Options at line 196) and pad 1 releases A in the same frame: line 154 still compares against `"play"`, so the game transitions to Mode Select. #### 54 SCREAMING constants in a `consts` namespace, holding content that belongs in JSON

- **File:** `game/states/main_menu.h:13-88`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Never ("SCREAMING constants — screaming means macro, nothing else"); T7

**What:** the largest game header opens with a namespace of 54 SCREAMING-cased non-macro constants, several of which are game copy rather than configuration.

**Evidence:**

    13:namespace main_menu_consts
    14:{
    15:	const static mattmath::Vector2F DEFAULT_RESOLUTION = { 1920.0f, 1080.0f };
    21:	const static std::string TITLE_FONT = "gill_sans_ultra_bold_144";
    82:	const static std::string SPRAYER_DESC = "Fires a powerful stream of paint in an arc pattern.\nGood for beginners.";

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS reserves screaming names for macros "so that a screaming name always signals preprocessor danger and nothing else ever does" — 54 counter-examples in one header defeat that signal outright, and the conventions passes that swept the rest of this tree stopped at this door. The same section calls this exact shape out by name: "A header full of numeric constants is usually tuning data in the wrong place — *which* and *how much* belong in JSON (T7). Constants that stay in code live next to the one thing they configure, not in a `consts` namespace collecting strays." `ViewportManager` (`viewport_manager.h:15-21`) already shows the shape the engine adopted for the same problem. Separately, `const` at namespace scope gives internal linkage, so each of the two TUs reaching this header gets its own copies of ~20 `std::string` and ~14 `Colour` objects, dynamically initialised before `main`. Exactly one constant is unused: `STAGE_SELECT_READY_SIZE` (line 69).

**Remedy:** move the descriptions, fonts, colours and spacings into the menu's JSON alongside the stage records; whatever survives becomes `snake_case` `constexpr` next to its one user.

- **File:** `game/states/main_menu.cpp:1140-1166`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6 (loud failure over graceful degradation)
- **Origin:** added-by-verifier

**What:** pressing A before choosing a team, and pressing B while another player is confirmed, both fall off the end of the `if`/`else if` chain with no sound, no message and no state change.

**Evidence:**

    1140:		if (inputs[i].action == MenuInputAction::back)
    1141:		{
    1142:			if (this->all_players_unconfirmed())
    1149:			}
    1150:			if (this->select_states_[i].state == ConfirmationState::confirmed)
    1155:			}
    1157:		}
    1158:		else if (inputs[i].action == MenuInputAction::proceed &&
    1159:			this->select_states_[i].team != PlayerTeam::none)

    1161:			this->play_wave(this->confirm_sound_);
    1162:			this->select_states_[i].state = ConfirmationState::confirmed;
    1163:		}

**Why it matters:** every player arrives on this screen with `PlayerTeam::none` — that is the default in `MenuPlayerSettings` (`menu_player_settings.h:7`) and `init()` seeds `select_states_` straight from it (`1327-1328`). The centre widget is drawn *selected* (`1251-1253`), so the screen looks like something is chosen; press A and the guard at 1159 fails, the next branch checks a direction that is `none`, and the frame ends silently. Symmetrically, a player who has not confirmed pressing B while a team-mate has gets nothing: `all_players_unconfirmed()` is false and their own state is not `confirmed`, so both inner branches miss. `MainMenuModeSelect` at least answers an impossible press with `error_sound_` (`651-662`); this page answers with nothing at all, and T6 names quiet failure "the most expensive kind".

and

    148:class MainMenuHome final : public MainMenuPage, public MenuHighlight

**Why it matters:** T11 asks for values that "live on the stack or inline in the containers that own them". `PlayerWidgets` is four `unique_ptr`s, and the raw pointers handed to `MContainer::add_child` (`1371-1375`) point at the *pointees*, whose addresses are stable regardless of vector reallocation — so `std::vector<PlayerWidgets>` is safe (the implicit move constructor exists and is `noexcept`) and the outer `unique_ptr` buys nothing but a second dereference per access, of which `deselect_and_unconfirm_all_widgets` alone makes six per player per frame. `MenuHighlight` (`menu_highlight.h:7-29`) holds one pointer and two colours behind protected accessors, declares no virtual function and no virtual destructor; it is a member wearing a base's clothes, and inheriting it puts four page classes into multiple inheritance for no dispatch. (It is not a delete-through-base hazard: destruction always goes through `State`'s virtual destructor.) `select_states_` on the very next line shows the shape both should have.

**Remedy:** `std::vector<PlayerWidgets> player_widgets_;` and `MenuHighlight highlight_;`.

---

#### Home's Exit destroys the window from inside `update()` and does not return, so the same tick still renders and Presents

- **File:** `game/states/main_menu.cpp:170-174`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** lifetime
- **Tenet:** T6 ("Not a licence for: throwing on the way out — teardown stays silent")
- **Origin:** added-by-verifier

**What:** the Exit branch calls `Application::quit()`, which calls `DestroyWindow` synchronously, and then falls through to keep processing the remaining pad slots; the enclosing tick goes on to render and present to the destroyed window.

**Evidence:**

    170:				if (highlighted_element == "exit")
    171:				{
    172:					this->main_menu_data()->application()->quit();
    173:				}
    174:			}

It is the only one of the twenty-one flow-exit points in this file with no `return` after it. `engine/app/application.cpp:207-213`:

    void Application::quit() const
    {
    	if (this->window_ != nullptr)
    	{
    		DestroyWindow(this->window_);
    	}
    }

and the loop that does not get to notice, `application.cpp:251-255`:

    void Application::tick()
    {
    	this->timer_.Tick([&]() { this->update(); });
    	this->render();
    }

**Why it matters:** `DestroyWindow` is synchronous, so by the time `update()` returns the `HWND` is gone; `render()` then clears, draws and calls `DeviceResources::Present()`, which routes any failing `HRESULT` that is not a device-removal into `ThrowIfFailed` (`device_resources.cpp:519-521`). The `while (message.message != WM_QUIT)` guard is only re-evaluated at the top of the next iteration, one full frame too late. Whether DXGI actually errors here is driver-dependent — what is not in question is that the shutdown path runs a whole frame against a destroyed window, that `window_` is never nulled so a second press repeats the `DestroyWindow`, and that a throw on the way out would surface as a message box titled "ArtAttack - startup failure" (`main.cpp:93-101`), which PHILOSOPHY explicitly rules out for teardown.

**Remedy:** `return;` after `quit()`, and make `Application::quit()` `PostQuitMessage(0)` — letting the message loop exit between ticks — rather than tearing the window down from inside a state's `update()`.

### Rejected

- **`#pragma region` violates ARCHITECTURE/The build ("Nothing IDE-specific is committed")** — rejected as a citation. That sentence governs build files and solution files; `#pragma region` is a compiler pragma the engine itself uses in `engine/ui/widget.cpp` and `engine/math/matt_math.cpp`. The observation (the regions measure the file's unnavigability) is kept inside finding 1; the rule reference is not.
- **"48 SCREAMING constants"** — corrected, not rejected. The namespace holds 54 (52 `const`/`const static`, 2 `constexpr`); I enumerated them and checked each for use — exactly one, `STAGE_SELECT_READY_SIZE`, is dead.
- **"three hardcoded switches" (weapon roster)** — corrected to two: `update_weapon_select_visuals` (1561) and `weapon_description` (1716). `cycle_weapons` is arithmetic, not a switch.
- **"2316 lines"** — corrected to 2,317 (1977 + 340).
- **"`main.cpp:76-83` proves the stage list non-empty"** — corrected: the comment is 76-78, the guard and throw are 79-84. The claim itself holds.
- **"four commented-out statements"** — corrected to five sites (332-333, 351, 589, 743, 1010).
- **"the audio refactor added five more resolutions behind [the mem-init hazard]"** — rejected. The six `resolve_*` calls are in the constructor body, which runs after all bases are complete; they are not exposed to the base-clause ordering at all.
- **Severity of the weapon roster (high)** — regraded to medium: T7 debt with no runtime defect, downstream of a structural item IMPLEMENTED.md already carries as outstanding.
- **Severity of the mem-initializer finding (medium)** — regraded to low: verified currently well-defined, latent only.
- **Severity of the weapon-select back edge (medium)** — regraded to low: wrong destination, one extra press to recover.
- **Not filed: `int i < inputs.size()` at line 56 as a `/W4 /WX` violation** — I suspected C4018 and tested it, compiling the pattern with this tree's own compiler (MSVC 19.51, `/W4 /WX /permissive- /std:c++20`). No diagnostic, and `main_menu.cpp.obj` is newer than the source, so the file builds clean as claimed.
- **Not filed: `selected_widget` null dereference at `main_menu.cpp:1264`** — `PlayerTeam` has exactly three enumerators, all three are cases in the switch above it, and a missing one would be a `/W4` C4062 error anyway.
- **Not filed: use-after-free at `transition_to`** — `StateContext::transition_to` (`state_context.cpp:21-26`) destroys the running page inside the assignment, so every page's `update()` continues on a destroyed `this`. I walked all 21 sites in this file: every one is followed immediately by `return` with no member access, so nothing here is defective. The hazard belongs to `engine/core/state_context`, not to the menu.
- **Not filed: fullscreen and selected resolution disagree after Apply** — `Application::set_fullscreen(true)` maximises the window while `ResolutionManager` keeps the chosen resolution, and `ViewportManager` sizes every viewport from the latter (`viewport_manager.cpp:15-19, 43-59`), so the picture occupies a sub-rectangle of the screen on any monitor larger than the selection. Real, but its cause is entirely in `Application`/`create_window` (which also passes a window size where a client size is wanted, with no `AdjustWindowRect`); filing it here would misdirect the fix. Routed to the app/window group.
