#### The parallel-render protocol is written by hand twice, because `ThreadPool` has no `parallel_for`

- **File:** `game/objects/level.cpp:397-417`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T4 ("Not a licence for: copy-paste in the name of readability")

**What:** "Ask the pool for its width, split a range with `Partitioner`, submit one lambda per
partition, block" appears twice in the game with no engine helper, and the two copies already
handle their command lists differently.

**Evidence:**

    // game/objects/level.cpp:397-417
    	int num_threads = this->thread_pool_->max_num_threads();
    	auto partitioned_players =
    		this->partitioner_->partition(this->player_objects_->size(), num_threads);
    	for (int i = 0; i < partitioned_players.size(); i++)
    	{
    		this->thread_pool_->add_task([this, i, partitioned_players, …]() { … });
    	}
    	this->thread_pool_->wait_for_tasks_to_complete();

    // game/states/menu_page.cpp:134-153 — the same shape
    	int num_threads = this->data()->thread_pool()->max_num_threads();
    	auto partitioned_mobjects =
    		partitioner->partition(mobjects->size(), num_threads);
    	for (int i = 0; i < partitioned_mobjects.size(); i++)
    	{
    		thread_pool->add_task([this, i, &partitioned_mobjects, …]() { … });
    	}
    	thread_pool->wait_for_tasks_to_complete();

    // engine/core/thread_pool.h:20-26 — everything the engine offers
            void add_task(std::function<void()> task);
            void wait_for_tasks_to_complete();

**Why it matters:** Both copies also carry the command-list half — `menu_page.cpp:157-166`
executes and releases the lists inline, `game_states.cpp:330-339` does the same for the level —
and that is where they diverged on the `RestoreContextState` flag (`TRUE` in the level path,
`FALSE` in the menu path). One is measurably slower per frame per view and nothing says which
is intended. The lambda in `level.cpp:406` also captures `partitioned_players` **by value** —
a `std::vector<std::pair<int,int>>` copied once per submitted task, per frame — while
`menu_page.cpp:145` captures the equivalent by reference; neither choice was made deliberately.

**Remedy:** Add `ThreadPool::parallel_for(count, fn)` owning the partition and the wait, and
fold the deferred-context record/execute pair into one engine RAII type both callers use.

#### The assets tests compile engine sources instead of linking the engine

- **File:** `tests/assets/CMakeLists.txt:6-19`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** testing
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Targets and layout ("Tests link libraries, never `#include` implementation files")

**What:** `AssetsTests` pulls two engine `.cpp` files into its own target rather than linking
`ArtAttackEngine`, and the comment says why: linking the engine drags D3D11 in.

**Evidence:**

    # The manifest loader reads a file and parses JSON, and that is all it does -
    # no device, no DirectXTK - so this target compiles the two translation units
    # directly rather than linking the engine and everything the engine drags in.
    add_executable(AssetsTests
        asset_manifest_loader_tests.cpp
        test_main.cpp
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/engine/assets/asset_manifest_loader.cpp"
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/engine/assets/json_loader.cpp"
    )

**Why it matters:** This is the build stating a fact the design docs deny. PHILOSOPHY/Tests
and toolchain says "Everything below the platform edge is testable headlessly, because the
boundary (targets) and the seams (renderer interface, parameterised draw) make it linkable and
constructible without a window" — but `ArtAttackEngine` is one static library that links
`d3d11 dxgi dxguid` PUBLIC (`engine/CMakeLists.txt:50-53`), so nothing can link a piece of it.
`tests/core` dodges the same problem differently, by testing only header-only types
(`tests/core/CMakeLists.txt:3-5`), which is why the two subsystems most in need of tests —
`Scene`-shaped logic and collision — have none. Compiling the same TU into two targets also
means the test binary can silently be built with different flags from the shipping one, which
is the exact class of bug IMPLEMENTED.md records for `/fp:fast` in the old test project.

**Remedy:** Split the engine at the platform edge — a device-free lower library the tests link,
with the D3D11 backend above it — which is the same seam the renderer interface needs anyway.

#### A game project must find and link the engine's third-party dependencies itself

- **File:** `samples/minimal/CMakeLists.txt:1-25`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** ARCHITECTURE/A game project ("A project is an ordinary C++ application that links two static libraries")

**What:** The sample — advertised in its own comment as "the whole build file for a game on
this engine" — has to `find_package` two of the engine's vcpkg dependencies and link
`Microsoft::DirectXTK` by name before it can use `ArtAttackEngine`.

**Evidence:**

    # xaudio2redist first: directxtk's config references Microsoft::XAudio2Redist
    # but does not find it itself.
    find_package(xaudio2redist CONFIG REQUIRED)
    find_package(directxtk CONFIG REQUIRED)
    …
    target_link_libraries(ArtAttackSample PRIVATE
        ArtAttackEngine
        Microsoft::DirectXTK
        artattack_settings
    )

**Why it matters:** The identical four lines are copy-pasted into `engine/CMakeLists.txt:7-10`
and `game/CMakeLists.txt:1-4`, including the same workaround comment — three copies of one
piece of knowledge about the bought edge. ARCHITECTURE promises the client sees "a dozen
honest lines"; what it actually sees is the engine's dependency list, which means a future
change to that list (an audio backend swap, a second graphics package) breaks every project
built on the engine rather than being absorbed by the library that chose it. This is the build
equivalent of the same failure as the D3D11 leak in `hello_state.cpp`: the platform edge is not
encapsulated in either dimension.

**Remedy:** Do the `find_package` calls once, at the root `CMakeLists.txt`, so the imported
targets exist for every subdirectory and a client's file is `add_executable` + `link
ArtAttackEngine artattack_settings`.

<a id="g-sweep-namespaces"></a>

## sweep-namespaces — Namespaces

*Group `sweep-namespaces` · 11 findings (3 high, 4 medium, 4 low) · source `review2/raw/sweep-namespaces.md`, cross-cutting sweep — no separate verifier, reported as written.*

I read CONVENTIONS/Namespaces, ARCHITECTURE and PHILOSOPHY first, then opened every
`namespace` declaration and every `using namespace` in `engine/`, `game/`, `samples/`,
`tests/`, `cmake/` and the root build files (`external/` excluded), and checked each
translation unit's wrapping structure with `grep -n "^namespace|^}"` before opening the
candidates. The recent wrap did most of its job well: **49 of the 50 engine headers and
all 35 engine `.cpp` files are wrapped in `artattack::` or `mattmath::`**, there is not a
single `using namespace` at namespace scope in any header anywhere in the repository,
no game file reopens `artattack::`, and the newest engine code (`asset_manifest_loader.cpp`,
`sprite_sheet_loader.cpp`) correctly nests an anonymous namespace *inside* `artattack` for
its TU-local helpers. The shape of what is left is a clean split by age. One engine file
was missed entirely — `engine/math/colour.h` still declares `colour_consts` in the global
namespace, and because `engine/render/draw_object.h:3` includes it, the engine's own public
API defaults are written against a global-namespace symbol. Everything on the game side is
untouched: 101 types across 66 headers sit in the global namespace, 17 `*_consts` namespaces
sit beside them, and 35 of 46 game `.cpp` files hoist three to five namespaces each,
including `using namespace artattack;` — which erases the one visible marker of which side
of the boundary a name is on, in the codebase whose whole job is to keep that boundary
honest. The surprise was `samples/minimal/`: it is brand-new code written after CONVENTIONS
existed, it is the file ARCHITECTURE tells strangers to copy, and it reproduces the game's
pattern exactly. I found no live name collision anywhere — I checked engine-vs-game type
names, `colour_consts` against every co-hoisted `*_consts` namespace, and `mattmath` against
`artattack` — so every finding below is a convention breach or a latent hazard, graded as
such, not a bug you can hit today.

### Themes

- The wrap was applied to files, not to the project: it stopped at the `engine/` directory
  boundary, so the one engine header with a global namespace and the whole of `game/` were
  never in scope for it.
- Constants are still organised by a `*_consts` namespace per file rather than by the thing
  they configure, which is precisely the arrangement CONVENTIONS/Constants names and rejects.
- The game's source uses `using namespace` as a substitute for a namespace of its own: five
  directives at the top of a file replace the qualification that would have said where each
  name came from.
- New code written since the conventions landed (`samples/minimal/`, `tests/`) inherited the
  old code's namespace habits rather than the document's rules, so the two examples a
  stranger is most likely to copy both teach the wrong thing.
- Qualification is applied inconsistently within a single namespace — `mattmath::` appears
  273 times inside `namespace mattmath` in three headers while identical declarations
  nearby are bare — so the reader cannot use qualification as a signal.
- Nothing in the repository is nested more than two levels and `detail` is used nowhere; the
  two places that do nest (`colour_consts::html`, and the anonymous namespaces inside
  `artattack`) went in opposite directions on whether nesting is allowed.

---

#### Move `colour_consts` into `mattmath::` — it is the one place the engine still claims the global namespace

- **File:** `engine/math/colour.h:5-7`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Namespaces

**What:** `engine/math/colour.h`, a header of the `MattMath` static library, declares
`colour_consts` at global scope with a second global-scope-reachable namespace `html`
nested inside it, and engine public headers write their default arguments against it.

**Evidence:**

`engine/math/colour.h:1-9`:

    #pragma once

    #include "engine/math/matt_math.h"

    namespace colour_consts
    {
        namespace html
        {
            const std::string ALICE_BLUE = "f0f8ff";

`engine/math/colour.h:159` and `:308-309`:

        const mattmath::Colour ALICE_BLUE = { html::ALICE_BLUE };
        ...
        const mattmath::Colour TEAM_BLUE = { 6, 52, 204, 255 };
        const mattmath::Colour TEAM_YELLOW = { 255, 255, 0, 255 };

`engine/render/text.h:15` — an engine public API default written against it:

            const mattmath::Colour& color = colour_consts::WHITE,

`engine/render/draw_object.h:3` — how it reaches nearly every TU:

    #include "engine/math/colour.h"

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS/Namespaces states "everything in `MattMath` lives in
`mattmath::`" and "The engine never claims the global namespace." This is the only file in
`engine/` that breaks it — every other header and `.cpp` under `engine/` opens `artattack`
or `mattmath` on its first declaration. The blast radius is not theoretical: twelve engine
headers name `colour_consts` (`animation_object.h`, `draw_object.h`, `sprite_sheet.h`,
`sprite_sheet_object.h`, `text.h`, `text_drop_shadow.h`, `text_object.h`, `texture_object.h`,
`viewport_manager.h`, `visual.h`, `widget.h`, and `colour.h` itself), so a stranger who
namespaces their game correctly still finds the engine's own default arguments reaching into
the global namespace, and `mattmath::Colour` and its named values live in two different
namespaces for no reason a reader can infer. The nested `html` is a second level of nesting
that is not `detail`, which the same paragraph rules out. Two secondary consequences are
worth recording while the file is open: namespace-scope `const` has internal linkage, so
every TU reached through `draw_object.h` gets its own copy of ~160 `std::string` and ~161
`Colour` objects with dynamic initialisers; and `TEAM_BLUE`/`TEAM_YELLOW`/`TEAM_ORANGE`/
`TEAM_PINK`/`TEAM_GREEN` at lines 308-312 are game nouns in the math library, which the
boundary litmus test in PHILOSOPHY (The boundary) rejects outright.

**Remedy:** Move the contents into `mattmath::` (the palette next to `Colour`, `html` folded
away or renamed `detail`), and move the five `TEAM_*` values into `game/objects/team_colour.h`
where the game already builds `TeamColour` out of them.

---

#### Give the sample's state a namespace — it is the file ARCHITECTURE tells strangers to copy

- **File:** `samples/minimal/states/hello_state.h:16`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Namespaces

**What:** `samples/minimal/`, written after CONVENTIONS existed and described by its own
`CMakeLists.txt` as "the new-project template", declares its one type in the global namespace
and hoists three namespaces at global scope in its two source files.

**Evidence:**

`samples/minimal/states/hello_state.h:16`:

    class HelloState : public artattack::State

`samples/minimal/states/hello_state.cpp:5-7`:

    using namespace DirectX;
    using namespace mattmath;
    using namespace artattack;

`samples/minimal/main.cpp:16`:

    using namespace artattack;

`samples/minimal/CMakeLists.txt:6`:

    # --- ArtAttackSample — the minimal sample, and the new-project template ---

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS/Namespaces says "Game code owns its own namespace";
ARCHITECTURE (A game project) says "Starting a game is copying `samples/minimal/`, renaming
the target, and owning everything inside"; PHILOSOPHY (Structural types) says "Structure comes
from example, not enforcement" and names this sample as the canonical shape. The example
therefore *is* the enforcement, and it currently teaches the opposite of the rule — every
project copied from it starts in the global namespace with the engine's namespace flattened
into it. This is the single cheapest finding in the sweep to fix (two files, one type) and
the most expensive to leave, because it propagates into code that is not in this repository.
It is also self-defeating as documentation: `hello_state.cpp:33` reads
`std::make_unique<Text>(...)` where the whole point of the sample is to show a stranger that
`Text` is the engine's.

**Remedy:** Wrap both sample files in `namespace minimal` (or `sample`), qualify
`artattack::` explicitly at least in `hello_state.h`, and keep `using namespace mattmath;`
in the `.cpp` — which is the one directive CONVENTIONS explicitly permits.

---

#### Give the game a namespace of its own — 101 types sit in the global one

- **File:** `game/objects/player.h:63`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Namespaces

**What:** No file under `game/` declares a namespace for the game; all 101 top-level types
across its 66 headers are declared at global scope, while every `.cpp` flattens `artattack::`
into that same scope with a using-directive.

**Evidence:**

`game/objects/player.h:63-64`:

    class Player final : public artattack::MovingObject, public ICollisionGameObject,
                         public artattack::AnimationObject, public artattack::TextureObject

`game/game_data.h:21`:

    class GameData

`game/objects/player.cpp:4-8`:

    using namespace DirectX;
    using namespace mattmath;
    using namespace player_consts;
    using namespace colour_consts;
    using namespace artattack;

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS/Namespaces is explicit — "Game code owns its own namespace
and never reopens the engine's" — and the engine's first client is the standing demonstration
of every rule the engine asks its users to follow. Concretely, in `player.cpp` after line 8,
`RectangleF` (MattMath), `RenderResources` (engine), `PlayerAnimationInfo` (game) and `GRAY`
(a global colour table shipped by the math library) all read identically, so a reader cannot
tell which side of the boundary any name is on without grepping — in exactly the codebase
whose stated job is to keep that boundary honest. I checked for live collisions between
`artattack::` and the game's global names and found none today; the hazard is that a
using-directive makes `artattack::X` appear at global scope, so the day the engine gains a
type the game already has (ARCHITECTURE plans `Scene`, and `Level` is slated to become a
game-side class owning one) every game TU becomes ambiguous at once. The cost of the fix
grows with every file added while the engine/game split is still in progress.

**Remedy:** Wrap `game/` in `namespace artattack_game` (or the game's own short name) and
delete the `using namespace artattack;` lines, qualifying the engine at its use sites.

---

#### Collapse the seventeen `*_consts` namespaces — CONVENTIONS names this exact arrangement and rejects it

- **File:** `game/objects/level.h:30`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Constants

**What:** Seventeen namespaces exist across the repository whose only purpose is to hold
constants, sixteen of them in `game/` and all seventeen at global scope.

**Evidence:** every `*_consts` namespace declaration in the repo, verified by opening each:

    engine/math/colour.h:5:namespace colour_consts
    game/directory_consts.h:8:namespace directory_consts
    game/objects/debug_text.h:8:namespace debug_text_consts
    game/objects/interface_gameplay.h:9:namespace interface_consts
    game/objects/level.h:30:namespace level_consts
    game/objects/paint_tile.h:9:namespace paint_tile_consts
    game/objects/player_consts.h:17:namespace player_consts
    game/objects/player_input.h:7:namespace player_input_consts
    game/objects/projectile_consts.h:5:namespace projectile_consts
    game/objects/structure_paintable.h:10:namespace structure_paintable_consts
    game/objects/team_colour.h:24:namespace team_colour_consts
    game/objects/weapon_consts.h:6:namespace weapon_consts
    game/states/end_menu.h:10:namespace end_menu_consts
    game/states/main_menu.h:13:namespace main_menu_consts
    game/states/menu_input.h:9:namespace menu_input_consts
    game/states/pause_menu.h:10:namespace pause_menu_consts
    game/states/results_menu.h:8:namespace results_menu_consts

`game/objects/level.h:30-34`:

    namespace level_consts
    {
        constexpr float TIMER = 240.0f;
        constexpr float START_TIMER = 3.0f;
        const static std::string COUNTDOWN_TEXT = "3";

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS/Constants says "Constants that stay in code live next to the
one thing they configure, not in a `consts` namespace collecting strays", and CONVENTIONS/
Namespaces allows one namespace per library. These are seventeen namespaces holding roughly
350 values between them, and the arrangement is what forces the using-directive stacking in
the next finding — a `.cpp` cannot write `TIMER` without hoisting `level_consts`, so every
file that touches tuning data hoists a namespace. The same paragraph also flags most of this
content as being in the wrong medium: `level_consts::TIMER = 240.0f` is *how much*, which
belongs in JSON (T7), and the two headers named for a namespace rather than a type
(`player_consts.h`, `projectile_consts.h`, `weapon_consts.h`) breach CONVENTIONS/Files, with
`player_consts.h:7` declaring an unrelated `struct PlayerAnimationInfo` above the namespace
to prove the point.

**Remedy:** Move tuning values into the JSON the loaders already walk, and make what
genuinely stays in code `static constexpr` members of the type they configure, deleting the
namespaces with them.

---

#### Stop stacking using-directives — 35 of 46 game `.cpp` files hoist three to five namespaces

- **File:** `game/objects/player.cpp:4-8`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Namespaces

**What:** Thirty-five of the game's forty-six `.cpp` files open with three to five
`using namespace` directives at global scope, against a convention that permits `mattmath`
and asks for others "sparingly".

**Evidence:** `game/objects/player.cpp:4-8` (five, the maximum; `interface_gameplay.cpp`,
`structure_paintable.cpp`, `main_menu.cpp`, `pause_menu.cpp` and `results_menu.cpp` also
carry five):

    using namespace DirectX;
    using namespace mattmath;
    using namespace player_consts;
    using namespace colour_consts;
    using namespace artattack;

`game/main.cpp:10-12`:

    using namespace DirectX;
    using namespace directory_consts;
    using namespace artattack;

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS/Namespaces reads "In a `.cpp`, `using namespace mattmath;` is
acceptable — math reads badly fully qualified — and others are used sparingly." Five per file
across three quarters of the game is not sparingly, and the directive that costs the most is
`using namespace artattack;`: it deletes the only textual signal of where the engine ends and
the game begins, in the client whose existence is justified by keeping that boundary visible.
`using namespace colour_consts;` alone hoists roughly 165 `Colour` objects and the nested
`html` namespace name into the file's global scope. I checked every co-hoisted pair for name
overlap (`colour_consts` against `player_consts`, `main_menu_consts`, `pause_menu_consts`,
`results_menu_consts`, `end_menu_consts` and `interface_consts`) and found none, so there is
no ambiguity today — but each directive is a standing bet that the two namespaces stay
disjoint, taken 35 times, and resolving one later means editing every file that took it.

**Remedy:** Keep `using namespace mattmath;`, drop the rest, and let the constants finding
above remove the `*_consts` directives by construction.

---

#### Rename the test namespaces to lowercase, or delete them — they duplicate the doctest suite name

- **File:** `tests/math/math_tests.cpp:9-20`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Namespaces

**What:** All seven namespaces in `tests/` are PascalCase, at global scope, and six of the
seven wrap nothing but a `TEST_SUITE` whose string argument repeats the namespace name.

**Evidence:** `tests/math/math_tests.cpp:9-20`:

    namespace MathTestConstants
    {
        constexpr float EPSILON_F = 0.000001f;
        constexpr float EPSILON_F_2 = 0.000002f;
        constexpr float EPSILON_F_100 = 0.0001f;
    }

    using namespace MathTestConstants;

    namespace EricsonMathTests
    {
        TEST_SUITE("EricsonMathTests")

The full set, each opened and confirmed: `MathTestConstants` (math_tests.cpp:9),
`EricsonMathTests` (:18), `MattMathTests` (:205), `NameTableTests`
(name_table_tests.cpp:16), `RegistryTests` (registry_tests.cpp:23), `CollisionToolsTests`
(collision_tools_tests.cpp:15), `AssetManifestLoaderTests`
(asset_manifest_loader_tests.cpp:57).

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS gives namespaces one form — "one lowercase word", `artattack`,
`mattmath` — and PascalCase names a type, so `namespace RegistryTests` tells a reader the
wrong thing about what follows. These are all new files added with the CTest conversion, so
they are the template every future test is copied from, and the convention they break is the
one the same conversion was meant to establish. `MathTestConstants` is additionally a
`*_consts` namespace by another name, hoisted straight back out at line 16, and each of the
six suite namespaces is redundant with the `TEST_SUITE(...)` on the very next line, which is
already doctest's grouping mechanism.

**Remedy:** Delete the six suite namespaces and keep the `TEST_SUITE` strings; move the three
epsilons into the anonymous namespace these files already use for local helpers.

---

#### Scope `projectile_type` — it leaks five one-word ALL-CAPS names into the global namespace

- **File:** `game/objects/projectile.h:9-16`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Constants

**What:** The codebase's only unscoped `enum` puts `SPRAY`, `JET`, `ROLLING`, `MIST` and
`BALL` directly into the global namespace of every TU that reaches `projectile.h`.

**Evidence:** `game/objects/projectile.h:9-16`:

    enum projectile_type
    {
        SPRAY,
        JET,
        ROLLING,
        MIST,
        BALL
    };

**Why it matters:** I grepped every `enum` declaration in `engine/`, `game/`, `samples/` and
`tests/`: this is the only one that is not `enum class`, so it is the only one whose
enumerators are not scoped to their type. Its reach is not small — `weapon_details.h` includes
`projectile.h`, `weapon.h` includes `weapon_details.h`, `player.h` includes `weapon.h` and
`level.h` includes `player.h`, so five generic, four-to-seven-character global identifiers are
live across most of the game, alongside `using namespace colour_consts;` in six of those files
and `using namespace artattack;` in nearly all of them. There is no collision today (I checked
these five names against `colour_consts` and against every `artattack` and `mattmath` name),
but `BALL` and `MIST` are exactly the kind of name a future header or SDK macro claims.
CONVENTIONS also requires `enum class`, a PascalCase type name and snake_case enumerators —
`WeaponType::sprayer` is the pattern the neighbouring `weapon_type.h` already follows
correctly.

**Remedy:** Make it `enum class ProjectileType` with snake_case enumerators, matching
`weapon_type.h` two files away.

---

#### Delete the `using namespace mattmath;` that sits directly above `namespace mattmath`

- **File:** `engine/math/collision_tools.cpp:3-5`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Namespaces

**What:** Two of the three MattMath `.cpp` files hoist `mattmath` into the global namespace
on line 3 and then open `namespace mattmath` on line 5, which is a no-op.

**Evidence:** `engine/math/collision_tools.cpp:1-6`:

    #include "engine/math/collision_tools.h"

    using namespace mattmath;

    namespace mattmath
    {

`engine/math/ericson_math.cpp:1-6` is byte-identical in shape. `engine/math/matt_math.cpp:6-8`
is the correct version — `using namespace DirectX;` only, then `namespace mattmath {`.

**Why it matters:** Every name in these two files is already in `mattmath` by virtue of the
namespace opened two lines below, so the directive changes nothing and reads as though the
author believed it were needed — which makes a reader stop and look for the name it was
supposed to reach. It is a small thing that survived a namespace pass whose entire purpose was
to make the namespace structure legible, and the third file in the same directory shows what
was intended.

**Remedy:** Delete line 3 in both files.

---

#### Qualify rapidjson's `Value` in the three loaders that hoist it

- **File:** `engine/assets/asset_manifest_loader.cpp:6`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Namespaces

**What:** Three engine translation units pull the whole of `rapidjson` into their global
namespace and then write `Value` and `Document` bare, in code where those names are otherwise
unremarkable identifiers.

**Evidence:** `engine/assets/asset_manifest_loader.cpp:6` and `:23-24`:

    using namespace rapidjson;
    ...
            const Value& require_member(const Value& parent, const char* key,
                const std::string& path, const std::string& context)

The other two: `engine/assets/sound_bank_loader.cpp:8` (alongside
`using namespace DirectX;` on line 7) and `engine/assets/sprite_sheet_loader.cpp:5`
(alongside `using namespace mattmath;` on line 4, whose `decode_sprite_frames` at line 11
takes `const Value& json`).

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS permits `using namespace mattmath;` in a `.cpp` by name and
asks that others be "sparing", with the rationale being that math reads badly qualified —
`Value` reads badly *un*qualified, since nothing in the parameter list of `require_member`
says the argument is a JSON node rather than one of the engine's own values. The headers get
this right (`engine/assets/json_loader.h:12` declares `rapidjson::Document read_json_file`
fully qualified), so the leak is confined to three implementation files; it is a readability
cost, not a correctness one.

**Remedy:** Drop the three directives and write `rapidjson::Value` / `rapidjson::Document` at
the roughly two dozen use sites.

---

#### Label the closing brace of every namespace, or none of them

- **File:** `engine/math/matt_math.h:1150`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** T4

**What:** Every namespace in the repository closes with a bare `}` except one, so in the
longest files there is no way to tell the namespace's closing brace from a type's.

**Evidence:** `engine/math/matt_math.h:1146-1150` — 1139 lines after `namespace mattmath` opened
at line 11:

        bool edges_valid() const;
    };

    typedef RectangleRotated OBB;
    }

`engine/app/application.h:194-195` and `engine/ui/widget.h:167-168` are the same shape. The
single exception is `engine/math/matt_math.cpp:4595`:

    } // namespace mattmath

**Why it matters:** T4 asks for the next reader, who in a 1150-line header or a 598-line
`.cpp` has to count braces to answer "am I still inside the namespace?" — a question that
matters here precisely because the whole point of the recent wrap was that the answer is now
always yes. One file already carries the comment, so the codebase is inconsistent about it
rather than deliberately terse.

**Remedy:** Append `// namespace artattack` / `// namespace mattmath` to the closing brace,
matching what `matt_math.cpp` already does.

---

#### Drop the `mattmath::` prefix inside `namespace mattmath`

- **File:** `engine/math/matt_math.h:57-58`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** T4

**What:** `mattmath::` appears 273 times inside `namespace mattmath` across the three math
headers, applied inconsistently — identical declarations a few lines apart differ on whether
they qualify.

**Evidence:** `engine/math/matt_math.h:57-61`, where `sign` and the two-argument `are_equal`
qualify and the one-argument `are_equal` does not:

        int sign(const mattmath::Vector2F& p1,
            const mattmath::Vector2F& p2, const mattmath::Vector2F& p3);

        bool are_equal(float a, float b, float epsilon = EPSILON);
        bool are_equal(const mattmath::Vector2F& a, const mattmath::Vector2F& b,

The two typedefs in the same header disagree with each other — `engine/math/matt_math.h:298`:

        typedef mattmath::RectangleF AABB;

`engine/math/matt_math.h:1149`:

        typedef RectangleRotated OBB;

Counts by file: `matt_math.h` 193, `ericson_math.h` 45, `collision_tools.h` 35.

**Why it matters:** A qualification that is sometimes present and sometimes absent within one
namespace carries no information, so a reader has to check whether the two forms mean
something different — they do not. It also doubles the width of most declarations in the
library a stranger reads first, and it is the kind of noise the namespace pass was an
opportunity to remove.

**Remedy:** Strip `mattmath::` from declarations inside `namespace mattmath` in the three
headers and their `.cpp` counterparts.

<a id="g-sweep-naming"></a>

## sweep-naming — CONVENTIONS: naming, across the whole repository

*Group `sweep-naming` · 21 findings (5 high, 13 medium, 3 low) · source `review2/raw/sweep-naming.md`, cross-cutting sweep — no separate verifier, reported as written.*

I read PHILOSOPHY.md, CONVENTIONS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md and IMPLEMENTED.md, then swept every
tracked `.h`/`.cpp` in `engine/`, `game/`, `samples/`, `tests/`, the five `CMakeLists.txt`
files, `cmake/`, and the JSON content the loaders name — excluding `external/`. Four
conventions passes have genuinely landed and I confirmed each: there is not one `#include`
guard, not one `get_` accessor anywhere in the tree, not one `using namespace` in a header,
no non-lowercase source filename, and every enum but one is an `enum class` with snake_case
enumerators. What is left is not scattered leftovers; it is four coherent blocks that the
passes did not have a rule to catch. First, the two type-prefix families — `I*` (135
occurrences) and `M*` (323) — which CONVENTIONS bans by name and even uses `IGameObject` as
its worked counter-example. Second, three DirectXTK template files (`device_resources.*`,
`step_timer.h`, `throw_if_failed.h`) that were moved into `engine/` and wrapped in `namespace
artattack` without being translated at all: 229 `m_` members, PascalCase methods, `Get*`
accessors, `c_`-prefixed constants and a `interface` keyword-macro, all reachable through
`Application`'s public base list. Third, SCREAMING constants — over 300 declarations outside
`colour.h` and 301 inside it — which is the single most-repeated breach in the repository.
Fourth, an abbreviation layer (`num`, `rect`, `vel`, `proj`, `wep`, `col`, `pos`, `prev`,
`rotat`, `desc`) that no pass has touched, reaching the engine's public API in
`ViewportManager(int player_num)`.

The thing that surprised me most: `engine/render/viewport_manager.h:15-21` and
`engine/render/camera_tools.cpp:10-22` both carry a comment citing "CONVENTIONS, Constants
and enumerators" by name, and both then spell their constants in the SCREAMING form that the
very section they cite reserves for macros. The *placement* half of that rule was applied
deliberately and the *casing* half was not, in code written specifically to comply. That is
the shape of the whole remaining problem: the passes fixed what was mechanically greppable
and left what needed a judgement call.

### Themes

- Type prefixes survive in exactly the two places CONVENTIONS names them: the `I*` interface
  family (4 types, 135 references, 37 files) and the `M*` widget family (6 types, 323
  references, 14 files, plus 82 lowercased `mobject` spellings in function and variable names).
- Three DirectXTK sample files were relocated into `engine/` and namespaced but never
  translated, so a stranger opening the engine's own headers meets a second naming dialect —
  `m_`, PascalCase methods, `c_` constants, camelCase parameters — inside `namespace artattack`.
- SCREAMING_SNAKE is the codebase's default for constants (600+ declarations), which is the
  one form CONVENTIONS reserves exclusively so that a screaming name always signals
  preprocessor danger; CONVENTIONS' own example constant, `max_velocity`, appears in the code
  as `MAX_VELOCITY`.
- Namespace discipline is inverted: the engine claims the global namespace in exactly one file
  (`colour.h`), and 99 of 115 game and sample files claim it for everything they declare.
- The abbreviation allowlist (`dt`, `id`, `src`, `dst`, `min`, `max`) is the rule with the
  fewest observed effects; `player_num` alone appears 171 times and reaches six public engine
  signatures.
- Type-alias casing is unsettled in the newest code: `TextureHandle`/`FontHandle` sit beside
  `frame_handle`/`strip_handle`/`handle`, and `SoundBank::EffectHandle` is defined in terms of
  `Registry<...>::handle`.
- The rules with a mechanical test (pragma once, `get_`, trailing underscore, lowercase
  filenames, `using namespace` in headers) are at or near 100% compliance; the rules requiring
  a judgement call are at close to 0%.

#### Rename the four `I`-prefixed types; CONVENTIONS uses one of them as its counter-example

- **File:** `engine/core/i_game_object.h:23`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Never ("`I`, `C`, `F`, `U` or any other type prefix") and CONVENTIONS/Types

**What:** Four types in the tree carry the `I` prefix, one of which is spelled exactly as the
worked counter-example in CONVENTIONS/Types, and three of them name their files too.

**Evidence:**

    engine/core/i_game_object.h:23        class IGameObject
    engine/render/device_resources.h:17       interface IDeviceNotify
    game/objects/i_collision_game_object.h:7  class ICollisionGameObject : public artattack::IGameObject
    game/objects/i_paintable_game_object.h:9  class IPaintableGameObject

CONVENTIONS/Types, verbatim:

    - **No prefixes, ever.** Interfaces are just types — `GameObject`, not
      `IGameObject`; whether a type is abstract is visible in its header, not
      encoded in its name.

**Why it matters:** `IGameObject` is the first type a stranger meets — it is the interface
PHILOSOPHY/The object model names as the game's entry point ("`GameObject` (update, draw,
bounds)"), and `samples/minimal` is advertised as the template a new project copies. The four
names account for 135 occurrences across 37 files (`IGameObject` 24, `ICollisionGameObject`
99, `IDeviceNotify` 7, `IPaintableGameObject` 5), and three filenames (`i_game_object.h`,
`i_collision_game_object.h`, `i_paintable_game_object.h`) plus every include of them. The cost
only grows: every game type written against the engine before the rename inherits the wrong
name into its own header.

**Remedy:** Rename to `GameObject`, `DeviceNotify`, `CollisionGameObject`, `PaintableGameObject`
and rename the three headers to match; it is a mechanical rename that the compiler verifies
completely.

- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Never ("`I`, `C`, `F`, `U` or any other type prefix"), T12

**What:** The engine's entire widget vocabulary is prefixed `M`, a type prefix carrying no
information, and the prefix has leaked lowercased into function and variable names.

**Evidence:**

    engine/ui/widget.h:9    class MObject : public IGameObject
    engine/ui/widget.h:33   class MContainer final : public MObject
    engine/ui/widget.h:59   class MWidget : public MObject
    engine/ui/widget.h:76   class MTexture final : public MWidget, public TextureObject
    engine/ui/widget.h:114  class MText final : public MWidget, public Text
    engine/ui/widget.h:140  class MTextDropShadow final : public MWidget, public TextDropShadow

and, in the game:

- **Severity:** high

**What:** Three files carrying the DirectXTK sample naming scheme were moved into `engine/` and
wrapped in `namespace artattack` without being translated, so the engine's own headers contain
a second, foreign naming dialect that CONVENTIONS bans on five separate counts at once.

**Evidence:** `engine/render/device_resources.h`:

    47        void CreateDeviceResources();

    104       void GetHardwareAdapter(IDXGIAdapter1** ppAdapter);
    107       Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<IDXGIFactory2>               m_dxgiFactory;

`engine/core/step_timer.h`:

    44        uint64_t GetElapsedTicks() const noexcept { return m_elapsedTicks; }
    58        void SetFixedTimeStep(bool isFixedTimestep) noexcept { m_isFixedTimeStep = isFixedTimestep; }

`engine/core/throw_if_failed.h`:

**Why it matters:** Five distinct CONVENTIONS/Never entries are breached in these three files —
`m_` (229 occurrences repo-wide, all of them here: 116 in `device_resources.cpp`, 72 in
`step_timer.h`, 41 in `device_resources.h`), a `c_` type/constant prefix, `Get`-prefixed
accessors, `ppAdapter`'s Hungarian double-pointer prefix, and PascalCase functions. This is not

`engine/app/application.h:9` includes and whose `IDeviceNotify` `Application` publicly

scratch. `StepTimer` is instantiated as `Application::timer_` (`application.h:149`). A stranger

#### SCREAMING_SNAKE is the default constant form, which is the one form reserved for macros

- **File:** `game/objects/player_consts.h:19-50`, `engine/render/viewport_manager.h:15-21`, `engine/render/camera_tools.cpp:10-22`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Constants and enumerators, CONVENTIONS/Never ("SCREAMING constants — screaming means macro")

**What:** Over 300 constant declarations outside `colour.h` (plus 301 inside it) use
SCREAMING_SNAKE, including CONVENTIONS' own example constant spelled in the banned form, and
two engine files spell them that way in code whose comment cites the rule being broken.

**Evidence:** `game/objects/player_consts.h` — CONVENTIONS' example `max_velocity` appears as:

    25        const mattmath::Vector2F MAX_VELOCITY = { 800.0f, 1900.0f };
    29        constexpr float GRAVITY = 2000.0f;

`engine/render/viewport_manager.h`, whose comment cites the section it breaks:

    15        // How a split-screen divider is drawn. They live on the class that shapes
    16        // the dividers rather than in a `consts` namespace of strays (CONVENTIONS,
    17        // Constants and enumerators); a game asks for the rectangles and then for
    18        // these to fill them.
    19        static inline const std::string DIVIDER_SHEET_NAME = "sprite_sheet_1";
    20        static inline const std::string DIVIDER_FRAME_NAME = "pixel";
    21        static inline const mattmath::Colour DIVIDER_COLOUR = colour_consts::BLACK;
    52        static constexpr float DIVIDER_THICKNESS = 2.0f;

`engine/render/camera_tools.cpp`, the same pattern:

    12            // camera chases a player and configure nothing else (CONVENTIONS,
    13            // Constants and enumerators).
    14            constexpr float DEFAULT_BORDER_RATIO_LEFT = 0.4f;

and in MattMath's public header:

    engine/math/matt_math.h:45  constexpr float PI = 3.14159265358979323846f;
    engine/math/matt_math.h:47  constexpr float EPSILON = 0.0001f;
    engine/math/matt_math.h:496 static const Vector2F ZERO;
    engine/math/matt_math.h:498 static const Vector2F DIRECTION_RIGHT;

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS states the purpose explicitly — "SCREAMING_SNAKE is reserved
for macros alone, so that a screaming name always signals preprocessor danger and nothing else
ever does". With 600+ non-macro screaming names, that signal carries zero information today, so
a reader cannot tell `MAX_VELOCITY` (a `Vector2F`) from `NOMINMAX` (a real macro, defined at
`cmake/settings.cmake:19` and `game/pch.h:15`) without looking it up. The count by file is
`player_consts.h` 60, `main_menu.h` 54, `results_menu.h` 33, `pause_menu.h` 22, `end_menu.h` 20,
`interface_gameplay.h` 20, `weapon_consts.h` 18, `level.h` 16, `projectile_consts.h` 13, plus
19 in engine files and 5 in tests. The two files that cite the rule are the tell: this is a
half-applied convention, not an unexamined one.

**Remedy:** Lower-case them (`max_velocity`, `divider_thickness`, `pi`, `Vector2F::zero`), in

#### `engine/math/colour.h` is the one engine file that claims the global namespace

- **File:** `engine/math/colour.h:5-7`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Namespaces ("The engine never claims the global namespace"), CONVENTIONS/Constants and enumerators

**What:** MattMath's colour constants live in a global two-level namespace `colour_consts::html`
rather than in `mattmath`, and hold 301 SCREAMING constants — breaching the one-namespace rule,
the no-nesting rule, the no-global rule, the no-`consts`-namespace rule and the casing rule
simultaneously.

**Evidence:**

    engine/math/colour.h:5    namespace colour_consts
    engine/math/colour.h:6    {
    engine/math/colour.h:7        namespace html
    engine/math/colour.h:9            const std::string ALICE_BLUE = "f0f8ff";
    …
    engine/math/colour.h:159      const mattmath::Colour ALICE_BLUE = { html::ALICE_BLUE };

CONVENTIONS/Namespaces, verbatim: "everything in `MattMath` lives in `mattmath::`… No deeper
nesting, with one exception: `detail`… The engine never claims the global namespace."
CONVENTIONS' own example of a correct constant is `Colour::white`.

**Why it matters:** I checked every tracked engine source file: this is the *only* one that
declares nothing inside `artattack` or `mattmath`. It is reached by `colour_consts::` 251 times
across 35 files including `engine/ui/widget.h:85` and `engine/render/viewport_manager.h:21`, so
a game linking `MattMath` gets two unqualified global namespaces it did not ask for, and any
game with its own `html` or `colour_consts` collides. Separately, `const std::string` at
namespace scope has internal linkage, so all 148 `std::string` and 153 `Colour` objects are
constructed at static-init time in *every* translation unit that includes the header —
measurable startup and binary-size cost for a header most files pull in for one or two colours.

**Remedy:** Move the constants into `mattmath` as `Colour::white`-style static members or a
`mattmath::colour` namespace, lower-case them, and make them `constexpr` packed values rather
than runtime-parsed `std::string`s.

#### Game and sample code declares 99 of 115 files' worth of types in the global namespace

- **File:** `game/objects/level.h:53`, `samples/minimal/states/hello_state.h:16`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Namespaces ("Game code owns its own namespace")

**What:** No game or sample type is in a namespace; 99 of the 115 tracked `.h`/`.cpp` files
under `game/` and `samples/` declare no namespace at all, and the 16 that do declare only
`*_consts`.

**Evidence:**

    game/objects/level.h:53                  class Level
    game/objects/player.h:63                 class Player final : public artattack::MovingObject, public ICollisionGameObject,
    game/game_data.h:21                      class GameData

    samples/minimal/states/hello_state.h:16  class HelloState : public artattack::State

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS is explicit — "Game code owns its own namespace and never
reopens the engine's" — and the sample is the file ARCHITECTURE/A game project tells a stranger
to copy ("Starting a game is copying `samples/minimal/`, renaming the target, and owning
everything inside"). Whatever the sample does is what every downstream project will do, so this
propagates. Concretely: `game/objects/level.h` defines a global `Level`, `player.h` a global

#### Type aliases are spelled in three different cases, including inside one type's own header

- **File:** `engine/core/registry.h:53`, `engine/render/sprite_sheet.h:18-19`, `engine/math/matt_math.h:298`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS ("Types — classes, structs, enums, aliases | PascalCase")

**What:** Aliases are PascalCase in some of the newest engine code, snake_case in the rest of
it, and SCREAMING in MattMath — and one correct alias is defined in terms of an incorrect one.

**Evidence:** correct:

    engine/render/render_resources.h:38   using TextureHandle = Handle<ID3D11ShaderResourceView>;
    engine/render/render_resources.h:39   using FontHandle = Handle<DirectX::SpriteFont>;
    engine/assets/resource_loader.h:27    using LoadAsset = std::function<void(const std::string& directory,
    game/objects/stage.h:26               using StageList = std::vector<Stage>;

snake_case:

    engine/core/registry.h:53             using handle = Handle<Resource>;
    engine/render/sprite_sheet.h:18       using frame_handle = Handle<SpriteFrame>;
    engine/render/sprite_sheet.h:19       using strip_handle = Handle<AnimationStrip>;
    engine/assets/json_loader.cpp:24      using unique_file = std::unique_ptr<FILE, file_closer>;

DirectXTK members, or commented-out code lifted from Ericson's book. `Viewport` sits beside
`x`, `y`, `width`, `height` — bare snake_case in the same struct — so one type carries both
schemes four lines apart. `min` and `max` are both on the abbreviation allowlist, so
`min_depth`/`max_depth` is legal with no other change. `mattmath::Viewport` is a public MattMath
type; a game reading `view.minDepth` is reading the engine's convention as camelCase.

**Remedy:** Rename to `min_depth`/`max_depth` (54 occurrences, every one of them inside
`engine/math/matt_math.h` and `matt_math.cpp`).

#### Abbreviations off the closed allowlist reach the engine's public signatures

- **File:** `engine/render/viewport_manager.h:34-45`, `game/objects/projectile_details.h:10-14`, `engine/render/drawer.h:23`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Variables and members ("The allowlist of short forms is small and closed: `dt`, `id`, `src`, `dst`, `min`, `max`")

**What:** Ten or more abbreviations outside the closed allowlist are in current use, including
in six public `ViewportManager` signatures and three public `ProjectileDetails` fields.

**Evidence:** in the engine's public API:

    engine/render/viewport_manager.h:34   void apply_player_viewport(int player_num,
    engine/render/viewport_manager.h:40   mattmath::Viewport player_viewport(int player_num) const;
    engine/render/viewport_manager.h:44   mattmath::RectangleF camera_adjusted_player_viewport_rect(
    engine/render/drawer.h:23                 const mattmath::RectangleI& rec,
    engine/render/device_resources.h:97   void create_deferred_contexts(int num);
    engine/math/matt_math.h:228           RECT win_rect() const;
    engine/math/matt_math.h:413           DirectX::XMFLOAT2 xm_vector() const;
    engine/math/matt_math.h:796           DirectX::SimpleMath::Viewport sm_viewport() const;

in the game:

    game/objects/projectile_details.h:10      artattack::RotationOrigin rotat_origin = artattack::RotationOrigin::no_rotation;
    game/objects/projectile_details.h:14      mattmath::Vector2F col_rect_size = { 0.0f, 0.0f };
    game/objects/weapon_details.h:44          projectile_type proj_type = SPRAY;
    game/objects/weapon.h:148                 std::unique_ptr<ProjectileBuilder> proj_builder_ = nullptr;
    game/objects/weapon.h:171                 mattmath::Vector2F wep_rotation_origin_offset(
    game/objects/weapon_type.h:16             max_prim_wep = random_primary
    game/states/main_menu.h:82                const static std::string SPRAYER_DESC = "Fires a powerful stream…

**Why it matters:** The rule is stated as closed, and the census says it has had close to no
effect: `player_num` 171 occurrences, `rect`-as-a-segment 164, `col_` (for collision) 67,
`vel` 31, `prev` 39, `init` 40, `proj` 10, `wep` 9, `desc` 18, `rotat` 7. `rotat` is not even a
word, and `col` is ambiguous with "colour" in a codebase that spells that word out everywhere
else. Six of these are in `ViewportManager`'s public interface, which PHILOSOPHY names as
engine mechanism ("Renderer interface, cameras, viewports, split-screen"), so `player_num` is
part of what a stranger's game calls. `sm_`/`xm_` encode the destination type in the name,
which CONVENTIONS/Never rejects as "type information smuggled into a name". Separately,
`State::init()` (`engine/core/state.h:14`) and `Application::initialize()`
(`engine/app/application.h:82`) are the same verb abbreviated in one place and not the other, on
two types a new project uses side by side.

**Remedy:** Spell them out (`player_number`, `rectangle`, `collision_`, `velocity`,
`projectile_`, `weapon_`, `rotation_origin`, `description`, `init` → `initialize`); adopt or
extend the allowlist deliberately if `num`/`rect` are wanted, but do it in CONVENTIONS.

#### MattMath's collision functions carry SCREAMING acronyms in snake_case names

- **File:** `engine/math/ericson_math.h:85-136`, `engine/math/matt_math.h:83-84`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Types ("Acronyms are cased as words"), CONVENTIONS/Variables and members (abbreviations)

**What:** Six public math functions mix snake_case with uppercase acronyms and non-allowlisted
abbreviations in the same identifier.

**Evidence:**

    engine/math/matt_math.h:83        bool AABB_intersects(const Shape* other) const;
    engine/math/matt_math.h:84        bool AABB_intersects(const Shape& other) const;
    engine/math/ericson_math.h:85     bool test_circle_AABB(const mattmath::Circle& s,
    engine/math/ericson_math.h:91     float sq_dist_point_AABB(const mattmath::Point2F& p,
    engine/math/ericson_math.h:94     void closest_pt_point_AABB(const mattmath::Point2F& p,
    engine/math/ericson_math.h:114    bool test_segment_AABB(const mattmath::Point2F& p0,
    engine/math/ericson_math.h:136    void closest_pt_point_OBB(const mattmath::Point2F& p, const mattmath::OBB& b,

**Why it matters:** `Shape::AABB_intersects` is a virtual on the base of every collision shape
and is called from game code (`game/objects/player.cpp:172`,
`game/objects/paint_tile.cpp:66`, `game/objects/projectile_ball.cpp:60`), so it is public
engine surface. A single name here carries three breaches: an uppercase acronym where
CONVENTIONS says acronyms are cased as words, `pt` and `sq_dist` off the abbreviation
allowlist, and a snake_case identifier that starts with a capital. PHILOSOPHY/Collision says
these primitives "carry documented contracts" and are part of what T9 justifies hand-rolling —
a hand-rolled library is held to library standard, and its names are the first part of that.

**Remedy:** `aabb_intersects`, `test_circle_aabb`, `squared_distance_point_aabb`,
`closest_point_on_aabb`, `closest_point_on_obb`.

#### `interface` is a macro reading as a keyword, in an engine header

- **File:** `engine/render/device_resources.h:17`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** T12 ("no macro that reads like a keyword"), CONVENTIONS/Never (type prefix)

**What:** `IDeviceNotify` is declared with `interface`, which is a Microsoft macro from
`combaseapi.h`, not C++ — the exact construct T12 was written to forbid.

**Evidence:**

    engine/render/device_resources.h:16    // Provides an interface for an application that owns DeviceResources to be notified of the device being lost or created.
    engine/render/device_resources.h:17    interface IDeviceNotify
    engine/render/device_resources.h:18    {
    engine/render/device_resources.h:19        virtual void OnDeviceLost() = 0;
    engine/render/device_resources.h:20        virtual void OnDeviceRestored() = 0;

T12, verbatim: "No macro that reads like a keyword… the line is that a macro may not invent
syntax, hide control flow, or change the meaning of a name that already had one."

**Why it matters:** `interface` expands to `struct` (with `__declspec(novtable)` under some
SDK configurations), which changes the default access and vtable emission of the type — so the
declaration means something a reader cannot determine from the source, which is T12's stated
objection to Unreal. `engine/app/application.h:71` publicly inherits this type
(`class Application : public IDeviceNotify, public StateContext`), so the macro is load-bearing
in the engine's shell. It also compiles only because `<Windows.h>` is included first at
`device_resources.h:7` — an include-order dependency invisible at the declaration.

**Remedy:** Write `struct` (or `class` with `public:`), and rename to `DeviceNotify` per the
`I`-prefix finding.

#### Seven test namespaces are PascalCase

- **File:** `tests/math/math_tests.cpp:9-205`, `tests/core/registry_tests.cpp:23`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS ("Namespaces | one lowercase word")

**What:** Every namespace declared under `tests/` is PascalCase and multi-word, against a rule
that says one lowercase word.

**Evidence:**

    tests/math/math_tests.cpp:9                       namespace MathTestConstants
    tests/math/math_tests.cpp:18                      namespace EricsonMathTests
    tests/math/math_tests.cpp:205                     namespace MattMathTests
    tests/math/collision_tools_tests.cpp:15           namespace CollisionToolsTests
    tests/core/name_table_tests.cpp:16                namespace NameTableTests
    tests/core/registry_tests.cpp:23                  namespace RegistryTests
    tests/assets/asset_manifest_loader_tests.cpp:57   namespace AssetManifestLoaderTests

`MathTestConstants` additionally holds three SCREAMING constants and is then opened globally:

    tests/math/math_tests.cpp:11    constexpr float EPSILON_F = 0.000001f;
    tests/math/math_tests.cpp:16    using namespace MathTestConstants;

**Why it matters:** PHILOSOPHY/Tests and toolchain makes tests part of the shipped engine ("A
new public primitive ships with behavioural tests in the same commit"), so test code is code a
stranger reads to learn the API. A PascalCase namespace reads as a type at the point of use.
`math_tests.cpp` is also 1013 lines covering two subjects, against CONVENTIONS/Files "Tests
are named for their subject: `vector2_tests.cpp`" — the file is named for the module and holds
`EricsonMathTests` (line 18) and `MattMathTests` (line 205) side by side.

**Remedy:** Drop the namespaces (doctest's `TEST_SUITE` already scopes the cases) or lower-case
them, and split `math_tests.cpp` by subject.

#### Four headers hold several primary types, or none matching their filename

- **File:** `engine/math/matt_math.h:69-1149`, `engine/ui/widget.h:9-140`, `game/states/game_states.h:13-45`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Files ("named for the primary type they hold", "One primary type per header")

**What:** Four headers break the file-to-type correspondence that makes an include path
predictable: one holds twenty types, one holds six none of which share its name, one holds two
unrelated states, and one names itself after its second type.

**Evidence:** `engine/math/matt_math.h` (1150 lines) declares, among others:

    69    struct Shape
    185   struct RectangleF : public Shape
    336   struct Vector : Matrix<T>
    399   struct Vector2F
    594   struct Colour
    775   struct Viewport
    816   struct Circle : public Shape
    856   struct Triangle : public Shape
    933   struct Quad : public Shape
    995   struct Segment
    1020  struct Camera
    1060  struct RectangleRotated : public Shape

`engine/ui/widget.h` holds `MObject`, `MContainer`, `MWidget`, `MTexture`, `MText`,
`MTextDropShadow` and no type named `Widget`. `game/states/game_states.h:13` and `:45` hold
`GameMenu` and `GameLevel`. `game/objects/i_paintable_game_object.h:3` declares `PaintTotal`
before `IPaintableGameObject` at `:9`.

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS/Files states the payoff — `#include "engine/render/renderer.h"`
tells you what you are getting — and it does not hold here: a reader wanting `Camera` has to
know it lives in `matt_math.h`, and `matt_math.h` is pulled in by essentially every engine
header, so `Colour`, `Viewport` and twenty other types arrive with the vector maths. That is
also the compile-time cost PHILOSOPHY/Tests and toolchain calls a maintained property ("light
headers, disciplined includes"). `widget.h`'s six types are the case the same section allows
partially — "Small types that exist only to serve it may ride along" — but `MTexture`, `MText`
and `MTextDropShadow` are three independent widgets, not helpers.

**Remedy:** Split `matt_math.h` into per-type headers (`vector2.h`, `rectangle.h`, `camera.h`,
`colour.h`, `viewport.h`, `shape.h`), give each widget its own header, and split
`game_states.h`.

#### Wave asset names are PascalCase, against the snake_case data rule

- **File:** `game/content/sounds/sound_bank_1.json:4-27`, `game/states/main_menu.h:73-79`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Data ("JSON keys, asset names, registry keys… snake_case")

**What:** The sound bank's wave names use four different casing schemes in one array, and those
names are then hardcoded into game headers as string constants.

**Evidence:**

    game/content/sounds/sound_bank_1.json:4     "BowlingBallRoll",
    game/content/sounds/sound_bank_1.json:5     "caramelldansen",
    game/content/sounds/sound_bank_1.json:6     "CartoonBoing",
    game/content/sounds/sound_bank_1.json:18    "Top_Of_The_Morning",
    game/content/sounds/sound_bank_1.json:19    "UI_Clicks01",
    game/content/sounds/sound_bank_1.json:22    "UIerror2",

and the code that names them:

    game/states/main_menu.h:74    const std::string DIRECTION_SOUND = "UI_Clicks14";
    game/states/main_menu.h:77    const std::string ERROR_SOUND = "UIerror2";
    game/states/main_menu.h:79    const std::string MUSIC = "Top_Of_The_Morning";

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS/Data gives the reason — "so a definition reads continuously from
file to loader" — and it does not here: every other asset name in the project is snake_case
(`sprite_sheet_1`, `gill_sans_mt_bold_24`, `king_of_the_hill`, and all 24 `sound_effect_instances`
entries in the same file, e.g. `"name": "sprayer_a0"` at line 33). These names are resolved by
`SoundBank`'s name table, so a casing slip is a load-time throw (T6) — correct behaviour, but
the throw is avoidable. Note the constraint: wave names come from the `.xwb` built by
`XWBTool.exe` from source filenames, so renaming means rebuilding the bank, not editing JSON.

**Remedy:** Rename the source waves to snake_case and rebuild `sound_bank_1.xwb`; the JSON and
the three constants follow.

#### Content directories with spaces and non-snake_case names are shipped beside the exe

- **File:** `game/CMakeLists.txt:91-95`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Files ("Files and directories | `snake_case`")

**What:** Four tracked content paths use spaces and free-form names, and the build copies their
parent directories wholesale into the output directory.

**Evidence:** the tracked paths:

    game/content/fonts/unuseed fonts/          (21 files)
    game/content/textures/old textures/        (~90 files)
    game/content/textures/new player textures/ (13 files)
    game/content/sounds/sound list.txt

and the build rule that ships them:

    game/CMakeLists.txt:91   foreach(content_dir textures levels fonts sounds)
    game/CMakeLists.txt:92       add_custom_command(TARGET artattack_content POST_BUILD
    game/CMakeLists.txt:93           COMMAND "${CMAKE_COMMAND}" -E copy_directory_if_different
    game/CMakeLists.txt:94               "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/content/${content_dir}"
    game/CMakeLists.txt:95               "$<TARGET_FILE_DIR:ArtAttackGame>/${content_dir}"

**Why it matters:** These are the only tracked paths in the repository outside `external/` that
contain a space or a capital, so the "snake_case files and directories" rule holds everywhere
except here. The `copy_directory_if_different` above copies the whole of `textures/` and

#### `Registry::get` and `NameTable::get` are the only lookups not named for their noun

- **File:** `engine/core/registry.h:98`, `engine/core/name_table.h:66`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Functions ("Accessors are the noun, bare")

**What:** The two newest core types settled on `get(handle)` for their per-frame read, while
every other lookup in the engine is named for the thing it returns — and CONVENTIONS bans
`get_` but says nothing about bare `get`.

**Evidence:**

    engine/core/registry.h:98      Resource* get(handle resource_handle) const
    engine/core/registry.h:117     Resource* get(const std::string& name) const
    engine/core/name_table.h:66    const Element& get(Handle<Element> element_handle) const

against the same operation, named the other way, one file over:

    engine/render/render_resources.h:60   ID3D11ShaderResourceView* texture(TextureHandle texture) const;
    engine/render/render_resources.h:61   DirectX::SpriteFont* sprite_font(FontHandle font) const;
    engine/render/sprite_sheet.h:37       const SpriteFrame& sprite_frame(frame_handle frame) const;

**Why it matters:** A pass has just removed every `get_` in the tree, so this is the one shape
of the rule left unsettled, and it is unsettled in the two types most likely to be copied by a
game writing its own registry. CONVENTIONS/Never lists "`get_` on accessors" and the Functions
section says accessors are "the noun, bare", which reads as banning bare `get` too — but it does
not say so, and `Registry` is generic so it has no noun to use. This is as much a gap in the
document as in the code.

**Remedy:** Either amend CONVENTIONS to state that a generic container's accessor may be `get`,
or rename these to `resource(handle)` / `element(handle)`.

- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** "-" (filed against CONVENTIONS, which is silent here)

**What:** CMake targets are PascalCase in some places and snake_case in others, and CONVENTIONS
has no entry for build-target names, so there is nothing to check a new target against.

**Evidence:**

    CMakeLists.txt:6                  project(ArtAttack LANGUAGES CXX RC)
    engine/CMakeLists.txt:12          add_library(ArtAttackEngine STATIC
    engine/math/CMakeLists.txt:9      add_library(MattMath STATIC

<a id="g-sweep-files-includes"></a>

## sweep-files-includes — CONVENTIONS: files, includes, headers

*Group `sweep-files-includes` · 19 findings (2 high, 14 medium, 3 low) · source `review2/raw/sweep-files-includes.md`, cross-cutting sweep — no separate verifier, reported as written.*

I read CONVENTIONS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md and PHILOSOPHY.md, then every `#include` line in
`engine/`, `game/`, `samples/` and `tests/` (208 tracked `.h`/`.cpp` files, `external/`
excluded), every `CMakeLists.txt`, `CMakePresets.json`, `vcpkg.json`, `.gitignore` and the
generated `out/build/x64-debug/build.ninja` — the last only as read-only evidence for what
the build actually passes to the compiler. The conventions passes landed cleanly on the
mechanical things: every header has `#pragma once`, there are no include guards, no
`using namespace` in any header, every quoted project include is written from the repository
root, and every engine `.cpp` opens with its own header. What has *not* landed is the part
that is structural rather than textual. The include wall the architecture document promises
does not exist — both static libraries put the repository root on their **PUBLIC** include
path, so `math` can include `game/` and nothing says no. Three files are still the Microsoft
Direct3D game template with their original naming dialect, one of them using the Windows SDK's
`interface` macro as if it were a keyword. Two headers carry twenty and six public types
respectively, and one 466-line header named `colour.h` contains no type at all — but does
contain five of the paint-shooter's team colours, inside `engine/math/`. The game's PCH is
force-included into all 46 of its translation units, thirteen of its nineteen DirectXTK
headers are unused, and the whole DirectXTK 3D stack is among them, in an engine whose
non-goals list starts with "3D". What surprised me most is how good the engine side's
own-header-first discipline is compared to everything downstream of it: the rules were
applied file by file, but never to the seams between files.

### Themes

- The walls the documents describe as compile-time are conventions in practice: one include
  root serves every target, so `ARCHITECTURE`'s "an engine file including a game header fails
  to compile" is currently false, and only the absence of such an include keeps it honest.
- Header size correlates with a type that never split, exactly as CONVENTIONS predicts:
  `matt_math.h` (20 types), `widget.h` (6), `main_menu.h` (9 page classes), each with a `.cpp`
  that grew to match.
- Filenames promise types that are somewhere else: `colour.h` holds no `Colour`, `widget.h`
  holds no `Widget`, `matt_math.h` holds no `MattMath`, `game_states.h` holds two states.
- Third-party and vendored code is not marked as such: three Microsoft template files live
  inside `engine/` speaking `m_`, `Get`, `c_` and `interface`, indistinguishable from
  hand-written engine code to a stranger.
- Constants live in headers as namespace-scope `const std::string` and `const Colour` objects
  with internal linkage, so they are duplicated into every translation unit that reaches them
  — and several of them are game content (weapon descriptions, team colours) rather than code.
- Include *order* fails where the file was written before the rule: eleven headers put the
  standard library or an external dependency ahead of project headers, and the game's PCH puts
  everything ahead of everything.
- The test tree does not exercise the shape the architecture describes: no test target links
  `ArtAttackEngine`, and the one that needs engine code compiles its sources a second time with
  a different set of preprocessor definitions.

---

#### Give each library its own include root; the engine/game wall does not currently exist

- **File:** `engine/CMakeLists.txt:46-49`, `engine/math/CMakeLists.txt:14`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** ARCHITECTURE/Modules, T5 (compile-time over run-time)

**What:** Both static libraries add the repository root as a **PUBLIC** include directory, so
`#include "game/objects/collision_object_type.h"` from an engine or math source compiles, and
for the game's header-only types links as well — the failure ARCHITECTURE.md promises does not
happen.

**Evidence:**

    engine/CMakeLists.txt:46
    target_include_directories(ArtAttackEngine PUBLIC
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}"
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/external/rapidjson/include"
    )

    engine/math/CMakeLists.txt:14
    target_include_directories(MattMath PUBLIC "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}")

against

    docs/design/ARCHITECTURE.md:16
    An arrow reads "links against"; no arrow ever points the other way — an
    engine file including a game header fails to compile, and that is the
    feature (T5).

**Why it matters:** `${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}` is `C:/VSProjects/ArtAttack`, and `game/` sits under
it, so the game's headers are on the include path of every engine and math translation unit.
I grepped: no engine or sample file includes `game/` today, so nothing is broken right now —
the wall is simply not load-bearing. It is also worse than "compiles but won't link" for the
files that matter most: `game/objects/collision_object_type.h`, `player_team.h`,
`weapon_type.h` and `level_mode.h` are header-only enums with `inline` helpers, so an engine
file that reached for one would compile *and* link with no diagnostic at all. That is the exact
shape of outstanding finding #13 (a game enum in the collision interface), and the mechanism
that would have stopped it re-happening is the one that is missing. `samples/minimal`'s own
build file claims the property too ("It links ArtAttackEngine and nothing from `game/`, so if a
mechanism ever drifts back into the paint-shooter, this stops building",
`samples/minimal/CMakeLists.txt:15-16`) and inherits the same open door via the engine's PUBLIC
include directory.

**Remedy:** Give each library an include root that contains only what it may see — e.g. install
`engine/` headers under a per-target interface directory, or keep the root but add a CI/CMake
check that no file under `engine/` contains `#include "game/`.

#### Split `matt_math.h`; twenty public types in one header, and `<d3d11.h>` inside the library that depends on nothing

- **File:** `engine/math/matt_math.h:1-1150` (types at 69, 185, 301, 336, 351, 399, 516, 575, 594, 663, 692, 758, 775, 816, 856, 908, 933, 995, 1020, 1060); `engine/math/matt_math.cpp:1-4594`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Files (one primary type per header; no huge files), ARCHITECTURE/Modules

**What:** `matt_math.h` declares twenty public types in 1150 lines under a filename that names
none of them, and includes `<d3d11.h>` so that the module ARCHITECTURE lists as depending on
*nothing* makes the graphics API a compile-time dependency of every file that touches a
`Vector2F`.

**Evidence:**

    engine/math/matt_math.h:1
    #pragma once

    #include "SimpleMath.h"
    #include "engine/math/shape_type.h"
    #include <d3d11.h>

    engine/math/matt_math.h:775
    	struct Viewport
    	{
    	public:
    ...
    engine/math/matt_math.h:794
    		Viewport(const D3D11_VIEWPORT& viewport);

    		DirectX::SimpleMath::Viewport sm_viewport() const;
    		D3D11_VIEWPORT d3d_viewport() const;
    		const D3D11_VIEWPORT* d3d_viewport_ptr() const;

against

    docs/design/ARCHITECTURE.md:129
    | `math` | nothing |

**Why it matters:** Three concrete costs. (1) A stranger opening the engine's math library
meets a 1150-line header holding `Shape`, `RectangleF`, `Matrix`, `Vector`, `Vector2I`,
`Vector2F`, `RectangleI`, `Vector4F`, `Colour`, `Vector3F`, `MatrixF`, `Matrix3x3F`,
`Viewport`, `Circle`, `Triangle`, `TriangleRightAxisAligned`, `Quad`, `Segment`, `Camera` and
`RectangleRotated`, with a 4594-line `.cpp` behind it — there is no smaller unit to read.
(2) Every one of the 157 files (of 208) that includes it, directly or transitively, compiles
`<d3d11.h>` and DirectXTK's `SimpleMath.h`, which is the opposite of "compile speed is a
maintained property — light headers, disciplined includes" (PHILOSOPHY, Tests and toolchain).
(3) `mattmath::Viewport` is not a math type at all: its reason to exist is converting to and
from `D3D11_VIEWPORT`, so a render concept is what pins the graphics API into `math`.
Note the include order is also inverted here — `SimpleMath.h` (external) precedes
`engine/math/shape_type.h` (project).

**Remedy:** Move `Viewport` (and its D3D conversions) into `engine/render/`, then split the
remaining types one primary type per header — `vector2f.h`, `rectangle_f.h`, `circle.h` — which
is also what lets `tests/math/` be named for its subjects.

#### Stop force-including the game PCH; no game header's self-containment is checked by the build

- **File:** `game/CMakeLists.txt:72`, `game/pch.h:1-80`, and the first line of all 46 game `.cpp` files
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Files (include order: own header first)

**What:** `target_precompile_headers` makes CMake force-include `game/pch.h` (via `/FI`) ahead
of everything in every `ArtAttackGame` translation unit, so the convention's stated purpose —
"own header first — proving every header compiles on its own" — cannot hold for any header in
`game/`; each `.cpp` then also includes the PCH explicitly, which is redundant.

**Evidence:**

    game/CMakeLists.txt:72
    target_precompile_headers(ArtAttackGame PRIVATE pch.h)

    out/build/x64-debug/build.ninja:635 (generated; read-only evidence)
      FLAGS = ... /FIC:/VSProjects/ArtAttack/out/build/x64-debug/game/CMakeFiles/ArtAttackGame.dir/cmake_pch.hxx

    out/build/x64-debug/game/CMakeFiles/ArtAttackGame.dir/cmake_pch.hxx (generated)
    #include "C:/VSProjects/ArtAttack/game/pch.h"

    game/objects/player.cpp:1
    #include "game/pch.h"
    #include "game/objects/player.h"

**Why it matters:** With `<Windows.h>`, 19 DirectXTK headers and 11 standard headers already in
scope before line 1 of any game header, a header that forgets `<vector>` or `<memory>` still
compiles. That is not hypothetical bookkeeping: `game/objects/level.h`, `player.h`, `weapon.h`,
`game_data.h`, `structure_paintable.h`, `states/main_menu.h`, `states/pause_menu.h` and
`states/results_menu.h` all name `std::string`, `std::vector` or `std::unique_ptr` with no
standard `#include` of their own. The day the paint-shooter is used the way ARCHITECTURE
describes a project being started — copied, renamed, owned — whichever headers go with it stop
compiling, and the build that was supposed to be the cheapest reviewer said nothing.

**Remedy:** Drop the explicit `#include "game/pch.h"` from every `.cpp` (CMake already injects
it), and add a build option or a periodic no-PCH configuration so header self-containment is
actually compiled at least once.

- **File:** `game/pch.h:59-77`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Tests and toolchain (compile speed is a maintained property), Non-goals (3D)

**What:** The game's precompiled header pulls in DirectXTK's model, geometric-primitive,
effects, primitive-batch, vertex-type, post-process, keyboard, mouse, screen-grab,
graphics-memory, buffer-helper and both texture-loader headers, none of which any game source
uses.

    #include "DDSTextureLoader.h"
    #include "DirectXHelpers.h"
    #include "Effects.h"

    #include "SpriteFont.h"

`Model`, `GeometricPrimitive`, `PostProcess`, `BasicEffect`/`IEffect`/`EffectFactory`,
`PrimitiveBatch`, `VertexPosition*`, `GraphicsMemory`, `Keyboard`, `Mouse`, `ScreenGrab`,

(`:31`), which `cmake/settings.cmake:19-20` already passes to every target — the policy now

#### `engine/math/colour.h` is a 466-line data table named for a type it does not contain

- **File:** `engine/math/colour.h:1-466`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Files (named for the primary type they hold), CONVENTIONS/Constants, T7

**What:** A header named `colour.h` declares no type — `mattmath::Colour` is at
`engine/math/matt_math.h:594` — and instead holds 149 `const std::string` HTML codes, 154
`const mattmath::Colour` objects and a 150-branch string-comparison function, all at namespace
scope with internal linkage.

**Evidence:**

    engine/math/colour.h:5
    namespace colour_consts
    {
    	namespace html
    	{
    		const std::string ALICE_BLUE = "f0f8ff";
    ...
    engine/math/colour.h:159
    	const mattmath::Colour ALICE_BLUE = { html::ALICE_BLUE };
    ...
    engine/math/colour.h:314
    	inline mattmath::Colour colour_from_name(const std::string& name)
    	{
    		if (name == "ALICE_BLUE") return colour_consts::ALICE_BLUE;

**Why it matters:** Three separate costs, all falling on every translation unit that reaches
it — 118 of the 208 sources in the tree, because `engine/render/draw_object.h:3` includes it and
`draw_object.h` is the base of `SpriteSheetObject`, `TextObject`, `TextureObject`, `Text`,
`TextDropShadow` and therefore every widget and every drawable in `game/`. (1) A `const` object
at namespace scope has internal linkage, so each of those TUs gets its own copy of ~300 objects
and its own dynamic initialiser for them; the linker cannot merge them. (2) Each `Colour` is
constructed by *parsing a hex string at run time*, at static-init, once per TU. (3) A reader
looking for the `Colour` type opens `colour.h` and finds a colour-name table — the filename
convention exists precisely to stop that. Separately, `colour_consts` is a second global
namespace in a library CONVENTIONS says holds one (`mattmath::`), and the engine "never claims
the global namespace".

**Remedy:** Rename the file for what it is (`colour_names.h`), make the constants `constexpr`
or `inline constexpr` so there is one copy, and construct the `Colour`s from literal channel
values rather than parsed strings.
