#### Make the engine/game include wall a real compile error, or stop documenting it as one

- **File:** `engine/CMakeLists.txt:46-49`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** T5 (also ARCHITECTURE/The targets, CONVENTIONS/Files)

**What:** Both static libraries put the repository root on a `PUBLIC` include path, so an engine
or math translation unit can `#include "game/..."` and it compiles — the wall the documents
promise three separate times does not exist.

**Evidence:**

    engine/CMakeLists.txt:46
    target_include_directories(ArtAttackEngine PUBLIC
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}"
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/external/rapidjson/include"
    )

    engine/math/CMakeLists.txt:14
    target_include_directories(MattMath PUBLIC "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}")

The three claims it is supposed to back:

    PHILOSOPHY.md:272   `game/…` — and every file picks its home the day it is created. An engine
    PHILOSOPHY.md:273   file including a game header fails to compile; that is the feature (T5).

    ARCHITECTURE.md:14  An arrow reads "links against"; no arrow ever points the other way — an
    ARCHITECTURE.md:15  engine file including a game header fails to compile, and that is the
    ARCHITECTURE.md:16  feature (T5).

    CONVENTIONS.md:112  file including `"game/..."` is thereby visible at a glance — and fails
    CONVENTIONS.md:113  to build (see ARCHITECTURE.md).

**Why it matters:** `PUBLIC` include directories apply to the target's own sources as well as its
consumers, so `${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}` is on the include path when `engine/collision/partitioner.cpp`
is compiled. `game/objects/player_team.h` is a self-contained eight-line `enum class` header with no
includes of its own; adding `#include "game/objects/player_team.h"` to any engine `.cpp` compiles
clean today. Header-only game code used from the engine would also *link* clean in `ArtAttackGame`,
because the game's objects are in the same final image; the first symptom would be a link failure in
`ArtAttackSample` only, and only for whichever object files the static-library linker happened to
pull in. I confirmed no such include exists yet — but the guarantee a reviewer and a future
contributor are told to rely on is a comment, not a mechanism, and the first breach will not
announce itself.

**Remedy:** Give the engine an include root that does not contain `game/` (e.g. stage engine headers
into a generated `include/` tree, or move the game out from under `CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR`), or add a
CMake/CI check that greps engine and math sources for `#include "game/`.

---

#### Add `[[nodiscard]]` — it is named in PHILOSOPHY and used zero times in the repository

- **File:** `engine/math/matt_math.h:450-456`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T5 (PHILOSOPHY/Tests and toolchain)

**What:** `[[nodiscard]]` does not appear once in `engine/`, `game/`, `samples/` or `tests/`,
even on the value-returning half of mutator/query pairs where discarding the result is a
silent no-op.

**Evidence:**

    $ grep -rn "nodiscard" --include=*.h --include=*.cpp engine game samples tests | wc -l
    0

The sharpest sites — two pairs where the two spellings differ by four characters and one of
them does nothing if the result is dropped:

    engine/math/matt_math.h:450
        Vector2F normalized() const;
        void normalize();
    engine/math/matt_math.h:455
        void clamp(const Vector2F& min, const Vector2F& max);
        Vector2F clamped(const Vector2F& min, const Vector2F& max) const;

and the load-bearing queries: `Handle::valid()`/`index()` (`engine/core/handle.h:30-31`),
`Registry::resolve()`/`get()`/`contains()` (`engine/core/registry.h:84,98,117,125`),
`NameTable::resolve()`/`get()`/`contains()` (`engine/core/name_table.h:53,66,77`),
`Partitioner::partition()` (`engine/collision/partitioner.h:12-16`),
`Drawer::calculate_draw_rectangle()`/`calculate_sprite_origin()` (`engine/render/drawer.h:22-31`),
`IGameObject::bounds()` (`engine/core/i_game_object.h:61`), and every `Shape::intersects()`.

**Why it matters:** PHILOSOPHY line 450 lists `[[nodiscard]]` beside `const` and `noexcept` as
information "the compiler enforces (T5)". `v.normalized();` and `v.clamped(lo, hi);` are both
well-formed statements that compile without a single warning at `/W4 /WX` and do nothing — the
exact class of bug this attribute exists to make impossible. I found no live instance, so this is
preventive, but the engine is being handed to strangers who will meet `normalize` and `normalized`
in the same header and pick wrong.

**Remedy:** Mark the pure queries `[[nodiscard]]`, starting with the `-ed` twins in `matt_math.h`
and the `Handle`/`Registry`/`NameTable` accessors that a game touches every frame.

#### The float and integer math types convert into each other implicitly and lossily

- **File:** `engine/math/matt_math.h:359,406,410,532`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T5

**What:** `Vector2F`↔`Vector2I` and `RectangleF`→`RectangleI` are all non-`explicit` converting
constructors, so the distinction the two types exist to express is not enforced at any call site.

**Evidence:**

    engine/math/matt_math.h:359    Vector2I(const mattmath::Vector2F& vector);
    engine/math/matt_math.h:406    Vector2F(float f);
    engine/math/matt_math.h:410    Vector2F(const mattmath::Vector2I& vector);
    engine/math/matt_math.h:528    RectangleI(const mattmath::Vector2F& position,
    engine/math/matt_math.h:529        const mattmath::Vector2F& size);
    engine/math/matt_math.h:532    RectangleI(mattmath::RectangleF rectangle);

**Why it matters:** `SpriteSheet::draw` takes destination rectangles only as `RectangleI`
(`engine/render/sprite_sheet.h:61`), and the engine's own call sites convert explicitly —
`camera.calculate_view_rectangle(destination_rectangle).rectangle_i()`
(`engine/render/texture_object.cpp:105`, `engine/render/animation_object.cpp:91`). The implicit
constructor at line 532 makes that `.rectangle_i()` optional: a game passing a world-space
`RectangleF` straight to `draw` compiles and silently truncates every sub-pixel coordinate, with
no diagnostic at `/W4 /WX`. `Vector2F(float)` broadcasts a scalar, so `v.dot(2.0f)` and any
function taking a `Vector2F` called with a bare float also compile. Both directions of
`Vector2F`↔`Vector2I` being implicit means the type pair carries no information the compiler will
act on — which is the same argument CONVENTIONS makes against Hungarian notation, inverted.

**Remedy:** Make every single-argument constructor in `matt_math.h` `explicit` except the widening
`Vector2I`→`Vector2F` one, and keep the named `.rectangle_i()` / `.vector_i()` conversions as the
only spelling for the lossy direction.

#### `Camera` accepts a `Viewport` implicitly, so the two are interchangeable on every draw call

- **File:** `engine/math/matt_math.h:1029`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T5

**What:** `Camera(const Viewport&, float scale = 1.0f)` is not `explicit`, so a `Viewport` converts
silently wherever the engine's central `draw(sprite_batch, camera)` signature is expected — and the
conversion throws away everything but the viewport's top-left corner.

**Evidence:**

    engine/math/matt_math.h:1029
        Camera(const mattmath::Viewport& viewport, float scale = 1.0f);

    engine/math/matt_math.cpp:4093
    Camera::Camera(const Viewport& viewport, float scale)
    {
        this->translation.x = viewport.x;
        this->translation.y = viewport.y;
        this->scale = scale;
    }

The interface it leaks into:

    engine/core/i_game_object.h:41
        virtual void draw(DirectX::SpriteBatch* sprite_batch,
            const mattmath::Camera& camera) const = 0;

**Why it matters:** `IGameObject::draw` is the one interface every game object in every game on
this engine implements, and it takes a `Camera&`. Passing a `Viewport` — an easy mistake, since
both are in scope together throughout `menu_page.cpp` and `level.cpp` and the viewport is what
`ViewportManager` hands you — compiles, and produces a camera translated to the viewport's screen
origin at scale 1. `MObject` compounds this: it declares a non-virtual
`draw(SpriteBatch*, const Viewport&)` (`engine/ui/widget.h:16-17`) whose whole body is
`this->draw(sprite_batch, Camera(viewport));` (`engine/ui/widget.cpp:21`), and every derived widget
(`MContainer`, `MTexture`, `MText`, `MTextDropShadow`) declares
`draw(SpriteBatch*, const Camera&) const override` with no `using MObject::draw;`, which hides it.
So `MTexture t; t.draw(batch, viewport);` resolves through the implicit conversion instead of the
overload written for it, and reads as if the overload were being used.

**Remedy:** Mark the constructor `explicit` and delete the redundant `MObject::draw(SpriteBatch*,
const Viewport&)` overload, or add `using MObject::draw;` to the derived widgets so it is visible
rather than reachable by accident.

#### `std::exception("message")` is an MSVC extension, used 47 times including inside MattMath

- **File:** `engine/render/animation_strip.cpp:22`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** boundary
- **Tenet:** T12 (also ARCHITECTURE/Targets and layout)

**What:** 47 throw sites construct `std::exception` with a message string — a constructor that does
not exist in standard C++ and is unique to Microsoft's library — while the newer engine code
correctly uses `std::runtime_error`.

**Evidence:**

    engine/render/animation_strip.cpp:20
        if (frame_index < 0 || frame_index >= this->frame_count_)
        {
            throw std::exception("frame_index out of range");
        }

    engine/render/viewport_manager.cpp:139
                throw std::exception("Invalid screen layout");

    $ grep -rn 'std::exception("' --include=*.cpp --include=*.h engine game samples tests | wc -l
    47

Distribution: `engine/math/ericson_math.cpp` (2, commented), `engine/render/` (4),
`game/` (41). The engine's own newer code does it correctly —
`engine/core/thread_pool.cpp:13` `throw std::runtime_error("Failed to create thread pool.")`,
`engine/app/application.cpp:93`, `game/objects/level.cpp:745`.

**Why it matters:** `std::exception` has no `const char*` constructor in ISO C++; this is
`<vcruntime_exception.h>`. Every one of these lines is a hard compile error on clang, gcc, or MSVC
with a conforming standard library, and `/permissive-` does not flag it because it is a library
extension, not a language one. ARCHITECTURE commits to "a second platform is an addition, not a
rewrite" and to platform code living only in `render/d3d11/` and `input/xinput/` — this is
platform-specific code in `engine/render/animation_strip.cpp` and in the shared math layer. It is
also two idioms for the same job in one library, which is what a stranger has to pick between.

**Remedy:** Replace all 47 with `std::runtime_error` / `std::out_of_range`, which is what the newer
engine code already uses.

#### `Application::sprite_batches() const` const_casts its own member to keep the `const` promise

- **File:** `engine/app/application.cpp:429-432`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T5

**What:** A `const` accessor strips `const` off a member and hands out a mutable pointer to it,
which is the marker that the `const` on the engine's whole service-accessor block carries no
information.

**Evidence:**

    engine/app/application.cpp:429
    std::vector<SpriteBatch*>* Application::sprite_batches() const
    {
        return const_cast<std::vector<SpriteBatch*>*>(&this->sprite_batch_ptrs_);
    }

The declaration it is satisfying, and the member it lies about:

    engine/app/application.h:129     std::vector<DirectX::SpriteBatch*>* sprite_batches() const;
    engine/app/application.h:163     std::vector<DirectX::SpriteBatch*> sprite_batch_ptrs_;

**Why it matters:** This is one of only two `const_cast` sites in the repository, and unlike the
other one (`game/game_data.cpp:68`, which is documented as transitional and named as such) it exists
purely so a signature can say `const` while returning a handle to mutable state. Every accessor in
that block — `device_resources()`, `render_resources()`, `thread_pool()`, `common_states()` — is
`const` and returns a non-const pointer, so `const Application&` grants full write access to the
entire engine. A reader who trusts `const` here will conclude a `const Application&` is safe to share
across the render workers; it is not, and the compiler will not tell them.

**Remedy:** Return `const std::vector<SpriteBatch*>&` (the pointers themselves are what callers
mutate through, not the vector), or drop `const` from the accessors that hand out mutable services
so the signature says what it means.

#### `StateContext::update()` and `draw()` are `const` and mutate the entire game

- **File:** `engine/core/state_context.cpp:5-20`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T5 (also PHILOSOPHY/Simulation and rendering)

**What:** Both entry points into the game's per-frame work are `const` member functions that reach
through a `std::unique_ptr` member — which does not propagate `const` — to call non-`const` `State`
methods; and `State::draw()` is non-`const` while `IGameObject::draw()` is `const`, so the
"const all the way down" chain breaks at the top.

**Evidence:**

    engine/core/state_context.h:13
        void update() const;
        void draw() const;
    private:
        std::unique_ptr<State> state_ = nullptr;

    engine/core/state_context.cpp:13
    void StateContext::draw() const
    {
        if (this->state_ == nullptr)
        {
            return;
        }
        this->state_->draw();
    }

    engine/core/state.h:12
        virtual void update() = 0;
        virtual void draw() = 0;

**Why it matters:** IMPLEMENTED.md's note on finding #16 identifies exactly this hole ("`Level`
holds them by `unique_ptr`, which does not pass its own constness on to what it points at") and
fixed it for `Level`'s drawables — but `StateContext`, the class that hole was found in, still has
it. `StateContext::update() const` runs the whole simulation; `draw() const` runs the whole render.
PHILOSOPHY line 364 says "`update()` writes; `draw()` is `const` all the way down"; the outermost
two frames of that chain are `const` where they should not be and non-`const` where they should be,
which is precisely backwards. A `const StateContext&` looks safe to hand to a worker and is not.

**Remedy:** Drop `const` from `StateContext::update()`/`draw()`, and make `State::draw()` `const`
so the pure-read contract holds from the state stack down to `IGameObject`.

#### `Camera::calculate_view_rectangle` has four overloads; two are out-parameter forms with no callers

- **File:** `engine/math/matt_math.h:1034-1044`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T5

**What:** The same arithmetic is written four times behind four overloads of one name, two of which
write through an out-parameter, and the value-returning and out-parameter member overloads differ
only in the constness of the argument — so what the call does depends on whether the caller's
rectangle happens to be `const`.

**Evidence:**

    engine/math/matt_math.h:1034
        mattmath::RectangleF calculate_view_rectangle(
            const mattmath::RectangleF& world_rectangle) const;
        void calculate_view_rectangle(
            mattmath::RectangleF& rectangle) const;
        static mattmath::RectangleF calculate_view_rectangle(
            const mattmath::RectangleF& world_rectangle,
            const Camera& camera);
        static void calculate_view_rectangle(
            const mattmath::RectangleF& world_rectangle,
            const Camera& camera,
            mattmath::RectangleF& view_rectangle);

All four bodies at `engine/math/matt_math.cpp:4109-4143` are the same four multiplications.
Callers, all four of them, use only the first overload:

    engine/render/animation_object.cpp:69, :91
    engine/render/texture_object.cpp:80, :105

**Why it matters:** `camera.calculate_view_rectangle(rect);` written as a statement means two
different things depending on `rect`'s constness: with a non-`const` `RectangleF` it selects the
`void` overload and mutates `rect` in place; with a `const` one it selects the value-returning
overload and discards the result (which nothing marks `[[nodiscard]]`). Neither produces a
diagnostic. The two dead overloads are the ones that make this possible and have zero callers, and
the duplicated arithmetic is four places to fix a camera bug instead of one.

**Remedy:** Delete both `void` overloads and the static value overload; keep the single `const`
member returning by value and mark it `[[nodiscard]]`.

#### `Partitioner::partition` divides by a caller-supplied count with no check, reachable from `ApplicationOptions`

- **File:** `engine/collision/partitioner.cpp:8-9`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6

**What:** `partition` divides by `num_partitions` without validating it, and `num_partitions` comes
from `ApplicationOptions::max_threads`, a public, documented, unvalidated `int` field that a game
sets before `initialize()`.

**Evidence:**

    engine/collision/partitioner.cpp:5
    std::vector<std::pair<int, int>> Partitioner::partition(int num_elements, int num_partitions) const
    {
        std::vector<std::pair<int, int>> result;
        int elements_per_partition = num_elements / num_partitions;
        int remainder = num_elements % num_partitions;

The path in:

    engine/app/application.h:46         int max_threads = 16;
    engine/app/application.cpp:134      this->thread_pool_ = std::make_unique<ThreadPool>(
                                            this->options_.min_threads, this->options_.max_threads);
    game/objects/level.cpp:397          int num_threads = this->thread_pool_->max_num_threads();
    game/objects/level.cpp:400          auto partitioned_players =
                                            this->partitioner_->partition(this->player_objects_->size(), num_threads);

**Why it matters:** `samples/minimal/` is documented as the file a new project copies, and
`ApplicationOptions` is documented as "what a game hands the shell before it opens a window"
(`engine/app/application.h:26`). The comment on `max_threads` states an upper meaning ("the widest
the renderer can ever go") and no lower bound. Setting it to `0` — a legal value of `int`, no
validation anywhere between the options struct and this division — kills the process with an integer
divide-by-zero on the first frame that draws, with no message. `min_threads > max_threads` is
similarly accepted. Both are exactly the "loud failure over graceful degradation" case T6 covers,
and both are ints where the type could have carried the constraint.

**Remedy:** Validate `ApplicationOptions` in `Application::initialize` and throw naming the field
(T6), and make `partition` throw or assert on `num_partitions < 1`.

#### `colour.h` defines 300+ internal-linkage constants and an `inline` function that names them

- **File:** `engine/math/colour.h:159-314`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T5

**What:** ~307 namespace-scope `const` objects (hence internal linkage, hence a distinct entity per
translation unit) sit in a header that nearly every engine and game TU includes, and an `inline`
function with external linkage references 150 of them — which is an ODR violation, IFNDR.

**Evidence:**

    engine/math/colour.h:9      const std::string ALICE_BLUE = "f0f8ff";
    ... 156 more ...
    engine/math/colour.h:159    const mattmath::Colour ALICE_BLUE = { html::ALICE_BLUE };
    ... 149 more ...
    engine/math/colour.h:314    inline mattmath::Colour colour_from_name(const std::string& name)
    engine/math/colour.h:316        if (name == "ALICE_BLUE") return colour_consts::ALICE_BLUE;
    ... 148 more ...
    engine/math/colour.h:464        return colour_consts::WHITE;

`Colour` has no `constexpr` constructor (`engine/math/matt_math.h:601-608`), so none of these can
be constant-initialised; each is a dynamic initialiser. `colour_from_name` is called from
`game/objects/level_object_builder.cpp:66, :128, :162, :182`.

**Why it matters:** Two separate defects from one cause. (1) `colour_from_name` is `inline`, so it
has external linkage and one definition is chosen at link time — but each TU's definition names a
*different* `colour_consts::ALICE_BLUE`, which [basic.def.odr] forbids and no compiler is required
to diagnose. It is benign today only because the values happen to be identical. (2) Every TU that
includes `colour.h` — which is nearly all of them, since `engine/render/draw_object.h:3` includes it
and everything drawable includes that — gets its own copy of 307 objects with 307 dynamic
initialisers, taxing startup, binary size and compile time, all of which PHILOSOPHY names as
maintained properties. The last line is a third, smaller defect: an unknown colour name silently
returns white instead of naming the bad content (T6).

**Remedy:** Make them `inline constexpr` (which needs a `constexpr Colour` constructor) or move the
definitions to `colour.cpp` and declare them `extern` — either one gives every TU the same entity
and one initialiser.

#### Pass `/utf-8`; the sample already carries the rule by hand and one engine file is already corrupted

- **File:** `cmake/settings.cmake:9-14`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** T5

**What:** The shared settings target sets `/W4 /WX /permissive- /sdl` but not `/utf-8`, no source
file has a BOM, and the consequence is already visible in the tree.

**Evidence:**

    cmake/settings.cmake:9
    target_compile_options(artattack_settings INTERFACE
        /W4          # highest regular warning level
        /WX          # warnings are errors, zero suppressions
        /permissive- # standards conformance mode
        /sdl         # additional security checks
    )

The rule being carried by comment instead, in the file documented as the new-project template:

    samples/minimal/main.cpp:25
        // ASCII only: this file gets copied into new projects, and a wide
        // literal's encoding depends on how the compiler was told to read the
        // source.
        options.window_title = L"ArtAttack - minimal sample";

And the damage already in the tree — `EF BF BD`, the UTF-8 encoding of U+FFFD REPLACEMENT
CHARACTER, four times in an engine source file:

    engine/math/ericson_math.cpp:532
        // Intersect AABBs <U+FFFD>a<U+FFFD> and <U+FFFD>b<U+FFFD> moving with constant velocities va and vb.
    engine/math/ericson_math.cpp:759
        // Project c onto ab, computing parameterized position d(t) = a + t*(b <U+FFFD> a)

(no file in the tree carries a BOM: `engine/math/ericson_math.cpp`, `matt_math.cpp`,
`samples/minimal/main.cpp` and `game/main.cpp` all start with source bytes.)

**Why it matters:** Without `/utf-8` and without a BOM, MSVC reads sources in the machine's ANSI
codepage, so what a narrow or wide string literal contains depends on the contributor's Windows
locale — for an engine "intended, eventually, for developers other than its author" that is a
per-machine behaviour difference in shipped strings. The author already knows: the sample carries a
hand-written rule for exactly this, which is a rule the build could enforce in one line. The
replacement characters in `ericson_math.cpp` show a mis-decoded round trip has already happened
(harmlessly, in comments).

**Remedy:** Add `/utf-8` to `target_compile_options` in `cmake/settings.cmake` and delete the
ASCII-only comment from the sample.

#### `Viewport::d3d_viewport_ptr()` reinterpret_casts `this` to an unrelated struct

- **File:** `engine/math/matt_math.cpp:3208-3211`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T2

**What:** A public MattMath accessor type-puns `this` into a `D3D11_VIEWPORT*`, which is undefined
behaviour regardless of how the two layouts happen to line up; it currently has no callers.

**Evidence:**

    engine/math/matt_math.cpp:3208
    const D3D11_VIEWPORT* Viewport::d3d_viewport_ptr() const
    {
        return reinterpret_cast<const D3D11_VIEWPORT*>(this);
    }

The type it is punning, whose field names give the game away:

    engine/math/matt_math.h:775
    struct Viewport
    {
    public:
        float x = 0.0f;
        float y = 0.0f;
        float width = 0.0f;
        float height = 0.0f;
        float minDepth = 0.0f;
        float maxDepth = 1.0f;

**Why it matters:** The two types are layout-compatible today by coincidence, not by any rule the
compiler will preserve — reading a `Viewport` object through a `D3D11_VIEWPORT` lvalue is an

    add_executable(AssetsTests
        asset_manifest_loader_tests.cpp
        test_main.cpp
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/engine/assets/asset_manifest_loader.cpp"
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/engine/assets/json_loader.cpp"
    )
    target_include_directories(AssetsTests PRIVATE
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}"
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/external/rapidjson/include"
    )
    target_link_libraries(AssetsTests PRIVATE
        doctest::doctest
        artattack_settings
    )

The rule:

    PHILOSOPHY.md:274   Tests link libraries, never `#include` implementation files.

`tests/core/CMakeLists.txt` links neither library (header-only, and says so);
`tests/math/CMakeLists.txt` links `MattMath` correctly. So `ArtAttackEngine` is linked by exactly
two targets, both `WIN32` GUI applications.

**Why it matters:** The intent of "tests link libraries" is that the thing tested is the thing
shipped. Here the two engine TUs are compiled a second time without `Microsoft::DirectXTK`'s
interface include directories and definitions, so the test build and the library build can diverge
the moment either file gains a DirectXTK include or a conditional. More broadly, PHILOSOPHY promises
"everything below the platform edge is testable headlessly, because the boundary (targets) and the
seams ... make it linkable and constructible without a window" — and `ctest` currently never links
the engine, so that claim is unexercised.

**Remedy:** Link `ArtAttackEngine` from `AssetsTests` (the manifest loader pulls in no device), and
if the engine is too heavy to link headlessly, that is the finding rather than the workaround.

- **File:** `engine/math/ericson_math.h:108-137`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T5

**What:** Eight public math functions return their results through non-const references while
returning `bool` for success, none of them documents that the out-parameters are untouched when the
result is `false`, and the internal caller passes an uninitialised `float` into one of them.

**Evidence:**

    engine/math/ericson_math.h:108
        bool intersect_moving_AABB_AABB(const mattmath::AABB& a,
            const mattmath::AABB& b,
            const mattmath::Vector2F& va,
            const mattmath::Vector2F& vb,
            float& tfirst, float& tlast);
    engine/math/ericson_math.h:120
        bool test_2D_segment_segment(const mattmath::Point2F& a,
            const mattmath::Point2F& b, const mattmath::Point2F& c,
            const mattmath::Point2F& d, float& t, mattmath::Point2F& p);
    engine/math/ericson_math.h:124
        void barycentric(const mattmath::Point2F& a,
            const mattmath::Point2F& b, const mattmath::Point2F& c,
            const mattmath::Point2F& p, float& u, float& v, float& w);

The false path never writes them:

    engine/math/ericson_math.cpp:717
                    t = a3 / (a3 - a4);
                    p = a + t * (b - a);
                    return 1;
                }
            }
            // Segments not intersecting (or collinear)
            return 0;

And the wrapper that already relies on that, with `t` uninitialised:

    engine/math/matt_math.cpp:577
    bool mattmath::segments_intersect(const Segment& a, const Segment& b)
    {
        float t;
        Point2F p;
        return segments_intersect(a, b, t, p);
    }

**Why it matters:** PHILOSOPHY says math primitives "carry documented contracts ... what throws —
each pinned by behavioural tests in the commit that creates them". These carry none: nothing in the
header says the out-parameters are only meaningful when the function returns true, and a caller who
reads `t` unconditionally gets whatever was on the stack. `barycentric`'s three adjacent `float&`
out-parameters are also silently transposable. The same header returns by value where it could —
`closest_pt_point_triangle` (line 80) returns a `Point2F` while `closest_pt_point_AABB` (line 94),
`closest_pt_point_segment` (line 132) and `closest_pt_point_OBB` (line 136) take an out-parameter —
so the file cannot even agree with itself. `test_segment_AABB` (line 114-115) takes `p0` by const
reference and `p1` by value.

**Remedy:** Return a small struct or `std::optional` from the bool-plus-out-parameter functions and
mark them `[[nodiscard]]`; at minimum, document in the header that the out-parameters are unwritten
on `false`.

#### Type aliases and nested types in new engine headers are lowercase

- **File:** `engine/core/registry.h:53`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Types

**What:** Five type names introduced by the recent engine work are snake_case, against the one rule
the whole conventions document falls out of.

**Evidence:**

    engine/core/registry.h:53        using handle = Handle<Resource>;
    engine/core/registry.h:149       struct entry
    engine/core/name_table.h         (clean)
    engine/core/thread_pool.h:34     struct task_item
    engine/render/sprite_sheet.h:18  using frame_handle = Handle<SpriteFrame>;
    engine/render/sprite_sheet.h:19  using strip_handle = Handle<AnimationStrip>;
    engine/core/throw_if_failed.h:10 class com_exception : public std::exception

The rule, and the reason it matters more here than most:

    CONVENTIONS.md:13   > **PascalCase names a type. snake_case names everything else.
    CONVENTIONS.md:18   | Types — classes, structs, enums, aliases | `PascalCase` | ...

**Why it matters:** These are not legacy: `Registry`, `NameTable`, `Handle`, `SpriteSheet` and
`ThreadPool` are the newest and most carefully documented headers in the engine, and they are the
first thing a stranger reads. `handle resolve(const std::string& name) const;`
(`engine/core/registry.h:84`) reads as a variable declaration until you find the alias, which is the
exact ambiguity the single-rule scheme exists to remove. `SpriteSheet::frame_handle` then appears in
public signatures across `texture_object.h` and `animation_object.h`, so the lowercase spelling has
already propagated.

**Remedy:** Rename to `Handle`/`Entry`/`TaskItem`/`FrameHandle`/`StripHandle`/`ComException` — a
`using Handle = artattack::Handle<Resource>;` inside the class is legal and reads correctly.

<a id="g-sweep-loud-failure"></a>

## sweep-loud-failure — T6: loud failure over graceful degradation

*Group `sweep-loud-failure` · 15 findings (1 critical, 6 high, 5 medium, 3 low) · source `review2/raw/sweep-loud-failure.md`, cross-cutting sweep — no separate verifier, reported as written.*

I read PHILOSOPHY/CONVENTIONS/ARCHITECTURE, then swept every first-party `throw`,
`catch`, discarded return value, `default:` arm and content-lookup miss in
`engine/`, `game/`, `samples/`, `tests/`, `cmake/` and the root build files, opening
each candidate before writing it down. The shape of the problem is not that T6 is
absent — it is that T6 is implemented *once per author sitting*, and the newest
code is far better than the code beside it. `engine/assets/asset_manifest_loader.cpp`
and `engine/core/registry.h` are exemplary: they name the file, the group, the key,
the resource and the kind, and the manifest loader has a test that asserts the
message contains all three. Fifteen lines below, in the same folder,
`sprite_sheet_loader.cpp` and `sound_bank_loader.cpp` read JSON through raw
`operator[]`/`GetString()`, whose asserts CMake compiles out in Release
(`/O2 /Ob2 /DNDEBUG`, confirmed in the cache), so a typo in a content file is a
null-pointer `std::string` construction rather than a sentence. The same split runs
through the whole tree: `ResourceLoader::load_sprite_font` catches DirectXTK's
useless `what()` and rethrows naming the font *and* the path, while
`load_sprite_font`'s neighbour `load_texture` — the more common failure by far —
reports `Failure with HRESULT of 80070002` and nothing else. The reverse breach
(T6's "not a licence for") is much rarer and mostly under control: the thread pool
captures and rethrows on join, `Weapon::stop_sounds` explicitly guards its handle so
teardown cannot throw, and both `main.cpp` files have a real barrier — but the
engine itself has none, and the frame is also driven from inside the window
procedure. Two things genuinely surprised me: `ViewportManager::calculate_viewport`
falls through between layout cases, so an out-of-range player index silently returns
*another layout's* geometry and finally the full-screen one, and it is reachable by
pausing a three-player match; and nothing on the pause-menu quit path stops the
players' looping weapon sounds, so quitting mid-fire leaves the sprayer looping over
the main menu for the rest of the session.

### Themes

- The engine now contains two incompatible conventions for reading content data — a
  `require_*` helper family that names file, group and key, and raw rapidjson
  accessors that are undefined behaviour in Release — and they sit in the same
  folder, written in the same era.
- Failure messages that do exist frequently omit the one fact the reader needs: the
  file, the name, or the value that was rejected, even when that value is in a local
  variable one line above the `throw`.
- `default:` and out-of-range arms across the tree substitute a plausible value —
  white, the full-screen viewport, one player, an unresolved handle — instead of
  rejecting the input, which converts a content bug into a rendering bug three
  screens later.
- Unchecked and discarded return values cluster at the platform edge, where the
  engine talks to Win32 and DirectXTK: `AudioEngine::Update`,
  `SetThreadpoolThreadMinimum`, `std::filesystem::create_directories`'s
  `error_code`, and `Save::write_save_file`'s `bool`.
- The engine's public configuration surface, `ApplicationOptions`, is validated
  nowhere, so a stranger's first misconfiguration surfaces as an access violation
  deep inside `Partitioner` rather than as a sentence naming the field.
- Teardown discipline is applied per call site rather than by design: one path
  guards its handle and documents why, its sibling does not, and one teardown path
  simply forgot half the work it was meant to do.
- The exception barrier that makes all this loudness safe lives in the *game's*
  `main`, not in the engine, and the engine also calls into game code from inside a
  Win32 callback where that barrier is not reliably reachable.

---

#### Stop reading asset JSON through rapidjson accessors whose checks vanish in Release

- **File:** `engine/assets/sprite_sheet_loader.cpp:11-67`
- **Severity:** critical
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6 (also T5, and PHILOSOPHY/Content and assets)

**What:** Both remaining engine asset decoders read JSON with raw `operator[]` and
`GetX()`, whose `RAPIDJSON_ASSERT` is `assert` and is compiled out by the `/DNDEBUG`
in `CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELEASE`, so a missing or mistyped key produces a null string
pointer instead of an error.

**Evidence:**

    NameTable<SpriteFrame> decode_sprite_frames(const Value& json)
    {
        NameTable<SpriteFrame> sprite_frames("sprite frame");
        for (auto& frame : json.GetArray())
        {
            std::string name = frame["name"].GetString();
            Vector2F origin = Vector2F::ZERO;
            bool rotated = false;
            RectangleI source_rectangle(
                frame["position"]["x"].GetInt(),

and, at the bottom of the same file:

    	return std::make_unique<SpriteSheet>(texture,
    		decode_sprite_frames(doc["sprite_frames"]),
    		decode_animation_strips(doc["animation_strips"]));

**Why it matters:** `external/rapidjson/include/rapidjson/document.h:1226-1238`
returns a thread-local placement-new'd null `GenericValue` after the assert, and
`document.h:1853` is `const Ch* GetString() const { RAPIDJSON_ASSERT(IsString());
return DataString(data_); }`. A default-constructed value has
`data_.f.flags = kNullFlag` over a zeroed union (`document.h:690`), so `GetString()`
returns `nullptr` and `std::string name = nullptr` is undefined behaviour —
in practice an access violation with no message. `out/build/x64-release/CMakeCache.txt:46`
confirms `CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELEASE:STRING=/O2 /Ob2 /DNDEBUG`. The path is reached by
editing a sprite-sheet JSON, which T7 makes an ordinary authoring action, and by
`Application::load_manifest` on every launch. `engine/assets/sound_bank_loader.cpp:17-19,
53-54, 73-78` has the identical defect (`wave.GetString()`, `effect["name"].GetString()`,
`doc["waves"]`, `doc["create_effect_instance_for_each_wave"].GetBool()`). The fix
already exists 40 lines away: `asset_manifest_loader.cpp:23-54` defines
`require_member`/`require_array`/`require_string`, with a comment (`:12-16`) stating
exactly this reasoning, and `tests/assets/asset_manifest_loader_tests.cpp:198-217`
pins the message.

**Remedy:** Move `require_member`/`require_array`/`require_string` into a shared
header under `engine/assets/` and route every read in both decoders through it, so
the failure names the path, the record index and the key.

#### Name the texture file that could not be loaded

- **File:** `engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:108-141`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6

**What:** A missing or misspelt texture fails with `Failure with HRESULT of
80070002` and no file name, while the font loader immediately below it catches and
rethrows naming both the asset and the path.

**Evidence:**

    	void ResourceLoader::load_texture(const std::string& directory,
    		const std::string& name) const
    	{
    		const std::string texture_path = directory + name + ".dds";

    		ComPtr<ID3D11ShaderResourceView> texture_view;
    		ComPtr<ID3D11Resource> resource;
    		ThrowIfFailed(
    			CreateDDSTextureFromFile(this->device_,
    				std::wstring(texture_path.begin(), texture_path.end()).c_str(),
    				resource.GetAddressOf(),
    				texture_view.ReleaseAndGetAddressOf()));

versus, seventeen lines later:

    		catch (const std::exception&)
    		{
    			// DirectXTK's what() does not say which font or where - T6 does.
    			throw std::out_of_range(
    				"SpriteFont " + name + " not found at " + font_path + ".");
    		}

**Why it matters:** PHILOSOPHY T6 names this exact case — "A missing texture is a
launch-time error naming the file". `ThrowIfFailed` throws `com_exception`
(`engine/core/throw_if_failed.h:27-33`), whose `what()` is
`sprintf_s(s_str, "Failure with HRESULT of %08X", ...)` into a function-local
`static char s_str[64]` (`:17-19`). The path from a typo in `manifest.json` runs
`load_manifest` → `load_texture` → `wWinMain`'s barrier
(`game/main.cpp:93-101`), which puts that HRESULT in a MessageBox. `load_sprite_sheet`
(`:143-153`) and `reload_sprite_sheet_texture` (`:155-162`) both go through
`load_texture`, so sprite sheets inherit it too. The shared `static` buffer is a
second defect in the same helper: two live `com_exception`s return the same
message, and a second `what()` call overwrites the first's text.

**Remedy:** Wrap the `CreateDDSTextureFromFile` call the way the font path is
wrapped, and give `com_exception` a `std::string` member instead of a function-local
static buffer.

#### Make an out-of-range player index a viewport error, not another layout's geometry

- **File:** `engine/render/viewport_manager.cpp:143-234`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6

**What:** `calculate_viewport`'s outer `switch` has no `break` or `return` after each
layout's inner `switch`, so an out-of-range `player_num` falls through into the next
layout's geometry and finally into a `default:` that silently returns the full-screen
viewport.

**Evidence:**

    	case ScreenLayout::two_player:
    		switch (player_num)
    		{
    		case 0:
    			...
    			return result;
    		case 1:
    			...
    			return result;
    		default:
    			break;
    		}
    	case ScreenLayout::three_player:

and the terminal arm:

    	default: //1P screen
    		result.x = 0.0f;
    		result.y = 0.0f;
    		result.width = screen_size.x;
    		result.height = screen_size.y;
    		return result;

**Why it matters:** Reachable from ordinary play. Selecting three players
(`game/states/main_menu.cpp:905-911`) sets `ScreenLayout::three_player`, which
`GameLevel::build_and_enter_level` (`game/states/game_states.cpp:131-137`) applies to
the shared `ViewportManager`. Pausing then draws a `MenuPage`
(`game/states/pause_menu.cpp:222`) through
`MenuPage::draw_mobject_in_viewports` (`game/states/menu_page.cpp:104-118`), which
calls `all_viewports()`. `all_viewports` pushes a fourth entry via
`this->player_viewport(4)` (`viewport_manager.cpp:88-91`) — index 4 in a
three-viewport layout — which falls through `three_player`'s inner default, then
`four_player`'s inner default, and lands on the full-screen arm. The loop at
`menu_page.cpp:108-111` then calls `apply_player_viewport(3)`, which falls through to
`four_player`'s `case 3:` and binds the bottom-right quadrant. So the widget is laid
out against a 1280×720 `Viewport` while the rasterizer and `SpriteBatch` projection
are a quarter of that, over player 2's quadrant. Separately, `two_player` with
`player_num == 2` silently receives the three-player bottom-left quadrant. MSVC does
not warn on switch fall-through even at `/W4 /WX`, so the build never said anything;
the previous review flagged the shape of both defects (README #187, #188) but not
this reachable path, and C++20 (`cmake/settings.cmake:7`) now makes
`[[fallthrough]]` available where the fall-through is genuinely wanted.

**Remedy:** Give each layout case an explicit terminator and throw
`std::out_of_range` naming the layout and the index instead of falling through; fix
`all_viewports` to stop asking for index 4.

#### Validate ApplicationOptions before the engine acts on it

- **File:** `engine/app/application.h:30-52`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T6 (also T5)

**What:** `ApplicationOptions` is the engine's entire configuration surface and
`Application::initialize` checks none of its fields, so an out-of-range value
surfaces as a crash far from the line that set it.

**Evidence:**

    		// The render thread pool. max_threads also sizes the deferred contexts and
    		// sprite batches, so it is the widest the renderer can ever go.
    		int min_threads = 1;
    		int max_threads = 16;

and, in `application.cpp:132-135`, the only thing done with them:

    		this->thread_pool_ = std::make_unique<ThreadPool>(
    			this->options_.min_threads, this->options_.max_threads);

**Why it matters:** `samples/minimal/main.cpp` is explicitly "the file a new project
starts from", and these fields are what a new project edits. With
`max_threads = 0`: `create_deferred_contexts(0)` succeeds silently
(`engine/render/device_resources.cpp:740-759`), `sprite_batches_.resize(0)` succeeds
(`application.cpp:156-159`), and the first draw hits
`Partitioner::partition`'s `int elements_per_partition = num_elements /
num_partitions;` (`engine/collision/partitioner.cpp:8`) — integer division by zero,
an access violation with no message. With `min_threads > max_threads`,
`SetThreadpoolThreadMinimum` returns `BOOL` and the result is discarded
(`engine/core/thread_pool.cpp:18-19`), so the pool silently keeps the default
minimum. `target_fps` feeds `1.0 / static_cast<double>(target_fps)` into
`SetTargetElapsedSeconds` (`application.cpp:74-75`) with no lower bound, and
`StepTimer::SecondsToTicks` is an unguarded `static_cast<uint64_t>(seconds *
TicksPerSecond)`. None of the fields document a valid range.

**Remedy:** Check every field at the top of `initialize()` and throw naming the
field, the value and the permitted range; document the range in the struct.

#### Stop the players' looping weapon sounds when the pause menu leaves the level

- **File:** `game/states/game_states.cpp:206-224`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6

**What:** Quitting or restarting from the pause menu calls `stop_music()` but never
`stop_player_sounds()`, so a looping weapon sound started before the pause keeps
playing after the level is gone.

**Evidence:**

**Why it matters:** `Level::stop_player_sounds()` exists (`game/objects/level.cpp:341-348`)

(`game_states.cpp:154-173`) only flips `state_`; it stops calling `level_->update()`

#### Check AudioEngine::Update instead of discarding it

- **File:** `engine/app/application.cpp:257-262`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6

**What:** `AudioEngine::Update()` returns false when the audio graph has entered
silent mode; the engine discards the result and never calls `IsCriticalError()` or
`Reset()`, so the game goes permanently mute with no diagnostic and no recovery.

**Evidence:**

    	void Application::update()
    	{
    		*this->dt_ = static_cast<float>(this->timer_.GetElapsedSeconds());
    		StateContext::update();
    		std::ignore = this->audio_engine_->Update();
    	}

**Why it matters:** DirectXTK's own header states the contract —
`out/build/x64-release/vcpkg_installed/x64-windows/include/directxtk/Audio.h:243`:
`bool __cdecl Update();  // Performs per-frame processing for the audio engine,
returns false if in 'silent mode'`, with `Reset()`, `IsAudioDevicePresent()` and
`IsCriticalError()` documented immediately below as the handling. Unplugging a
headset or switching the default playback device mid-match puts the engine into
silent mode; from then on every `SoundBank::play_wave`/`play_effect` is a no-op for
the rest of the session. This is not the "expected absence" T6 exempts — no audio
device at startup is a state, but a graph halted by a critical error is a failure the
engine can both report and repair, and it does neither. The previous review recorded
it (`docs/review/all-findings.md:691, 880`) and it is not in `IMPLEMENTED.md`; what
is new is that the `std::ignore` now makes the discard deliberate-looking rather than
an omission.

**Remedy:** `if (!audio_engine_->Update() && audio_engine_->IsCriticalError())
{ audio_engine_->Reset(); }`, and report the transition once rather than every frame.

---

#### Reject a duplicate asset name in the manifest instead of overwriting

- **File:** `engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:74-92`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6

**What:** The manifest walk registers every entry through `Registry::add`, which
refills an existing name's slot rather than rejecting it, so a name listed twice in
`manifest.json` silently keeps whichever entry the walk reached last.

**Evidence:**

    		for (const AssetEntry& entry : manifest.entries)
    		{
    			const auto kind = this->kinds_.find(entry.kind);
    			if (kind == this->kinds_.end())
    			{
    				throw std::out_of_range("Asset '" + entry.name + "' in '" +
    					manifest.source_path + "' is of kind '" + entry.kind +
    					"', which nothing registered.");
    			}
    			kind->second.load(entry.directory, entry.name);
    		}

with `engine/core/registry.h:63-71`:

    		void add(const std::string& name, Storage resource)
    		{
    			const auto it = this->indices_.find(name);
    			if (it != this->indices_.end())
    			{
    				this->entries_[static_cast<size_t>(it->second)].resource =
    					std::move(resource);
    				return;
    			}

**Why it matters:** The overwrite behaviour is correct and load-bearing for device
restore — `registry.h:60-62` says so — but it is the wrong answer for a first load,
and the loader that sits next door already knows it:
`engine/assets/sound_bank_loader.cpp:56-63` explicitly checks `instances.contains(name)`
first with the comment "Registry::add refills a name's slot rather than rejecting it,
so the duplicate check has to happen here: two definitions claiming one name is a
content bug, not an overwrite." The manifest walk has no equivalent. The game's own
`level` kind makes the consequence visible: `game/main.cpp:62-70` does
`stages.push_back(...)` *and* `level_infos.add(name, ...)`, so a level named twice in
the manifest yields two stage-select entries backed by one registry slot.

**Remedy:** Track the names seen during a walk and throw naming the duplicate and
the manifest path, keeping `Registry::add`'s replace semantics for reload only.

#### Put the engine's exception barrier in the engine, not only in each game's main

- **File:** `engine/app/application.cpp:187-205, 462-475`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T6

**What:** The only handler for a T6 throw lives in each game's `wWinMain`, and the
frame is also driven from inside the Win32 window procedure, where an exception must
unwind out of a system callback before it can reach that handler.

**Evidence:**

    		case WM_PAINT:
    			// While the user drags the window Windows owns the loop, so the only
    			// way to keep drawing is from inside the paint message.
    			if (in_sizemove && app)
    			{
    				app->tick();
    			}

**Why it matters:** `tick()` runs `update()` and `render()`, i.e. the whole game
(`application.cpp:251-255`), and the tick path contains live throws —
`game/objects/level.cpp:337` `throw std::runtime_error("Player out of bounds");`,
which `docs/review/IMPLEMENTED.md` records as deliberately left loud. Outside a drag,
`window_proc` is entered from `DispatchMessage` at `application.cpp:196`, inside the
game's `try`; during a drag it is entered from the modal loop Windows runs inside
`DefWindowProc`, so the same throw must unwind through several `user32` frames the
engine neither controls nor documents. `Application::run`'s header comment
(`application.h:88-90`) says nothing about exceptions at all, yet both
`game/main.cpp:24-101` and `samples/minimal/main.cpp:21-49` wrap it — a contract
taught only by copying the sample. An engine offered to strangers should own the
barrier that makes its own loudness safe.

**Remedy:** Catch inside `Application::run` (and around the WM_PAINT tick), report
through one engine-owned path, and document in `application.h` what escapes `run()`.

---

#### Delete the two `throw new std::exception` sites

- **File:** `game/states/menu_input.cpp:62-68, 120-124`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6

**What:** Two branches throw a *pointer* to an exception, which no
`catch (const std::exception&)` can match, and both encode "two buttons pressed at
once" as a fatal error.

**Evidence:**

    	else if ((proceed && back) ||
    		(proceed && pause) ||
    		(pause && back))
    	{
    		throw new std::exception(
    			"2 or more of proceed, back or pause pressed at same time");
    	}

**Why it matters:** Both branches are provably unreachable: at `:62` the earlier arms
have already established `proceed`, `back` and `pause` are all false, so every
conjunction is false; at `:120` the same is true of `up`. So this cannot fire today —
but if it ever did, the throw would sail past the only barrier in the process
(`game/main.cpp:93`) into `std::terminate` with no message, and leak the exception
object. It also states the wrong policy: a player mashing A and B together is the
world being the world, which T6 explicitly exempts. The previous review reported
these two sites (`docs/review/README.md:866, 946`) and `IMPLEMENTED.md` does not list
them as fixed; they survived the move into `game/states/` and four conventions
passes.

**Remedy:** Delete both branches — they are dead and the condition they describe is
not an error.

---

#### Give StepTimer's four throws a message

- **File:** `engine/core/step_timer.h:29-37, 74-79, 94-97`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6

**What:** Four throws in an engine core header construct a default
`std::exception`, so the message a user sees is `Unknown exception`.

**Evidence:**

    			if (!QueryPerformanceFrequency(&m_qpcFrequency))
    			{
    				throw std::exception();
    			}

    			if (!QueryPerformanceCounter(&m_qpcLastTime))
    			{
    				throw std::exception();
    			}

**Why it matters:** These are the least informative failures in the engine, in a
header included by `engine/app/application.h:7`, and the two in `ResetElapsedTime`
and `Tick` are on the per-frame path — so if one ever fires, the game's barrier
(`game/main.cpp:97-99`) puts `startup failure: Unknown exception` on screen mid-match.
`QueryPerformanceCounter` failing is vanishingly unlikely on supported Windows, which
is why this is low, but T6 asks for names and this file names nothing. The file is
verbatim DirectXTK sample code that the split moved into `engine/core/` without
review — it still carries `m_` members, which CONVENTIONS/Never forbids.

**Remedy:** Throw `std::runtime_error` naming the API that failed and
`GetLastError()`.

#### Do not fold an out-of-range team or player number into "this weapon has no sound"

- **File:** `game/objects/weapon.cpp:269-304`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6

**What:** `resolve_loop_sound` returns an unresolved handle for an invalid team or an
out-of-range player number, which every caller reads as "nothing to do", so a
programming error becomes silence at load time.

**Evidence:**

    	if (team != PlayerTeam::a && team != PlayerTeam::b)
    	{
    		return {};
    	}
    	if (player_num < 0 || player_num > 3)
    	{
    		return {};
    	}

**Why it matters:** The comment above these lines explains that Sniper and Bucket
legitimately have no looping instance, and that the unresolved handle exists so
`stop_sounds` — "a teardown path with no catch anywhere above it" — cannot throw.
That reasoning is sound and the `valid()` guard in `stop_sounds` (`:263-266`) already
delivers it. What these two guards add is different: they map two distinct broken
contracts onto the same silent value, so a weapon built with a bad team or player
index simply never makes a sound and nothing says why. I could not reach either
branch from the menus, which currently only produce teams `a`/`b` and indices 0–3, so
this is a latent trap rather than a live bug.

**Remedy:** Throw naming the team and player number for the two invalid-argument
cases, and keep `{}` for the weapon types that genuinely have no loop.

#### Report a failed save somewhere the player can see

- **File:** `game/save.cpp:71-121`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6

**What:** Every failure on the save path is either swallowed or reported to
`std::cout` in a process built with `WIN32` subsystem, which has no console — and the
timestamp line prints an `errno_t` rather than a time.

**Evidence:**

    	auto start = std::chrono::system_clock::now();
    	auto legacy_start = std::chrono::system_clock::to_time_t(start);
    	char buffer[30];
    	std::cout << ctime_s(buffer, sizeof(buffer), &legacy_start) << " Saving...\n";
    	if (write_save_file(this->save_data_))
    	{
    		std::cout << "Save was successful.\n";
    	}
    	else
    	{
    		std::cout << "Save was unsuccessful.\n";
    	}

**Why it matters:** `game/CMakeLists.txt:11` is `add_executable(ArtAttackGame WIN32 ...)`,
so the process runs under `/SUBSYSTEM:WINDOWS` and nothing reads `std::cout`.
`set_resolution_and_save` and `set_full_screen_and_save` (`:123-133`) both route
through here, so a settings change that fails to persist — read-only directory,
disk full, `create_directories` failing with the `std::error_code` at `:78-79` that
nothing reads — is completely invisible; the player changes the resolution, restarts,
and finds it reverted. `ctime_s` returns `errno_t`, so line 112 prints `0` where a
timestamp was intended. The `catch` at `:63-68` that falls back to defaults on a
corrupt save is the one thing here that is right, and it says why.

**Remedy:** Return the failure from `save_to_file` and let the caller surface it in
the options menu; drop the `std::cout` reporting or route it through
`OutputDebugString`.

<a id="g-sweep-clarity-duplication"></a>

## sweep-clarity-duplication — T4: duplication, dead code, divergence

*Group `sweep-clarity-duplication` · 19 findings (2 high, 10 medium, 7 low) · source `review2/raw/sweep-clarity-duplication.md`, cross-cutting sweep — no separate verifier, reported as written.*

I read every `.cpp` and `.h` under `engine/`, `game/`, `samples/`, `tests/`, plus the
root and per-target CMake files, hunting for bodies that exist more than once and for
code with no caller. The shape of the problem is that this codebase has almost no
shared helpers: where a concept needs to appear in five places it has been typed five
times, and where a helper *does* exist (`is_projectile()`, `Drawer::calculate_sprite_origin`,
`ResolutionManager::convert_ivec_to_resolution`) the call sites re-implement it instead
of calling it — in one case shadowing the free function with a local variable of the
same name. Three of the copy sets have already diverged into live defects: `Projectile`'s
hand-written "is a structure" test omits the two ramp types that `is_structure()` lists,
so projectiles fly through the ramp in `king_of_the_hill.json`; `ProjectileMist` was
copy-pasted from `ProjectileSpray` and still declares itself `SPRAY`, which makes the
whole `projectile_mist_*` half of the collision enum unreachable; and `triangles_intersect`
hand-unrolled the edge loop its twin `rectangles_rotated_intersect` writes properly,
testing 4 of 9 edge pairs. On the dead-code side, the shipped math library carries
roughly 490 lines of commented-out source — 272 of `ericson_math.cpp`'s 788 and 165 in
one block of `matt_math.cpp` — and `engine/render/drawer.cpp` exists almost entirely to
provide three protected helpers nobody calls, one of which the game re-implements. What
surprised me most is how much of the duplication sits *in the engine*, not the game:
`TextureObject` and `AnimationObject` are the same five draw overloads twice, `Drawer`
duplicates `Weapon`, and `viewport_manager.h` hardcodes the paint-shooter's sprite-sheet
name in a public engine header.

### Themes

- Where a helper predicate exists, the call sites re-type its body instead of calling it — `collision_object_type.h` defines seven inline predicates and four of them have zero callers while their disjunctions appear verbatim at five other sites.
- Copy-paste has already produced live defects, not just maintenance debt: the ramp omission, the `SPRAY`-labelled mist, and the truncated triangle edge loop are all "the copy was edited and the original was not".
- The five projectile subclasses and the five weapon subclasses are one class each, parameterised by a `details` constant; the per-subclass files exist to hold a constructor and a byte-identical `is_colliding`.
- Menu pages are the largest copy set in the repo: twelve byte-identical `draw()` bodies, six hand-written widget-navigation rings, and four `*_menu_consts` namespaces re-declaring the same fonts, shadow offsets and sound names.
- The engine ships public API with no caller anywhere in the repository — a `// TODO: Implement this function` stub, three `Drawer` helpers, two Ericson primitives — which is exactly the surface a stranger reads first.
- Large blocks of commented-out code sit inside the two files a new contributor to MattMath must read, including a 165-line commented `Matrix<T>` implementation and a 152-line commented transcription of the Ericson source.
- Constants that belong in one place are spelled in several: `"sprite_sheet_1"` at 25+ sites including a public engine header, `{1920, 1080}` in five, and the resolution↔integer-vector table twice across two targets.

---

#### Add the ramp collision types to Projectile's structure test

- **File:** `game/objects/projectile.cpp:96-99`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T4 (duplication is the opposite of clarity at scale)

**What:** `Projectile` hand-writes its own "is this a structure" disjunction and omits `structure_ramp_left` / `structure_ramp_right`, which the shared `is_structure()` helper two files away does list, so projectiles never collide with ramps.

**Evidence:**

`game/objects/projectile.cpp:94-104` (and the identical copy at `:120-130`):

    CollisionObjectType other_type = other->collision_object_type();

    bool structure_collision =
        other_type == CollisionObjectType::structure ||
        other_type == CollisionObjectType::structure_paintable ||
        other_type == CollisionObjectType::structure_jump_through;

    if (structure_collision)
	{
		return true;
	}

`game/objects/collision_object_type.h:73-80` — the helper that exists for this:

    inline bool is_structure(CollisionObjectType type)
    {
    	return type == CollisionObjectType::structure ||
    		type == CollisionObjectType::structure_paintable ||
    		type == CollisionObjectType::structure_jump_through ||
    		type == CollisionObjectType::structure_ramp_left ||
    		type == CollisionObjectType::structure_ramp_right;
    }

**Why it matters:** `game/content/levels/king_of_the_hill.json:258-272` defines
`mountain_level_1_ramp_east` with `"collision_type": "STRUCTURE_RAMP_RIGHT"`, and
`game/objects/level_object_builder.cpp:134-136` turns it into a `Structure` carrying
`CollisionObjectType::structure_ramp_right`. `Level::update` pairs collision objects at
`game/objects/level.cpp:299` (`if (object->is_colliding(object_2.get()))`); the projectile
is the `object`, and its `is_colliding` (e.g. `game/objects/projectile_spray.cpp:52-58`)
returns false immediately because `is_matching_collision_object_type` rejects the ramp.
The other direction is dead too — `Structure::is_colliding` at `game/objects/structure.cpp:40-43`
returns `false` unconditionally. So every shot fired at the King of the Hill ramp passes
straight through it: no deletion, no paint, no damage falloff. Players collide with the
ramp correctly (`Player::is_matching_collision_object_type` at `game/objects/player.cpp:151-156`
*does* call `is_structure`), which is what makes the two behaviours inconsistent.

**Remedy:** Replace both hand-written disjunctions in `projectile.cpp` with `is_structure(other_type)`, and decide deliberately whether a ramp deletes a projectile.

#### Test all nine edge pairs in triangles_intersect

- **File:** `engine/math/matt_math.cpp:398-405`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T9 (built code must meet library standard)

**What:** `triangles_intersect` hand-unrolls the edge-crossing loop to four of the nine edge pairs, where its structural twin `rectangles_rotated_intersect` writes the full nested loop, so two overlapping triangles whose only boundary crossings involve the third edge of either are reported as not intersecting.

**Evidence:**

`engine/math/matt_math.cpp:393-405`:

    		// get edges of each triangle
    		std::vector<Segment> a_edges = a.edges();
    		std::vector<Segment> b_edges = b.edges();

    		// check if any of the edges intersect
    		for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++)
    		{
    			if (segments_intersect(a_edges[i], b_edges[0]) ||
    				segments_intersect(a_edges[i], b_edges[1]))
    			{
    				return true;
    			}
    		}

`engine/math/matt_math.cpp:646-659` — the same algorithm, written correctly:

    		// check if any of the edges of one rectangle intersect the other
    		std::vector<Segment> a_edges = a.edges();
    		std::vector<Segment> b_edges = b.edges();

    		for (const Segment& edge : a_edges)
    		{
    			for (const Segment& other_edge : b_edges)
    			{
    				if (segments_intersect(edge, other_edge))
    				{
    					return true;
    				}
    			}
    		}

**Why it matters:** `Triangle::edges()` (`engine/math/matt_math.cpp:3496-3505`) returns
`[p0p1, p1p2, p2p0]`, so pair `(a_edges[2], *)` and `(*, b_edges[2])` are never tested —
5 of 9. Concrete false negative: `a` = `Triangle((100,5), (0,4.9), (-100,5))` (the long
horizontal side is `a_edges[2]`) and `b` = `Triangle((5,10), (0,0), (10,0))` (the two
slanted sides are `b_edges[0]` and `b_edges[2]`). The horizontal side of `a` slices
through `b`, but no vertex of either lies inside the other, so the containment checks at
`:385-391` fail and the only crossings are on `(a2,b0)` and `(a2,b2)` — both unchecked.
`triangles_intersect` returns false for two plainly overlapping triangles. The function is
public MattMath API reached by `Triangle::intersects(const Triangle&)`, `quads_intersect`
and `triangle_quad_intersect`, and `tests/math/math_tests.cpp:601-628` passes because every
one of its six cases is a vertex-containment case. The game does not currently build two
triangle shapes that get compared (`Structure::is_colliding` returns false), so no gameplay
path reaches it today — but PHILOSOPHY makes the primitive itself the deliverable.

**Remedy:** Replace the unrolled loop with the nested range-for the rotated-rectangle version already uses, and add a test with the edge-crossing, no-containment configuration.

`game/objects/projectile_mist.cpp:19-22`:

    	DiffusingProjectile(velocity, team, player_num, team_colour,

#### Collapse the six verbatim copies of is_colliding

- **File:** `game/objects/projectile_spray.cpp:52-83`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T4

**What:** The narrow-phase `is_colliding` body is byte-for-byte identical in all five projectile subclasses and near-identical in `Player`, and a seventh partial copy sits in `PaintTile`.

**Evidence:** After substituting the class name, the bodies at
`projectile_spray.cpp:52-83`, `projectile_mist.cpp:52-83`, `projectile_jet.cpp:50-81`,
`projectile_rolling.cpp:48-79` and `projectile_ball.cpp:51-82` hash identically
(`md5 9162b38b8d942482fc9e3a951ea3df28`). The shared text:

    	// type check
    	if (!this->is_matching_collision_object_type(other))
    	{
    		return false;
    	}

    	// aabb check
    	if (!this->shape()->AABB_intersects(other->shape()))
    	{
    		return false;
    	}
    	else // AABBs are intersecting
    	{
    		// if the other object is a rectangle, then we have a collision
    		// since the AABB check passed
    		ShapeType other_shape_type = other->shape()->shape_type();
    		if (other_shape_type == ShapeType::rectangle)
    		{
    			return true;
    		}
    	}

    	// narrow phase check
    	if (this->shape()->intersects(other->shape()))
    	{
    		return true;
    	}

    	return false;

`game/objects/player.cpp:157-194` is the same body with a dead-state guard prepended;
`game/objects/paint_tile.cpp:63-88` is the same body with the type check dropped.

**Why it matters:** The "AABB hit and the other shape is a rectangle means a hit" shortcut
is a real correctness assumption about the broad/narrow-phase split, and it is currently
asserted in seven places. Fixing or tightening it — for instance when a non-rectangular
projectile is added, at which point the shortcut is wrong for *this* shape rather than the
other one — means finding and editing all seven. PHILOSOPHY places broad phase, narrow
phase and manifolds in `engine/collision/`, which today contains only `partitioner.cpp`;
this body is the engine's narrow-phase entry point living seven times in game code.

**Remedy:** Hoist the body into one function (engine-side, taking two `Shape*`), and let each subclass supply only its type filter.

#### Delete or use the collision_object_type predicates

- **File:** `game/objects/collision_object_type.h:29-71`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T4

**What:** Four of the seven inline predicates in this header have no caller anywhere in the repository, while their exact bodies are typed out inline at five other sites — including one where a local `bool` shadows the free function of the same name.

**Evidence:** `grep` over `engine/ game/ samples/ tests/` finds definitions but no calls for
`is_player` (`:29`), `is_dead_player` (`:35`), `is_team_a_projectile` (`:55`) and
`is_team_b_projectile` (`:64`). `is_projectile` (`:41`) also has no call; instead:

`game/objects/level.cpp:687-700` re-types it *and shadows it*:

    		CollisionObjectType type = object->collision_object_type();

    		bool is_projectile =
    			type == CollisionObjectType::projectile_spray_team_a ||
    			type == CollisionObjectType::projectile_spray_team_b ||
    			...
    			type == CollisionObjectType::projectile_mist_team_b;
    		if (is_projectile)

`game/objects/structure_paintable.cpp:56-67` re-types the same ten terms as
`is_offensive_projectile`. `game/objects/paint_tile.cpp:97-101` and `:105-109` re-type
`is_team_a_projectile` / `is_team_b_projectile`; `game/objects/player.cpp:212-217` and
`:223-228` re-type them again.

**Why it matters:** Adding a sixth projectile type means editing six places, and the
compiler helps with none of them — a missed site makes the new projectile invisible to
paint tiles, or uncounted in the debug overlay, or unable to damage a player. The local
`bool is_projectile` in `level.cpp` is the sharpest signal: the author reached for the
name, got a variable, and wrote the body out rather than noticing the function was
already in scope from the same header.

and `MTextDropShadow` — no focus, no navigation, no button; the focus concept lives
game-side in `game/states/menu_highlight.h`.

**Why it matters:** PHILOSOPHY, UI: "The engine ships a small widget set … with the two
things every controller game needs solved once: focus, and navigation between widgets
(stick/d-pad movement, per-viewport focus for split-screen)." Neither exists, so the

#### Stop duplicating the resolution table in Save

- **File:** `game/save.cpp:134-174`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T4

**What:** `Save` carries verbatim copies of `ResolutionManager`'s two resolution conversion tables because the engine's versions are private, so the mapping from `ScreenResolution` to pixels exists twice across two build targets.

**Evidence:** `game/save.cpp:158-174`:

    Vector2I Save::convert_resolution_to_ivec(
        ScreenResolution resolution) const
    {
        switch (resolution)
        {
        case ScreenResolution::s_1280_720:
            return {1280, 720};
        case ScreenResolution::s_1920_1080:
            return {1920, 1080};
        case ScreenResolution::s_2560_1440:
            return {2560, 1440};
        case ScreenResolution::s_3840_2160:
            return {3840, 2160};
        default:
            return {-1, -1};
        }
    }

`engine/render/resolution_manager.cpp:48-64` is the same function, and
`game/save.cpp:134-157` duplicates `engine/render/resolution_manager.cpp:153-176`.
`engine/render/resolution_manager.h:28-37` declares both as `private`.

**Why it matters:** Adding a resolution (1366x768, ultrawide) requires editing
`engine/render/resolution_manager.cpp` and `game/save.cpp` and hoping. If they diverge,
`Save::load_from_json` (`game/save.cpp:28-29`) resolves the saved pixel pair to one
enumerator while `ResolutionManager::set_resolution(Vector2I)` resolves it to another —
the game would launch at a resolution its own save file does not describe. The
duplication exists purely because the engine hid an obviously reusable mapping.

**Remedy:** Make the conversions public (or static) on `ResolutionManager` and have `Save` call them; the game should not know pixel counts at all.

#### Fix the fall-through in calculate_viewport that all_viewports depends on

- **File:** `engine/render/viewport_manager.cpp:143-233`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T4

**What:** The four layout blocks in `calculate_viewport` are copy-pasted and none of them terminates its `case`, so an out-of-range `player_num` silently falls through to the next layout's table — and `all_viewports()` relies on that by asking for viewport 4.

**Evidence:** `engine/render/viewport_manager.cpp:155-197` (each inner `default:` is
`break`, and the enclosing `case` has no `break` or `return` after it):

    	case ScreenLayout::two_player:
    		switch (player_num)
    		{
    		case 0:
    			...
    			return result;
    		case 1:
    			...
    			return result;
    		default:
    			break;
    		}
    	case ScreenLayout::three_player:
    		switch (player_num)
    		{

`engine/render/viewport_manager.cpp:87-91`:

    		// Add a 4th viewport if there are 3 players
    		if (player_count == 3)
    		{
    			result.push_back(this->player_viewport(4));
    		}

**Why it matters:** Reachable path: a 3-player match (`GameLevel::build_and_enter_level`
sets `ScreenLayout::three_player` at `game/states/game_states.cpp:133-134`) then a pause,
results or end menu. `MenuPage::draw_mobject_in_viewports`
(`game/states/menu_page.cpp:104-118`) takes `all_viewports()` — four entries — and for
each index `i` calls `apply_player_viewport(i, ...)` and then
`widget->draw(sprite_batch, viewports[i])`. For `i == 3`: `calculate_viewport(three_player, 3)`
falls through to the `four_player` table and returns the *bottom-right* quadrant, which
is already player 1's viewport in a three-player layout, so that quadrant is drawn twice;
meanwhile `viewports[3]` came from `player_viewport(4)`, which falls all the way to the
`default:` fullscreen branch at `:227-232`, giving `Camera` translation `(0, 0)`
(`engine/math/matt_math.cpp:4093-4098`) instead of the quadrant's origin. Net effect: the
genuinely empty top-right quadrant never receives the menu, and the bottom-right quadrant
gets a second, half-screen-offset copy of it drawn over the correct one. MSVC `/W4` does
not diagnose switch fall-through, so `/WX` did not catch this.

**Remedy:** Terminate every `case` in `calculate_viewport` (`break` into the shared fullscreen default), then give `all_viewports()` an explicit way to name the unused quadrant rather than an out-of-range index.

#### Link the engine library in the assets test instead of compiling its sources

- **File:** `tests/assets/CMakeLists.txt:6-11`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY "Targets and layout"

**What:** `AssetsTests` lists two engine `.cpp` files as its own sources, producing a second compilation of engine code with different flags and a different dependency closure from the one the game links.

**Evidence:** `tests/assets/CMakeLists.txt:6-19`:

    add_executable(AssetsTests
        asset_manifest_loader_tests.cpp
        test_main.cpp
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/engine/assets/asset_manifest_loader.cpp"
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/engine/assets/json_loader.cpp"
    )
    target_include_directories(AssetsTests PRIVATE
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}"
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/external/rapidjson/include"
    )
    target_link_libraries(AssetsTests PRIVATE
        doctest::doctest
        artattack_settings
    )

`tests/math/CMakeLists.txt:8-12` does it the way the document asks, linking `MattMath`.

**Why it matters:** PHILOSOPHY, Targets and layout: "Tests link libraries, never
`#include` implementation files." The intent behind that line — the tested artefact is
the artefact that ships — is defeated the same way here. Concretely: the day
`asset_manifest_loader.cpp` gains an include of anything else in `engine/`, this target
stops linking and the fix will be to append another engine `.cpp` to the list, growing
the divergence. It also means `AssetsTests` never proves that `ArtAttackEngine` itself
links. The comment at `:3-5` states the reason (avoiding DirectXTK), which is a real cost
— but it is an argument for splitting the library, not for a second build of its sources.

**Remedy:** Either link `ArtAttackEngine`, or promote the device-free part of `assets/` to its own static library that both the engine and the test link.

- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T4

**What:** Two `else if` branches sit after chains that already cover their conditions, so neither can execute — and both hide a `throw new std::exception(...)`, which throws a pointer.

**Evidence:** `game/states/menu_input.cpp:50-72`:
