#### Ship the wave bank the game requires, or the pipeline that rebuilds it

- **File:** `.gitignore:365-368`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** ARCHITECTURE/A game project ("`content/` — definitions, levels, tuning, assets")

**What:** The only audio file the game loads, `sound_bank_1.xwb`, is excluded from the
repository by `.gitignore`, and so are the `.wav` files it is built from, so a fresh clone
produces a game that stops at startup and cannot be repaired from the repo.

**Evidence:**

    .gitignore:365-368
    # Audio files
    *.wav
    *.xwb
    *.mp3

    game/content/manifest.json:32-38
            {
                "kind": "sound_bank",
                "directory": "./sounds/",
                "names": [
                    "sound_bank_1"
                ]
            }

    engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:167-181
        const std::string wave_bank_path = directory + name + ".xwb";
        ...
            throw std::runtime_error(
                "Failed to load wave bank: " + wave_bank_path);

`git ls-files game/content/sounds` lists `sound_bank_1.json`, `sound_bank_1/XWBTool.exe` and
`sound_bank_1/cmd.txt` — no `.xwb` and no `.wav`. `git status --ignored` confirms both are
present locally and ignored.

**Why it matters:** The reachable path is exact: `game/main.cpp:74` calls
`app.load_manifest(MANIFEST_PATH)`; `ResourceLoader::load_manifest` (resource_loader.cpp:76-86)
walks the entry of kind `sound_bank`; that dispatches to `load_sound_bank`
(resource_loader.cpp:64-71, 164-186); the `WaveBank` constructor throws on the missing file;
the `runtime_error` reaches `main.cpp:93` and the process exits 1 with a message box. The
committed `XWBTool.exe` cannot rebuild the bank either, because the 24 `.wav` inputs its own
`cmd.txt` names are ignored by the same rule. Nobody but the author can run the game the engine
exists to prove.

**Remedy:** Commit `sound_bank_1.xwb` (or the `.wav` sources plus a build step that produces it)
and narrow the audio ignore rule to whatever it was actually protecting.

#### Stop mirroring 320 MB of content before every relink

- **File:** `game/CMakeLists.txt:84-99`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** T10 ("Build time is iteration time… a build-time regression is a defect")

**What:** The content target content-compares and copies all of `game/content/` into the output
directory on every build, including 147 MB of `.wav` source material and three toolchain `.exe`s
the game never opens.

**Evidence:**

    game/CMakeLists.txt:84-98
    add_custom_target(artattack_content ALL)
    add_custom_command(TARGET artattack_content POST_BUILD
        COMMAND "${CMAKE_COMMAND}" -E copy_if_different
            "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/content/manifest.json"
            "$<TARGET_FILE_DIR:ArtAttackGame>/manifest.json"
        VERBATIM
    )
    foreach(content_dir textures levels fonts sounds)
        add_custom_command(TARGET artattack_content POST_BUILD
            COMMAND "${CMAKE_COMMAND}" -E copy_directory_if_different
                "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/content/${content_dir}"
                "$<TARGET_FILE_DIR:ArtAttackGame>/${content_dir}"
            VERBATIM
        )
    endforeach()
    add_dependencies(ArtAttackGame artattack_content)

Measured on disk: `content/sounds` 294.6 MB (of which `content/sounds/sound_bank_1/` is 147.3 MB
of `.wav` plus `XWBTool.exe`), `content/textures` 20.0 MB (8.1 MB of it `old textures/`),
`content/fonts` 5.8 MB (2.3 MB of it `unuseed fonts/`). Both configured presets already carry a
full copy: `out/build/x64-debug/game` is 575.7 MB, `out/build/x64-release/game` 454.9 MB.

**Why it matters:** `copy_directory_if_different` decides "different" by comparing file contents,
so every build — including a one-line edit that only relinks — reads roughly 320 MB off disk per
preset before the exe is allowed to link, because `add_dependencies` puts the content target
ahead of it. Over half of that byte traffic is for files nothing at runtime opens: the game reads
`./sounds/sound_bank_1.xwb` and `./sounds/sound_bank_1.json` (`resource_loader.cpp:167,184`) and
never touches `sounds/sound_bank_1/`.

**Remedy:** Separate authoring sources from shipped content (e.g. `content/` holds only what the
manifest names, sources move to a sibling directory outside the copy), and copy per-file rather
than per-directory so the build knows what actually changed.

#### The engine/game compile wall the documents promise does not exist

- **File:** `engine/CMakeLists.txt:46-49`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** boundary
- **Tenet:** T5 (compile-time over run-time); CONVENTIONS/Files; ARCHITECTURE/The targets

**What:** The engine's include path is the repository root, which contains `game/`, so an engine
file including a game header compiles cleanly — the exact thing two design documents state is
impossible.

**Evidence:**

    engine/CMakeLists.txt:46-49
    target_include_directories(ArtAttackEngine PUBLIC
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}"
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/external/rapidjson/include"
    )

    CONVENTIONS.md:110-113
    - Include paths are written from the repository root, so every include
      states its module: `#include "engine/render/renderer.h"`. An engine
      file including `"game/..."` is thereby visible at a glance — and fails
      to build (see ARCHITECTURE.md).

    ARCHITECTURE.md:14-16
    An arrow reads "links against"; no arrow ever points the other way — an
    engine file including a game header fails to compile, and that is the
    feature (T5).

`${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}` is `C:/VSProjects/ArtAttack`, and `game/objects/player.h` resolves
relative to it. `PUBLIC` include directories apply to the target's own compilation as well as
its consumers.

**Why it matters:** T5's whole argument is that the wall is a build error, not a review comment.
Today it is a review comment. `grep -rn '#include "game/' engine/` returns nothing, so the wall
is currently intact — but nothing stops the next migration commit from leaning a partly-moved
engine file on a game header, and because `ArtAttackEngine` is a static library an unresolved
symbol is not diagnosed when the archive is created; it would surface only when
`ArtAttackSample` links, one target away from the mistake. Header-only or inline game code would
not fail even then.

**Remedy:** Give the engine an include root that does not contain `game/` (per-target include
roots, e.g. sources under an `include/` prefix), or amend CONVENTIONS.md:110-113 and
ARCHITECTURE.md:14-16 to say review enforces the direction and the compiler does not.

#### Replace `CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR` — it breaks the moment the engine becomes a submodule

- **File:** `engine/CMakeLists.txt:47-48`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** ARCHITECTURE/The build; ARCHITECTURE/A game project

**What:** Every path in the build is written against `CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR`, the *top-level* source
directory, so the whole project stops configuring the moment it is added to another project with
`add_subdirectory`.

**Evidence:** Ten uses across five files:

    engine/CMakeLists.txt:47        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}"
    engine/CMakeLists.txt:48        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/external/rapidjson/include"
    engine/math/CMakeLists.txt:14   target_include_directories(MattMath PUBLIC "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}")
    game/CMakeLists.txt:65          "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/external/rapidjson/include"
    game/CMakeLists.txt:105         -P "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/seed_save.cmake"
    tests/assets/CMakeLists.txt:9   "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/engine/assets/asset_manifest_loader.cpp"
    tests/assets/CMakeLists.txt:10  "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/engine/assets/json_loader.cpp"
    tests/assets/CMakeLists.txt:13  "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}"
    tests/assets/CMakeLists.txt:14  "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/external/rapidjson/include"
    tests/core/CMakeLists.txt:11    target_include_directories(CoreTests PRIVATE "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}")

**Why it matters:** ARCHITECTURE's premise is that a game project is "an ordinary C++ application
that links two static libraries" and that starting a game is copying `samples/minimal/`. The
first stranger who vendors this engine into their own tree and calls
`add_subdirectory(external/artattack-engine)` gets `CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR` pointing at *their* root:
`ArtAttackEngine`'s public include directory becomes their project root, the rapidjson path does
not exist, and `AssetsTests` cannot find the two `.cpp` files it compiles. The root file also
calls `enable_testing()` and `add_subdirectory(tests/...)` unconditionally, so an embedding
project is forced to acquire doctest and build this project's tests.

**Remedy:** Use `PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR` (or `ArtAttack_SOURCE_DIR`) throughout, and guard
`enable_testing()`/the test subdirectories behind `PROJECT_IS_TOP_LEVEL` or a `BUILD_TESTING`
option.

#### Guard the MSVC-only flags in the shared settings target

- **File:** `cmake/settings.cmake:9-21`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** ARCHITECTURE/The build ("the eventual second platform… cannot be reached from a `.sln`")

**What:** `artattack_settings` applies `/W4 /WX /permissive- /sdl` and `WIN32 _WINDOWS`
unconditionally, so any compiler that is not MSVC or clang-cl fails on the first translation
unit.

**Evidence:**

    cmake/settings.cmake:9-21
    target_compile_options(artattack_settings INTERFACE
        /W4          # highest regular warning level
        /WX          # warnings are errors, zero suppressions
        /permissive- # standards conformance mode
        /sdl         # additional security checks
    )

    target_compile_definitions(artattack_settings INTERFACE
        UNICODE _UNICODE
        WIN32 _WINDOWS
        NOMINMAX             # std::min/max, never the Windows.h macros
        WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
    )

**Why it matters:** The stated reason for leaving the `.sln` behind is that a second platform
cannot be reached from one, and every target in the tree links this file. A contributor who
configures with clang or gcc — reachable today, since the presets use the Ninja generator, which
happily drives either — gets `error: unknown argument: '-permissive-'` on every file, with
nothing in the build saying why. The `WIN32`/`_WINDOWS` pair is also already in CMake's default
MSVC flags, so those two lines are dead where they do apply.

**Remedy:** Wrap the options in `$<$<CXX_COMPILER_ID:MSVC>:...>` (or a `if(MSVC)` branch with a
GNU/Clang arm carrying `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`), and drop the redundant `WIN32`/`_WINDOWS`.

#### MattMath is not the independent library the architecture declares

- **File:** `engine/math/CMakeLists.txt:14-18`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** boundary
- **Tenet:** ARCHITECTURE/Modules (`math` | may depend on: **nothing**)

**What:** MattMath links DirectXTK `PUBLIC` and its primary public header includes `<d3d11.h>`
for a type that wraps `D3D11_VIEWPORT`, so the "depends on nothing" library drags the graphics
API into every consumer, including the headless math tests.

**Evidence:**

    engine/math/CMakeLists.txt:14-18
    target_include_directories(MattMath PUBLIC "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}")
    target_link_libraries(MattMath
        PUBLIC Microsoft::DirectXTK
        PRIVATE artattack_settings
    )

    engine/math/matt_math.h:3-5
    #include "SimpleMath.h"
    #include "engine/math/shape_type.h"
    #include <d3d11.h>

    engine/math/matt_math.h:794-798
        Viewport(const D3D11_VIEWPORT& viewport);
        ...
        D3D11_VIEWPORT d3d_viewport() const;
        const D3D11_VIEWPORT* d3d_viewport_ptr() const;

`grep -n "D3D11" engine/math/*.h engine/math/*.cpp` shows `mattmath::Viewport` is the only
reason `<d3d11.h>` is there.

**Remedy:** Move the `D3D11_VIEWPORT` conversions out of `mattmath::Viewport` into the render
module (or a free function in `render/`), drop `<d3d11.h>` from `matt_math.h`, and reduce the
DirectXTK link to what SimpleMath actually needs — then the table entry "math | nothing" becomes
true, and PHILOSOPHY's "everything below the platform edge is testable headlessly" starts
holding for the one library it should hold for first.

#### `AssetsTests` rebuilds engine translation units instead of linking the engine

- **File:** `tests/assets/CMakeLists.txt:6-19`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** testing
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Targets and layout ("Tests link libraries, never `#include` implementation files")

**What:** The assets test target compiles two engine `.cpp` files into itself rather than linking
`ArtAttackEngine`, duplicating part of the engine's source list in a second place.

**Evidence:**

    tests/assets/CMakeLists.txt:6-19
    add_executable(AssetsTests
        asset_manifest_loader_tests.cpp
        test_main.cpp
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/engine/assets/asset_manifest_loader.cpp"
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/engine/assets/json_loader.cpp"
    )
    target_include_directories(AssetsTests PRIVATE
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}"
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/external/rapidjson/include"
    )
    target_link_libraries(AssetsTests PRIVATE
        doctest::doctest
        artattack_settings
    )

The same two files also appear at `engine/CMakeLists.txt:14-15`.

**Why it matters:** The rule exists because a test that rebuilds the code under test is not
testing the artefact that ships — this target has its own include directories, does not link
`MattMath` or DirectXTK, and would compile the same source under different macros if the settings
target ever grew a per-target branch. It is also a divergence waiting to happen: the day
`asset_manifest_loader.cpp` gains a dependency or is split, the engine builds and the test fails
with an unresolved symbol pointing at a file nobody edited. The stated motivation — avoiding "the
engine and everything the engine drags in" — is a symptom of ArtAttackEngine being one
undifferentiated library, not a reason to fork its sources.

**Remedy:** Link `ArtAttackEngine`; if the D3D dependency in the link line is the real obstacle,
that is an argument for promoting `assets` (or the JSON layer) to its own target, not for
compiling engine sources twice.

#### `settings.cmake` claims values were carried over; two were dropped

- **File:** `cmake/settings.cmake:1-4`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** T4 (clarity); T2 (correctness over speed)

**What:** The comment states the compiler settings came across from the replaced solution, but
`/fp:fast` and `/Zc:__cplusplus` were set in all four configurations of the old project file and
appear nowhere in the CMake build.

**Evidence:**

    cmake/settings.cmake:1-4
    # The shared compiler-settings target (docs/design/ARCHITECTURE.md, The
    # build): every real target links artattack_settings, so compiler
    # strictness lives in exactly one place (T5). Values carried over from the
    # solution this build replaced.

    git show 6a15785^:ArtAttack/ArtAttack.vcxproj   (the file this replaced)
    :95   <FloatingPointModel>Fast</FloatingPointModel>
    :98   <LanguageStandard>stdcpp20</LanguageStandard>
    :99   <AdditionalOptions>/Zc:__cplusplus %(AdditionalOptions)</AdditionalOptions>
    (repeated at 119/121/122, 144/147/148, 172/173/175)

**Why it matters:** Dropping `/fp:fast` changes float codegen across a codebase full of exact
`==` comparisons on floats, in a project whose headline value is speed (T8) — it is very likely
the right call, and the previous review argued for it five times, but it is a semantic and
performance change made silently under a comment that says nothing changed. The next person
comparing a profile before and after the CMake conversion will not find the cause here.
`/Zc:__cplusplus` costs nothing today (rapidjson and DirectXTK both read `_MSVC_LANG` on MSVC)
but is the flag that makes `__cplusplus` tell the truth, and any future third-party header will
expect it.

**Remedy:** Either restore the two flags or amend the comment to record which were deliberately
dropped and why.

#### The new-project template opens with an engine-internal vcpkg workaround

- **File:** `samples/minimal/CMakeLists.txt:1-4`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** T4 ("Not a licence for: copy-paste"); ARCHITECTURE/A game project

**What:** The build file ARCHITECTURE names as the thing a stranger copies to start a project
begins with a two-line comment and two `find_package` calls that exist only to work around a
packaging bug in the engine's own dependency, and then links the engine's SDK directly.

**Evidence:**

    samples/minimal/CMakeLists.txt:1-4
    # xaudio2redist first: directxtk's config references Microsoft::XAudio2Redist
    # but does not find it itself.
    find_package(xaudio2redist CONFIG REQUIRED)
    find_package(directxtk CONFIG REQUIRED)

    samples/minimal/CMakeLists.txt:21-25
    target_link_libraries(ArtAttackSample PRIVATE
        ArtAttackEngine
        Microsoft::DirectXTK
        artattack_settings
    )

The identical four-line block appears at `engine/CMakeLists.txt:7-10`,
`engine/math/CMakeLists.txt:4-7` and `game/CMakeLists.txt:1-4` — four verbatim copies.

**Why it matters:** ARCHITECTURE:167 promises "a short `CMakeLists.txt`" and ARCHITECTURE:173-174
a project that "links two static libraries"; ARCHITECTURE:176-178 makes copying
`samples/minimal/` the documented way to start. What is actually copied teaches the new user that a game must know
about xaudio2redist, must call `find_package` for the renderer backend, and must name

- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** ARCHITECTURE/The tree (`content/` — "the manifest, and everything it names: JSON definitions, levels, textures, sounds")

**What:** `game/content/` carries three committed Windows executables, three Publisher documents,
a GIMP source file and four notes files, none of which the manifest names, and all of which the
build ships into the output directory.

**Evidence:** `git ls-files game/content` includes:

    game/content/fonts/MakeSpriteFont.exe            41,416 bytes
    game/content/fonts/cmd.txt
    game/content/levels/close_quarters.pub          113,152 bytes
    game/content/levels/king_of_the_hill.pub        121,344 bytes
    game/content/levels/turebulence.pub             120,832 bytes
    game/content/levels/player_movement_notes.txt
    game/content/save/save_data.txt

and the `cmd.txt` files are the asset pipeline, recorded as prose:

#### Nothing in the repository says how to build it

- **File:** `CMakePresets.json:11-12`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** docs
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/The public face; T10

**What:** There is no README at the repository root, and the only configure preset silently

    CMakePresets.json:9-12
      "binaryDir": "${sourceDir}/out/build/${presetName}",
      "installDir": "${sourceDir}/out/install/${presetName}",

`git ls-files | grep -i readme` returns only `docs/review/README.md` and

#### `vcpkg.json` uses the deprecated `version-string` and makes doctest everyone's dependency

- **File:** `vcpkg.json:2-13`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** T9 ("The bought edge… is declared, not clicked"); ARCHITECTURE/The build

**What:** The manifest declares its version with the deprecated `version-string` field and lists
`doctest` as an unconditional dependency rather than behind a test feature.

**Evidence:**

    vcpkg.json:1-14
    {
      "name": "artattack",
      "version-string": "0.1.0",
      "dependencies": [
        {
          "name": "directxtk",
          "features": [ "xaudio2redist" ]
        },
        "doctest"
      ],
      "builtin-baseline": "d92484ed3c5020c6679d095ad3e5add907887b62"
    }

ARCHITECTURE:60-62 describes this file as naming "DirectXTK and the XAudio2 redistributable";
doctest is a third entry the document does not mention.

**Why it matters:** `version-string` opts the port out of vcpkg's version comparison entirely,
which matters as soon as anything depends on this manifest — the submodule topology the roadmap
describes. Declaring doctest unconditionally means anyone consuming the engine installs a test
framework they do not use, which is the same shape of problem as the unconditional
`add_subdirectory(tests/...)` in the root file.

**Remedy:** Use `"version": "0.1.0"` and move `doctest` under a `"tests"` feature enabled by the
presets that build tests.

---

#### ARCHITECTURE's tree says `external/` holds DirectXTK; it holds only rapidjson

- **File:** `docs/design/ARCHITECTURE.md:105`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** docs
- **Tenet:** ARCHITECTURE/The build

**What:** The tree diagram contradicts the same document's own build section about where
DirectXTK comes from.

**Evidence:**

    ARCHITECTURE.md:105
    ├── external/               third-party source: rapidjson, DirectXTK

    ARCHITECTURE.md:60-62
    - The bought edge (T9) is declared, not clicked: `vcpkg.json` (manifest
      mode) names DirectXTK and the XAudio2 redistributable; header-only
      rapidjson stays vendored in `external/`.

`ls external/` returns `rapidjson` and nothing else; `vcpkg.json:5-10` names directxtk.

**Why it matters:** The tree is described at ARCHITECTURE.md:6-7 as "the authoritative roster of
modules and folders", and this is the first place a stranger looks to answer "where does DirectXTK
come from". Two answers, one document.

**Remedy:** Change line 105 to `third-party source: rapidjson` — the code is right, the document
is wrong.

#### Seed the save file from a target that actually runs, and drop the dead `save_data.txt`

- **File:** `game/CMakeLists.txt:101-107`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** T4 (clarity)

**What:** The save seeding is a `POST_BUILD` on `ArtAttackGame` — the exact pattern the comment
twenty lines above rejects for content — and it seeds a file no code reads.

**Evidence:**

    game/CMakeLists.txt:78-83   (the reasoning applied to content, not to this)
    # Its own target, not a POST_BUILD step on ArtAttackGame: a POST_BUILD only
    # runs when the exe relinks, so editing or adding an asset without touching a
    # source file never reached the build directory - ...

    game/CMakeLists.txt:101-107
    add_custom_command(TARGET ArtAttackGame POST_BUILD
        COMMAND "${CMAKE_COMMAND}"
            "-Dsrc=${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/content/save"
            "-Ddst_parent=$<TARGET_FILE_DIR:ArtAttackGame>"
            -P "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/seed_save.cmake"
        VERBATIM
    )

    cmake/seed_save.cmake:4-6
    if(NOT EXISTS "${dst_parent}/save")
        file(COPY "${src}" DESTINATION "${dst_parent}")
    endif()

`game/content/save/` contains both `save_data.json` and `save_data.txt`, but
`game/directory_consts.h:11` reads only the former:

    const static std::string SAVE_FILE_PATH = "./save/save_data.json";

**Why it matters:** Delete the output `save/` directory (a reasonable thing to do when chasing a
save-file bug) and rebuild without touching a source file: nothing relinks, the `POST_BUILD` does
not run, and the game starts with defaults instead of the seeded file — the identical failure the
content comment describes at length. The stale `save_data.txt` is a leftover of the pre-JSON save
format, and is copied into both output directories on every fresh build.

**Remedy:** Hang the seed step off the existing `artattack_content` target and delete
`game/content/save/save_data.txt`.

<a id="g-sweep-content-data"></a>

## sweep-content-data — Content and data

*Group `sweep-content-data` · 14 findings (1 critical, 3 high, 8 medium, 2 low) · source `review2/raw/sweep-content-data.md`, cross-cutting sweep — no separate verifier, reported as written.*

I read every data file the repo ships (`game/content/manifest.json`, the three
live levels plus the four in `levels/unused/`, `textures/sprite_sheet_1.json`,
`sounds/sound_bank_1.json`, `sounds/unused/wave_bank_1.json`,
`save/save_data.json`, `samples/minimal/content/manifest.json`), every loader
that reads one (`engine/assets/json_loader.cpp`, `asset_manifest_loader.cpp`,
`sprite_sheet_loader.cpp`, `sound_bank_loader.cpp`, `resource_loader.cpp`,
`game/objects/level_loaded_info.cpp`, `level_object_builder.cpp`,
`game/save.cpp`), the three tuning headers, and the build files that stage
content (`game/CMakeLists.txt`, `samples/minimal/CMakeLists.txt`,
`cmake/seed_save.cmake`, `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`). I cross-checked every
`frame_name`, `icon_frame` and `music_name` in the level files against
`sprite_sheet_1.json` and `sound_bank_1.json` with a script, and confirmed the
rapidjson missing-member and wrong-type behaviour by reading the vendored
`document.h` rather than assuming it.

The shape of the problem is a **split personality between two halves of the same
data path**. One half is genuinely finished: `asset_manifest_loader.cpp` checks
every read and names the file and the group, `AssetEntry`/`AssetManifest` are
documented, `Stage`/`StageList` really did delete the `LevelStage` enum so
adding a level is a `.json` plus a manifest line, and there is a unit test.
The other half — the two sibling loaders in the *same folder*, `LevelLoadedInfo`,
and every weapon/projectile/player number — is untouched: unchecked
`operator[]`, tuning frozen into headers, and vocabularies the rename passes
walked past. The manifest loader's own comment (`asset_manifest_loader.cpp:12-16`)
names the exact hazard its two neighbours still have, in the same commit's
module.

The single biggest surprise was arithmetic: the build stages **178 files and
336 MB** of `content/` beside the exe on every build, of which the manifest
names **14 files and 160 MB**. From a clean clone it is 153 files staged, 13
named. Three third-party EXEs (`texconv.exe`, `MakeSpriteFont.exe`,
`XWBTool.exe`), 355 KB of Microsoft Publisher level sketches, `unuseed fonts/`,
`old textures/` and `levels/unused/` all get copied next to the game. The second
surprise was that the conventions pass that renamed `CollisionObjectType`'s
enumerators to `snake_case` (commit `dcd8f6f`) stopped at the `.cpp` boundary:
the JSON still says `"STRUCTURE_JUMP_THROUGH"`, so the file and the loader no
longer read continuously — which is the one thing CONVENTIONS/Data exists to
guarantee. And the wave bank the game cannot start without is still gitignored,
with no README anywhere in the repo to say so.

### Themes

- Validation is per-file, not per-module: the manifest loader is exemplary and
  its two siblings in `engine/assets/` were left exactly as they were, so the
  engine's asset boundary has one hardened door and two open ones.
- rapidjson's `operator[]`/`GetX()` degrade three different ways under NDEBUG —
  `GetFloat()` → `0.0`, `GetBool()` → `false`, `GetString()` → `nullptr` — and
  the codebase reaches for all three unchecked, so identical-looking code is
  variously silent, wrong, or a crash.
- The four conventions passes renamed code and did not touch data, leaving
  enumerator, registry-key and abbreviation spellings in JSON that no longer
  match the C++ they map to.
- T7 is half-delivered: level *geometry* is data, level *tuning* (weapon damage,
  projectile lifetime, player gravity) is C++ aggregate initialisers in headers,
  and PHILOSOPHY states the finished property as if it held.
- Content is treated as "the whole folder" rather than "what the manifest
  names", so dead weight, source assets and asset-pipeline tools flow through
  the build into the runtime directory.
- Cross-file references (`icon_frame` → sprite frame, `music_name` → wave)
  happen to be consistent today, and nothing anywhere checks them; the failure
  surfaces mid-menu rather than at load.
- Nothing in `tests/` reads a single shipped content file, so "adding a level
  rebuilds nothing" also means "adding a broken level is caught by nobody".

---

#### Check every JSON member in the engine's sprite-sheet and sound-bank loaders

- **File:** `engine/assets/sprite_sheet_loader.cpp:16-51`, `engine/assets/sound_bank_loader.cpp:53-78`
- **Severity:** critical
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6 (loud failure), T2 (correctness over speed)

**What:** Both engine loaders read JSON members with rapidjson's unchecked
`operator[]` and `GetX()`, so a missing `"name"` key yields `std::string(nullptr)`
in a Release build — the exact hazard their sibling `asset_manifest_loader.cpp`
was written to avoid, documented in a comment eight lines from the top of the
same folder.

**Evidence:**

`engine/assets/sprite_sheet_loader.cpp:16-23`:

    std::string name = frame["name"].GetString();
    Vector2F origin = Vector2F::ZERO;
    bool rotated = false;
    RectangleI source_rectangle(
        frame["position"]["x"].GetInt(),
        frame["position"]["y"].GetInt(),
        frame["size"]["w"].GetInt(),
        frame["size"]["h"].GetInt());

`engine/assets/sound_bank_loader.cpp:53-54` and `:76-78`:

    std::string name = effect["name"].GetString();
    std::string wave = effect["wave"].GetString();
    ...
            doc["waves"],
            doc["sound_effect_instances"],
            doc["create_effect_instance_for_each_wave"].GetBool());

and `engine/assets/asset_manifest_loader.cpp:12-16`, the sibling's comment:

    // rapidjson's operator[] asserts on a missing member and GetArray() asserts
    // on the wrong type - a crash in debug and undefined behaviour in release.
    // The manifest is the one file a person edits by hand to add an asset, so
    // every read below goes through these instead and a typo comes back as a
    // sentence naming the file and the group it was in (T6).

**Why it matters:** I read the vendored rapidjson to pin the consequence rather
than assert it. `operator[]` on a missing member (`external/rapidjson/include/rapidjson/document.h:1225-1254`)
hits `RAPIDJSON_ASSERT(false)` — `assert()` by default (`rapidjson.h:437`), compiled
out under `NDEBUG`, which CMake's `CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELEASE` supplies for the
`x64-release` preset — and returns a placement-new'd `GenericValue()`. That
default ctor is `data_() { data_.f.flags = kNullFlag; }` (`document.h:690`), i.e.
a zeroed payload. `GetString()` (`:1853`) then calls `DataString()` (`:2107`),
which for a non-inline flag returns `data.s.str` — **a null pointer**. So
`std::string name = effect["name"].GetString();` constructs a `std::string` from
`nullptr`: undefined behaviour, an access violation in practice. The same path
gives `GetFloat()` → `0.0` and `GetBool()` → `false`, silently. Reachable by the
documented authoring workflow ("adding a weapon or a level-object type edits
JSON", T7) — and `game/content/sounds/unused/wave_bank_1.json` is a file already
in the tree that would take the `create_effect_instance_for_each_wave` branch,
because it has no such key. This is now *engine* code offered to strangers, so a
stranger's typo in their own sprite sheet is a crash with no message.

**Remedy:** Move the `require_member`/`require_array`/`require_string` helpers out
of `asset_manifest_loader.cpp`'s anonymous namespace into a shared internal
header and route both loaders through them.

#### Stop reading a level's sound block unchecked; the class's own comment understates the debt

- **File:** `game/objects/level_loaded_info.cpp:90-101`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6

**What:** `LevelLoadedInfo` grew a checked `required_string` for `display_name`
and `icon_frame` on the grounds that those are "the keys a person adding a stage
has to write by hand", but `sound.sound_bank_name` and `sound.music_name` are
hand-written per level too and are read with a raw `GetString()` that returns
`nullptr` under NDEBUG.

**Evidence:**

`game/objects/level_loaded_info.cpp:90-97`:

    std::string LevelLoadedInfo::sound_bank_name() const
    {
        return this->json_doc_["sound"]["sound_bank_name"].GetString();
    }
    std::string LevelLoadedInfo::music_name() const
    {
        return this->json_doc_["sound"]["music_name"].GetString();
    }

`game/objects/level_loaded_info.h:41-47`:

    // Reads a string the level file must carry, and throws naming the file and
    // the key if it does not. The rest of this class still reaches into the
    // document unchecked - that is the loaders' standing validation debt, and
    // it is not paid here. These two are checked because they are the keys a
    // person adding a stage has to write by hand, so getting one wrong is the
    // likely mistake rather than a corrupt file (T6).

**Why it matters:** The comment draws the line in the wrong place, which is worse
than no line — a reader trusts it. Every one of the three shipped levels carries
a hand-written `"sound"` block (`close_quarters.json:4-9`, and the same in the
other two), and each names a different track. Misspell `music_name` and the
process dies in `std::string(nullptr)` with no message; misspell
`music_volume` and `GetFloat()` quietly returns `0.0` and the level plays
silently. The two failure modes for adjacent keys in the same three-line object
are "crash" and "silence", and neither says which file. The float accessors at
`:48-80` are the milder half of the same problem.

**Remedy:** Route all of `LevelLoadedInfo` through the same checked helpers as
the manifest loader, and delete the comment's claim that only two keys need
checking.

#### Move weapon, projectile and player tuning into data, or amend T7

- **File:** `game/objects/weapon_consts.h:8-171`, `game/objects/projectile_consts.h:7-105`, `game/objects/player_consts.h:19-120`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T7 (data over code)

**What:** Every weapon, projectile and player number is a C++ aggregate
initialiser in a header, so PHILOSOPHY's "Adding a weapon ... edits JSON and a
registration line, and rebuilds nothing" and "Tuning changes rebuild nothing"
are both false today for the only game on the engine.

**Evidence:**

`game/objects/weapon_consts.h:39-53` — one weapon, positionally initialised, field
names in trailing comments:

    static const WeaponDetails DETAILS_SPRAYER =
    {
        { 0.0f, 0.0f },		//offset
        { 70.0f, 30.0f },	//size
        { projectile_consts::DETAILS_SPRAY.size.x / 2.0f, 0.0f },   //nozzle_offset
        0.0f,						//shoot_interval
        1100.0f,                    //starting_vel_length
        0.007f,                              //ammo_usage
        "sprite_sheet_1",               //sheet_name
        "sprayer",                        //frame_name
        SPRAY,         //projectile_type
        "sound_bank_1",                 //sound_bank_name
        "WaterSprayIntoBucket",                  //shoot_sound_name
        1.0f,                           //shoot_sound_volume
    };

against `docs/design/PHILOSOPHY.md:121-124`:

    ### T7. Data over code
    Content is data files; code is machinery. Adding a weapon or a level-object
    type edits JSON and a registration line, and rebuilds nothing.

**Why it matters:** The asymmetry is the tell: level *geometry* is JSON, level
*tuning* is C++. Changing the sprayer's fire rate recompiles 14 of the game's 46
translation units (I computed the transitive include closure: `weapon_consts.h`
→ `weapon.h` → `player.h` → `level.h`) and relinks the exe. The mechanism to fix
it already exists and costs the engine nothing: `ResourceLoader::register_kind`
(`engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:30-34`) is exactly the `map<string, factory>`
the philosophy describes, and `game/main.cpp:60-72` already uses it to teach the
loader what a level is — a `"weapon_definitions"` kind would be the same eight
lines. The data these headers hold is already half in JSON anyway: they spell
`"sprite_sheet_1"`, `"sound_bank_1"` and wave names like
`"WaterSprayIntoBucket"` that only exist because `sound_bank_1.json` says so, and
nothing checks the two agree. `projectile_consts::DETAILS_DEFAULT:23` names
animation strip `"test"`, which does not exist in `sprite_sheet_1.json` (the
strip is `player_test`) — dead today only because nothing references that
constant.

**Remedy:** Add a `weapon`/`projectile` asset kind and move `WeaponDetails` and
`ProjectileDetails` into `content/`, or amend T7 to say tuning is data *for
level-object types only* and name what stays in code.

#### Restore the wave bank to the repository, or say in writing that the game cannot run without it

- **File:** `.gitignore:365-368`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** T6

**What:** `manifest.json` requires `sounds/sound_bank_1.xwb`, `*.xwb` and `*.wav`
are gitignored, so no clone of this repository can start the paint-shooter — and
there is no README, no doc, and no comment anywhere that says so.

**Evidence:**

`.gitignore:365-368`:

    # Audio files
    *.wav
    *.xwb
    *.mp3

`game/content/manifest.json:32-38`:

            {
                "kind": "sound_bank",
                "directory": "./sounds/",
                "names": [
                    "sound_bank_1"
                ]
            }

`engine/assets/resource_loader.cpp:167-181`:

    const std::string wave_bank_path = directory + name + ".xwb";
    std::unique_ptr<WaveBank> wave_bank;
    try { wave_bank = std::make_unique<WaveBank>(...); }
    catch (const std::exception&)
    {
        // DirectXTK's what() is just "WaveBank" - T6 wants the path.
        throw std::runtime_error(
            "Failed to load wave bank: " + wave_bank_path);
    }

**Why it matters:** `git check-ignore -v` confirms both
`game/content/sounds/sound_bank_1.xwb` and every `.wav` under
`sound_bank_1/` are ignored; `git ls-files game/content/sounds` returns only
`sound list.txt`, `sound_bank_1.json`, `sound_bank_1/XWBTool.exe`,
`sound_bank_1/cmd.txt` and `unused/wave_bank_1.json`. The path is deterministic:
`wWinMain` → `app.load_manifest(MANIFEST_PATH)` (`game/main.cpp:74`) → the
`sound_bank` kind → `load_sound_bank` → throw → MessageBox → `return 1`, before
a window has anything in it. The tool that would regenerate the `.xwb` is
committed and its exact command line is preserved
(`game/content/sounds/sound_bank_1/cmd.txt`), but its 24 `.wav` inputs are
ignored too, so the recipe cannot be run either. This was reported against the
pre-split tree and is unchanged; what is new is that the split has now made it
*only* the game's problem — `samples/minimal` needs one tracked `.spritefont`
and runs from a clone — so the engine is demonstrable to a stranger and its
flagship client is not. There is still no README or LICENSE at the repo root.

**Remedy:** Commit the `.xwb` (or take the audio via Git LFS), and add a README
that states how to get a clone into a runnable state.

#### Stage what the manifest names, not the whole content folder

- **File:** `game/CMakeLists.txt:74-98`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** T7, ARCHITECTURE/The build

**What:** The content step copies four whole directories, so every build stages
178 files / 336.4 MB beside the exe when the manifest names 14 files / 160.4 MB
— including three third-party executables, 355 KB of Microsoft Publisher level
sketches, `levels/unused/`, `fonts/unuseed fonts/` and `textures/old textures/`.

**Evidence:**

`game/CMakeLists.txt:74-76` and `:91-98`:

    # The game resolves content relative to its working directory
    # (directory_consts.h), so mirror content/ beside the built exe and it runs
    # from anywhere. The manifest sits at the top of it and names the rest.
    ...
    foreach(content_dir textures levels fonts sounds)
        add_custom_command(TARGET artattack_content POST_BUILD
            COMMAND "${CMAKE_COMMAND}" -E copy_directory_if_different
                "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/content/${content_dir}"
                "$<TARGET_FILE_DIR:ArtAttackGame>/${content_dir}"
            VERBATIM
        )
    endforeach()

**Why it matters:** I measured the tree rather than estimating. Staged: 178
files, 336,378,781 bytes. Manifest-named: 14 files, 160,390,642 bytes. 176.0 MB
is copied for nothing. From a clean clone (no `.wav`s) it is 153 files staged,
13 named, 140 files / 21.6 MB of dead weight. What lands beside the exe includes
`textures/texconv.exe` (944 KB), `fonts/MakeSpriteFont.exe`,
`sounds/sound_bank_1/XWBTool.exe`, three `.pub` Publisher documents totalling
355 KB (one of them misspelt `turebulence.pub`), `player_movement_notes.txt`
("max jump height 200"), a byte-identical duplicate of the shipped
`courier_new_bold_16.spritefont` inside `unuseed fonts/`, and four
`levels/unused/*.json` in a schema the loader can no longer read — all four use
`"level_name"` where the live files use `"display_name"`, so adding one to the
manifest now throws from `required_string` (`level_loaded_info.cpp:17-27`), and
`unused/test_1.json:94` and `:136` use `"STRUCTURE_FLOOR_PAINTABLE"` and
`"STRUCTURE_WALL"`, strings no branch of the builder accepts. Separately,
`copy_directory_if_different` compares equal-sized files by content, so an
unchanged build re-reads the whole tree; PHILOSOPHY (Tests and toolchain) calls a
build-time regression a defect. `samples/minimal/CMakeLists.txt:31-44` names its
one content directory explicitly and is the right shape.

**Remedy:** Delete `unused/`, `unuseed fonts/`, `old textures/`, the `.pub`
sketches and the committed tool EXEs; stage the directories the manifest names,
or generate the copy list from `manifest.json`.

#### Bring the JSON's enumerator spellings in line with the code the rename pass changed

- **File:** `game/content/levels/close_quarters.json:96-97`, `game/objects/level_object_builder.cpp:25-35`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Data, CONVENTIONS/Never

**What:** `dcd8f6f` ("Rename enum types and enumerators — conventions pass 3b of
4") renamed `CollisionObjectType`'s enumerators to `snake_case` and did not touch
the level files, so the data still spells the same enumerators SCREAMING_SNAKE
and the `type` key still spells registry keys PascalCase.

**Evidence:**

`game/content/levels/close_quarters.json:85-98`:

            "name": "boundary_wall_left",
            "type": "Structure",
            ...
            "collision_type": "STRUCTURE",
            "colour": "SADDLE_BROWN"

`game/objects/collision_object_type.h:3-9`:

    enum class CollisionObjectType
    {
        structure,
        structure_paintable,
        structure_jump_through,

`game/objects/level_object_builder.cpp:24-31`:

    std::string collision_type = json["collision_type"].GetString();
    if (collision_type == "STRUCTURE")
    {
        col_type = CollisionObjectType::structure;
    }
    else if (collision_type == "STRUCTURE_JUMP_THROUGH")
    {
        col_type = CollisionObjectType::structure_jump_through;
    }

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS/Data exists for exactly one reason — "so a
definition reads continuously from file to loader" — and after the rename it no
longer does: `"STRUCTURE_JUMP_THROUGH"` in the file, `structure_jump_through` in
the loader, and a hand-written ladder in between whose job is now to translate
between two spellings of one name. CONVENTIONS/Never lists "SCREAMING constants
— screaming means macro, nothing else"; I counted 188 SCREAMING values across
the three live level files (`collision_type` and `colour`), plus 103 PascalCase
`"type"` values naming C++ classes where the table says registry names are
`snake_case`. The rename pass is recorded as complete ("4 of 4"), which means a
future reader will take the current spelling as intended. `git log --oneline
game/content/levels/close_quarters.json` shows the file untouched since `97bf3b1`,
two commits before the rename.

**Remedy:** Lowercase the `type`, `collision_type` and `colour` values in the
three level files and the ladders that read them, in one commit, and note it in
the conventions-pass record.

#### Make the level schema's three closed vocabularies fail the same way

- **File:** `game/objects/level_object_builder.cpp:33-36`, `engine/math/colour.h:314-465`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6

**What:** A level object names three values out of closed sets — `type`,
`collision_type` and `colour` — and a wrong value in each fails differently: two
throw a message that names neither the file nor the object nor the bad string,
and the third silently returns white.

**Evidence:**

`game/objects/level_object_builder.cpp:33-36` (and identically at `:76-79`,
`:142-145`, `:165`, `:185`):

            else
            {
                throw std::exception("Invalid collision type");
            }

`engine/math/colour.h:314` and `:463-465`:

    inline mattmath::Colour colour_from_name(const std::string& name)
    ...
        if (name == "YELLOW_GREEN") return colour_consts::YELLOW_GREEN;
        return colour_consts::WHITE;
    }

**Why it matters:** These are the three keys a person authoring a level types by
hand. Get `colour` wrong and the object renders white with no diagnostic
anywhere — a bug you find by looking at the screen. Get `collision_type` wrong
and the game dies with the six-word string "Invalid collision type", which does
not tell you which of the 34 objects in `turbulence.json` is at fault, or which
of the three level files was being read; `LevelObjectBuilder` never sees the
path, and the `"name"` field that every object carries is not read (see the last
finding). PHILOSOPHY, Content and assets, states the target directly: "unknown
types fail naming the type and file (T6)". Also `std::exception(const char*)` is
an MSVC extension, which puts these eight sites in the way of the cross-platform
goal in Targets and layout. Finally, the `rectangle_tlbr` branch
(`level_object_builder.cpp:46-53` and its verbatim copy at `:89-96`) is dead: I
grepped `game/content/` and no file uses that key, so half the rectangle schema
exists only in code.

**Remedy:** Pass the file path and the object's `name` into the builder and
include both plus the offending string in every throw; make `colour_from_name`
return a failure the caller must handle rather than white.

#### Pick one rectangle encoding across the data files

- **File:** `game/content/textures/sprite_sheet_1.json:6-12`, `game/content/levels/close_quarters.json:89-95`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Data, T4

**What:** The shipped content spells the same concept — an axis-aligned rectangle
— three different ways, and one of the three uses `w`/`h`, abbreviations that are
not on CONVENTIONS' closed allowlist.

**Evidence:**

`game/content/textures/sprite_sheet_1.json:6-12` (animation strips):

            "first_frame":
            {
                "x": 0,
                "y": 1150,
                "w": 52,
                "h": 120
            },

the same file's `sprite_frames` entries, which use nested `position` and `size`
objects (`engine/assets/sprite_sheet_loader.cpp:19-23` reads
`frame["position"]["x"]` and `frame["size"]["w"]`), and
`game/content/levels/close_quarters.json:89-95`:

            "rectangle":
            {
                "x": -100.0,
                "y": 0.0,
                "width": 100.0,
                "height": 7000.0
            },

**Why it matters:** CONVENTIONS/Data says JSON keys follow code-side variable
naming, and CONVENTIONS/Variables closes the abbreviation list at "`dt`, `id`,
`src`, `dst`, `min`, `max`. Everything else earns its letters." `w` and `h` are
off that list, and they sit in the same file as a second spelling (`position` +
`size`) and one directory from a third (`width`/`height`). A person authoring
content has to remember which of three a given file wants, and the loaders
cannot share a `read_rect` helper until they agree. This is the first thing a
stranger writing their own sprite sheet meets.

**Remedy:** Standardise on `x`/`y`/`width`/`height` everywhere and migrate
`sprite_sheet_1.json` and `sprite_sheet_loader.cpp` in one commit.

---

#### Resolve `icon_frame` at load, where the manifest already guarantees the sheet exists

- **File:** `game/main.cpp:60-72`, `game/states/main_menu.cpp:1847`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** correctness
- **Tenet:** T6

**What:** A level's `icon_frame` is copied out of the level file at load and
never checked against the sprite sheet, so a typo becomes a
`std::out_of_range` thrown from a menu update the first time a player scrolls to
that stage.

**Evidence:**

`game/main.cpp:62-70`:

                [&level_infos, &stages](const std::string& directory,
                    const std::string& name)
                {
                    auto info = std::make_unique<LevelLoadedInfo>(
                        (directory + name + ".json").c_str());
                    stages.push_back(Stage{ name, info->display_name(),
                        info->icon_frame() });
                    level_infos.add(name, std::move(info));
                },

`game/states/main_menu.cpp:1846-1848`:

            const Stage& stage = stages->at(static_cast<size_t>(slot));
            this->stage_icon_->set_sprite_frame(stage.icon_frame);
            this->stage_name_->set_text(stage.display_name);

**Why it matters:** `set_sprite_frame` reaches `TextureObject::set_frame`
(`engine/render/texture_object.cpp:37-40`) → `resolve_sprite_frame` →
`NameTable::resolve` (`engine/core/name_table.h:53-62`), which throws
`"no sprite frame named 'x'"`. The path is `MainMenuStageSelect::update` →
`update_stage_select_visuals`, i.e. the player scrolling the stage carousel:
that is caught only by the `try` around `app.run()` in `wWinMain`, so the game
dies mid-menu. PHILOSOPHY, T6: "A missing texture is a launch-time error naming
the file, not an invisible sprite." The fix costs one line and nothing else,
because the mechanism is already documented and already used:
`AssetManifest`'s header says "Walked in order: the file's order is the load
order, so a kind that has to exist before another can be sequenced by moving a
line", and `manifest.json:16-31` already puts `sprite_sheet` above `level`. The
registration lambda above is already calling `info->icon_frame()`; it just does
not resolve it.

**Remedy:** In the `level` kind's lambda, call
`render_resources()->sprite_sheet(...)->resolve_sprite_frame(info->icon_frame())`
and let it throw at load.

#### The game only runs when its working directory is the exe directory, and the build comment says otherwise

- **File:** `game/CMakeLists.txt:74-76`, `game/directory_consts.h:8-12`, `samples/minimal/main.cpp:37`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** docs
- **Tenet:** T4, ARCHITECTURE/A game project

**What:** Every content path is relative to the process working directory and
nothing sets it, so the game fails on `./manifest.json` when launched from any
other directory — while the comment introducing the content step claims the
opposite.

**Evidence:**

`game/CMakeLists.txt:74-76`:

    # The game resolves content relative to its working directory
    # (directory_consts.h), so mirror content/ beside the built exe and it runs
    # from anywhere. The manifest sits at the top of it and names the rest.

`game/directory_consts.h:5-12`:

    // The two paths the game knows before it has read anything. ...
    namespace directory_consts
    {
        const static std::string MANIFEST_PATH = "./manifest.json";
        const static std::string SAVE_FILE_PATH = "./save/save_data.json";
    }

`samples/minimal/main.cpp:37`, the file a new project copies:

            app.load_manifest("./manifest.json");

**Why it matters:** "It runs from anywhere" is precisely wrong: mirroring content
beside the exe makes it run when the *working directory* is the exe directory. I
grepped `engine/`, `game/` and `samples/` for `SetCurrentDirectory`,
`GetModuleFileName` and `std::filesystem::current_path` — the only hits are
inside the two committed third-party EXEs. `out/build/x64-debug/game/ArtAttackGame.exe`
run from a shell at the repo root dies at `read_json_file - cannot open
'./manifest.json'`. Double-clicking in Explorer and the VS CMake debugger both
happen to set the CWD correctly, which is why this has not bitten; a desktop
shortcut with a different "Start in", or any CI invocation, will. The sample is
the new-project template, so the pattern propagates to every project started on
this engine.

**Remedy:** Resolve content against the executable's own directory
(`GetModuleFileNameW` once at startup) or state the working-directory
requirement in the comment instead of contradicting it.

#### Decide where the default save lives — the seeded file and the code disagree

- **File:** `cmake/seed_save.cmake:4-6`, `game/content/save/save_data.json:1`, `game/save.h:12-13`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T7

**What:** A committed `save_data.json` holding one developer's 1920x1080 setting
is seeded beside the exe, while `SaveData`'s member initialisers default to
1280x720 — two defaults for one value, and which one a fresh build gets depends
on whether a `save/` directory happens to exist.

**Evidence:**

`cmake/seed_save.cmake:4-6`:

    if(NOT EXISTS "${dst_parent}/save")
        file(COPY "${src}" DESTINATION "${dst_parent}")
    endif()

`game/content/save/save_data.json` (the whole file):

    {"resolution":{"x":1920,"y":1080},"fullscreen":false}

`game/save.h:10-14`:

    struct SaveData
    {
        artattack::ScreenResolution resolution = artattack::ScreenResolution::s_1280_720;
        bool fullscreen = false;
    };

**Why it matters:** `Save::load_save_file` (`game/save.cpp:50-69`) already
handles a missing file by writing the defaults, so the seed is not needed for
correctness — it exists only to preset a value, and it presets a different one
from the code. A first run therefore starts at 1920x1080 on a machine whose
monitor may be smaller, and the same build with the `save/` directory deleted
starts at 1280x720. The guard tests the *directory*, so deleting only
`save_data.json` also silently switches which default applies. The file is also
mutable user state under version control: any developer who changes resolution
in-game and later copies it back commits their monitor into the repo.
`game/content/save/save_data.txt` (`1920x1080\nfalse`) is a dead predecessor of
the same file, still tracked and still copied.

**Remedy:** Delete `content/save/` and `cmake/seed_save.cmake` and let
`SaveData`'s initialisers be the single default, or keep the seed and make the
code read its values instead of duplicating them.

#### Add a test that parses the content the game ships

- **File:** `tests/assets/CMakeLists.txt:5-11`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category:** testing
- **Tenet:** T5, PHILOSOPHY/Tests and toolchain

**What:** The only content test in the repo builds synthetic manifests in a temp
directory; no test opens `game/content/manifest.json`, the three level files,
`sprite_sheet_1.json` or `sound_bank_1.json`, so a data-only edit is validated by
nothing until someone launches the game.

**Evidence:**

`tests/assets/CMakeLists.txt:5-11`:

    add_executable(AssetsTests
        asset_manifest_loader_tests.cpp
        test_main.cpp
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/engine/assets/asset_manifest_loader.cpp"
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/engine/assets/json_loader.cpp"
    )

`tests/assets/asset_manifest_loader_tests.cpp:11-13`:

        // A manifest on disk, deleted when the test leaves. The loader takes a
        // path, so testing it means writing files - there is no in-memory door in,
        // and adding one for the tests would be a second parse path to keep honest.

**Why it matters:** The whole point of T7 is that content changes without a
rebuild, which also means content changes without any of the compile-time
guarantees T5 buys. `ctest` currently proves the manifest *loader* works and says
nothing about the manifest. I verified by script that today's cross-references
all resolve — every `frame_name` and `icon_frame` in the three levels exists in
`sprite_sheet_1.json`, every `music_name` exists in `sound_bank_1.json` — but
that is luck, not a property: nothing would have caught it, and
`levels/unused/test_1.json` already contains two `collision_type` strings the
builder rejects. A headless "every file the manifest names parses and every name
it references resolves" test needs no device and would run in `tests/assets/`
today.

**Remedy:** Add a test that walks `game/content/manifest.json` and checks each
named file parses and each cross-reference resolves.

#### `directory_consts` is the header CONVENTIONS names twice as the thing not to write

- **File:** `game/directory_consts.h:8-12`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** conventions
- **Tenet:** CONVENTIONS/Constants, CONVENTIONS/Never

**What:** Two SCREAMING_SNAKE constants in a namespace called `*_consts`, which
CONVENTIONS forbids on both counts.

**Evidence:**

`game/directory_consts.h:8-12`:

    namespace directory_consts
    {
        const static std::string MANIFEST_PATH = "./manifest.json";
        const static std::string SAVE_FILE_PATH = "./save/save_data.json";
    }

against `docs/design/CONVENTIONS.md:71-74`:

    - A header full of numeric constants is usually tuning data in the wrong
      place — *which* and *how much* belong in JSON (T7). Constants that stay
      in code live next to the one thing they configure, not in a `consts`
      namespace collecting strays.

and CONVENTIONS/Never: "SCREAMING constants — screaming means macro."

**Why it matters:** The conventions passes renamed enumerators, members and
namespaces and left every `*_consts.h` in `game/` untouched — this one,
`player_consts.h`, `weapon_consts.h`, `projectile_consts.h` and the
`colour_consts` namespace in `engine/math/colour.h`, which is an engine header
sitting in the global namespace. `main.cpp:11` also does `using namespace
directory_consts;` at file scope to reach two strings. Both constants are
`const static std::string` at namespace scope in a header, i.e. internal linkage
and one dynamically-initialised copy per translation unit.

**Remedy:** Make them `inline constexpr std::string_view manifest_path` /
`save_file_path` beside the one place each is used, or fold them into
`ApplicationOptions`.

#### Read the `name` key or delete it — three level files already carry a duplicate

- **File:** `game/content/levels/close_quarters.json:165,210`
- **Severity:** low
- **Category:** design
- **Tenet:** T7

**What:** Every object in every level carries a `"name"`, no loader reads it, and
all three shipped levels contain the same copy-paste duplicate that a
name-aware loader would have caught.

**Evidence:**

`game/content/levels/close_quarters.json:164-166` and `:209-211` — team B's
ceiling still calling itself team A's:

            {
                "name": "spawn_a_ceiling",
                "type": "Structure",
    ...
            {
                "name": "spawn_a_ceiling",
                "type": "Structure",

The second is at x=5700 (team B's side, `:216`), the first at x=0 (`:171`).
`game/objects/level_object_builder.cpp:20` onwards reads `type`,
`collision_type`, `sheet_name`, `frame_name`, `rectangle`, `paintable_faces` and
`colour` — never `name`.

**Why it matters:** `king_of_the_hill.json` and `turbulence.json` have the same
duplicated `spawn_a_ceiling`, which is direct evidence the three files were
produced by copy-paste and nothing has ever read the field that would have
flagged it. The cost is not the duplicate itself — the objects are distinct and
both load — but that the one identifier the schema has is decorative, so the
builder's error messages cannot name the offending object (see the closed-
vocabularies finding above) and no tool can diff two levels by object.

**Remedy:** Thread `name` into `LevelObjectBuilder` and use it in every throw,
and reject duplicates at load; or drop the key from the schema.

<a id="g-sweep-public-face"></a>

## sweep-public-face — headers, docs, teachability

*Group `sweep-public-face` · 18 findings (1 critical, 8 high, 8 medium, 1 low) · source `review2/raw/sweep-public-face.md`, cross-cutting sweep — no separate verifier, reported as written.*

I opened all 50 headers under `engine/`, both sample files, all six `CMakeLists.txt`
and the presets/manifest, and traced every claim back to a call site. The shape of the
problem is **bimodal, and the seam runs exactly along the recent work**. The headers the
CMake/const/handle passes touched — `registry.h`, `name_table.h`, `handle.h`,
`resource_loader.h`, `asset_manifest_loader.h`, `texture_object.h`, `sprite_sheet_object.h`,
`i_game_object.h`, `application.h` — are genuinely excellent: contract, intent, rationale,
and in `asset_manifest_loader.h` a worked example. They are better than most commercial
engine headers. Everything the passes did not touch has *nothing*: `state.h` (a named seam
interface), `visual.h` (the only concrete `GameObject` the engine ships), `widget.h` (the
entire widget set, six types), `partitioner.h`, `moving_object.h`, `text.h`,
`animation_strip.h`, `sprite_frame.h` and the whole of `matt_math.h`'s twenty types carry
no contract at all. So "a stranger starts from the headers" is true for about half the
surface and false for the other half, and the false half contains the two things a first
game needs first: how a state works and how you draw.

What surprised me most is what is missing *around* the code rather than in it. There is no
`README.md` and no licence anywhere in the repository, and `docs/design/ARCHITECTURE.md`'s
authoritative tree lists neither — so the destination as written does not include an entry
point. `CMakePresets.json` requires `$env{VCPKG_ROOT}` and nothing tells anyone that. Second
surprise: `engine/render/device_resources.h` and `engine/core/step_timer.h` are Microsoft's
`DeviceResources.h`/`StepTimer.h` — `git show 3ed124a:ArtAttack/DeviceResources.h` opens with
`namespace DX` — now re-namespaced into `artattack` with no attribution, and they are the
source of the `m_` members, the PascalCase methods and the `interface` keyword that make the
engine's most public class declaration read like a different codebase. Third: the new sample,
which is the standing answer to "how do I start", exercises exactly four engine types and
teaches `FinishCommandList`/`ExecuteCommandList`/`Release` as the way to draw a string.

### The honest answer: what a stranger must read, in what order, today

1. `docs/design/ARCHITECTURE.md` — the only file that says what the targets are. They will
   have to infer the build from `CMakePresets.json` because nothing documents it.
2. `CMakePresets.json` + `vcpkg.json` — to discover they need vcpkg, Ninja, MSVC and
   `VCPKG_ROOT` set. Nothing states this.
3. `samples/minimal/CMakeLists.txt`, `main.cpp`, `hello_state.h`, `hello_state.cpp` — the
   only end-to-end example. ~150 lines, well commented, and the best thing in the repo.
4. `engine/app/application.h` — properly documented; they will get the three-step boot from it.
5. `engine/core/state.h` — 21 lines, zero prose. They must read `state_context.cpp` to learn
   that `transition_to` calls `init()` and destroys the previous state.
6. `engine/render/text.h` → `text_object.h` → `draw_object.h` — three headers to find out
   what arguments a `Text` takes, one of which is undocumented.
7. `engine/math/matt_math.h` — 1150 lines, twenty types, to find `Vector2F` and `Colour`.
8. `engine/render/render_resources.h` and `engine/assets/asset_manifest_loader.h` — both
   excellent — to author `manifest.json`.
9. For anything beyond one string: `engine/core/i_game_object.h`, `engine/render/visual.h`,
   `engine/ui/widget.h` and the paint-shooter's `game/objects/level.cpp`, because the sample
   demonstrates none of it and `widget.h` documents none of it.

**The first three things that stop them:**

1. **They cannot build it.** No README, no prerequisites, no `VCPKG_ROOT`, no licence
   (finding 1).
2. **They cannot start a project outside this tree.** `samples/minimal/` is advertised as the
   thing to copy, but the engine publishes `${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}` as its public include
   directory and exports nothing, so the copy compiles only while it stays a subdirectory of
   this repository (finding 2).
3. **They cannot draw.** The promised `draw_sprite(...)` renderer interface does not exist;
   the sample's `draw()` is five D3D11 concepts and a manual COM `Release()`, and it is the
   only worked example there is (finding 5).

### Themes

- Documentation quality tracks recent commits exactly: everything the handle/const/CMake
  passes touched is exemplary, everything they did not touch has zero prose.
- The repository has no front door — no README, no licence, no stated prerequisites — and
  ARCHITECTURE.md's tree does not plan for one either.
- Third-party code (Microsoft's `DeviceResources`/`StepTimer`, Ericson's collision routines)
  has been absorbed into engine namespaces with no attribution, and it is what sets the house
  style in the most public headers.
- The split moved files without moving vocabulary: this game's team colours and asset names
  now live inside `MattMath` and `ArtAttackEngine` as public API.
- The three seam interfaces have diverged: `GameObject` got `dt`, `const` and documentation;
  `State` got none of them and the sample teaches the old shape.
- New code spells the same concept two ways in the same header — `Registry::handle` beside
  `RenderResources::TextureHandle` — so the conventions pass has not converged.
- The sample is the mechanism PHILOSOPHY relies on to keep the boundary honest, and it
  currently exercises four of the engine's ~50 public types.

---

#### Give the repository a front door: no README, no build instructions, no licence

- **File:** `docs/design/ARCHITECTURE.md:75-109`
- **Severity:** critical
- **Category:** docs
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/The public face

**What:** The repository contains no `README.md`, no licence file, and no statement anywhere
of what is required to build it, and the authoritative tree in ARCHITECTURE.md does not plan
for any of the three.

**Evidence:**

`git ls-files | grep -i 'readme\|licen'` returns exactly one path — `docs/review/README.md`,
which is the old review's narrative. The tree that ARCHITECTURE.md declares authoritative
lists no README and no licence:

    /
    ├── CMakeLists.txt          the root build file: lists the targets, nothing else
    ├── CMakePresets.json       the configurations: debug, release
    ├── vcpkg.json              the bought edge, declared (T9)
    ├── cmake/                  the shared settings target, helper modules
    ├── engine/                 the product
    ...
    └── docs/
        ├── design/             philosophies, conventions, this document
        └── review/             findings against the current code

The one hard prerequisite is stated only as a variable expansion, in `CMakePresets.json:11`:

    "toolchainFile": "$env{VCPKG_ROOT}/scripts/buildsystems/vcpkg.cmake",

**Why it matters:** PHILOSOPHY opens with "intended, eventually, for developers other than
its author" and The public face promises the headers are where a stranger starts. A stranger
never reaches the headers: cloning gives them a tree with no entry point, a configure step
that fails with a CMake toolchain error naming a variable nobody told them to set, and — with
no licence of any kind — no legal permission to use the result even if they get it building.
This is the cheapest finding in the review to fix and the one that gates every other.

**Remedy:** A root `README.md` with prerequisites (vcpkg + `VCPKG_ROOT`, Ninja, MSVC, Windows
SDK), the two preset commands, and a link to the three design docs; a `LICENSE` file; and add
both to ARCHITECTURE.md's tree.

---

#### Stop publishing `${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}` as the engine's public include directory

- **File:** `engine/CMakeLists.txt:46-49`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** build
- **Tenet:** ARCHITECTURE/A game project

**What:** Both library targets publish the *top-level* source directory as their `PUBLIC`
include directory, and neither has `install()` or `export()` rules, so the engine is only
consumable from inside this repository.

**Evidence:**

`engine/CMakeLists.txt:46-49`

    target_include_directories(ArtAttackEngine PUBLIC
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}"
        "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/external/rapidjson/include"
    )

`engine/math/CMakeLists.txt:14`

    target_include_directories(MattMath PUBLIC "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}")

`grep -rn "install(\|export(" --include=CMakeLists.txt --include=*.cmake` over
`engine/ game/ samples/ tests/ cmake/ CMakeLists.txt` returns nothing.

**Why it matters:** `CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR` is the top-level project's source directory, not this
one's. ARCHITECTURE.md says "Starting a game is copying `samples/minimal/`, renaming the
target"; do that outside this tree and add the engine by `add_subdirectory` or `FetchContent`
— the intended submodule topology — and `ArtAttackEngine`'s public include directory resolves
to the *consumer's* root. Every `#include "engine/render/text.h"` then fails unless the
consumer happens to have placed the engine at exactly `<their-root>/engine/`. With no
install/export rules there is no packaged alternative. Nothing in the repository currently
exercises this path, so it has never been caught.

**Remedy:** Use `${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/..` (or `${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}`) with a
`BUILD_INTERFACE`/`INSTALL_INTERFACE` generator expression, and add install/export rules for
`ArtAttackEngine` and `MattMath`.

---

#### Half the public engine headers document no contract at all

- **File:** `engine/core/state.h:1-21`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** docs
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/The public face

**What:** Twenty-two of the fifty headers under `engine/` contain no prose describing what
their types promise, including two of the three named seam interfaces' neighbourhoods and the
entire widget set.

**Evidence:** headers with zero contract documentation, verified by opening each:

    engine/core/state.h              engine/render/visual.h
    engine/core/state_context.h      engine/render/draw_object.h
    engine/core/moving_object.h      engine/render/text.h
    engine/collision/partitioner.h   engine/render/animation_strip.h
    engine/input/connection_state.h  engine/render/sprite_frame.h
    engine/ui/widget.h               engine/render/resolution_manager.h
    engine/math/colour.h             engine/render/camera_tools.h
    engine/math/dimension.h          engine/render/screen_layout.h
    engine/math/shape_type.h         engine/render/screen_resolution.h
    engine/math/matt_math.h          engine/render/rotation_origin.h
    engine/math/collision_tools.h    engine/render/border_thickness.h

`engine/collision/partitioner.h:12-16` is the sharpest single case — public via
`Application::partitioner()` (`engine/app/application.h:122`), two overloads, no contract:

        std::vector<std::pair<int, int>>
            partition(int num_elements, int num_partitions) const;

        std::vector<std::pair<int, int>>
            partition(size_t num_elements, int num_partitions) const;

Only `partitioner.cpp` says the ranges are half-open, that at most `min(num_elements,
num_partitions)` pairs come back (`for (int i = 0; i < num_partitions && i < num_elements;`),
and that `num_partitions == 0` divides by zero at line 8.

**Why it matters:** The public face target says "A stranger starts from the headers, not from
reading the implementation." For these twenty-two they cannot: the only way to learn whether
`partition` returns `[start, end)` or `[start, end]`, or what `MContainer` does with a child
pointer, is to open the `.cpp`. The contrast with `registry.h`, `name_table.h`,
`resource_loader.h` and `asset_manifest_loader.h` — which do this superbly — shows the
standard is reachable; it has just not been applied outside the files the recent passes
touched.

**Remedy:** Treat "no undocumented public header" as the exit condition for the split, and
work the list above in the same style as `registry.h`.

#### `State` was left behind by the `dt` and `const` passes

- **File:** `engine/core/state.h:7-20`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** PHILOSOPHY/Services and lifetimes; Simulation and rendering

**What:** `State` — one of the three interfaces PHILOSOPHY names as the whole seam — still
takes no frame time and still has a non-`const` `draw()`, so the two rules the engine just
spent two commits enforcing on `GameObject` are not enforced on the interface every game
implements first.

**Evidence:**

`engine/core/state.h:7-20`

    class State
    {
    public:
        State() = default;
        virtual ~State() = default;
        virtual void update() = 0;
        virtual void draw() = 0;
        virtual void init() = 0;
        void set_context(StateContext* context);
    protected:
        StateContext* context() const;
    private:
        StateContext* context_ = nullptr;
    };

The consequence is taught by the sample, `samples/minimal/states/hello_state.cpp:53-55`:

        // dt is a pointer because the objects reading it outlive any one
        // frame; the shell rewrites the value behind it every fixed step.
        const float dt = *this->app_->dt();

and `engine/app/application.h:133-134` keeps the shared-state accessor alive to serve it:

        // Seconds the last fixed step covered. A pointer because the objects that
        // read it are built once and outlive any particular frame; the value
        // behind it is rewritten every update.
        const float* dt() const;

**Why it matters:** PHILOSOPHY/Services and lifetimes says "Frame time is a parameter —
`update(float dt)` — not shared state", and `i_game_object.h:27-34` documents at length why
the `const float*` pattern was removed from eleven classes. `State` is the one interface a
first-time user is guaranteed to implement, so the pattern the engine just eliminated is the
first one it teaches. Simulation and rendering likewise says "`draw()` is `const` all the way
down"; `State::draw()` is the top of that chain and is not, so the compiler-enforced pure-read
contract stops one level below the entry point.

**Remedy:** `virtual void update(float dt) = 0;` and `virtual void draw() const = 0;`, then
delete `Application::dt()`.

#### Drawing anything requires D3D11 command lists, and the sample teaches it as the way

- **File:** `samples/minimal/states/hello_state.cpp:62-85`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** api
- **Tenet:** T10

**What:** There is no renderer interface; the smallest possible draw in the engine's own
new-project template requires deferred contexts, `FinishCommandList`, `ExecuteCommandList`
and a manual COM `Release()`.

**Evidence:**

    void HelloState::draw()
    {
        // Drawing goes through a deferred context so it can be recorded off the
        // main thread; with one string there is nothing to spread, so this uses
        // worker 0 and executes its list immediately. A game with a scene's worth
        // of objects fans the same shape across every context the shell created.
        artattack::DeviceResources* device = this->app_->device_resources();
        ID3D11DeviceContext* deferred = device->deferred_context(0);
        SpriteBatch* sprite_batch = this->app_->sprite_batches()->at(0);

        sprite_batch->Begin(SpriteSortMode_Deferred);
        this->greeting_->draw(sprite_batch);
        this->hint_->draw(sprite_batch);
        sprite_batch->End();

        ID3D11CommandList* commands = nullptr;
        if (FAILED(deferred->FinishCommandList(FALSE, &commands)))
        {
            throw std::runtime_error("HelloState::draw - FinishCommandList failed");
        }

        device->GetD3DDeviceContext()->ExecuteCommandList(commands, FALSE);
        commands->Release();
    }

`grep -rn "draw_sprite" engine/` returns nothing.

**Why it matters:** T10's acceptance test is "a feature that can't be explained in an
introductory series has an API that is too hard." This one needs: what a deferred context is,
why `sprite_batches()->at(0)` must pair with `deferred_context(0)` (verified — the batches are
constructed against the deferred contexts at `engine/app/application.cpp:162-164`, so the
pairing is load-bearing and stated nowhere), command-list recording, the immediate-versus-
deferred distinction, and COM reference counting. That is five D3D11 concepts and one manual
`Release()` before "hello world" appears. PHILOSOPHY/Simulation and rendering specifies
`draw_sprite(texture, src, dst, tint, rotation, origin, depth)` with D3D11 behind it; that
seam does not exist, so this protocol is not a temporary detail, it is the public API.

The old review reported the absence of a renderer abstraction. What is new is that
`samples/minimal/` was written *after* it and enshrines the protocol as the canonical shape
for every project copied from the template.

**Remedy:** Land the renderer interface before the sample is advertised; until then have the
shell open and close the frame so a state's `draw()` receives only a batch.

#### Microsoft's `DeviceResources` and `StepTimer` are presented as engine code with no attribution

- **File:** `engine/render/device_resources.h:1-24`
- **Severity:** high
- **Category:** docs
- **Tenet:** T9; ARCHITECTURE/The tree

**What:** Two files in `engine/` are Microsoft's DirectX template sources, re-namespaced into
`artattack` with the copyright and licence notice absent, and they are what sets the naming
style in the engine's most public header.

**Evidence:**

`engine/render/device_resources.h:1-3` and `:14-17`

    //
    // DeviceResources.h - A wrapper for the Direct3D 11 device and swapchain
    //
    ...
    namespace artattack
    {
        // Provides an interface for an application that owns DeviceResources to be notified of the device being lost or created.
        interface IDeviceNotify

`git show 3ed124a:ArtAttack/DeviceResources.h` and `...:ArtAttack/StepTimer.h` both open with
the same comment banner and `namespace DX` — the DirectX Win32 Game template's own namespace.
`engine/core/step_timer.h:1-3, 12`:

    //
    // StepTimer.h - A simple timer that provides elapsed time information
    //
    ...
    namespace artattack

`grep -rn "Copyright\|Microsoft Corporation\|MIT" engine/` finds no notice in either file.

**Why it matters:** ARCHITECTURE.md's tree reserves `external/` for "third-party source", and
T9 draws the built/bought line at the platform edge — this is bought code filed as built. For
a project meant to be handed to strangers that is a licence-compliance defect, and it is also
why `application.h`, the engine's flagship header, declares
`class Application : public IDeviceNotify, public StateContext` and overrides `OnDeviceLost()`
/`OnDeviceRestored()` — PascalCase methods and an `I`-prefixed type, both on CONVENTIONS'
Never list — alongside thirty `m_`-prefixed members at `device_resources.h:107-138`, also on
the Never list. A reader cannot tell which style is the engine's.

**Remedy:** Restore Microsoft's copyright/MIT header on both files and either move them under
`external/` or state the provenance and the local modifications at the top of each.
